The results show that the highest accuracy values are obtained with the DeiT model at 96.5% in the chest X-ray dataset, the PVTv2 model at 91.6% in the breast histology dataset, the PVTv2 model at 91.3% in the retina fundus dataset, and the Swin model at 91.0% in the skin lesion dataset.
keywords: ["vision transformer", "medical image classification", "Swin Transformer", "color fundus images", "skin lesion classification", "chest X-ray classification", "breast histology", "model performance comparison", "long-range dependencies"]

title: G-HCF: Product Recommendation by GNN Based Hybrid Collaborative Filtering
abstract: In general, product recommendation by collaborative filtering approaches aim at learning an optimum mapping between customer and product representations. The main input they use is the customer-product matrix. These approaches, at best, utilize the customer-customer and product-product relations indirectly. The proposed method uses a customer-product graph, enriched by the customer-customer and product-product relations, with graph neural networks to predict the customer-product relations. These relations are extracted from data by matrix decomposition. Comparative assessment on real data showed improved performance compared to pure matrix decomposition and standard graph models.
keywords: ["product recommendation", "collaborative filtering", "graph neural networks", "hybrid collaborative filtering", "matrix factorization", "recommender systems"]

title: A Novel Approach for Microwave Oven Technology Mikrodalga Firin Teknolojisine Yeni Bir Yaklaşim
abstract: Microwave ovens incorporate a perforated cover design to enable visualization of the interior while in operation. The heating of food within these ovens is facilitated by electromagnetic (EM) waves, which are generated inside and cannot escape through the cover's perforations, as their diameter is smaller than the wavelength of the EM wave. This study aims to modify the cover design and operating frequency of a microwave oven in a theoretical and simulation environment. The proposed design operates at a frequency of 4 GHz and features a cover with 49 full, 14 half and 1 quartile round holes, each with a diameter of 2 mm. The EM waves are emitted from the upper posterior wall on the right side of the cover (port 1), and only escape through the cover's perforations (port 2) due to the metal covering on all walls. Loose steel material with 1008 properties was utilized for simulation purposes, and open air boundary conditions were applied to the cover's zone while conducting wall boundary conditions were utilized in other sections. The study also analyzed the EM field propagation characteristics and found that a minimum of -164.1 dB was achieved at 3.98 GHz and -163.7 dB at 4 GHz. The results demonstrate the creation of a cap that functions as a band-stopping filter, and the investigation of S parameters, particularly S21. Finally, this study presents a novel microwave oven technology.
keywords: ["microwave oven", "electromagnetic wave propagation", "band-stop filter", "S-parameters", "S21", "electromagnetic simulation", "food heating"]

title: Modified QPSK Modulation for Frequency Multiplied Transmission
abstract: In this study, a new proposal has been made about the frequency multiplication method. In the modified QPSK modulator developed for data transmission used frequency multiplication, the constellation diagram has been modified. It has been shown that data transmission can be provided with a little power loss without any change on the receiver side in a real-time system through the change perform in the transmitter. This proposed method was experimentally implemented using USRP. As a result of the performance analysis, BER graphs and eye diagrams obtained by applying both standard QPSK and proposed modified QPSK modulation are presented.
keywords: ["frequency multiplication", "QPSK modulation", "constellation diagram", "power loss reduction", "USRP", "bit error rate", "eye diagram", "data transmission"]

title: Employing Transformer Encoders for Enhanced Functional Connectivity Mapping
abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) provides a way to spatially and temporally map brain activity, making it a crucial tool in many advanced psychology and neuroscience studies. A variety of techniques are suggested to analyze the four-dimensional data produced by fMRI scans. When it comes to classification tasks, the most prevalent method involves examining functional connectivity. This process involves dividing the brain volume into separate regions and determining the correlation between the series of events occurring over time in these regions. While deep graph models and deep convolutional models are frequently employed to process functional connectivity, these methods can sometimes overcomplicate the procedure. In contrast, we present a straightforward approach that utilizes transformer encoders to map functional connectivity to labels. Our method demonstrates superior performance in gender classification tasks when compared to existing deep graph and convolution models. We've validated this on two publicly accessible datasets.
keywords: ["functional connectivity", "Transformer encoder", "functional MRI", "brain region classification", "gender classification", "brain activity mapping"]

title: Radar Intrapulse Modulation Classification with Deep Learning
abstract: Identification of threat radar signals is extremely important for electronic support systems. Radar intrapulse modulations are used by electronic support systems to identify radar systems. In this work, radar intrapulse modulations are classified using signal processing and deep learning techniques. Short Time Fourier Transform, Fourier Synchrosqueezed Transform and Smoothed Pseudo Wigner Ville Distrubution are used to extract time-frequency images of radar signals. After feature extraction, convolutional neural network is used as classifier and %98 modulation classification performance is achieved at 0 dB signal to noise ratio.
keywords: ["automatic modulation classification", "electronic support systems", "short-time Fourier transform", "smoothed pseudo Wigner-Ville distribution", "time-frequency analysis", "convolutional neural networks", "feature extraction"]

title: DoG-Loss for Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Semantic segmentation is an important machine vision problem with many applications. It aims to classify images based on pixels and label each pixel. One of the main challenges of this problem is to ensure that the contours of the objects are accurate and the areas they cover are detected in a holistic manner. In addition, the successful learning of low-frequency classes in the datasets by the model and the preservation of object integrity also significantly affect the success. In this study, a difference of Gaussian (DoG) based loss function is proposed to improve segmentation accuracy and class estimation. In this way, the segmentation model focuses on the contours of the objects to better preserve their shape integrity. Experiments show that the proposed DoG loss function achieves up to %3.9 better results than the commonly used segmentation loss functions.
keywords: ["semantic segmentation", "loss function design", "pixel classification"]

title: Elimination of Elevation Induced Errors in Hybrid Direction Finding
abstract: In electronic support systems, direction finding plays a critical role in detecting the location of threat radar signals. Phase comparison direction finding method obtains direction information by measuring the phase differences between radar signals received by different antennas. However, this method introduces phase ambiguity. The hybrid method, which combines phase and amplitude comparison methods, is used to resolve these ambiguities. In this study, the performance of a hybrid direction finding system consisting of two antennas was tested against threat signals coming from different elevations. The aim of the study is to increase the immunity of the amplitude comparison algorithm to elevation differences within the hybrid method.
keywords: ["phase comparison", "amplitude comparison", "phase ambiguity resolution", "electronic support systems", "two-antenna systems"]

title: Crowd Counting via Joint SASNet and a Guided Batch Normalization Network
abstract: Recent studies on crowd counting have achieved promising results by using convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures. However, due to the large variation in scene distribution in real-world crowd datasets, it remains a challenge to achieve high performance using standard CNN methods. Such methods often suffer from performance drops. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a new crowd-counting approach that combines three state-of-the-art methods: Guided-Batch-Normalization, which adapts the model using unseen dataset normalization parameters; the Scale Adaptive Selection Network, which uses a multi-level network to obtain variation feature representations; and Distribution-Matching-Count, which uses a new loss function between prediction and ground truth maps. Combining these methods results in improved performance. Extensive experiments across multiple datasets have demonstrated that the proposed approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
keywords: ["crowd counting", "multi-level feature representation"]

title: Automatic Selection of Compiler Optimizations by Machine Learning
abstract: Many widely used telecommunications applications have extremely long run times. Therefore, faster and more efficient execution of these codes on the same hardware is important in critical telecommunication applications such as base stations. Compilers greatly affect the properties of the executable program to be created. It is possible to change properties such as compilation speed, execution time, power consumption and code size using compiler flags. This study aims to find the set of flags that will provide the shortest run time among hundreds of compiler flag combinations in GCC using code flow analysis, loop analysis and machine learning methods without running the program.
keywords: ["compiler flags", "GCC", "execution time prediction", "loop analysis", "telecommunication applications", "base station", "power consumption", "program size", "machine learning"]

title: Third Level Identification with Hyperspectral Imaging in Fingerprints
abstract: Fingerprints are accepted as the key evidence in reaching the crime and the criminal. Identification from fingerprints is done at three levels. At the first level; fingerprint groups and subgroups, at the second level; fingerprint line characteristics, and at the third level, details such as pores, papilla structure, width, mold area and fractures. With the developing technology, algorithms are developed in which fingerprint direction and angle, combinations of placement between papillary characteristics and papillary flows are included in the evaluation process. In the study, 1–n queries were made in a dataset created from 800 fingerprints by manually and automatically extracted features with the blob detection algorithm, by randomly generating the latent fingerprints on which the pore details were displayed on the fingerprint line characteristics with hyperspectral imaging. In the fingerprint query, the latent fingerprints and the plain tenprints in the dataset were ranked using a score-based approach using the iterative closest point algorithm. According to the results obtained, it was observed that the score of the first candidate was higher and the scores of the candidates who came after it, were lower with the increase in the number of pores marked on the papilla lines and the accurate marking of these pores.
keywords: ["fingerprint recognition", "hyperspectral imaging", "latent fingerprints", "pore detection", "papillary pattern", "blob detection", "iterative closest point", "fingerprint matching"]

title: Context and Sentiment Aware Chatbot for Tourism Applications
abstract: Recently, advances in the informatics field have changed the tourism and hospitality sectors drastically. The interaction between the service provider and the customer is revolutionized by employing sophisticated chatbots. Although there are a lot of chatbots, most of them are not sentiment and contextaware. In this study, we developed a context and sentiment-aware chatbot for tourism applications. First, we created a database that includes frequently asked questions in the tourism area. We then automatically correct mistakes in the customer queries and compute the similarity of queries with existing sentences in the database and respond to them with the corresponding answer. We also monitor the sentiment of users continuously and try to estimate the context (before sales and after-sales). The proposed system has promising results for real-life applications.
keywords: ["chatbots", "tourism applications", "frequently asked questions", "query correction", "query similarity", "customer service", "hospitality"]

title: OAI-Based Software Defined Radio Implementation
abstract: Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) has become crucial in today's world, where the need for communication is increasing day by day. A recently surfaced need for private networks caused by the diversed applications can be given as one of the examples. One of the most important initiatives, which has contributed to many fields from the industry just like Open RAN, is Open Air Interface (OAI). Today, open source codes of 5G technology are readily available in OAI platforms. In this way, it is possible to test the compliance of the newly developed methods with the standards or the existing cellular communication standards in the laboratory environment. In this study, data rate measurement is realized for different values of the modulation and coding scheme (MCS) in a test environment constituted by using 5G open source codes. Additionally, I/Q samples of the Physical Uplink Shared Channel (PUSCH) are observed. The real-time results obtained are compared with the theoretical analyzes found in the standards.
keywords: ["OpenAirInterface", "software-defined radio", "Open RAN", "5G", "modulation and coding scheme", "PUSCH", "IQ samples"]

title: Gaze Estimation by Attention Using a Two-Stream Regression Network
abstract: Determining the point of view of people is an important human-computer interaction problem that has been studied for a long time. This subject, which has many applications, is used in different fields such as marketing, automotive, medical, games and entertainment. In this study, we propose a remote eye tracking method that makes gaze estimation using convolutional neural network based on regression. The proposed method uses a two-stream deep learning architecture that utilizes eye images and iris segmentation masks obtained through segmentation neural network. The architecture employed selective attention-based mechanisms to enhance its performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the attention-based two-stream architecture outperforms both single-stream deep learning architectures and architectures without attention mechanisms.
keywords: ["gaze estimation", "remote eye tracking", "selective attention", "eye image analysis", "human-computer interaction", "convolutional neural networks"]

title: Location-Based Visible Light Communication
abstract: Visible light communication (VLC) takes its place among wireless access technologies as an alternative to radio frequency (RF) systems. Although VLC has significant advantages over RF systems (not being affected by electromagnetic interference (EMI), having a wide spectrum range, energy efficiency, etc.), it also has its own problems. One of these problems is the high correlation between channels in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) structures. In this paper, a receiver structure with adjustable azimuth and elevation angles is proposed for MIMO VLC. The position of the receiver is determined by means of the receiver signal strength indicator (RSSI) parameter. The best angles were set for the MIMO receiver using positioning data. Repetition coding (RC) and spatial multiplexing (SMP) are used as MIMO schemes and bit error rate (BER) performance is obtained. The proposed receiver structure provides SNR gains at different locations in both schemes.
keywords: ["visible light communication", "MIMO VLC", "location-based communication", "azimuth and elevation angles", "receiver positioning", "repetition coding", "spatial multiplexing", "bit error rate", "channel correlation"]

title: Roadside Barrier Detection and Tracking with Radar: A Real Life Application
abstract: Perception is one of the key elements in the autonomous driving systems. Especially, it is vital to track the states of the vehicles and the obstacles around the ego vehicle to avoid collision or accidents. These surrounding objects which are detected by radars that are integrated in the outer part of the autonomous driving vehicles. However, the measurements of the static obstacles such as barriers and guardrails are interfering with the measurements of the surrounding vehicles nearby the ego vehicle. Hence,it is essential to develop an algorithm which can remove the barrier and guardrail measurements. In this paper, a heuristic algorithm is developed in order to detect the barrier data which are among all the measurements and distinguish them from the relevant object measurements detected by radars. The algorithm detects the barrier measurements with 1D clustering and fits curves to the measurements, then tracks the already fit barrier curves with individual Kalman Filters. Once the filtered barriers are established, the algorithm removes the measurements that are in a distance from the tracked barriers.
keywords: ["autonomous driving perception", "obstacle tracking", "curve fitting", "Kalman filter", "measurement interference"]

title: Insult Detection in the Turkish Language Through Different Machine Learning Algorithms
abstract: In this research paper, we propose to use the Turkish Court of Cassation- Yargitay- cases to build a dataset for insult detection tasks and compare machine learning models trained on this dataset. We accumulated studies available in the literature compiling Court of Cassation cases and generated a train and test set for testing machine learning algorithms for insult detection. Although machine learning is not capable of understanding the legal context, cultural background, and the nature of insults or non-insults, it can help identify insults with proper training data created by experts. As far as for the authors knowledge this is the first study to use machine learning for the purpose of automatically distinguishing between insult and non-insult cases within the Turkish justice system. Our research, though its is in its first steps, represents a significant contribution to the field, as it addresses a gap in the existing literature and provides a machine learning approach to improving the efficiency and accuracy of legal decision-making.
keywords: ["Turkish language", "legal text classification", "classifier comparison", "legal decision-making", "annotated dataset"]

title: Error Performance of DCO-OFDM Based Visible Light Communication System with Signal Space Diversity
abstract: In this study, direct current optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM), which is one of the multicarrier transmission techniques designed for intensity modulation/direct detection method applied to visible light communication (VLC) systems, has been studied. The error performance of the modeled DCO-OFDM based VLC system is enhanced significantly by integrating signal space diversity (without causing any additional computational complexity).
keywords: ["DCO-OFDM", "visible light communication", "signal space diversity", "error performance", "intensity modulation and direct detection", "multicarrier transmission", "optical OFDM"]

title: Creation of Annotated Synthetic UAV Video Dataset for Object Detection and Tracking
abstract: In order for object detection and tracking in videos obtained from unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) by deep convolutional neural networks (DCNN), extensive ground truth optical flow, occlusion and segmentation datasets, of various objects or vehicles, are required during the training and testing processes. The mentioned ground truth informations are not widely available in the literature due to the difficulty of labeling or extracting them from real-life recorded UAV video images. In this study, ground truth optical flow, occlusion and segmentation datasets were produced synthetically for the first time with the UAV point of view in a novel way, so as to fill the gap in literature. The ground truth datasets were created for each vehicle by subjecting the triangles (mesh) automatically generated by the Unity engine to the homography method. With this method, 1920x1080 and 250x250 sized synthetic datasets consisting of 100 scenarios were obtained.
keywords: ["synthetic video dataset", "UAV video", "object detection", "object tracking", "occlusion", "semantic segmentation", "homography", "Unity game engine", "vehicle tracking"]

title: Denoising Diffusion Adversarial Models for Unconditional Medical Image Generation
abstract: Unconditional medical image synthesis is the task of generating realistic and diverse medical images from random noise without any prior information or constraints. Synthesizing realistic medical images can enrich the quality and diversity of medical imaging datasets, which in turn, enhance the performance and generalization of deep learning models for medical imaging. Prevalent approach for synthesizing medical images involves generative adversarial networks (GAN) or denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPM). However, GAN models that implicitly learn the image distribution are prone to limited sample fidelity and diversity. On the other hand, diffusion models suffer from slow sampling speed due to small diffusion steps. In this paper, we propose a novel diffusion-based method for unconditional medical image synthesis, Diff-Med-Synth, that generates realistic and diverse medical images from random noise. Diff-Med-Synth combines the advantages of denoising diffusion probabilistic models and GANs to achieve fast and efficient image sampling. We evaluate our method on two multi-contrast MRI datasets and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of quality, diversity, and fidelity of the synthesized images.
keywords: ["denoising diffusion probabilistic models", "generative adversarial networks", "multi-contrast MRI"]

title: Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis Using Olfactory Stimulus Evoked Electroencephalography Signals
abstract: Olfactory loss is commonly recognized as one of the first symptoms of Alzheimer's disease, which makes it a potential biomarker for early diagnosis. However, psychophysical and electrophysiological tests, routinely used for diagnosis, are often not sufficient for detection of olfactory loss. In this study, chemosensory evoked electroencephalography (EEG) signals were characterized via brain-computer interface feature extraction methods to classify Alzheimer's patients and healthy individuals. Results showed that combining EEG features and University of Pennsylvania Smell Identification Test (UPSIT) scores commonly used for diagnosis of olfactory loss, achieved a conspicuous success rate of nearly 92% in diagnosis. The findings suggest that the proposed approach can be considered as a new strategy for early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease
keywords: ["Alzheimer's disease", "olfactory loss", "EEG feature extraction", "brain-computer interface", "UPSIT", "early diagnosis", "biomarkers", "patient classification"]

title: Victim Detection System via Geophone Arrays
abstract: This study introduces a hardware and software system that utilize a seismic sensor (geophone) array for automatic detection of earthquake victims. In the hardware system, highresolution external analog-to-digital converters and microprocessors are used to collect data from geophones. The collected data is then transferred to the operation computer via wired or wireless networks. The results of the location determination, based on a fast and operator-independent method using time delay, are displayed on an enhanced interface. Ongoing research is focused on improving the accuracy of direction estimation through cross- correlation calculations and further processing steps.
keywords: ["geophone array", "seismic sensors", "time delay estimation", "direction estimation", "cross correlation function", "analog-to-digital converter", "wireless data transmission", "disaster response"]

title: Performance Analysis under Signal Jammer in Relay Aided Ambient Backscatter Cognitive Radio Networks
abstract: In this study, the first system model with a single IoT (Internet of Things), one relay user and the second system model with two IoT, two relay users are proposed. Both systems are considered as a cognitive radio based ambient backscatter network model, allowing users to harvest energy with the signal emitted by the power station. It is assumed that the jammer in the network deteriorates the quality of the signal reaching the receiver. The IoT device both performs active transmission using the energy it harvests and transmits data to the information receiver via backscatter. The relay user, decodes the information scattered by the IoT device and then forwards it to the receiver. In this collaborative structure, how long the IoT device will backscatter, harvest energy and actively transmit data is presented as a problem. Our goal is to maximize the number of bits reaching the information receiver. After finding the system variables through numerical analysis, the total number of bits reaching the receiver was obtained. In the results discussed, in addition to comparing both models with each other, it is considered as a benchmark in different scenarios. The results show that the increase in the number of relays and IoT clearly improves the performance.
keywords: ["ambient backscatter", "cognitive radio", "jamming", "Internet of Things", "energy harvesting", "bit rate maximization", "cooperative communication"]

title: Accelerometer-Based Timing Analysis for Parkinson's Disease Classification
abstract: Parkinson's disease is a neurodegenerative disorder caused by dopamine deficiency in the basal ganglia, resulting in cognitive and motor impairments. In this study, accelerometer signals were used to estimate the delay time between the command to start pedaling and the actual movement onset in three groups: healthy individuals (n=13), Parkinson's disease patients (n=13), and patients with freezing of gait symptoms (n=13). Features were extracted from the delay time distributions for each participant and subjected to a triple classification. Linear support vector machine achieved a classification accuracy of 69. 2% for all participants. Notably, the average time to start pedaling was found to be significantly different among the three groups, and accelerometer-based timing analysis could be used as a diagnostic tool to assist clinical tests.
keywords: ["Parkinson's disease", "freezing of gait", "accelerometer signals", "timing analysis", "motor impairment", "Parkinson's disease classification", "support vector machine", "wearable sensors", "diagnosis"]

title: NER2Map: Positive Transfer from Named Entity Recognition to Address Parsing in Low Data Regimes
abstract: In natural language processing, the time and human resource costs associated with data labeling have led to a focus on solving problems with limited data. In this study, two separate models for Address Parsing were developed using transfer lear-ning methods. Specifically, the BERT model was first fine-tuned on the NER dataset, and then the effects of fine-tuning on a relatively small Address Parsing dataset were examined, resulting in a method called NER2Map. Experimental results show that the NER2Map model achieves higher accuracy in predicting correct labels with limited data compared to directly fine-tuned BERT Address Parsing model. Additionally, the importance of transfer learning in this problem and the ability to achieve good results using a small amount of data have been observed.
keywords: ["named entity recognition", "transfer learning", "BERT fine-tuning", "low-resource data", "limited training data"]

title: Building Segmentation on Satellite Images and Performance of Post-Processing Methods
abstract: Researchers are doing intensive work on satellite images due to the information it contains with the development of computer vision algorithms and the ease of accessibility to satellite images. Building segmentation of satellite images can be used for many potential applications such as city, agricultural, and communication network planning. However, since no dataset exists for every region, the model trained in a region must gain generality. In this study, we trained several models in China and post-processing work was done on the best model selected among them. These models are evaluated in the Chicago region of the INRIA dataset. As can be seen from the results, although state-of-art results in this area have not been achieved, the results are promising. We aim to present our initial experimental results of a building segmentation from satellite images in this study.
keywords: ["building segmentation", "satellite imagery", "post-processing", "semantic segmentation", "model generalization", "INRIA dataset", "Chicago", "urban planning"]

title: Heterogeneous Network Design for mmWave Channels with Blockage Model
abstract: In this study, an artificial neural network (ANN) model that predicts handover (HO) among cells for user equip-ments that take place in millimeter wave (mmWave) and Sub-6GHz networks is proposed. In the proposed model, a dataset containing the reference signal received power (RSRP) values of the base stations where the UEs are registered and neighboring is used. Existing algorithms can be disadvantageous due to the nature of mmWave networks being extremely sensitive to the conditions of the communication environment. This model is more practical compared to existing HO algorithms, and the simulation results show that HO procedures can be performed with high accuracy using this model.
keywords: ["millimeter-wave channels", "handover prediction", "artificial neural networks", "RSRP", "user equipment", "base station selection"]

title: A Novel Motor Imagery Recognition Approach Based On Perception Latency and Short-Lived Synchronizations
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach for investigating a brain-computer interface that considers the temporal organization of brain activity, explicitly accounting for perception latency. To this end, we aligned the onset of task periods with the concurrence of left parietal and parieto-occipital electrodes to obtain the timings of perception latencies. Then, activity-specific synchronization timings between channel pairs were calculated using the time-aligned task periods. The perception latency and activity-specific synchronization timings were subsequently used for feature extraction and classification. The proposed approach achieved significantly better performance when comparing the proposed approach with the method that did not account for the perception latency
keywords: ["motor imagery recognition", "brain-computer interface", "feature extraction", "EEG classification"]

title: Design of Three-Stage Two-Way and Four-Way 2-6 GHz Power Combiner
abstract: In this study, Wilkinson type two-way and four-way power dividers (PD) are designed to be used in broadband high-power amplifier designs, circuit and electromagnetic (EM) simulations are made. RT5870 with a dielectric thickness of 31 mil and a copper thickness of 35 μm was used as the substrate. Vishay RCP series resistors were chosen as isolation resistors to be suitable for high power applications. A 3-stage design has been made to provide required bandwidth. The circuit and EM simulation results overlap. According to the EM simulation results, -3.2 dB of insertion loss and less than -14 dB of return loss values were obtained over the band for two-way PD. A 4-way PD is obtained by cascading two-way PDs. In the EM simulation results of this circuit, -6.7 dB of insertion loss and less than -10 dB of return loss were obtained over the band. The isolation values between the ports are lower than -20 dB over the band in all PDs.
keywords: ["power divider", "Wilkinson power divider", "two-way power divider", "four-way power divider", "2.6 GHz", "isolation resistor", "insertion loss", "return loss", "electromagnetic simulation"]

title: Mackey-Glass Time Series Prediction with Immune Plasma Programming
abstract: Automatic Programming (AP) is one of the subfields of artificial intelligence that enables efficient modeling of systems. Immune Plasma Programming (IPP), one of the newly proposed AP methods, is developed taking inspiration from plasma tre-atment. In this study, mathematical models using IPP for time series prediction are proposed. It is also compared with well-known AP methods such as Genetic Programming and Artificial Bee Colony Programming. According to the simulation results, IPP has proven that it can be applied to real-world problems by showing superior performance on various performance criteria compared to other methods.
keywords: ["Mackey-Glass time series", "time series forecasting", "program synthesis", "genetic programming", "mathematical modeling"]

title: A Reinforcement Learning based Collection Approach
abstract: Reaching out to customers for debt collection is an important process for banks. The most commonly used channels for reaching out are text messages and phone calls. While phone calls are more effective, there is a daily capacity limit. Currently, the customers to be called are determined by a rule-based system. The rules are based on the customer's risk segment and the number of late days. It is anticipated that making a customer specific decision is more efficient than using general segments. In this study, an offline reinforcement learning-based approach that uses the existing data to make call decisions for individual customers has been developed. In this approach, customer information, customer behaviors and previous collection actions define the state space and whether to call the customer or not define the action space. Furthermore, a reward function that uses the call costs and late days is designed. This formulation is then used to learn a Q-value model using the random ensemble method. A call-decision approach is developed using the output of this model alongside daily call capacity and additional rules. In live A-B tests, the developed method was observed to yield better results than the current rule-based method.
keywords: ["debt collection", "reinforcement learning", "customer segmentation", "late payment", "Q-learning", "random ensembles", "reward function", "call capacity", "A/B testing"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Automatic Detection of Aortic Valve on Echocardiographic Images
abstract: Aortic stenosis is the narrowing of the aortic valve due to structural damage. Common cause is the formation of calcification in the aortic valve, which occurs with age. An expert cardiologist generates an approximate score for the volume and severity of calcification by focusing on the aortic regions of interest in echocardiography images for the diagnosis of aortic stenosis. In this study, a novel dataset consisting of echocardiography images of the aortic valve was created. The regions of interest in the aortic valve were manually annotated in the training and validation datasets, and the images in the training dataset were used to train the four sub-versions of the YOLOv5 model. The validation dataset was used to evaluate the performance of the network during the training process, and the test dataset were used to evaluate the performance of the trained models. The highest mAP value of 99.5% was achieved with the YOLOv5-x model at an IoU threshold of 0.9. Additionally, the precision value was 99.9% and the recall value was 97.5%. The models demonstrated the ability to detect aortic valves very close to the expert cardiologist's accurately labeled ground-truth, even in aortic valves of different scales and orientations.
keywords: ["aortic stenosis", "echocardiography", "YOLOv5", "object detection", "aortic valve calcification", "medical image annotation", "deep learning"]

title: Secrecy Outage Probability of SWIPT-OFDMA Schemes with Transmit Antenna Selection
abstract: This study examines the wireless communications secrecy performance of multi-user (MU) simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) scheme employing transmit antenna selection (TAS) and maximal-ratio combining (MRC). In order to address the user scheduling requirement of MU-SWIPT scheme, orthogonal frequency-division multiple access (OFDMA) has been utilized, and the secrecy outage probability (SOP) performance is examined via simulations. In the study, it is aimed to examine a realistic scenario where eavesdropper might detect the sub-carrier indices of the legitimate users. In addition, the variation of the SOP performance has been revealed for different values of the number of legitimate users, the number of eavesdropper antennas, the power division factor related to the SWIPT process and the noise variance introduced by the information decoder.
keywords: ["secrecy outage probability", "simultaneous wireless information and power transfer", "transmit antenna selection", "OFDMA", "maximum ratio combining", "wireless network security"]

title: Online Improvement of CCA Performance in BCI Spellers
abstract: The performance enhancement of Steady-State vi-sually evoked potential (SSVEP) based brain computer studies are mainly based on finding subject-based patterns and combi-nations. Finding person-based patterns and making use of them for the system involves a training process. It may not be easy or possible for people to attend long and tiring training sessions. The training process can be shortened or even eliminated by integrating already prepared patterns regarding the similarity between subject's data and existing patterns. In addition to the already existing templates, using an adaptive algorithm will eventually come up with patterns that have a better handle on the subjects’ data. In this conference paper, we describe the combination of an adaptive algorithm with the integration of various filters formed from already existing data sets.
keywords: ["steady-state visual evoked potentials", "adaptive algorithms", "template-based classification", "filter integration", "training-free classification"]

title: A Hybrid Text Classification Approach for Chatbots
abstract: Chatbots are preferred in many fields due to their ability to provide fast and uninterrupted customer service at all hours. Most chatbots work by classifying input text and responding accordingly. In this work, a hybrid chatbot app-roach is presented by combining a commercial system and a deep learning-based text classification model. Additionally, active learning-based label correction and data expansion approaches are used to increase chatbot performance and keep it up-to-date. In offline tests, the hybrid method made three times fewer errors than the methods it was composed of. Online evaluations performed after deployment show that the hybrid method was able to preserve its superiority and that keeping the dataset up-to-date had positive contributions.
keywords: ["chatbots", "text classification", "hybrid classification", "deep learning", "active learning (machine learning)", "label correction", "data expansion", "customer service", "online assessment"]

title: Improving Direction Finding Performance with SBI Algorithm in Interferometry Method
abstract: In this paper, the accuracy performance of the SBI (SODA-Based Inference) direction-finding algorithm, which has a fast and high accuracy capability for electronic support systems, was analysed. The SBI algorithm aims to estimate the angle of arrival of the threat radar signal without producing ambiguity using three or more collinear antennas. The main principle of the SBI algorithm is composed of the interferometry and SODA method. Interferometry estimates the angle of arrival of the threat radar signal by using the phase difference between the two antennas. However, in interferometry, when the physical distance between two antennas is more than half of the wavelength of the threat radar signal, there is ambiguity in the angle estimation. Therefore, the SODA method proposes adding a third antenna to the system to make an unambiguous angle of arrival estimation. Moreover, the SBI algorithm aims to significantly improve the accuracy of the SODA method by using all antennas in the system.
keywords: ["direction finding", "interferometry", "angle of arrival estimation", "electronic support systems", "radar signal detection", "phase difference", "ambiguity resolution"]

title: Federated Learning in Predicting Heart Disease
abstract: Heart diseases are a significant health problem worldwide, and early diagnosis and prediction are of great im-portance. Artificial intelligence and machine learning techniques have become effective tools in predicting heart diseases. However, when traditional centralized approaches are used, challenges arise in terms of data privacy and security. The federated learning approach is presented as an important solution to address these issues. In this study, our aim is to predict heart diseases while preserving patient privacy and confidentiality using the federated learning approach. Experiments were conducted using the open-source dataset "PTB Diagnostic ECG Database" to compare the results of centralized and federated learning. Through this comparison, it has been shown that federated learning can achieve results close to centralized learning in cases where sharing sensitive data such as health data is problematic. Additionally, in the experiments conducted using different feature selection and machine learning models, both logistic regression and support vector machines showed the best accuracy results with mRMR feature selection in both centralized (86%) and federated training (85%). When examining the F1-Score results, applying feature selection in both classification models allowed for the best results (federated learning: 91%, centralized learning: 92%).
keywords: ["federated learning", "heart disease prediction", "data privacy", "patient confidentiality", "PTB Diagnostic ECG Database", "feature selection", "minimum redundancy maximum relevance", "logistic regression", "support vector machine", "health data sharing"]

title: Wind Power Prediction Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Algorithms
abstract: In this study, it has been tried to predict the wind power generation values in a long-term period by using a dataset containing the wind power generation values of 10 zones using machine learning and deep learning methods. In this context, the importance of accurately predicting renewable energy production was emphasized by associating it with machine learning and deep learning methods. The methods to be used in the study were selected based on the literature review and the characteristics of the time series datasets. Since the dataset includes the basic wind components, a detailed feature analysis was performed, and the dataset was enriched with the newly added features. The hyperparameters of the utilized models were optimized for all regions in the dataset separately and the models were run with these hyperparameters. The results of the models were evaluated with different error metrics and compared with each other, and the models with the lowest error scores were determined.
keywords: ["wind power forecasting", "renewable energy generation", "time series forecasting", "feature engineering", "hyperparameter optimization", "model comparison"]

title: Alternative Data Sources and Psychometric Scales Supported Credit Scoring Models
abstract: This study aims to evaluate individuals with limited access to banking services and enhance credit scoring models with alternative data sources. A psychometric-based credit scoring model was developed and tested. Despite limited data, significant potential findings were obtained. However, clarification of the distinction between credit payment intention and ability and validation of the results with more data are necessary.
keywords: ["alternative data", "psychometric scale", "credit scoring models", "creditworthiness assessment", "behavioral data"]

title: A Transformer-Based Prior Legal Case Retrieval Method
abstract: In this work, BERTurk-Legal, a transformer-based language model, is introduced to retrieve prior legal cases. BERTurk-Legal is pre-trained on a dataset from the Turkish legal domain. This dataset does not contain any labels related to the prior court case retrieval task. Masked language modeling is used to train BERTurk-Legal in a self-supervised manner. With zero-shot classification, BERTurk-Legal provides state-of-the-art results on the dataset consisting of legal cases of the Court of Cassation of Turkey. The results of the experiments show the necessity of developing language models specific to the Turkish law domain.
keywords: ["transformer language models", "masked language modeling", "zero-shot classification", "legal text retrieval", "domain-specific language models"]

title: Federated Topology Preserving Domain Adaptation for Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Federated Learning enables decentralized training of machine learning models by collaborating with multiple clients without sharing their data. However, limited labeled data in clients' domains can lead to overfitted local models and compromise the performance of the global model. To overcome this, we propose a novel approach by adopting a single source and multiple targets, considering variations in the style and movements of each client as distinct domains within Human Activity Recognition (HAR). The Modified Topology Preserving Domain Adaptation (modTPDA) is utilized to align the topological structure and preserve the underlying data manifold. Integrating modTPDA with the FL aims to adapt public source data in the server to various target domains with private data, accounting for their data topology. The proposed approach effectively addresses the issue of limited labeled data in Federated Learning for Human Activity Recognition.
keywords: ["federated learning", "domain adaptation", "human activity recognition", "limited labeled data"]

title: The Effect of Optimal Selection of ADC Frequencies on Performance in Multirate Sampling Receivers
abstract: In this work, the effect of optimal selection of ADC frequencies on the success of frequency estimation in multirate sampling receivers. The receivers that use different number of ADCs are compared with different input bandwiths.
keywords: ["frequency estimation", "input bandwidth", "receiver performance"]

title: On the Use of Kinect V2 For the Assessment of Upper Extremity Movements
abstract: Upper extremity assessment is an important step in rehabilitation and treatment of upper extremity impairments. Current assessment methods are mostly based on likert type scales. For example, Fugl-Meyer test is one of the common but subjective tests for upper extremity assessment. The aim of this study is to test the reliability of Kinect V2 camera as an assessment tool of upper extremity movements in the FuglMeyer test. Thirty volunteers participated in the study performed ten upper extremity movements in front of a Kinect V2 camera. After data acquisition, collected data is used to calculate the joint angles. Calculated angle values are examined in terms of relative reliability via Intraclass Correlation Coefficient (ICC), and absolute reliability via Standard Error of Measurement (SEM), Minimum Detectable Change (MDC) for both within-day, and between-days measurements. Results indicate that Kinect V2 provides good to excellent ICC values for within-day, and medium to good ICC values for betweendays. In addition, Kinect V2 has higher absolute reliability in within-day measurements than between-days measurements.
keywords: ["Kinect v2", "Fugl-Meyer Assessment", "joint angle measurement", "reliability statistics", "intraclass correlation coefficient", "standard error of measurement", "minimal detectable change", "rehabilitation", "motion capture"]

title: FSO-Based Backhauling for Airborne THz Base Stations
abstract: Airborne nodes in the form of high-altitude platform stations (HAPSs) or unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) can be used for backhauling and wireless access. In this paper, we investigate the cascaded free space optical (FSO)/terahertz (THz) link in which the FSO link serves as a backhaul between the gateway and the airborne node. In contrast, the THz link provides wireless communication between the airborne node and the user. We present channel models, including the atmospheric attenuation, geometrical loss, and fading effect. The FSO sub-system builds upon intensity-modulation direct-detection (IM/DD), while the THz sub-system employs coherent modulation and demodulation. Under the assumption of decode-and-forward relaying, we derive the end-to-end bit error rate (BER). We present numerical results to demonstrate the performance of cascaded airborne links.
keywords: ["free-space optical communication", "terahertz communication", "backhaul", "high-altitude platforms", "unmanned aerial vehicles", "atmospheric attenuation", "channel modeling", "intensity modulation and direct detection", "coherent modulation", "decode-and-forward relaying", "bit error rate"]

title: Spoofing Detection and Anti-Spoofing Kalman Filter Design for an Accelerometer-Integrated GNSS Receiver
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) measurements are frequently used, especially in autonomous vehicle navigation, as they can provide successful positioning solutions. Therefore, the importance of positioning accuracy of the GNSS receiver in these vehicles has increased. On the other hand, with spoofing attacks, receivers can produce a positioning solution in a way that they think they are in a different place than their actual location. For this reason, it is important to use spoofing detection and countermeasure algorithms in GNSS receivers. In this paper, a Kalman filter design is proposed to be used in the navigation block, just before producing the final positioning solution, of the accelerometer-integrated GNSS receivers for spoofing detection and countermeasure. The proposed approach detects spoofing by comparing the residual values of the solutions of accelerometers and GNSSs with each other. The performance of the filter was examined with Monte Carlo simulations for different spoofing trajectories and interpreted by plotting Receiver Operating Characteristic curves.
keywords: ["GNSS spoofing detection", "anti-spoofing", "Kalman filter design", "autonomous vehicle navigation", "positioning accuracy", "residual analysis", "spoofing countermeasures", "receiver operating characteristic"]

title: A Structural Damage Assessment Model Based on Deep Learning
abstract: The rapid and accurate damage assessment of the buildings in the residential areas after the earthquake is an important issue for the reconstruction of the damaged cities. This study aims to automatically classify the damage conditions of structural load-bearing elements such as columns and beams with deep learning models through photographs taken from the buildings after the earthquake. ConvNeXt model, which is a new generation deep convolutional neural network, has been used as a deep learning method. Thanks to the trained model, it is possible to distinguish between two types of structural and nonstructural damage classes. In addition, the position of cracks on the existing structural element, which has an important place for engineers in damage detection, can also be determined. As the training dataset, reinforced concrete building images taken after the Elazi earthquake and labeled by experts were used. In the g current ConvNeXt model, a reliable model with high accuracy has been obtained using different transfer learning strategies and fine-tuning, data augmentation, and regularization techniques. The results obtained were compared with other convolutional neural network methods accepted in the literature, and it was observed that the ConvNeXt-based method produced faster and more accurate results.
keywords: ["structural damage assessment", "earthquake damage detection", "ConvNeXt", "reinforced concrete buildings", "beams and columns", "crack localization", "post-earthquake reconstruction", "transfer learning", "fine-tuning", "data augmentation", "regularization", "image-based damage classification"]

title: Joint Detection and Tracking of Occluded Target Using Lidar
abstract: Target tracking in transportation vehicles is important from both civilian and military perspectives. Objects that obstruct the sensor's field of view create occlusion regions in target tracking. The literature has developed dynamic solutions to address the problems arising from the target entering the sensor's occlusion spot behind an obstacle and detecting occlusion regions. In this study, target tracking using lidar is performed with a stationary vehicle obstacle and a moving vehicle in the Gazebo simulation environment. A solution is proposed for velocity disturbances during entry into the occlusion region in this environment. After comparing the performance of target tracking filters in the simulation environment, the algorithms are tested in a real-world scenario where a similar simulation environment is set up. Two different Bernoulli filters are implemented based on the nearest neighbor and probabilistic data association mechanisms. The results are evaluated using the Optimal SubPattern Assignment metrics.
keywords: ["LiDAR", "Bernoulli filter", "probabilistic data association", "nearest neighbors", "velocity disturbances", "Gazebo simulation"]

title: Anomaly Detection in Predicted Water Treatment Data Using Hybrid CNN-LSTM Network Model
abstract: Water treatment systems are among the industrial control systems where it is essential to detect anomalies accurately and efficiently due to the potential threat to public health. With advances in computer science, machine learning models have been successfully used in the anomaly detection process in recent years. In this paper, a hybrid CNN-LSTM network model is proposed to detect anomalies in water systems. Using a statistical window-based anomaly detection approach, the performance of the proposed model in detecting different types of attacks is analyzed on the open SWaT dataset. Experimental results show that the precision, recall and Fl-score values of the proposed model are 0.994, 0.973 and 0.983, respectively, and can be successfully used to detect anomalies in water treatment systems.
keywords: ["anomaly detection", "water treatment systems", "CNN-LSTM hybrid model", "SWaT dataset", "industrial control systems", "attack detection", "cyber-physical security"]

title: Muğla Wildfires Burn Severity and Vegetation Difference Analysis with Remote Sensing Techniques
abstract: Due to the fire incidents taking place in our country in recent years, it has become increasingly important to analyze the effects of the fire with various metrics on the basis of burned areas. The size of the burned areas by area determines the performance of the field analysis. With the advancement of technology, analysis from satellite images has become popular, especially in cases with wide spread areas, for the analysis of fire, examination of vegetation, and comparison with the old state of the region. In this study, NBR (Normalized Combustion Rate) and NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) indexes of Bodrum-Milas and Marmaris fire zones were analyzed using remote sensing techniques using Sentinel 2 satellite images, and the intensity of burning and the ratio of these intensities to the percentile area were calculated. A comparison was made with other studies conducted for these regions and the performance was measured by accepting them as separate references.
keywords: ["forest fires", "burn severity", "vegetation change", "Normalized Burn Ratio", "NDVI", "Sentinel-2", "burned area", "fire intensity", "post-fire vegetation"]

title: A Comparative Performance Analysis of Different Modulations in IM/DD Wireless Communication Systems
abstract: In this paper, the performances of the ACO-OFDM waveform, one of the optical OFDM waveforms developed for IM/DD wireless communication systems, are analyzed in the multipath fading ceiling bounce optical channel environment with different modulations such as M-CSK and M-QAM modulations. Channel coding techniques such as Reed Solomon (RS) and 1/2 rate convolutional encoder (CC) are utilized to improve the bit error rate (BER) performance of the ACO-OFDM waveform. The performances of the RS and 1/2 CC encoded ACO-OFDM waveform using M-CSK and M-QAM modulations are compared over the BER-SNR performance metric in the 5-tap ceiling bounce wireless optical channel environment. From the produced numerical results, it is seen that nearly 2.5 dB SNR difference occurs between M-CSK and M-QAM modulations. Also, it is observed that 1/2 CC channel coding is approximately 2-3 dB better than RS channel coding.
keywords: ["intensity modulation and direct detection", "optical wireless communication", "multipath fading", "M-QAM modulation", "Reed-Solomon codes", "bit error rate", "SNR performance"]

title: Outage Performance of User-Assisted Alamouti/MRC-SWIPT NOMA Network
abstract: This study investigates the outage performance of a dual-hop single-phase non-orthogonal multi-access system. The base station applies the Alamouti orthogonal space-time block coding technique and communicates simultaneously with two mobile users. One of these users works as a full-duplex relay for the other one. The system model is developed, and fundamental analytical equations are defined. The outage probability of the considered system is investigated in Rayleigh fading channels via Monte Carlo simulations.
keywords: ["outage probability", "non-orthogonal multiple access", "Alamouti space-time block coding", "maximum ratio combining", "simultaneous wireless information and power transfer", "dual-hop relay", "full-duplex relaying", "Rayleigh fading"]

title: Finding Islands on Encrypted Graphs
abstract: Cloud computing services have found widespread use recently. Offloading computations to public clouds has many benefits albeit harming the privacy of users and data. Homomorphic encryption facilitates cloud computing services that can do computations over encrypted data without requiring decryption and this enables privacy-preserving applications. In this paper, we propose an approach for confidentially finding islands (connected components) in a graph. We present various performance evaluation results and show that privacy-preservation can be achieved with a cost of computation overhead.
keywords: ["homomorphic encryption", "connected components", "privacy-preserving computation", "cloud computing", "encrypted data", "computational overhead"]

title: Reducing Carbon Emissions in Websites: Estimation and Sustainable Practices for Eco-Friendly Web Development
abstract: As technology advances, the size of websites has increased due to factors such as the advanced systems used and the intensive use of visuals. Consequently, the amount of carbon emissions caused by the data of these websites has also increased. Considering that a significant portion of the world's population are now internet users, substantial amounts of carbon emissions are produced daily due to internet sites alone. This paper aims to estimate the carbon emissions produced by transferring bytes of data on the internet using SustainableWeb Design (SWD) and 1byte digital emission estimation models, and propose methods to reduce these emissions.
keywords: ["CO2 emissions", "digital carbon footprint", "emission estimation model", "emission reduction"]

title: Acoustic Direction Estimation with MEMS Microphone Array
abstract: In this study, MEMS microphone array was designed and a data collection setup was created. The direction of the acoustic signal is determined by estimating the time delay between the array signals. The method is based on determining the angle of incidence using the calculation of cross correlations between the array signals. The results are discussed in this paper.
keywords: ["MEMS microphone array", "time delay estimation", "cross correlation function", "angle of incidence", "microphone array design", "sound localization"]

title: Performance of Multiuser MIMO-SWIPT Layered Transmission Systems
abstract: In this study, the performance of multiuser multiinput multi-output (MIMO) simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT) layered transmission system is investigated under downlink scenario. For the first time in the literature, each user is assumed to simultaneously perform energy harvesting (EH) and information decoding (ID) under the MIMO-SWIPT layered transmission system. To this end, antenna switching technique is used at the receivers and the idea that while a set of receive antennas is reserved for EH, the remaining antennas are exploited for ID is adopted. In addition, power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access is utilized for multiuser multiple access process. A number of numerical results are presented on the amount of harvested energy, attained data rate, and outage probability.
keywords: ["multi-user MIMO", "simultaneous wireless information and power transfer", "layered transmission", "antenna switching", "energy harvesting", "information decoding", "power-domain non-orthogonal multiple access", "downlink", "outage probability", "harvested energy", "data rate"]

title: ORTPiece: An ORT-Based Turkish Image Captioning Network Based on Transformers and WordPiece
abstract: Recent transformers-based systems are advancing image captioning applications. However, those works have been mainly applied to English-based image captioning problems. In this paper, we introduce a transformers-based Turkish-based image captioning algorithm. Our proposed algorithm uses appearance and geometry features from the input image and combines them along with the WordPiece embeddings to generate the Turkish-based caption. Our experimental results show improvement when compared to the other existing techniques including the original ORT and the show-and-tell algorithms.
keywords: ["image captioning", "Turkish language", "ORT", "transformer models", "multilingual captioning", "show and tell"]

title: Ballistic Target Classification Using Machine Learning
abstract: Weapon locating radars are actively being used by militaries around the world, in order to protect a predetermined area from enemy fires. They achieve this by predicting the launch and impact points of ballistic targets which they detect. One of the most important steps in predicting the launch and impact points of an incoming ballistic target is to correctly identify the type of it. In this work, a ballistic target classifier with multiple decision steps using machine-learning methods is proposed and further research possibilities in this direction are discussed.
keywords: ["impact point prediction", "military air defense"]

title: Social and Categorical Signals in Contrastive Learning for Recommendation Systems
abstract: Social recommendation systems that use graph neural network (GNN) models are effective in addressing the data sparsity issue present in collaborative filtering models. Social homophily and item similarities are critical factors that affect users' preferences, and GNN models must capture these factors while incorporating users' interaction behaviors. In this work, we propose SCCL, a recommendation model that jointly captures social influence and item similarity signals with crossview contrastive learning.We constructed a user-user social graph from social networks and item-item graphs from common tags. In our model, user-user relations are represented as a homogeneous graph, and item-item relations are represented as hypergraphs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our model on two real-world datasets.
keywords: ["social recommendation", "collaborative filtering", "data sparsity", "graph neural networks", "cross-view contrastive learning", "social homophily", "item similarity", "social influence", "hypergraphs"]

title: Transaction Volume Estimation in Financial Markets with LSTM
abstract: In this study, it was aimed to determine the transaction volume that will be encountered in the future (hourly) in the factoring sector, and then to take financial and operational action early. For the study, the LSTM model, which is a kind of recurrent neural network (RNN) that can capture long and short- term dependencies, was applied by using data-driven approaches to estimate the check amounts of hourly transactions. As a result of the results, it was aimed to increase the operational efficiency in a broad scope by allowing the factoring company to determine the loan amounts to be obtained from banks in the most optimal way, and then to take early action within the scope of both the workforce and business management of the financial resource allocation management process and operational activities. MAPE score was used as a measure of error in the time series analysis model. MAPE scores were found as %5.05 for 30 days, %4.18 for 10 days, %3.47 for 5 days, %3.09 for 3 days and %1.83 for 1 day. According to the MAPE scores calculated for different days, the enterprise will be able to decide on the loan to be drawn from banks both in terms of time and amount, and the necessary action will be taken.
keywords: ["factoring", "LSTM", "budget allocation", "operational efficiency"]

title: A Learning-Based Coloring Algorithm for Register Allocation Problem
abstract: The register allocation problem involves assigning variables in a program to physical registers in a computer's processor. It can be modeled as a weighted node coloring problem by representing each variable as a node in a graph and assigning a weight to each node corresponding to the number of times the variable is used in the program. The purpose of the problem is to allocate all the variables in the program to the least number of registers. In this study, a learning- based coloring algorithm was designed to solve the problem. The performance of the proposed work has been tested on DIMACS samples by comparing it with the leading evolutionary algorithms in the literature. Experimental studies show that the proposed learning-based coloring algorithm achieves the best results for DIMACS instances in a shorter time than evolutionary algorithms in the literature.
keywords: ["register allocation", "learning-based algorithms", "variable assignment", "DIMACS benchmarks", "evolutionary algorithm comparison"]

title: Sensitivity Improvement in Optical Phase Diffraction Using Empirical Mode Decomposition
abstract: Phase diffraction is a potent property used in transparent dielectric film characterization. The measured diffraction pattern on the camera is evaluated by matching numerically computed diffraction patterns to determine the optical properties of the ultra-thin films (refractive index, thickness, etc.). However, the obtained diffraction data is not only a nonlinear and non-stationary signal but also exhibits micron-scale variations, thus limiting the measurement accuracy. Therefore, it is challenging to identify shifts in minima and deviations in amplitude on diffraction data to extract information about the optical properties of phase objects. In this study, it is aimed to improve the thickness sensitivity of the system by applying Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) to plane wave-based near- field phase diffraction data. Since EMD is very sensitive to abrupt changes in the signal due to the spatial frequency components, the nanoscale variations in the film thickness become more observable and detectable. Experimental outputs and numerical simulations show that the decomposition increases the thickness sensitivity comparing the classical matching technique.
keywords: ["empirical mode decomposition", "refractive index measurement", "plane wave diffraction", "Fresnel diffraction"]

title: Big Data Analytics for Anomaly Detection in Blockchain
abstract: The ability to make fast and automatic transactions anonymously without intermediary institutions offered by blockchain technology has made this technology widespread in the use of money transfer. With its widespread use, it has also become a preferred transfer method for illegal transactions such as tax evasion and the sale of illegal goods. This has increased the importance of anomalous transactions and anomalous user detection studies in transactions. In this study, a solution is presented that enables the detection of anomalies and anomalous users in blockchain transfers by using big data storage and data processing tools. A scalable structure has been created in order to deal with the increase in the size and frequency of blockchain transfers with the use of big data technologies. In the solution, first of all, the users making the transfers and the transfer transactions are clustered using the K-Means method. Transfer information and attributes that represent the blockchain network as a graph are used as features. After clustering, anomalies were found by measuring the distance of the elements from the cluster center. The performance of the clustering was calculated using the silhouette score. When the results are analyzed, the model that reduces the size to two with principal component analysis for clustering users showed the highest scores with a silhouette score of 0.51, and the model that reduces the size of graph-based attributes with principal component analysis for clustering transfers showed the highest scores with a silhouette score of 0.87. These models were applied to real time transactions.
keywords: ["blockchain", "anomaly detection", "blockchain transactions", "K-means clustering", "graph features", "principal component analysis", "silhouette coefficient", "big data analytics", "tax evasion", "money laundering", "real-time transaction monitoring"]

title: Sample Picking in Synthetic Irides for Wolf Attacks
abstract: In this study, samples with higher potential to succeed in wolf attacks are picked among synthetically generated iris images, and the composed subset is shown to pose a more significant threat toward an iris recognition system backed by a Presentation Attack Detection (PAD) module with respect to randomly selected samples. Iris images generated by Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Networks (DCGAN) are firstly filtered by rejection sampling on PAD score distribution of real iris image PAD scores. Next, the probability of zero success in all attack attempts is calculated for each synthetic iris image, using real iris images in the training set, and match and non-match score distributions are calculated on those. Synthetic images with the lowest probabilities of zero success are included in the final set. Our hypothesis that this set would be more successful in wolf attacks is tested by comparing its spoofing performances with randomly selected sample sets.
keywords: ["wolf attacks", "anti-spoofing", "DCGAN", "sample selection", "biometric spoofing"]

title: Music Note Detection Using Matrix Pencil Method
abstract: Musical note detection is a field that has been studied throughout the years and is still improving. There have been successful studies proposed, as well as numerous music software programs. This paper attempts to contribute to the existing body of knowledge on this subject. Unlike traditional Fourier-based approaches, Matrix Pencil Method (MPM) is used for detecting and identifying signal parameters. The algorithm is explained step by step, problems faced are discussed, and solutions proposed. Finally, software for detecting musical notes of monophonic songs has been developed. The suggested algorithm has been tested on two distinct songs and the note accuracy rate of the algorithm for these two songs was determined as 95.22 percent and 89.97 percent.
keywords: ["matrix pencil method", "monophonic music", "fundamental frequency estimation", "audio signal processing"]

title: Numerical Model Sensitivity Analysis for Breast Cancer Microwave Hyperthermia Treatment
abstract: Microwave hyperthermia, which locally increases body temperature, offers significant improvement in tumor treatment for breast cancer. During treatment planning, breast models are typically created from magnetic resonance images due to their high resolution, but this process is costly. In order to reduce costs, the hyperthermia performance of breast models created at low resolution has been investigated. The resolution of the breast model was reduced using Gaussian filters with variances of σ =3D 0.1, 0.5,1, 2, 5,10. Treatment planning was conducted for each model, and their temperature focusing performances were examined.
keywords: ["microwave hyperthermia", "breast cancer", "model resolution", "Gaussian filtering", "treatment planning", "sensitivity analysis", "low-resolution models"]

title: Cell Coverage Analysis of UAV Networks
abstract: In the next generation mobile communication technologies, providing service to users far from terrestrial base stations by using non-terresterial networks (NTNs) is purposed. Components to be used in NTN for this purpose cause high mobility problem and make the studies on this problem important. In recent years, the use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), one of the NTN components, as base stations has gained popularity. This situation makes essential studies on handover (HO) and coverage in networks using UAVs. In this study, HO rate and coverage area analysis are performed on a mobility model using a UAV base station. It is investigated whether the connection between the users and the base stations is line of sight. Then, the path loss and shadowing fading values are calculated according to the connection type. Moreover, the number of connections made by users to base the stations is examined for different UAV altitudes. Since more realistic calculations are used in the analyzes which are made within the scope of the study, more realistic results are obtained about the optimum UAV altitude. Also, since the results of the analysis made from three different perspectives which are number of connections, HO ratio and coverage probability, are combined; more realistic results about optimum UAV altitude are obtained.
keywords: ["unmanned aerial vehicles", "UAV base stations", "non-terrestrial networks", "handover rate", "coverage probability", "lines of sight", "path loss", "UAV altitude optimization", "user mobility"]

title: Comparative Analysis of Prediction Models for Estimating Passenger Volumes in Airline
abstract: Accurately forecasting passenger flow in airports is crucial for optimizing operations, improving the passenger experience, and allocating resources effectively. This article proposes a novel approach using the 2-steps algorithm to forecast airport passenger volume, leveraging various input variables. Our predictive model utilizes comprehensive flight data, including flight duration, departure and arrival times, previous passenger records, and other relevant information, to uncover hidden patterns and trends influencing passenger movement. The LightGBM algorithm effectively captures the complex interactions between these variables, yielding precise estimates of projected passenger numbers. The forecasts generated by our model can aid airport authorities, airlines, and other stakeholders in making data-driven decisions, such as resource allocation, security measures, and terminal capabilities, ultimately enhancing operational efficiency and the passenger experience. Through a comparative analysis of five prediction models, including SDCA, L-BFGS (Poisson), Light-GBM, Fast-Tree, and Fast-Forest, we demonstrate that Light-GBM consistently outperforms the other models in terms of accuracy. Furthermore, we introduce a Linear Regression Activator that combines the predictions of the individual models, resulting in improved prediction accuracy compared to selecting the best or average predictions. These findings emphasize the importance of selecting an appropriate prediction model and highlight the potential of machine learning in revolutionizing airport operations and enhancing the travel experience. Future research can explore advanced modeling techniques and consider additional variables to enhance prediction accuracy and robustness further.
keywords: ["LightGBM", "ensemble forecasting", "model comparison", "flight data", "flight time", "airport operations", "resource allocation", "terminal capacity"]

title: A Three-User 2x2 MIMO Alamouti/MRC NOMA System Implementation
abstract: Multi-antenna systems (MIMO) that increase data rate, capacity and performance via diversity schemes, and nonorthogonal multiple access (NOMA) that increases spectral efficiency reveal an important potential for next generation communication systems (5G+). Although there are many efforts on the areas, real-time implementations are quite limited. In this paper, we implement a downlink single hop three-user 2x2 MIMO NOMA system with software defined radio (SDR). The transmitter and receiver diversity schemes are Alamouti that doesn't need channel state information and MRC that provides optimum performance. This paper considers power domain NOMA. The performance of the system is empirically examined over the bit error rate (BER) and outage probability (OP) parameters.
keywords: ["non-orthogonal multiple access", "MIMO", "Alamouti code", "maximum ratio combining", "power-domain NOMA", "software-defined radio", "downlink transmission", "bit error rate", "outage probability", "5G"]

title: Analysis of Subword Tokenization Approaches for Turkish Language
abstract: Various tokenization approaches have been proposed in natural language processing research. These approaches have further evolved from character- and word-level representations to subword-level representations. However, the impact of tokenizations on model performance has not been thoroughly discussed, especially for morphologically rich languages. In this paper, we comprehensively analyze subword tokenizers for Turkish which is a highly inflected and morphologically rich language and we propose a morphologically-based approach. Also, we examine how the tokenizer parameters like vocabulary and corpus sizes change the characteristics of tokenizers.
keywords: ["subword tokenization", "Turkish language", "morphologically rich languages", "vocabulary size", "corpus size", "inflectional morphology"]

title: Implications of Node Selection in Decentralized Federated Learning
abstract: Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) offers a fully distributed alternative to Federated Learning (FL). However, the lack of global information in a highly heterogeneous environment negatively impacts its performance. Node selection in FL has been suggested to improve both communication efficiency and convergence rate.
