keywords: ["vehicle color recognition", "image preprocessing", "contrast adjustment", "saturation enhancement", "Gaussian smoothing", "shadows and reflections", "model robustness", "stolen vehicle detection"]

title: Examination of Neurological Diseases with Image Processing-Based Deep Learning Methods
abstract: NNeurological diseases are complex disorders that affect brain functions and often impair individuals’ abilities to walk, speak, learn, and move. Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, stroke, and Multiple Sclerosis (MS) are common examples of such conditions. The lack of a definitive cure for these diseases further highlights the importance of early diagnosis in improving patients’ quality of life. In the literature, classification models have mostly been developed for Alzheimer’s and Parkin-son’s diseases. However, developing a model capable of classifying four different neurological diseases simultaneously would provide significant support in clinical diagnosis processes. This study aims to classify Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease, stroke, and MS using deep learning methods and to compare the performance of these approaches. For this purpose, ResNet50, AlexNet, EfficientNetB0, and a custom-designed Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture were employed. Experimental results showed that the EfficientNetB0 model achieved the highest accuracy.
keywords: ["Alzheimer's disease", "Parkinson's disease", "stroke", "multiple sclerosis", "image processing", "convolutional neural networks", "EfficientNetB0", "ResNet50", "AlexNet", "early diagnosis"]

title: TR-MMLU Benchmark for Large Language Models: Performance Evaluation, Challenges, and Opportunities for Improvement
abstract: Language models have made significant advancements in understanding and generating human language, achieving remarkable success in various applications. However, evaluating these models remains a challenge, particularly for resource-limited languages like Turkish. To address this issue, we introduce the Turkish MMLU (TR-MMLU) benchmark, a comprehensive evaluation framework designed to assess the linguistic and conceptual capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in Turkish. TR-MMLU is based on a meticulously curated dataset comprising 6,200 multiple-choice questions across 62 sections within the Turkish education system. This benchmark provides a standard framework for Turkish NLP research, enabling detailed analyses of LLMs’ capabilities in processing Turkish text. In this study, we evaluated state-of-the-art LLMs on TR-MMLU, highlighting areas for improvement in model design. TR-MMLU sets a new standard for advancing Turkish NLP research and inspiring future innovations.
keywords: ["Turkish language models", "large language models", "benchmark", "multiple-choice questions", "Turkish education system", "low-resource languages", "LLM evaluation"]

title: Performance Analysis of Wired and Wireless Optical Communication Systems in the Sea of Marmara
abstract: In this study, submarine cable and wireless optical communication systems between Büyükada and Yalova are analyzed using the OptiSystem 7.0 simulation program. In the submarine investigation, fiber optic cable and wireless optical communication channel (OWC channel) are used. A Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) design is implemented for both systems. The transmission distance for the submarine optical communication system is determined using the Google Earth application. Transmitter power levels of 0,5,10,15, and 20 dBm are evaluated for both the submarine fiber optic and wireless optical communication systems. The best performance is observed at 10 dBm for the submarine fiber optic communication system and 20 dBm for the OWC system. Data rate, which is among thecritical parameters, is assessed at values of 0.5,1,5,10, and 15 Gbit/s. System performance is evaluated based on key indicators of reliability and accuracy, including the maximum Q-factor obtained from the Bit Error Rate (BER) analyzer and eye diagram analyses. The results from this study provide valuable insights for optimizing optical communication systems used in the Marmara Sea region.
keywords: ["submarine optical communication", "optical wireless communication", "optical fiber cable", "wavelength division multiplexing", "transmitter power", "bit error rate", "quality factor", "eye diagram", "Marmara Sea", "Büyükada", "Yalova"]

title: Restoring Degraded Receipt Images with Generative Approach
abstract: Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technologies play a crucial role in processes such as document processing and expense management. Since receipts can easily fade, OCR-based automation often leads to the need for manual corrections. This results in additional time spent by employees and extra costs. Without proper oversight, these issues can cause significant problems in accounting. Therefore, we propose a model to correct degraded documents using a generative AI framework based on transformer architecture. The experiments show that the proposed model provides significant improvements and enhances OCR results.
keywords: ["optical character recognition", "generative AI", "transformer models", "document image enhancement"]

title: Enhanced Training with Adaptive Vertex Mixup Against Adversarial Attacks in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning is a modern machine learning approach that enables data to be processed on local devices without being sent to a central server, offering advantages such as privacy and scalability. However, due to the nature of this distributed structure, various challenges arise regarding the security of the model and especially adversarial attacks can compromise the integrity of the system. To address this challenge, this study proposes a defense mechanism against adversarial attacks called Adaptive veRtex Mixup Federated Adversarial Training (ARM-FAT). ARM-FAT introduces a coefficient that adaptively controls the loss obtained from its underlying AVmixup algorithm, as well as providing loss values representing robustness and clean data. ARM-FAT is compared with the adversarial training methods in the literature on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets. The results show that the ARM-FAT method outperforms the existing methods against adversarial attacks.
keywords: ["federated learning", "adversarial attacks", "adversarial training", "robustness", "arm fat", "CIFAR-10", "CIFAR-100"]

title: Ship Detection and Classification Using Electro-Optic Cameras
abstract: This study aims to develop an artificial intelligence-based system for ship detection and classification using electro-optic (EO) cameras positioned along the Bosphorus Strait. A large-scale ship dataset consists of 22.118 image was created, and a semi-automated annotation tool supported by AIS messages was developed for efficient dataset labeling. Deep learning models, YOLOv10-L, YOLOv11-L, and RT-DETR-L, were trained and evaluated for ship detection and classification. Among these models, YOLOv11-L achieved the highest performance with an mAP@0.5 of 89.6%. Error analysis revealed high misclassification rates among large ship categories and challenges in detecting smaller vessels. Future work aims to enhance model robustness under challenging environmental conditions by increasing dataset diversity and integrating AIS and radar data.
keywords: ["ship detection", "ship classification", "Bosphorus Strait", "YOLOv11", "YOLOv10", "RT-DETR", "semi-automatic annotation", "maritime surveillance", "object detection", "small vessel detection"]

title: Enhanced Design in Passive RFID Tag Antenna
abstract: This study presents the design and performance evaluation of a microstrip patch antenna for passive RFID tag applications at 2.4 GHz. Simulated using CST Microwave Studio, the proposed antenna achieved a return loss of -49.67 dB. Performance tests conducted with five different dielectric materials, covering relative permittivity values up to 78, confirmed stable impedance matching, gain, and directivity. Simulation results demonstrated the antenna’s robustness across various container compositions. These findings highlight its potential for RFID-based sensing in pharmaceutical and chemical applications, enabling reliable wireless identification and material characterization in complex dielectric environments.
keywords: ["microstrip patch antenna", "2.4 GHz", "dielectric materials", "dielectric constant", "impedance matching", "antenna gain and directivity", "RFID sensing", "pharmaceutical applications", "applied chemistry", "wireless identification"]

title: Impact of Teacher Forcing Training on Blood Glucose Prediction Performance
abstract: In this study, the accuracy of blood glucose prediction was improved using the teacher forcing LSTM (TFLSTM) method, and the model was compared with a traditional LSTM approach. The model was trained using the OhioT1DM dataset and the DMMS.R simulation program, which contain data obtained from patients with Type 1 diabetes. Models were trained with past window lengths of 15, 30, and 45 minutes, and their performance was analyzed for the corresponding prediction horizons. The findings of this study indicate that the teacher forcing LSTM method significantly reduced prediction error, particularly in short-term predictions using the OhioT1DM dataset. However, in the DMMS.R dataset, a partial decline in model performance was observed as the prediction horizon increased. The impact of individual differences on prediction performance was also analyzed, revealing that while error decreased significantly for some patients, improvements were more limited for others. Overall, these findings demonstrate that the TF-LSTM method is effective in blood glucose level prediction, especially for short-term prediction horizons.
keywords: ["blood glucose prediction", "teacher forcing", "LSTM", "type 1 diabetes", "short-term forecasting", "prediction horizon"]

title: Yakın Mesafe Algılayan Yumuşak Robotik Duyargalar için Sistem Tanılama Yöntemlerinin Karşılaştırılması Comparison of System Identification Methods for Close-Proximity Sensing Soft Antennae
abstract: The design and manufacturing of compliant structures using soft materials are gaining importance due to their unique advantages in robotics and sensing applications. This study presents research conducted to analyze the close-proximity depth perception capabilities of low-cost, soft robotic antennae produced in a laboratory environment for use in insect-like robots. The characteristic properties of these antennae in both the time and frequency domains have been determined using different methods, and the advantages of these methods over one another have been discussed.
keywords: ["system identification", "depth perception", "compliant structures", "soft materials", "time-domain analysis", "frequency domain analysis", "low-cost sensors"]

title: Liking State Estimation Using Time-Frequency Image Representation of EEG Signals
abstract: In recent years, there has been a significant increase in research on emotion and preference state estimation. In this study, a preference prediction method is proposed for use in neuromarketing studies by utilizing time-frequency (TF) energy distribution images derived from electroencephalogram (EEG) signals. EEG signals recorded while participants watched commercials from two different automobile brands were evaluated using deep learning techniques to estimate their preference states. After viewing the advertisements, participants were shown selected visual segments from the commercials (e.g., front view, dashboard, etc.) and asked to rate their preferences on a scale from 1 to 5. The EEG signals corresponding to these segments were transformed into two-dimensional RGB-scaled scalogram/spectrogram images using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT). Using deep learning models, the proposed method achieved maximum classification accuracies of 86.61% and 87.26%, respectively.
keywords: ["EEG", "time-frequency representation", "neuromarketing", "emotion recognition", "continuous wavelet transform", "short-time Fourier transform", "scalogram", "spectrogram", "brand preference"]

title: Comparison of Sub-Models and Examination of Factors Enhancing Performance in a Deep Learning Model Adaptable to Embedded Systems
abstract: In this study, the performance of the YOLOv7 model, which can be implemented on embedded systems and FPGAs, was examined for detecting desired targets using civilian and military unmanned aerial vehicles. The performance of its sub-models, YOLOv7-X and YOLOv7-Tiny, was evaluated at different altitudes. The study discusses possible improvements to enable the YOLOv7-Tiny model, which achieved the highest performance, to detect targets from altitudes of up to 500 meters. Initially, the Cycar dataset was used for training To enhance detection at higher altitudes, dataset augmentation was applied, and the DOTA dataset was also utilized. It was observed that the numerical increase in dataset samples significantly contributed to the results
keywords: ["YOLOv7", "YOLOv7-tiny", "object detection", "embedded systems", "FPGA implementation", "unmanned aerial vehicles", "target detection", "altitude", "data augmentation", "DOTA dataset", "model performance comparison"]

title: Development and Simulation of a Robot Arm Functional Mockup Unit (FMU) for Digital Twins
abstract: Simulation-based verification methods are gaining importance to test the accuracy, speed and error detection capabilities of industrial robots. In this study, an FMU-based model is developed to model and validate the kinematic and dynamic behavior of the RS005L robot arm. Forward and inverse kinematic calculations are performed using Denavit-Hartenberg (DH) parameters and Jacobian-based inverse kinematic solution is integrated. Torque calculations were performed with the Newton-Euler dynamic model and PD controller, and motion was updated with Euler integration. The model packaged with UniFMU was tested in FMPy environment. The study aims to provide high accuracy and efficiency for digital twin applications by providing co-simulation capabilities and cross-platform portability.
keywords: ["robot manipulators", "Functional Mock-up Units", "digital twin", "forward kinematics", "inverse kinematics", "Denavit-Hartenberg parameters", "Newton-Euler dynamics", "PD control", "co-simulation"]

title: Neural Architecture Search for Histopathological Image Classification
abstract: The accurate classification of histopathology images is important in medical diagnosis processes. In recent years, Neural Architecture Search (NAS) methods have been developed to optimize the model selection process, one of the important problems in this field, by enabling the automatic design of deep learning models. This study proposes a new neural architecture search method for histopathology image classification using the Opposition-Based Differential Evolution (ODE) algorithm. The proposed method is based on the PBC-NAS architecture and includes a search strategy developed to solve plateau problems. The performance of the proposed method is evaluated on the Enteroscope Biopsy Histopathological H&E (EBHI) image dataset. In the experimental studies, the proposed method is compared with deep learning models such as ResNet, MobileNet, and DenseNet, which are widely used in the literature in terms of accuracy and processing time. The proposed method achieves highly competitive results (0.5 points difference) with up to 5 times less computation time, which is crucial for medical image analysis.
keywords: ["neural architecture search", "histopathological image classification", "Plateau problem", "computational efficiency"]

title: Comparative Analysis of YOLOv11 and YOLOv9 for Eye Regions Segmentation
abstract: accurate segmentation of the retina, optic discs, and other anatomical structures of the eye from eye images is crucial for ophthalmic diagnosis and the evaluation of eye diseases. In previous studies, the DeepLabv3 model was used for segmenting eye regions, achieving an average Dice score of 81%. In this study, the latest YOLO models, YOLOv9 and YOLOv11, were utilized due to their potential to achieve an optimal balance between accuracy and efficiency in medical image analysis.Experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv11n outperforms other models. YOLOv11n achieved MAP50, MAP50-95, and Dice scores of 90.6%, 49.3%, and 90%, respectively. In contrast, YOLOv9-C obtained MAP50, MAP50-95, and Dice scores of 89%, 47.6%, and 88.9%, respectively.These findings indicate that the YOLOv11n model improves segmentation accuracy for eye images, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to previous models.
keywords: ["YOLOv11", "YOLOv9", "eye region segmentation", "optic disc segmentation", "eye images", "medical image segmentation", "ophthalmic diagnosis"]

title: Spoiler Detection with Deep Learning in Turkish-Written Movie Reviews
abstract: Before deciding to watch a movie, it is usually consulted the reviews of those who have already watched that movie. However, reviews containing spoilers are a serious problem for those who have not yet watched the movie. This study is the first research on automatic spoiler detection on movie reviews written in Turkish. A dataset of 3,000 reviews of 10 popular movies was collected and manually labelled. Additionally, another 2,000 synthetic audience reviews containing spoilers were generated with ChatGPT for the same movies. In classification experiments using transformer architecture based deep learning models, tests were carried out first with the original dataset and then the synthetic data were included in the training phase. As a result of the experiments, the highest performance was obtained as 95.09% F1-score with the BERTurk (128K) model in the test where synthetic data was also included. Also, it was found that the inclusion of synthetic data in the training process generally increased the performance.
keywords: ["movie reviews", "Turkish language", "synthetic data", "BERTurk", "transformer models", "text classification", "audience reviews"]

title: Diagnosis of Mild Traumatic Brain Injury with Machine Learning-Based Decision Support Systems
abstract: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) is a significant health concern, particularly common in children, requiring a careful diagnostic process in emergency departments. Traditional diagnostic methods may lead to unnecessary radiation exposure in pediatric patients, making the development of alternative approaches highly important. This study examined the effectiveness of machine learning (ML) models in diagnosing mild TBI. The PECARN-ciTBI dataset was analyzed, and the class imbalance was addressed using the SMOTE method. Various ML models were optimized and compared, including decision trees, ensemble models, artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and k-nearest neighbor classifiers. Among these models, which were enhanced through hyperparameter optimization, decision trees, and ensemble models achieved high accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity values. Specifically, decision trees provided 99.94% accuracy, 97.19% sensitivity, and 99.9% specificity, while ensemble models yielded the best results with 99.93% accuracy, 97.19% sensitivity, and 100% specificity. The results indicate that machine learning models offer a reliable and effective alternative for pediatric TBI diagnosis.
keywords: ["mild traumatic brain injury", "pediatric traumatic brain injury", "computer-aided diagnosis", "decision support system", "class imbalance", "SMOTE", "ensemble learning", "decision tree", "artificial neural networks", "support vector machine", "k-nearest neighbors", "emergency department diagnosis"]

title: Inverse Skill Learning From Demonstrations via Reinforcement Learning
abstract: In robotics, most semantically meaningful skills can be utilized to learn similar skills. Forward - inverse skill pairs are such a family of semantically meaningful skills where one skill can be used to learn the other. In this paper, we propose an architecture that is able to learn an inverse skill given the demonstrations of the forward skill using Reinforcement Learning (RL) coupled with Learning from Demonstrations (LfD). Our architecture uses learns and appropriate reward function for the inverse skill using the demonstrations of the forward skill, warm-starts the policy by learning to imitate the rewinded version of the demonstrations using Behaviour Cloning, and continues training with RL using the learned reward function. This approach mitigates the poor sample efficiency, tedious reward shaping and difficult high-dimensional exploration problems of RL while being able to create novel skills different from the given demonstrations, something that can’t be done by pure LfD.
keywords: ["imitation learning", "reinforcement learning", "reward function learning", "sample efficiency", "reward shaping"]

title: 3D Sparse Face Model-based Liveness Detection with Point Nets
abstract: Nowadays, face-based authentication systems play a critical role in high-security areas. These systems are widely preferred due to their contactless and fast usage advantages, significantly improving security processes. However, digital fraud techniques such as printed photos, screen images, and video-based spoofing threaten the reliability of face recognition systems. In this study, a real-time and high-accuracy face liveness detection method is proposed to detect face spoofing performed through passive methods. The proposed system analyzes the three-dimensional structure of the face using a stereo imaging technique and classifies real and fake faces through a deep learning model trained on a specially created dataset. This passive face liveness analysis method, which does not require any active user interaction, provides an effective solution against spoofing attempts, enhancing the reliability of face recognition-based authentication systems in high-security areas. Experimental studies have shown that the proposed method achieves a high accuracy rate against photo and screen-based attacks.
keywords: ["face liveness detection", "face spoofing detection", "stereoscopic imaging", "anti-spoofing"]

title: Comparison of TDE and FDE Equalizers Used in ACO-OFDM Communication Systems
abstract: In this paper, we analyze the performance of the asymmetrically clipped optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ACO-OFDM) waveform, the most widely studied waveform in visible light communication systems, in a multipath wireless optical channel environment. Time domain (TDE) and frequency domain (FDE) equalizers are used to equalize the wireless optical channel. From the computer simulation studies, it is observed that the performance of the TDE equalizer is better than the FDE equalizer at low level modulations, whereas the performance of the FDE is better than the TDE at high level modulations.
keywords: ["asymmetrically clipped optical OFDM", "ACO-OFDM", "visible light communication", "time-domain equalizer", "frequency domain equalizer", "channel equalization", "modulation level"]

title: Effects of Extended Features on BERT Performance: Depression Detection
abstract: In this study, the effects of categorical and numerical additional features obtained from Twitter posts on depression detection were investigated. Depression detection performances of the BERT large language model and SVM classifier were compared on the dataset balanced with the oversampling method. The effects of two different feature addition methods, Unimodal and Concat, were evaluated on the BERT model. The results show that oversampling improves the performance of the BERT classifier, but feature addition methods do not provide significant improvement in the model performance. The findings of the experiments reveal the success of the BERT model in the field of classification and that it does not require additional features for the detection of depression. It is believed that this study will guide research in the field of depression detection and help researchers identify more effective areas of study.
keywords: ["depression detection", "BERT", "tweets", "text classification", "oversampling", "feature addition", "categorical variables", "numerical attributes", "multimodal features", "support vector machine"]

title: Development of a Fashion Outfit Recommendation System Using Deep Feature Extraction and Graph-Based Learning
abstract: In online fashion retail, the demand for automated recommendation systems that help users create compatible clothing outfits is steadily increasing. This study presents a graph-based outfit recommendation system to reduce workload, optimize inventory management, and enhance user experience. Product images are segmented using the SegFormer model to separate each fashion item, and multi-layered features are extracted using the ResNet50 architecture. Product similarities are calculated using the cosine similarity metric to determine the most suitable outfits. The proposed system models fashion products as nodes and their relationships as edges, forming a graph-based structure. This approach automates the outfit creation process, reducing workload and saving time. The results demonstrate that the system successfully generates compatible outfits based on both style and category and has the potential to contribute to inventory management.
keywords: ["graph-based recommendation", "deep feature extraction", "SegFormer", "ResNet50", "cosine similarity", "online fashion retail", "inventory management"]

title: Performance Comparison of BERT and DistilBERT Models on SQuAD Dataset
abstract: In this study, the performance of BERT and DistilBERT models, which are widely used in the field of natural language processing (NLP), on the SQuAD dataset is investigated. Standard metrics such as Exact Match (EM) and F1 scores were used to evaluate the success of the models. Within the scope of the study, the performance of BERT and DistilBERT models on different text types and difficulty levels were compared and the differences in terms of accuracy, speed and resource efficiency were revealed. The results show that BERT achieves high accuracy rates thanks to its bidirectional contextual understanding, but the computational cost is high. DistilBERT, on the other hand, works faster and consumes fewer resources, showing that it can be an alternative, especially in resource-constrained situations. The rich structure of the SQuAD dataset and its various difficulty levels allow the models to be tested in real-world scenarios.
keywords: ["BERT", "DistilBERT", "SQuAD", "question answering", "exact match", "F1 score", "model efficiency", "resource efficiency", "computational cost", "question difficulty"]

title: Performance Comparison of Classification Algorithms Used in Stroke Prediction
abstract: Stroke is a life-threatening condition that occurs as a result of interrupted blood flow to the brain. As with many diseases, early diagnosis and intervention play a critical role in preventing stroke cases. This study aims to predict strokes using different machine learning algorithms. In this context, Logistic Regression (LR), Random Forest (RF), Decision Tree (DT), and Gaussian Naive Bayes (NB) models were applied, and the accuracy, F1 score, recall, and precision performances of the models were compared. Due to the imbalanced distribution of the dataset used in the study, the effects of class imbalance on model performances were examined. At the end of the study, the models providing the highest performance were identified. Additionally, the impact of data balancing on the models’ prediction results has been presented. By performing hyperparameter optimization, it was aimed to increase the prediction accuracy of the models.
keywords: ["stroke risk prediction", "classifier comparison", "class imbalance", "data balancing", "hyperparameter optimization", "logistic regression", "random forest", "decision tree", "Gaussian naive Bayes", "early stroke diagnosis"]

title: A Logistic Regression and Neural Network Based Approach for Disease Detection from Physiological Sensors
abstract: Early diagnosis of developmental, neurological, and functional disorders is of critical importance for improving individuals’ quality of life and developing appropriate intervention strategies. This study aims to distinguish between dyslexia, obstetric brachial plexus injury (OBPI), intellectual disability (ID), and typical development (TD) classes through the analysis of physiological signals. Data were collected while participants played two different serious games while wearing Empatica E4 wristbands; blood volume pulse (BVP), electrodermal activity (EDA), and skin temperature (ST) signals were obtained. Stress labels given by three different experts were added to each segment. Using the obtained data, logistic regression and multilayer perceptron artificial neural network models were developed and comparative classification analysis was performed. The logistic regression model performed classification using a one-vs-all approach, while the neural network model directly produced multi-class outputs. With the logistic regression model, 60%, 85%, 78%, and 95% accuracy was achieved in dyslexia, OBPI, intellectual disability, and typical development classes, respectively. The neural network model provided accuracy of 93%, 92%, 92%, and 99% in the same order. The overall accuracy rate reached 92% in the neural network model. The findings indicate that physiological signals are an effective tool in the classification of neurodevelopmental disorders, and artificial intelligence-based models can support diagnostic processes.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Analysis of Microscopic Images of Dermatophyte Fungi
abstract: Dermatophytes are a type of fungus that can infect the hair, nails, and skin, making them a significant cause of dermatological diseases. Infections caused by dermatophytes negatively impact the quality of life and pose a particular risk for individuals with weakened immune systems. The potential of artificial intelligence in image classification plays a crucial role in ensuring accurate diagnosis and expediting the treatment process. In this study, deep learning models VGG16, EfficientNetB0, and MobileNetV3 were employed for the classification of microscopic images of dermatophytes. Among these models, VGG16 demonstrated the most balanced performance, achieving an accuracy of %78.9.
keywords: ["dermatophytes", "dermatophyte identification", "fungal infection diagnosis", "image classification", "deep learning", "VGG16", "EfficientNetB0", "MobileNetV3", "skin diseases"]

title: Data Imbalance in Large-Scale Face Recognition
abstract: In this study, proposals have been presented to improve various recognition problems encountered in large-scale face databases related to the open-set face recognition problem. Based on the experiments conducted, the most successful face detection model was determined to be SCRFD-BNKPS. For the face recognition problem, a embedding vector extraction model that provides high discrimination capability was selected from among the ArcFace models. The biggest issue observed when these extracted feature vectors were classified into identity classes using popular nonlinear classifiers was the varying number of identities within each class. To address this, the ROS and ENS algorithms were employed to ensure that classes with a small number of samples provided sufficient feedback to the classifier. Additionally, the k-NN algorithm, used to avoid the need for training a wholesale classifier in the open-set classification problem, was improved using the LMNN metric learning method.
keywords: ["open-set face recognition", "class imbalance", "face detection", "ArcFace", "vector embeddings", "k-nearest neighbors", "identity classification"]

title: Radar Target Detection using Improved Transformer Neural Network
abstract: In this study, a method based on the improved Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture is proposed for radar target detection instead of traditional signal processing techniques. Instead of the conventional Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) structure, an advanced network architecture has been employed to enhance target detection performance in cluttered environments. The study utilizes both synthetic and real data. The proposed method has been compared with SO-CA CFAR, GO-CA CFAR, CA-CFAR, OS-CFAR, and CNN in terms of target detection accuracy. The results indicate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional CFAR methods and the deep learning-based CNN method, particularly in the presence of clutter.
keywords: ["radar target detection", "vision transformer", "cluttered environments", "constant false alarm rate", "synthetic aperture radar", "deep learning"]

title: Performance Evaluation of Filter-Based Gene Selection Methods in Cancer Classification
abstract: With the advances in microarray technology, gene expression levels can be measured efficiently, and this data can be used to solve important problems such as cancer classification. However, microarray data suffers from the high-dimensionality problem and requires dimensionality reduction techniques such as feature selection. This study addresses the cancer classification problem using microarray datasets and comparatively evaluates the performance of different filter-based gene (feature) selection methods. To this end, 11 microarray datasets have been evaluated using 6 different filter methods, and experimental results are presented. According to the findings, the gene selection methods used can improve classification performance by 5% to 30%. Using 5-fold cross-validation, the highest accuracy rates were achieved with 32 genes selected by the gain ratio filter for the Breast and Colon datasets, and with 8 genes selected by the information gain filter for the CNS dataset.
keywords: ["gene selection", "filter-based feature selection", "cancer classification", "gene expression microarrays", "dimensionality reduction", "high-dimensional data", "breast cancer", "colon cancer", "CNS cancer"]

title: Target Parameter Estimation with ISAC-OTFS Systems
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space modulation (OTFS) has demonstrated superior error performance compared to its predecessor, Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM), primarily designed for low Doppler environments. This paper develops an OTFS- Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems informed by a mono-static Single Input Single Output (SISO) radar for ISAC. In the proposed system, OTFS frames are transmitted and received by a collocated transmitter and receiver. By taking advantage of the reflected signals, we could estimate the velocity and distance of targets with high accuracy for each target while maintaining much less complexity than the methods in the literature by eliminating the need to invert the matrix thanks to the iterative estimation of delay, Doppler shift, and channel gain for each path. The proposed method demonstrates superiority in terms of accuracy and error-performance Normalized Mean Squared Error (NMSE) estimation, as well as the ability to sense the surrounding environment and estimate the velocity and distance of each target individually.
keywords: ["orthogonal time frequency space", "integrated sensing and communication", "target parameter estimation", "velocity estimation", "distance estimation", "time delay estimation", "Doppler frequency estimation", "channel gain estimation", "iterative estimation"]

title: Duty Cycle Compatible Fresh Data Tranmission with LoRa
abstract: Low Power Wide Area Networks (LPWANs) using the ISM band are constrained by serious duty-cycle limitations in Europe and in various other parts of the world. This constraint particularly limits the freshness of IoT data that can be conveyed using these networks. Earlier literature introduced the DutyCycle Compliant Threshold ALOHA (DCCTA), that aims to optimize the age of information (AoI) in a duty-cycle constrained LPWAN setting. In this paper, we report on the implementation of a system where end nodes use DCCTA and LoRa-enabled end nodes. A custom gateway is implemented, to evaluate the performance of our protocol under two cases: end nodes receive or do not receive packet success feedback from the gateway. Measurement and simulation results both reveal that under dutycycle constraints, skipping the feedback achieves significantly better efficiency and data freshness. Our findings, grounded in both simulation and practical implementation, underscore the potential of our protocol in reducing AoI under stringent dutycycle regulations.
keywords: ["age of information", "duty cycle constraints", "LoRa", "low-power wide-area networks", "ISM band"]

title: Comparison of Helmholtz-MREPT and cr-MREPT Methods in Terms of Tissue Boundary Artifacts
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Electrical Property Tomography (MREPT) is a noninvasive reconstruction method used to image tissue electrical properties. Helmholtz-EPT and cr-MREPT are the most commonly used methods in this field. This study compares these two methods regarding artifacts at tissue boundaries of objects with different sizes. The Helmholtz-EPT method usually detects anomaly boundaries sharply. However, it cannot completely eliminate boundary artifacts in some cases. Errors and artifacts occur in the calculated conductivity values, especially in noisy data. The cr-MREPT method is more robust against boundary transitions and noise. However, it exhibits a low-pass filter performance in forming the conductivity distribution.
keywords: ["boundary artifacts", "electrical conductivity reconstruction", "noise robustness", "low-pass filtering", "conductivity distribution"]

title: Ship Detection using Global-Local RX Detector
abstract: Anomaly detection is useful for environmental surveillance, maritime observation, and various other remote sensing applications. Among various anomaly detectors, the Reed-Xiaoli (RX) detector is one of the most well-established, with global/local and linear/nonlinear variants. The Global RX detector struggles with complex backgrounds and small-scale anomalies due to its reliance on global statistical data, while Local RX is slow, noisy, and challenging to tune. We propose a tile-based RX detection method that maintains global context while effectively capturing localized patterns. To handle background complexity within each tile, we employ Randomized RX (RRX) as an efficient approximation of kernel RX (KRX). As validated by our experiments, our method achieves high accuracy with execution time comparable to Global RX by leveraging the strengths of global and local approaches through RRX.
keywords: ["ship detection", "anomaly detection", "maritime surveillance", "background complexity"]

title: Tokenization Standards and Evaluation in Natural Language Processing: A Comparative Analysis of Large Language Models on Turkish
abstract: Tokenization is a fundamental preprocessing step in Natural Language Processing (NLP), significantly impacting the capability of large language models (LLMs) to capture linguistic and semantic nuances. This study introduces a novel evaluation framework addressing tokenization challenges specific to morphologically-rich and low-resource languages such as Turkish. Utilizing the Turkish MMLU (TR-MMLU) dataset, comprising 6,200 multiple-choice questions from the Turkish education system, we assessed tokenizers based on vocabulary size, token count, processing time, language-specific token percentages (%TR), and token purity (%Pure). These newly proposed metrics measure how effectively tokenizers preserve linguistic structures. Our analysis reveals that language-specific token percentages exhibit a stronger correlation with downstream performance (e.g., MMLU scores) than token purity. Furthermore, increasing model parameters alone does not necessarily enhance linguistic performance, underscoring the importance of tailored, language-specific tokenization methods. The proposed framework establishes robust and practical tokenization standards for morphologically complex languages.
keywords: ["tokenization", "Turkish language", "large language models", "morphologically rich languages", "low-resource languages", "vocabulary size", "token counts", "model parameter size"]

title: Classification and Comparison of Diabetic Retinopathy Using Deep Learning Methods
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy is one of the complications of diabetes. As a result of diabetes, vascular deterioration and hemorrhages occur in the retinal layer. If left untreated, this condition can lead to blindness. Due to the complex structure of diabetic retinopathy and the insufficient number of specialist physicians, early diagnosis of the disease becomes challenging. Therefore, the use of computer-based systems in the diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy is of great importance. In this study, diabetic retinopathy classification was performed using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) methods from the literature. Xception, EfficientNetB0, ResNet50, and a custom-designed CNN model were compared. The experiments were conducted on the APTOS 2019 dataset. Image enhancement techniques were applied to the images in the dataset. Additionally, data augmentation methods were used due to the imbalance in the dataset. A five-class classification was performed, and the highest accuracy was achieved using the Xception and EfficientNetB0 models.
keywords: ["diabetic retinopathy", "retinal image classification", "convolutional neural networks", "APTOS 2019 dataset", "Xception", "EfficientNetB0", "ResNet50", "custom CNN", "image enhancement", "data augmentation", "class imbalance", "early diagnosis"]

title: Optimizing CNNs via Sorensen-Dice Based Pruning
abstract: Deep learning, particularly Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), has revolutionized many fields, including image recognition, natural language processing, and object detection. However, the high computational complexity and memory requirements of these models hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, a novel kernel pruning framework is proposed that leverages the robust Sorensen-Dice similarity coefficient to identify and remove redundant kernels within each convolutional layer. This method efficiently reduces model complexity while preserving essential structural information and accuracy. Extensive experiments on popular CNN architectures and benchmark datasets demonstrate the advantages of this approach over other pruning methods.
keywords: ["convolutional neural network pruning", "model compression", "resource-constrained deployment", "computational complexity reduction"]

title: Underwater Turbid Image Restoration Using Diffusion Models
abstract: Underwater images often face challenges due to turbidity caused by suspended particles, leading to hazy and distorted visuals. The lack of real-life underwater data also reduces the efficiency of trained models. This paper introduces a diffusion model-based denoising architecture to restore underwater turbid images. The method first quantifies the turbidity noise by optimizing the variance parameter using a dataset that replicates the diffusion process of forward noise addition. The trained U-Net architecture then iteratively reconstructs turbid images by implementing a reverse Markov diffusion chain process. In addition to visual enhancements, restored images are evaluated using perceptual evaluation measures such as entropy and the naturalness image quality evaluator. The results of this project will contribute significantly to underwater research by facilitating the monitoring of marine ecosystems and studying fish migration patterns.
keywords: ["underwater image restoration", "turbidity", "image denoising", "diffusion models", "U-Net", "reverse diffusion", "image quality assessment", "marine ecosystem monitoring"]

title: Touch Location Error Analysis of a Low-Cost Piezoresistive Array Sensor
abstract: In this paper, we investigate error characteristics of touch location for a very low-cost piezoresistive array sensor. The act of touch is performed by placing 100 g and 150 g weights on two different sensors designed as 5x5 and 7x7 array formations. Center of pressure calculation is performed two different ways; by using the whole measurement matrix and one of its submatrices. The accuracy and precision of the sensor is reported qualitatively, with a visual representation. It is demonstrated that 7x7 sensor and the submatrix give better results as compared to their alternatives.
keywords: ["capacitive touch sensing", "center of pressure", "low-cost sensors", "sensor accuracy and precision"]

title: Artificial Intelligence for Edge Computing in 6G Technology
abstract: This study provides a concise literature review of Edge Artificial Intelligence (Edge AI) in the context of 6G networks, emphasizing its foundational concepts, current advancements, and future potential. Fundamental components, including federated learning, self-learning, task-oriented learning, and security-oriented learning, are explained to give a comprehensive insight into core principles. Scalability, resource optimization, and emerging technologies like Quantum AI and Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS), which are critical in Edge AI for 6G, are included. Moreover, prominent challenges, including computational limitations, data privacy concerns, and adversarial threats, are identified. The paper identifies future research directions by emphasizing the need for lightweight AI models, security-enhanced frameworks, and standardized protocols. This study also provides valuable insights into the transformative role of AI at the edge in next-generation wireless networks.
keywords: ["edge AI", "6G", "federated learning", "self-learning", "task-based learning", "quantum artificial intelligence", "reconfigurable intelligent surface", "resource optimization", "data privacy", "adversarial threats", "lightweight AI models", "next-generation wireless networks"]

title: Human Stress State Analysis from Foot Movements with Deep Learning
abstract: In this study, 9-axis sensor data were used to classify people's stress levels. Given the significant effects of stress on psychological and physiological health, the development of such a classification system is of critical importance. The data collection process was carried out by having the participants play the Tetris game. During the game, as the user's level increases, the game speed and the probability of making errors also increase; this leads to an increase in the stress levels of individuals. By analyzing how foot movements change during stressful moments in individuals, a more in-depth understanding of stress is provided. The developed classifier models were created with Support Vector Machine (SVM), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and AutoEncoder (AE) algorithms. Sensor data were examined for classification after a detailed preprocessing and feature extraction process. Performance analysis showed that the models gave quite successful results in stress classification. The results provide an important basis for the development of data augmentation and fusion methods for classes with different sample numbers.
keywords: ["stress state classification", "foot movement", "wearable sensors", "stress detection", "support vector machine", "long short-term memory", "autoencoder", "feature extraction", "class imbalance", "data augmentation"]

title: Detection of the Ionospheric Disturbances During 2023 Kahramanmaraş Earthquakes Using Random Forests Algorithm
abstract: In this study, a new approach based on Random Forest algorithm is presented for the detection of earthquake precursors in the ionosphere. Total Electron Content (TEC) data estimated from TUSAGA-Active stations belonging to three quiet and three disturbed days and the 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake period are used in the study. 9 different features derived from TEC data are used in the proposed model. Random Forest algorithm successfully has detected earthquake-related ionospheric disturbances with 95.45% Accuracy rate. It is observed that the model can also effectively distinguish disturbances caused by solar activity and geomagnetic storms.
keywords: ["earthquake precursors", "ionospheric disturbances", "total electron content", "2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquakes", "random forest", "geomagnetic storms", "solar activity", "ionospheric monitoring"]

title: Automatic Determination of Listening Comprehension Level in English as a Foreign Language Using Symbolic Aggregate Approximation Features
abstract: Listening comprehension in English as a foreign language is currently assessed using various testing techniques. However, a significant drawback of these techniques is their lack of sufficient objectivity. Because the listening comprehension skills of test takers may vary depending on the structure of the exam, the interpretation of the examiner, and the evaluation criteria. It is crucial to develop an objective and rapid method for evaluating an individual’s proficiency without relying on any test, oral examination, or survey. The human brain has the capacity to process and evaluate all types of sensory inputs. Leveraging this capability, this study proposes a method to determine individuals’ English listening comprehension status by analyzing neural activities. The proposed method is based on an adaptive noise-enhanced complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (ICEEMDAN) and symbolic aggregate approximation (SAX). Brain activity data were recorded from 15 healthy participants using electroencephalography. In the preprocessing stage, intrinsic mode functions (IMFs) were computed using the ICEEMDAN algorithm. Subsequently, features were extracted from the IMFs using the SAX algorithm. The extracted features were used to classify participants’ comprehension of English listening texts as understood or not understood using various classification algorithms, including k-nearest neighbors (k-NN), support vector machines, linear discriminant analysis, and artificial neural networks. The highest classification accuracy was achieved using the k-NN classifier on IMF7, with an accuracy of 86.27%.
keywords: ["listening comprehension", "English as a foreign language", "EEG", "brain-computer interface", "ICEEMDAN", "symbolic aggregate approximation", "intrinsic mode functions", "k-nearest neighbors", "EEG feature extraction"]

title: On Measuring the Contribution of Human Operator in Collaborative Human-Robot Load Carrying Tasks
abstract: In this study, collaborative human-robot interaction is aimed and realized using an inherently unstable mobile robot called ballbot. Three different experiments are considered for scenarios of guidance of the ballbot by the human operator and collaborative/cooperative human-robot load carrying activities. The force applied by the human operator is measured with a force gauge sensor and considered as a measure of the effort provided by the human. Based on this measure, the contribution of the human operator in collaborative/cooperative human-robot load carrying scenarios is investigated.
keywords: ["human-robot collaboration", "ballbot", "force measurement", "mobile robots"]

title: Comparing Pre-trained and Fine-Tuned Transformer-Based Models for Sentiment Analysis in Turkish Comments in Student Surveys
abstract: Student surveys are essential for evaluating teaching quality and course content, but analyzing open-ended responses is challenging due to their unstructured and multilingual nature. This study applies sentiment analysis to Turkish educational survey responses using three transformer-based models: SAVASY, DBMDZ BERT Base Turkish Cased, and XLM-RoBERTa Base. A labeled dataset of real-world student comments was used, with sentiment labels assigned using the Gemini AI tool to facilitate model fine-tuning. Evaluation metrics included accuracy, F1-score, precision, recall, and confidence scores. Results show that fine-tuning improves sentiment classification, effectively identifying positive, negative, and neutral sentiments. This highlights the value of transformer models in analyzing Turkish student feedback.
keywords: ["sentiment analysis", "student survey", "Turkish language", "transformer models", "XLM-R", "open-ended survey responses", "student feedback", "teaching quality evaluation"]

title: Enhancing Complex Disease Group Scoring with miRGediNET: A Multi-Algorithm Machine Learning Framework Based on the GSM Approach
abstract: Integrating biological prior knowledge for disease gene associations has shown significant promise in discovering new biomarkers with potential translational applications. This work investigates the application of a multi-algorithm machine learning framework based on the Grouping-Scoring-Modeling (G-S-M) approach for improving the prediction of complex diseases. The study identifies the primary gene and miRNA interactions in various complex diseases with the help of miRGediNET, which is a machine-learning based tool that integrates data from three biological databases. Traditional methods have only focused on independence between features; the G-S-M method focuses on aggregating genes based on biological interactions, pinpointing the scoring of gene groups for a disease, and modeling its predictive capability using advanced machine learning algorithms. In this research paper, seven algorithms, including Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, and CatBoost, were applied to eight datasets extracted from the GEO database. This framework proved very robust in ranking gene clusters, thus predicting critical biomarkers while doing 100-fold randomized cross-validation within the evaluation. The results indicate this approach's high potential for refining disease and supporting research for choosing the best algorithm that can provide biological insights and computational advances.
keywords: ["miRNA-gene interactions", "gene-disease association", "biomarker discovery", "gene clustering", "CatBoost", "GEO datasets"]

title: Stock Price Prediction with Multimodal Data
abstract: In today's financial markets, the influence of dynamic factors is becoming increasingly evident, and markets are affected by real-time data from various sources. In this study, a multimodal machine learning approach is adopted by integrating traditional technical analysis metrics, tweets, and news articles with historical price data. Market sentiment and investor psychology are measured through sentiment analysis of textual data using both the FinBERT and ChatGPT-4o models, and the obtained outputs are combined with financial metrics to construct an LSTM-based stock price prediction model. To enhance the model's stability, LSTM models derived from different training sessions are merged using an ensemble learning method, and the two approaches are compared. The results demonstrate that the ensemble model outperforms the standard LSTM model, and integrating financial indicators with tweet and news data, as opposed to relying solely on price data, leads to increased overall profit.
keywords: ["stock price prediction", "multimodal fusion", "technical indicators", "social media sentiment", "Twitter", "news articles", "FinBERT", "GPT-4o", "LSTM", "ensemble learning", "investor psychology", "market sentiment"]

title: Generative 6G Network Architecture and Service: From Native AI to Native Network Generative AI
abstract: Establishing endogenous intelligence capabilities within telecommunication networks in the form of native artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a significant topic of research for promoting the prospects of 6th Generation (6G) networks. In the upcoming 6G era, the network is expected to provide services for building and deploying distributed AI applications in the network infrastructure, and such applications will be used solely by the network or offered to operators or third parties as new services. This paper begins by analysing the current status of standardisation in the network AI domain, and next elaborates on the major shortcomings of the current approaches for natively setting up network AI services. On this basis, we present the concept of Native Network Generative AI (NNGAI), which builds on and further advances the concept of native AI for telecom networks. To formulate the paradigm of NNGAI, we first devise the network architecture, and then finally the underlying logical flow of network services to realize NNGAI by carefully inserting generative AI technologies into both the architecture and the service flow of 6G networks.
keywords: ["6G", "generative AI", "network architecture", "telecommunications networks"]

title: High-Efficiency Penta-Band Coaxial-Fed Slotted Patch Antenna
abstract: In this study, a multi-band coaxially fed slotted patch antenna is numerically analyzed, optimized and the obtained results are discussed. The proposed antenna has dimensions of 37 × 32 × 1.524 mm3and utilizes Isola I-Tera MT40 as the substrate, which has a relative permittivity of 3.45 and a loss tangent of 0.0031. The antenna features L-shaped slots on the patch plane and rectangular ring-shaped slots on the ground plane. The optimization results indicate that the antenna operates efficiently with the magnitude of reflection coefficient better than − dB in the 2–12 GHz frequency range, making it suitable for applications in the S, C, and X bands. Additionally, the antenna exhibits a frequency-dependent radiation pattern, being either bidirectional or omnidirectional depending on the operating frequency. The E-plane gain values vary between 2.58 and 5.09 dBi. The average total antenna efficiency is found to be 90.42%.
keywords: ["penta-band antenna", "coaxial feed", "slotted patch antenna", "L-shaped slots", "antenna efficiency"]

title: Non-Uniform Subband Partitioning For CLI Measurement In SBFD Networks
abstract: Subband full-duplex (SBFD) technology aims to enhance uplink (UL) capacity in 5G and 6G networks; however, it is significantly affected by cross-link interference (CLI), which degrades system performance. Accurate CLI measurement is crucial for effective interference mitigation, yet traditional methods such as wideband measurement and uniform subband partitioning (USP) fail to adequately model frequency-dependent interference. In this paper, we propose the non-uniform subband partitioning (NUSP) technique, where subband lengths are adaptively adjusted based on the frequency-dependent CLI trend, enabling more precise interference modeling. Simulation results demonstrate that NUSP outperforms WB and USP techniques in CLI estimation accuracy.
keywords: ["cross-link interference", "interference measurement", "uplink capacity", "interference mitigation", "5G/6G networks"]

title: A Comparative Study of Multi-label Supervised Contrastive Losses for the Content-based Image Retrieval of Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Contrastive loss has been extensively studied for both supervised and unsupervised learning, and its success has led to its extension towards multi-label classification scenarios. Its application to multi-label content-based image retrieval however has been very limited. This study provides a systematic comparison in the context of content based remote sensing image retrieval where ever-growing data collections require efficient and effective management tools. Four multi-label supervised contrastive losses were investigated along with three benchmark datasets: BigEarthNet, UC Merced, and ML-AID. The weighted MulSupCon method achieved up to 90.11% mAP on ML-AID and 70.32% mAP on UC Merced, demonstrating its effectiveness in multi-label remote sensing retrieval tasks.
keywords: ["contrastive loss", "content-based image retrieval", "remote sensing images", "multi-label classification", "BigEarthNet"]

title: Impact Analysis of the Elevation Angle on Azimuth Angle of Arrival Estimation
abstract: This paper examines the impact of the elevation angle on the accuracy of azimuth angle estimation using the phase comparison method. Additionally, it proposes a technique to reduce the overall estimation error. The phase comparison method provides an unambiguous angle of arrival estimation when the distance between two antennas is less than half the wavelength of the input signal. Depending on the dimensional arrangement of the antenna array, both the azimuth and elevation angles can be measured. The elevation angle directly affects the phase difference used to estimate the azimuth angle. When the elevation angle is unknown in the azimuth estimation equation, estimation errors arise and vary depending on the actual elevation angle. These errors can be minimized by considering an estimation of possible elevation values.
keywords: ["elevation angle", "angle of arrival estimation", "estimation error", "antenna arrays", "elevation angle estimation", "phase difference"]

title: Enhancing Ottoman Word Recognition via Self-Supervised Pretraining Using a Siamese Swin Transformer
abstract: The Ottoman archive contains millions of handwritten documents, and their efficient management and retrieval is of paramount significance to historians. In this paper, a semi-supervised method is presented for Ottoman word recognition from handwritten historical documents. The approach involves a two-stage process: self-supervised pretraining followed by super-vised training with triplet loss. A Siamese network architecture with a Shifted Window Transformer backbone is used to learn robust feature representations. It is shown that pretraining significantly enhances the model’s ability to discriminate between similar Ottoman words. The method is evaluated on a historical dataset of labeled Ottoman word crops. To foster reproducibility and future research, we release the full code and dataset at https://github.com/Sadiq04/Ottoman-KWS-IEEE-SIU
keywords: ["self-supervised pre-training", "Siamese network", "Swin Transformer", "triplet loss", "semi-supervised learning", "feature representation learning", "Ottoman script", "document retrieval"]

title: An Achievable Design of a Metasurface Reflector Microstrip Patch Antenna with Enhanced Bandwidth and Gain
abstract: In antenna design, improving gain and bandwidth is critical for enhancing performance. The literature on increasing the gain and bandwidth of rectangular microstrip patch antennas includes designs made under ideal conditions using PEC (Perfect Electric Conductor). However, this study presents a practical design using copper conductors. The rectangular patch antenna has a 2.4 GHz resonant frequency with an FR4 substrate and a partial ground plane. The partial ground plane significantly reduces the gain of the patch antenna. To enhance the gain, a metasurface reflector placed beneath the ground plane is used.
keywords: ["metasurface reflector", "microstrip patch antenna", "antenna gain enhancement", "bandwidth enhancement", "partial ground plane", "copper conductors", "2.4 GHz", "FR4 substrate", "rectangular patch antenna"]

title: Analysis of Oxygen Saturation Measurement in Ink Model with Photoacoustic Imaging
abstract: Determining the oxygen level in the blood is critically important for ensuring the proper functioning of the body and monitoring the status of many diseases. One of the applications of photoacoustic tomography (FAT), a hybrid medical imaging technique, is the determination of oxygen saturation ( SpO2) value in blood. Oxyhemoglobin ( HbO2) and deoxyhemoglobin ( HbR) in the blood have different absorption coefficients and the SpO2value can be determined by measuring the photoacoustic signals produced by them at different amplitudes. In this study, a measurement setup that can detect SpO2value in blood with FAT was designed and a new technique was developed for the analysis of photoacoustic data. Due to ethical constraints, red and blue inks that mimic the hemoglobin forms HbO2and HbR were used. An analysis method was developed to determine the concentration ratio of ink mixtures representing the level of SpO2with FAT.
keywords: ["oxygen saturation", "photoacoustic tomography", "blood oxygenation", "oxyhemoglobin", "deoxyhemoglobin", "absorption coefficient", "measurement setup"]

title: Learning-Based MRI Reconstruction via a State-Space U-Net Model
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a widely used medical imaging technique that provides high-contrast visu-alization of soft tissues without ionizing radiation. However, long scan times impose significant limitations on clinical workflows, reducing patient comfort and increasing healthcare costs. Accelerated MRI techniques aim to shorten scan times by acquiring fewer k-space samples; however, this leads to undersampling artifacts and a decline in image quality. MRI reconstruction techniques are widely used to mitigate these artifacts by generating high-quality images from undersampled k-space data. In this study, we introduce MambaCC, an innovative State-Space Model (SSM)-based method that effectively captures long-range dependencies with low computational requirements, enabling efficient MRI reconstruction. MambaCC operates on a U-shaped deep learning network, where its outputs are enhanced with channel-mixing blocks to account for the effects of artifacts at the channel level. The performance of the proposed method has been evaluated on the fastMRI dataset and compared against state-of-the-art methods, including MoDL, U-Net, TransUNet, and UMamba. The results demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance in terms of PSNR and SSIM metrics. The findings highlight the significant potential of SSM-based architectures in enabling high-accuracy and efficient brain MRI reconstruction.
keywords: ["MRI reconstruction", "accelerated MRI", "state-space model", "Mamba", "U-Net", "channel mixing", "k-space undersampling", "long-range dependencies", "brain MRI", "scan time reduction", "artifact reduction"]

title: Bladder Volume Estimation from Computed Tomography Images: YOLO-Based Segmentation
abstract: Accurate bladder volume estimation in the pelvic region diseases play a crucial role in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. In this study, a You Only Look Once (YOLO)-based model was developed to determine bladder volume. The YOLOv11s-seg segmentation model was employed to delineate bladder boundaries in computed tomography (CT) images. The model was trained on a private dataset comprising five patients, with data augmentation techniques applied to enhance accuracy. The YOLOv11s-seg model demonstrated high-precision segmentation, achieving an accuracy of 97.2%, recall of 83%, and mAP50 of 90.9%. Additionally, three-dimensional (3D) bladder models were generated using segmentation results, and volume calculations were performed. The model’s rapid and efficient segmentation capability suggests it as a reliable alternative for bladder volume estimation. Future studies aim to validate the model in clinical settings and improve its accuracy using larger datasets.
keywords: ["bladder volume estimation", "bladder segmentation", "CT images", "pelvic diseases", "data augmentation"]

title: FMCW Signal Detection in Challenging Spectral Conditions using LSTM Networks
abstract: Detecting Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave or Continuous Wave (FMCW / CW) signals in complex spectral environments is a challenging task since the signals may overlap and contaminated by the noise-like components. This article presents a depth first search (DFS) algorithm integrated with a pre-trained Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to identify and separate FMCW emitter signals using time-frequency representations. The LSTM network, trained on FMCW and non-signal waveforms, serves as a scoring function to guide the selection of optimal sequence of signal peaks. Simulation results show that our approach is able to handle diverse interference scenarios, effectively.
keywords: ["continuous wave signals", "depth-first search", "time-frequency representation", "spectral interference", "signal overlap"]

title: Semantically Guided Gradient Matching for Open-Set Domain Generalization
abstract: Neural networks assume training and test data share the same distribution and label space, but real-world violations degrade performance when domain and category shifts occur simultaneously. Open Set Domain Generalization addresses recognizing unseen classes in unseen domains. Current approaches using one-vs-all classifiers suffer from biased decision boundaries due to class imbalance, while meta-learning methods ignore semantic relationships between classes. This paper proposes a semantically-guided gradient matching framework extending dualistic meta-learning with joint domain-class matching by incorporating a semantic encoder for modeling continuous class relationships. The key innovation is weighted gradient matching using semantic similarity to guide decision boundary formation. Experiments on PACS dataset show this approach outperforms previous methods in open set scenarios while maintaining competitive closed-set generalization, resulting in more balanced decision boundaries.
keywords: ["gradient matching", "meta-learning", "semantic encoder", "semantic similarity", "class imbalance", "unseen classes", "unseen domains"]

title: An Alternative Method for Determining the Location of the Interfering Signal Source in Satellite Communication
abstract: Fast and high-capacity satellite communication, which enables long-distance communication, is frequently used today for both civilian and military communication purposes. Disruptions in communication may occur due to intentional or unintentional interfering signals. The negative impact on communication can lead to significant problems, such as satellite operators like TÜRKSAT being unable to provide proper service to users or the failure to maintain coordination between military units. To resolve such issues, it is essential to determine the source of the interfering signal. This paper examines the dual-satellite positioning method used to identify the locations of interfering signal sources that negatively affect satellite communication. By simulating the orbital motion of the TÜRKSAT 4A and TÜRKSAT 4B satellites via software, real-time position and velocity data of the satellites were obtained. These values were used in TDOA (Time Difference of Arrival) and FDOA (Frequency Difference of Arrival) equations to form systems of nonlinear equations. These systems were then solved using Newton and Broyden numerical analysis methods, enabling high-accuracy localization of interfering signal sources positioned in different regions of the Earth. Thus, the feasibility of the developed method has been theoretically demonstrated.
keywords: ["satellite communication", "time difference of arrival", "frequency difference of arrival", "Newton's method", "Broyden's method", "nonlinear equation systems"]

title: AviBERT: Transformer-based Aircraft Text Classification
abstract: In recent years, transformer-based models pre-trained on extensive corpora have played a critical role in the advancement of Natural Language Processing methodologies. Particularly, methods based on BERT have demonstrated remarkable performance across various tasks by offering robust capabilities in deeply understanding texts semantically. However, despite these advancements, there is a notable scarcity of studies applying these technologies in the aviation sector. This paper develops a multi-class classification model for aviation-specific texts using variants of BERT. The study encompasses the processes of collecting web content related to aircraft, labeling and model training. The details of the dataset are explained and the outcomes of the study are assessed based on the macro F1-score and accuracy of different models.
keywords: ["BERT", "transformer models", "multi-class text classification"]

title: Applications of Bilateral Orthogonality Generative Acquisitions Method for Transmit Field Inhomogeneity Correction at 7T
abstract: Transmit field inhomogeneity effects at 7T, severely degrades the image quality, limiting the clinical utilization of 7T MRI. In this work, applications of Bilateral Orthogonality Generative Acquisitions (BOGA) method for the transmit field correction at 7T are demonstrated for gradient echo acquisitions, Turbo Spin Echo acquisitions, Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping (QSM) and Chemical Exchange Saturation Transfer (CEST). It is shown that homogeneous images without the transmit field inhomogeneity effects of the 7T can be obtained via the BOGA method.
keywords: ["7T MRI", "gradient echo", "fast spin echo", "quantitative susceptibility mapping", "chemical exchange saturation transfer", "ultra-high field MRI", "image quality"]

title: Time Series Forecast on Kubernetes Metrics
abstract: This study focuses on time series forecasting of central processing unit (CPU) usage from metric values collected via Prometheus from Kubernetes clusters. Kubernetes is a widely used platform for container orchestration, and CPU usage is a critical indicator of system performance and health. In this study, time series forecasting models were tested on CPU usage data collected from a ten-node Kubernetes cluster. CPU usage percentage predictions were made using statistical models such as ARIMA, Seasonal Naive, as well as the DeepAR deep learning model and the pre-trained large-scale time series forecasting model Chronos-Bolt. Model performances were evaluated with Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Mean Squared Error (MSE) metrics. While DeepAR and Chronos-Bolt models generally performed better, differences were observed in capturing instantaneous changes. While the ARIMA model yielded successful results in some nodes, the Seasonal Naive model was successful in capturing instantaneous changes despite its low prediction accuracy. This study provides guidance in selecting the most suitable model when estimating CPU usage of Kubernetes environments.
keywords: ["time series forecasting", "Kubernetes", "CPU utilization", "Prometheus metrics", "container orchestration", "ARIMA", "DeepAR", "model comparison"]

title: Multi-Class Classification for IoT Attack Detection: An LLM-Based Approach
abstract: With the widespread adoption of IoT devices, cyberattacks targeting IoT networks have increased, making the detection of security threats a significant research topic. Traditional ML-based approaches exist for mitigating these threats; however, they suffer from certain limitations, such as limited generalization ability and practical applicability. In this study, a LLM-based approach is proposed for intrusion detection in IoT networks. The open-source CIC IoT 2023 dataset was utilized for attack detection in IoT networks. The detection process was conducted using the DistilBERT model. Initially, the contribution of all features in the dataset to the model’s classification performance was examined. Subsequently, the most important 30 features were selected using the RFE method, and the model’s performance was analyzed. Before feature selection, the fine-tuned DistilBERT model achieved an accuracy of 81%, whereas, after feature selection and further fine-tuning, the model’s accuracy improved to 94%. The obtained results demonstrate that feature selection significantly enhances model performance.
keywords: ["IoT attack detection", "intrusion detection", "multi-class classification", "large language models", "DistilBERT", "feature selection", "recursive feature elimination", "IoT network security"]

title: Deep Learning-Enhanced Physical Layer Security in XL-MIMO: A Visibility Region-Based Authentication Framework
abstract: Physical layer authentication (PLA) is crucial for securing wireless networks against spoofing attacks. In extra-large (XL)-MIMO systems, the visibility region (VR) concept offers a unique opportunity to enhance authentication using spatial diversity. However, dynamic environments pose challenges for maintaining reliability. This paper proposes an AI-driven PLA approach leveraging VR characteristics to generate robust signatures. A convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to capture spatial-temporal variations, ensuring high authentication accuracy with minimal false alarms. Simulation results demonstrate the method’s effectiveness across diverse scenarios, highlighting AI’s potential in securing next-generation wireless networks.
keywords: ["physical layer authentication", "physical layer security", "visibility regions", "spoofing attacks", "spatial diversity", "convolutional neural networks", "wireless network security", "spatiotemporal variation"]

title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning for HVAC Systems Using an LSTM-based Surrogate Simulator
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has shown great potential in optimizing the operation of HVAC systems, improving energy efficiency, and enhancing user comfort. However, the slow input/output operations associated with simulation tools like EnergyPlus significantly hinder the training process. This paper proposes a novel approach to accelerate RL training by using a data-driven LSTM model to replicate the behavior of a building energy simulator. By training the LSTM model on a set of observations and actions, the model learns to approximate the simulator’s dynamics, providing a faster and more efficient training environment for RL agents. We demonstrate that using the LSTM-based surrogate simulator leads to substantial reductions in computational time while maintaining the accuracy of the system’s behavior.
keywords: ["HVAC systems", "reinforcement learning", "LSTM surrogate model", "building energy simulation", "EnergyPlus", "training acceleration", "energy efficiency", "user comfort", "building operation optimization"]

title: Analysis of Model-Agnostic Meta-Reinforcement Learning on Automated HVAC Control
abstract: This paper introduces a Model-Agnostic Meta-Reinforcement Learning framework for HVAC automation, integrating Model Agnostic Meta-Learning with Double Deep Q-Networks to improve adaptability across varying environmental conditions. The proposed approach is evaluated using Sinergym, an EnergyPlus-integrated RL Simulation framework, and benchmarked against conventional RL-based HVAC controllers. Results demonstrate that Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning integrated Double Deep Q-Network achieves a 7% reduction in overall power consumption while dynamically adapting to climate variations. These findings highlight the potential of Model Agnostic Meta-Learning in optimizing HVAC control strategies.
keywords: ["model-agnostic meta-learning", "meta-reinforcement learning", "HVAC control", "double deep Q-network", "energy consumption reduction", "climate change adaptation", "EnergyPlus"]

title: CS-REG-NET: A Self-Supervised Visual-State-Space based Architecture for Cross-Spectral Registration of Thermal and Optical Imagery
abstract: Modern deep models for multispectral image matching typically rely on large, supervised datasets, which can be prohibitively expensive. To overcome this challenge, we introduce CS-REG-NET, a self-supervised, detector-based framework that requires no external labels. Instead, it uses RIFT2 detector to generate pseudo-ground-truth keypoints. A VMamba encoder, pre-trained on a segmentation task, processes image pairs, while two output heads learn feature heatmaps and descriptors. CSREG-NET significantly outperforms existing methods, delivering superior keypoint detection and homography estimation.
