Classical methods typically correct these distortions using images acquired in reversed phase-encoding (PE) directions. However, these methods rely on iterative optimization techniques, making them impractically slow for clinical usage. Recently, an unsupervised deep learning model called Forward Distortion Network (FD-Net) was proposed for rapid distortion correction. FD-Net predicts a corrected image and a displacement field, and enforces physics-based consistency between forward-distorted versions of the corrected image and the input reversed-PE image. In this work, we propose a 4-way PE Forward Distortion Network (4PE-FD-Net), which utilizes EPI images acquired in four different PE directions for improved physics-based consistency. 4PE-FD-Net outperforms the FD-Net variants that rely on reversed-PE images, while offering rapid correction.
keywords: ["echo planar imaging", "unsupervised deep learning", "displacement field estimation", "magnetic resonance imaging", "distortion correction"]

title: Logic Locking-Based FPGA System Design for Third-Party IP Protection
abstract: In the FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Arrays) development environment, IP (Intellectual Property) is frequently used to implement standard or customized operations quickly and reliably without requiring labor resources. In cases where IP developers do not transfer their intellectual property rights, methods are implemented with the developer or FPGA manufacturer to protect these rights. Logic locking method is a concept developed to secure the chip design against hardware trojans or elements involved in the chip manufacturing production stages. This paper proposes a cryptographic solution based on logic locking to ensure that the functional structure of the IP cannot be obtained by treating the FPGA manufacturer as secure.
keywords: ["logic locking", "FPGA", "intellectual property protection", "hardware Trojans", "cryptographic hardware security", "hardware obfuscation"]

title: Deep Learning Aided MU-MIMO Systems
abstract: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology has become a critical component in Beyond 5G (B5G) wireless communication systems, enhancing spectral efficiency and system capacity. However, accurate channel estimation remains a significant challenge, especially in high-mobility environments. In this study, conventional and deep learning-based channel estimation approaches were analyzed for 2×2, 4×4, and 8×8 Multi User MIMO, (MU-MIMO) systems. Least Squares (LS) method is compared with the proposed deep learning (DL)-based model, and the analyses are conducted under both perfect channel state information (P-CSI) and imperfect CSI (I-CSI) scenarios. The results demonstrate that the proposed DL-based approach achieves performance close to the P-CSI case and significantly improves estimation accuracy compared to traditional methods.
keywords: ["multi-user MIMO", "channel estimation", "deep learning", "beyond 5G", "imperfect channel state information", "least squares comparison", "high-mobility environments", "spectral efficiency"]

title: Integrating Multi-Input Data in CNN-LSTM Models for AI-Based Cooking Termination in Smart Ovens
abstract: In this study, an AI-powered smart oven system is proposed, which can automatically terminate the cooking process based on user preferences (rare, regular, or well-done). A camera-integrated oven prototype was developed for five different food types (fresh pizza, frozen pizza, tray pastry, mini pastry, and salmon), and a comprehensive dataset was created using images captured throughout the cooking process. Visual data were subjected to feature extraction using image processing techniques, and the resulting features were combined with numerical inputs such as temperature and cooking time to form the input of an LSTM-based deep learning model. The model was evaluated using both the collected dataset and real-world user scenarios, and was shown to perform with high accuracy. The developed system adapts to individual cooking preferences, prevents overcooking, and contributes to energy efficiency and reduction of food waste.
keywords: ["CNN-LSTM", "food waste reduction", "energy efficiency"]

title: SSDiffusion: State-Space Diffusion Model for Medical Image Synthesis
abstract: Medical image synthesis enables imputation of missing slices from acquired modalities, thereby reducing the need for repetitive and prolonged procedures in diagnostics. However, this is a non-trivial task due to the ill-posed and nonlinear characteristics of the problem. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) have shown promise in addressing these challenges. However, GANs can suffer from instability and mode collapse. Denoising diffusion models (DDMs) are recently demonstrated to be superior to GANs in terms of training stability and high fidelity. Yet, existing diffusion-based techniques rely on U-Net backbones, which are suboptimal for capturing contextual relationships between different tissue parts. Although transformers are adept at extracting the global context, their quadratic complexity makes them impractical for processing individual pixels rather than image patches. State-space models (SSMs) provide an efficient alternative with lower complexity, enabling the handling of extremely long sequences while effectively extracting contextual relationships. In this paper, we introduce SSDiffusion, a novel state-space diffusion model designed for multimodal medical image translation. By leveraging the strengths of state-space representations, our approach effectively captures contextual dependencies improving the translation performance. We evaluate SSDiffusion on a variety of medical image translation tasks. Experiments indicate that SSDiffusion outperforms state-of-the-art GAN and diffusion methods.
keywords: ["medical image synthesis", "denoising diffusion probabilistic models", "state-space model", "contextual dependencies", "mode collapse"]

title: Development of Real-Time Monitoring Systems with Comprehensive Intraoperative Electromyography (EMG) Data: A Preliminary Study on Brain Tumor Surgeries
abstract: Intraoperative neurophysiologic monitoring (IONM) is a vital technique to preserve the functional integrity of nerves during surgery. It plays an important role in preventing nerve damage by providing instant feedback to the surgeon, especially in brain tumor surgeries where motor and sensory nerves should not be damaged. Data on this surgery are very rare. In this study, for the first time in the literature, intraoperative electromyography (iEMG) data from 11 brain tumor surgery patients, labeled by professional neurophysiologists, were used for classification. This unique dataset, which is collected from 6 different muscle regions of the human face and contains 7 different signal events each, allows for signal identification and large-scale analysis. The features in this dataset were extracted using the 50% overlap method. These features were then analyzed with 5 different classifiers. In the analysis, the Bagged Trees model gave the most successful results with an accuracy rate of 97.13%. It is thought that this study may be effective in laying the foundations for a patient-independent, highly accurate and automatic warning system that surgeons can instantly monitor the patient's nerve damage status during brain tumor surgeries over a large data set.
keywords: ["intraoperative electromyography", "intraoperative neuromonitoring", "brain tumor surgery", "real-time monitoring", "EMG signal classification", "bagged trees"]

title: Temel Seviye Kategorilerin Otomatik Tespiti Automatic Detection of Basic Level Categories
abstract: Basic level categories (BLCs), which can be defined as the most inclusive level at which a concrete mental image of the entire category can be formed, have proven to be useful in a variety of applications in natural language processing (NLP) and computer vision (CV) tasks, such as word sense disambiguation, image searches, image description, and retrieval. Limiting their practical applications, current methods for detecting BLCs predominantly rely on rule-based methods and external knowledge sources rather than the information extracted directly from the text. In this manuscript, we propose a novel approach to detect BLCs that is merely based on the information obtained from the word embeddings, including Gaussian word embeddings (W2G) and embeddings retrieved from transformer-based models such as BERT and GPT-2. The proposed method significantly outperforms existing works in performance and practicality, demonstrating the effectiveness of contextual word embeddings for BLC detection.
keywords: ["basic-level categories", "word embeddings", "contextual word embeddings", "BERT", "GPT-2", "word sense disambiguation", "picture description", "image retrieval"]

title: Investigation of the Effects of DC Bias Addition on Equalizers Used in DCO-OFDM Waveform
abstract: This paper investigates the performance of the most widely used optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (O-OFDM) waveform, the spectrum efficient direct current biased optical OFDM (DCO-OFDM) waveform, in a multipath wireless optical channel environment. Time domain (TDE) and frequency domain (FDE) equalizers are used to equalize the multipath wireless optical channel. This study is the first in the literature to analyze the effects of adding different DC bias voltages in the DCO-OFDM waveform using TDE and FDE equalizers. From the obtained results, it is seen that adding DC bias at low level modulations contributes more to TDE equalizers, whereas adding DC bias at high level modulations benefits FDE equalizers more.
keywords: ["DC bias", "DCO-OFDM", "optical OFDM", "equalizer", "time-domain equalization", "frequency-domain equalization", "spectral efficiency"]

title: Analysis of Photonic UWB Pulse Generation in S, C, L Wavelengths
abstract: In this study, ultra-wideband (UWB) pulses were obtained in photonic circuits with S (short, 1460-1530 nm), C (conventional, 1530-1565 nm), L (long, 1565-1625 nm) wavelength fiber transmission lines. Time and frequency analyzes of the pulses were performed. The communication circuit was evaluated for three cases. First, the photonic circuit with a fiber transmission line with S, C, L wavelengths, in the second case, a semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) was added to the existing circuit, and in the third case, SOA and bandpass filter (BPF) were added to the existing circuit. In the first case, a UWB Gaussian double pulse was produced, and in the second and third cases, a Gaussian triple pulse was produced. Frequency analyzes for all three cases were found to be compatible with the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) mask. In the frequency analysis, the fractional bandwidth (FBW) percentage is in the S band, respectively; 168, 133, 102; 173, 136, 120 in C band; 186, 130, 123 in L Band. It was determined that the FBW values in the three bands were close to each other and relatively better values were obtained in the L band. FBW of the Double pulse obtained in Case 1 and the Triple pulse produced in Case 2; It was found to be higher than studies in the literature.
keywords: ["ultra-wideband pulses", "S-band", "C-band", "L-band", "optical fiber transmission lines", "semiconductor optical amplifier", "bandpass filter", "Gaussian pulse", "fractional bandwidth", "time-frequency analysis"]

title: Energy Optimization for Green Embedded Systems: Investigation of the Relationship Between Time Complexity and Power Usage
abstract: Power usage is a crucial point for embedded/IoT devices. Historically, theoretical time complexities were utilized during the choice of algorithm for these devices. But how accurate is this? In this research; Bubble, Insertion, Merge, Quick, Heap, Gnome, Radix, Shell, Comb and Pancake Sort algorithms have been ran on Arduino Uno R3 and R4 and current draws have been measured. Combining this with voltage, total power consumption has been calculated. The results show a [0.98, 1.0] correlation between the theoretical time complexities and power consumptions (p < 0.0001). The results indicate that optimizing for time spent also optimizes for power consumption. Comparison of power consumption of code generated by different large language models have also been analyzed and some preliminary results have been found.
keywords: ["energy optimization", "power consumption", "time complexity", "sorting algorithms", "embedded systems", "Internet of Things", "Arduino Uno", "large language models", "code generation", "green computing"]

title: Medical Image Segmentation via 3D Rubik Convolutions
abstract: Accurate segmentation of volumetric medical images presents a significant challenge, particularly in modeling spatial dependencies across different anatomical planes. Although 3D fully convolutional networks (FCNs) are widely used, the effectiveness of spatial feature extraction in such architectures may remain limited. In this study, a method called 3D Rubik Convolution, which applies 3D convolutions independently along the transaxial, coronal, and sagittal planes, is proposed. Unlike conventional convolution approaches that process the entire volume from a single perspective, the proposed method aims to extract spatial information separately across multiple anatomical planes while preserving full 3D representation. The method was evaluated on a COVID-19 lung computed tomography (CT) dataset and demonstrated higher segmentation accuracy compared to a baseline FCN architecture. The obtained results indicate that multi-view convolutional strategies can enhance segmentation performance by more effectively modeling spatial relationships.
keywords: ["medical image segmentation", "volumetric medical images", "3D convolution", "spatial feature extraction", "anatomical planes"]

title: Sentiment Analysis in Call Center Conversations Using Large Language Models and BERT
abstract: Although sentiment analysis (SA) has been widely studied in various domains such as social media, e-commerce, and movie and book reviews, research on SA in dialogues remains highly limited. In Task Oriented Dialogue Systems (TODS), such as call center conversations, SA is a highly valuable task that can provide significant automation benefits. In this study, a total of 12 different models, including Large Language Models (LLMs) such as GPT-4o and o3-mini, as well as BERT and RoBERTa, were used for SA on TODS data. Additionally, to examine the impact of training datasets in domains where publicly available datasets do not exist, the Winvoker dataset and a synthetic dataset generated using GPT-4o were compared with an indomain dataset annotated by experts. The findings indicate that when LLMs are used in a few-shot instruction-based manner without fine-tuning, their performance falls significantly below that of BERT models.
keywords: ["sentiment analysis", "task-oriented dialogue systems", "large language models", "BERT", "RoBERTa", "GPT-4o", "synthetic training data", "domain-specific training data"]

title: Evaluation of Ensemble Learning Methods for Flood Prediction
abstract: Flooding in India, exacerbated by heavy rainfall from tornadoes, has caused significant damage in recent years. This study aims to enhance flood prediction using machine learning techniques. It evaluates the performance of ensemble learning methods—Voting, Blending, Stacking, Bagging, and Boosting—alongside traditional models such as k-nearest neighbors (KNN), decision tree (DT), random forest (RF), support vector machine (SVM), logistic regression (LR), and a Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) based deep learning model. Notably, this is the first study to comprehensively compare various ensemble methods for flood prediction. Models were assessed based on accuracy, recall, precision, F1-measure, and ROC score. The findings demonstrate that ensemble methods, particularly Stacking, outperform individual models. While the KNN model showed the lowest accuracy at 78%, the GRU model achieved 89%, and the Stacking ensemble delivered the highest accuracy at 92%. These results underscore the potential of ensemble learning to improve flood prediction, offering valuable insights for disaster preparedness and mitigation strategies

title: Spatial Segregation-Based Machine Learning Approach for Water Consumption Forecasting
abstract: Water scarcity is an increasing concern world-wide, heightened by factors such as population growth, industrialization, and climate change. Effective water resource management is critical in regions where consumption outpaces natural replenishment, and predictive models can help optimize resource allocation, improve distribution strategies, and promote sustainable water use. Recent advances in machine learning offer promising results in water consumption forecasting, often outperforming traditional statistical methods. This study employs Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting Machines (GBM), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) - popular machine learning techniques known for their high predictive accuracy in large datasets - to forecast water demand. A spatial segregation-based approach is proposed to address data irregularities in water usage data sets by partitioning data to account for geographic variations. The results show that the spatial segregation method improves the predictive accuracy of RF, GBM, and XGBoost methods by 25%, 19%, and 21%, respectively, compared to the classical approach.

title: Comparison of Deep Learning and Tree-Based Models for Internet Traffic Speed Prediction
abstract: This study addresses the prediction of internet traffic speed using time-dependent data from an internet service provider through different modeling approaches. On an anonymized dataset, the performance of the moving average method, various deep learning models (N-BEATS, N-HITS, TimesNet, TSMixer, LSTM), and the XGBoost regression model enhanced with feature engineering was compared. Time series cross-validation and random hyperparameter search were used for model training. According to the results, the XGBoost model achieved the highest accuracy with 98.7% explained variance (R2), while among the deep learning models, N-BEATS and N-HITS achieved the best performance with R2values around 90%. The findings indicate that tree-based methods supported by carefully selected features can offer higher accuracy and computational efficiency compared to complex deep learning models in internet traffic forecasting.
keywords: ["time series forecasting", "N-BEATS", "N-HiTS", "TimesNet", "LSTM", "XGBoost", "tree-based models", "deep learning models", "feature engineering", "moving average", "internet service providers", "model comparison"]

title: New Approaches to Named Entity Recognition in Turkish: Improving Performance through Architecture Modification of Causal Large Language Models
abstract: This study investigates how the performance of Named Entity Recognition (NER) in Turkish documents can be improved through supervised fine-tuning of modern text-generating Large Language Models (LLMs). Encoder-based models such as Turkish BERT, multilingual mBART, mT5, and the Turkish-specific TURNA are compared with the decoder-only LLaMA model. Leveraging a recent study, the LLaMA model was restructured to support bidirectional attention in order to overcome the limited context processing capacity of its unidirectional architecture. This modification led to a significant improvement in NER performance, especially in terms of macro F1 score. The results indicate that converting LLMs like LLaMA into bidirectional token classifiers can yield substantial performance gains in Turkish texts. Furthermore, the findings suggest that larger and more powerful decoder-based models can be effectively and efficiently used for Turkish token and sequence classification tasks.
keywords: ["named entity recognition", "Turkish language", "large language models", "bidirectional attention", "llamas", "causal language models", "encoder-only models", "decoder-only models", "supervised fine-tuning", "token classification", "sequence classification"]

title: Comparison of Attention Mechanisms in the AutoInt Model for CTR and CVR Prediction
abstract: Attention mechanisms have become essential components in modern deep learning models, particularly in tasks involving feature interaction and representation learning. We implement and evaluate various attention mechanisms within the AutoInt model for Click-Through Rate (CTR) and Conversion Rate (CVR) prediction tasks. We compare dot product, additive, cosine, bilinear, sparse, and linformer attention mechanisms, using both public datasets and real-world advertisement traffic data. Our results reveal that linformer attention achieves the best overall performance, while cosine similarity-based attention with a trainable temperature parameter achieves second best results. Hybrid attention mechanisms, such as multi-relation and cosine-linformer, also show competitive performance. Our rankings provide insights for selecting effective attention mechanisms and we obtain improvements in all datasets and overall.
keywords: ["attention mechanism", "click-through rate prediction", "conversion rate prediction", "Linformer", "dot-product attention", "additive attention", "sparse attention", "hybrid attention mechanism", "feature interaction"]

title: Interaction Combination Machine for Recommendation Systems
abstract: In advertisement recommendations, click-through rate (CTR) prediction is a hugely sparse problem where embedding techniques and interaction models are needed to extract useful information from the data. We develop the interaction combination machine (ICM), which generates CTR prediction models that combine multiple beneficial layers into a single model for better performance. ICM automatically finds the best model combination by efficiently searching within exponential possibilities. Our experiments demonstrate that ICM generated models achieve better AUC and loss than the 7 other models we compared on both of the two commonly used CTR prediction datasets and improves F1 results. The improvements reach 0.26% in terms of AUC, 0.43% in terms of loss, and 1.8% in terms of F1.
keywords: ["click-through rate prediction", "advertisement recommendation", "data sparsity", "embeddings", "interaction model", "model combination", "recommender systems"]

title: CDBC: Continuous Distribution-based Clustering for High-Dimensional Data Streams
abstract: We introduce Continuous Distribution-based Clustering (CDBC), an innovative method for online clustering of high-dimensional data streams. CDBC overcomes the curse of dimensionality and adapts rapidly to shifting data distributions by continuously updating cluster parameters (e.g., mean, variance) with each new sample. Extensive experiments (50k samples, 2k features, 10 classes) demonstrate that CDBC outperforms K-Means, GMM, BIRCH, CluStream, and DenStream in ARI, NMI, and Silhouette metrics, highlighting its superior accuracy and adaptability in dynamic, high-dimensional environments.
keywords: ["online clustering", "data streams", "high-dimensional data", "curse of dimensionality"]

title: Artificial Intelligence based Social Protest Effectiveness Analysis
abstract: Collective action has been employed across various historical contexts to influence societal change. Examples such as the suffragist and civil rights movements in the United States and recent farmers’ protests in Europe demonstrate its potential impact. However, predicting protest outcomes remains difficult due to the interaction of multiple factors. In this study, the factors associated with protest success are examined, and a machine learning approach is proposed to estimate their effectiveness. After data rebalancing, outlier removal, and hyperparameter tuning, the Random Forest model achieved 75% accuracy and a 59% F1 score on the Global Protest Tracker dataset. The proposed method is intended to support computational assessments of protest dynamics and to encourage collaboration between social and computational sciences.
keywords: ["social protest", "collective action", "protest effectiveness", "random forest", "machine learning prediction", "social movements", "data rebalancing", "outlier removal"]

title: Spectrum Allocation via Deep Q-learning for 6G Terahertz Band Drone Communications
abstract: Efficient resource allocation in Terahertz (THz) drone-to-drone communications is a critical challenge for 6G systems, as the high path loss inherent to the THz band severely hinder the establishment of reliable high-capacity links. Current approaches achieve high capacity but fail in practice due to excessive complexity. In this paper, we introduce a novel framework based on dueling double deep Q-learning that optimizes channel selection, substantially reducing computational overhead while maintaining competitive capacity performance. Simulations under both linearly-aligned and real drone trace scenarios show that our method matches state-of-the-art capacity while reducing complexity by 104, proving its viability for 6G aerial communications.
keywords: ["spectrum allocation", "terahertz communication", "drone-to-drone communication", "6G", "deep Q-learning", "dueling double deep Q-network", "channel selection", "resource allocation", "computational complexity reduction", "aviation communication", "capacity maximization"]

title: Partial Pulse Usage in LFM and NLFM Radar Signals: PSL and ISL Analysis for Jamming
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of partial pulse usage (head, center, or tail) in radar signals employing LFM (Linear Frequency Modulation) and NLFM (Non-Linear Frequency Modulation) on the matched filter output, particularly focusing on the Peak Sidelobe Level (PSL) and Integrated Sidelobe Level (ISL). Partial pulse usage reduces memory and processing requirements while enabling the generation of multiple false targets within the same pulse duration. However, this approach may increase sidelobe levels, adversely affecting radar detection performance. Analytical and numerical results reveal that, for ideal LFM signals, fixed-duration partial pulses yield similar PSL/ISL values regardless of their position, whereas in NLFM signals the chosen segment can result in significantly different sidelobe behavior.
keywords: ["linear frequency modulation", "nonlinear frequency modulation", "radar jamming", "peak sidelobe level", "integrated sidelobe level", "matched filter output", "false target generation", "sidelobe suppression", "radar detection performance"]

title: Adapter-Based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Vision-Language Models in Radiology
abstract: Since the emergence of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in natural image analysis, researchers have been working to extend their success to medical imaging, particularly for the joint processing of radiological images and reports. However, training a VLM from scratch is both compute-intensive and time-consuming, and it typically yields suboptimal performance compared to models in the natural image domain. Inspired by the recent successes of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods, we propose a novel approach for fine-tuning a pre-trained VLM instead of training all parameters or starting from scratch. Our proposed approach is a fine-tuning strategy that efficiently adapts the relationship between images and reports using linear adapter layers added to the end of the model. Experiments based on the BiomedCLIP model demonstrate that our approach outperforms many state-of-the-art VLMs in radiology while significantly reducing training time and the number of trainable parameters.
keywords: ["vision-language models", "parameter-efficient fine-tuning", "radiology", "BiomedCLIP", "report generation", "training efficiency"]

title: Interference Mitigation in Joint Communication and Sensing: A Precoding-Based Framework with SSK Modulation
abstract: This paper proposes a joint communication and sensing (JCS) system that integrates multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) communication and radar functionalities within a shared spectrum. A novel precoder design incorporating Maximal Ratio Combining (MRC) is proposed to eliminate radar-induced and multi-user interference (MUI), ensuring robust communication while maintaining radar sensing accuracy. The communication subsystem leverages spatial shift keying (SSK) to enhance spectral efficiency, while the radar employs a co-located MIMO configuration for precise target detection. Simulation results show that the proposed system achieves a bit error rate (BER) below 10−2at 20 dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and a radar detection probability exceeding 90% at 5 dB SNR, validating its effectiveness in interference management. This approach enables seamless integration of communication and sensing, making it a promising solution for autonomous driving, smart cities, and next-generation wireless networks.
keywords: ["integrated sensing and communication", "MIMO radar", "precoder design", "maximum ratio combining", "multi-user interference", "interference mitigation", "radar target detection", "spectrum sharing", "bit error rate", "detection probability"]

title: A MARS-Based Approach for PVC Localization Using Clinical Data
abstract: Electrocardiographic Imaging (ECGI) is a noninvasive technique for identifying premature ventricular contraction (PVC) origins, which aids radiofrequency ablation (RFA). This study evaluates a framework based on Multivariate Adaptive Regression Splines (MARS) across different geometric models, including homogeneous, inhomogeneous, and hybrid models, using clinical data. Patient-specific heart surface potentials were simulated, and corresponding body surface potentials (BSPs) were computed using the boundary element method (BEM). These BSPs, along with the heart surface potentials, were used to train the regression model. Activation times were computed, and the earliest activation point was identified as the estimated origin. The performance was evaluated using localization error (LE), and compared with Tikhonov regularization. The best-performing geometric model demonstrated better or comparable performance compared to Tikhonov regularization.
keywords: ["electrocardiographic imaging", "premature ventricular contractions", "multivariate adaptive regression splines", "body surface potentials", "Tikhonov regularization", "radiofrequency ablation", "boundary element method"]

title: NAO and Expert Imitating Each Other: A New Robot Action Dataset
abstract: Today, with the rapid spread of robots, the significance of robot training has increased. Imitation learning plays a significant role in robot training, and numerous scientific studies are published in this field each year. In this method, robots can be controlled by imitating human movements and this process is called teleoperation. In teleoperation studies, the mapping between human and robot skeletal systems is performed using two fundamental approaches: the mathematical model and the artificial intelligence model. However, the number of datasets in the literature that simultaneously record human and robot skeletal data to enable a comprehensive comparison of these two approaches is quite limited. In this study, we created two separate datasets containing human and robot skeletal data and experimentally compared two different teleoperation methods. The experimental findings indicate that the artificial intelligence model, when trained with unbiased datasets, outperforms the mathematical model in teleoperation processes.
keywords: ["telerobotics", "imitation learning", "human-robot interaction", "skeleton data", "robot training"]

title: SSDV: An Offline Signature Detection and Verification Dataset
abstract: Signatures have long been used as a basic means of authentication. With the increase in digitization and document forgery, signature verification has gained greater importance than ever before. This study introduces the SSDV (Sabanci Signature Detection and Verification) dataset, developed for signature detection and verification. SSDV provides a rich dataset that simulates real-world scenarios for signature verification and detection. This dataset, expanded with various types of noise and forged signature data, is designed to test and improve the robustness of signature verification systems. The scope of the dataset reflects the challenges encountered in current research and applications, providing a valuable resource for developing new models and algorithms in this field.
keywords: ["signature verification", "signature-based detection", "document forgery", "handwritten signatures", "noise simulation", "forged signatures", "authentication", "benchmark dataset"]

title: Multi-Class Heart Sounds Classification Using Machine Learning and Transfer Learning Approaches
abstract: Early detection and accurate diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are of great importance for public health. This study examines machine learning and transfer learning–based deep learning approaches for classification of phonocardiogram (PCG) signals. Heart sound recordings obtained from the GitHub and Pascal datasets were preprocessed using various techniques to generate spectral representations, which were then classified. k Nearest Neighbors (kNN), Support Vector Machines (SVM), Random Forest (RF), and transfer learning–based VGG16 (finetuning) and ResNet50 (fine-tuning) models were compared. The RF model achieved the highest accuracy at 99.82%, while among transfer learning approaches VGG16 (fine-tuning) performed best with 96.51% accuracy. This work aims to identify the most suitable method for PCG signal analysis by comparing different classification techniques.
keywords: ["heart sound classification", "phonocardiogram", "cardiovascular disease diagnosis", "transfer learning", "VGG16", "ResNet50", "random forest", "k-nearest neighbors", "support vector machine", "spectral properties", "signal preprocessing"]

title: K-Complex Detection from Sleep EEG by One-Dimensional Local Binary Pattern Method
abstract: In the presented study, a one-dimensional local binary pattern-based (1D-LBP) method was proposed for the automatic detection of k-complexes from sleep electroencephalogram (EEG). According to the sleep study protocol, EEG signal scored in 30 second epochs was divided into 1 second segments, and histograms of the one-dimensional local binary pattern were obtained for each segment. Features belonging to the segments with and without k-complex were extracted from the histogram. In a total of 1045 epochs, the number of second-stage non-rapid eye movements (NREM2) in the recording is 690. At these stages, training and test data sets were created from k-complex epochs scored jointly by three sleep medicine specialists. In order to demonstrate the effectiveness of the classification process, evaluation metrics were calculated and tests were conducted with the best four classification models. As a result, high performance rates have been achieved in detecting k-complexes with the presented method.
keywords: ["sleep EEG", "EEG classification", "sleep stage classification"]

title: Improving Skin Lesion Classification with Pretrained Deep Learning Models
abstract: Skin cancer is the most common type of cancer. Cancer can be defined as a disease characterized by the uncontrolled division and spread of cells. As with other types of cancer, early diagnosis and treatment play a crucial role in combating skin cancer. Since diagnosis is made through visual examination, factors such as the level of expertise and image artifacts negatively affect diagnostic accuracy and slow down the process.Computer-aided applications used to analyze such images provide faster and more accurate results. Additionally, these methods eliminate factors that reduce diagnostic accuracy during the classification and segmentation of skin lesions.This study classifies skin cancer to benign or malignant using deep learning and machine learning methods. In particular, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) have shown promising results in medical image classification. The study evaluates six pre-trained CNN models—VGG16, EfficientNetB7, EfficientNetV2L, DenseNet, ConvNeXtBase and MobileNet—for binary skin lesion classification using the ISIC 2019 dataset. The study first preprocesses and balances the data to enhance performance. The results indicate that the ConvNeXtBase model achieved the highest success with accuracy rate of 84.63% after balancing the data that we have.
keywords: ["skin lesion classification", "skin cancer", "benign versus malignant differentiation", "pre-trained convolutional neural networks", "ISIC 2019", "ConvNeXt", "EfficientNet", "MobileNet", "data balancing", "computer-aided diagnosis", "medical image classification"]

title: Fall Detection Using UWB Data
abstract: In this study, fall detection was aimed using only distance data from Ultra-Wideband (UWB) systems. After performing missing data imputation, noise reduction, and data standardization, One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) models were trained, successfully performing high-accuracy fall detection. The models were tested on individuals not included in the training set, demonstrating successful generalization performance. The proposed method, which does not require fixed anchor position information or additional sensors, can be easily adapted to different environments and enables rapid intervention.
keywords: ["fall detection", "ultra-wideband", "distance data", "wearable sensors", "1D convolutional neural network", "long short-term memory", "bidirectional LSTM", "missing data imputation", "noise reduction", "elderly monitoring"]

title: Learning Shared Encoding of Related Robotic Tasks
abstract: Conventional techniques usually solve the task transfer problem through bottom-up approaches or cleverly designed tricks, such as Reinforcement Learning or reverse execution. However, leveraging the common semantic context between executions of similar or related tasks may promote learning performance by enabling the utilization of shared representations. In this study, we propose a Learning-from-Demonstration model that simultaneously learns from semantically related demonstrations while actively attempting to discover the common representations of both. By doing so, our model learns to generate trajectories from related demonstrations. We showcased the performance of our model in synthetically generated trajectories. Later, we assessed our model with a daily, related task couple in a simulation environment.
keywords: ["imitation learning", "task transfer", "shared representations", "robotic manipulation", "trajectory generation", "robot learning", "synthetic trajectories", "simulation environment"]

title: Performance Comparison of Support Vector Machines in Quantum Machine Learning Using Qiskit, Cirq, and Pennylane Frameworks
abstract: Quantum computing has the capability to efficiently solve complex problems that would require significantly longer processing times on classical computing systems. This study investigates the practical applications of quantum machine learning by comparing the performance of classical Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) across three simulation-based quantum computing platforms: Qiskit, Cirq, and Pennylane. Through experiments conducted on various datasets, the study examines the influence of different feature mapping techniques—ZFeatureMap, ZZFeatureMap, and Pauli-FeatureMap—on the encoding of data into quantum states within QSVM models. The results demonstrate that both the choice of computational environment and the feature mapping strategy play a crucial role in determining the performance of quantum machine learning applications. The findings underscore the potential advantages of quantum-based approaches for tackling complex computational problems.
keywords: ["quantum support vector machine", "quantum machine learning", "feature mapping", "Qiskit", "Cirq", "PennyLane", "performance comparison"]

title: LLaVa-RS: A Unified Model for Image and Change Captioning in Remote Sensing
abstract: Visual instruction tuning has significantly advanced the functionality of Multimodal Large Language Models (MLMMs), enabling enhanced comprehension and response capabilities in many forms of data. However, existing open MLLMs remain largely focused on tasks with general types of images, with little exploration into remote sensing applications and captioning differences at two images. To adress these issues we propose LLaVa-RS, a MLLM that is focused on remote images with features such as image captioning, and change captioning. Code available at https://github.com/ChangeCapsInRS/LLAVA-RS.
keywords: ["multimodal large language models", "remote sensing images", "image captioning", "change detection", "change captioning", "visual instruction tuning", "open-source models"]

title: Complementary Square Ring Resonator Loaded MIMO Antenna Design for 5G NR n258 Frequency Band
abstract: Considering the current trajectory of telecommunications, it is evident that 5G NR frequencies and related research in these bands will guide future 6G studies. The n258 (24.25 - 27.50 GHz) band, which falls within the 5G NR FR2 frequency range, is evaluated within this context. In this study, initially, a microstrip patch reference antenna design was addressed and configured to operate within the relevant band. Additionally, a MIMO antenna unit cell design was achieved by integrating a complementary square ring resonator structure into the antenna design. The efficiency of the proposed metasurface within the n258 band was demonstrated, and its impact on the unit cell was presented. The unit cell antenna design achieved a bandwidth of 1.88 GHz and a return loss value of -39.63 dB at the center frequency of 26.08 GHz. Based on the unit cell design, a 2×2 MIMO antenna design was developed. The designed MIMO antenna exhibits a bandwidth of 1.95 GHz and a return loss value of -48.58 dB at the center frequency of 26.09 GHz.
keywords: ["MIMO antenna", "metasurfaces", "28 GHz", "microstrip patch antenna", "antenna bandwidth", "return loss"]

title: Design of an Ankle-Brachial Index Detection System for the Preliminary Diagnosis of Peripheral Arterial Disease
abstract: Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD) is a condition that typically occurs in the arteries (blood vessels) of the legs. This disease develops due to plaque buildup or narrowing in the arteries, resulting in restricted blood flow. The primary objective of this study is to adopt a non-invasive Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) approach to support the early diagnosis of conditions such as cardiac arrhythmias or leg blockages in individuals with Peripheral Artery Disease (PAD). This study focuses on developing an Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) measurement system, which is one of the diagnostic methods for Peripheral Artery Disease. The study aims to create a diagnostic system model based on these measurements. The developed measurement system was tested using the PETAŞ Bedside Monitor, and an accuracy rate of 98.86% was observed. As part of the study, Ankle-Brachial Index (ABI) calculations were performed using a dataset consisting of systolic pressure values.
keywords: ["ankle-brachial index", "peripheral arterial disease", "non-invasive diagnosis", "arterial stenosis", "diagnostic system design"]

title: Task-Oriented Optimization of Pre-Trained Language Models with Task Projection Network
abstract: Large-scale artificial learning models are trained with large data sets and made suitable for general use. However, adapting these models to a specific topic or specific task often involves updating all the weights. This process results in high memory consumption and increased computational costs. In this study, instead of fine-tuning an entire model, we consider the method of customizing it with a task projection network added in front of it. This approach preserves the general structure of the model, while allowing it to be used directly for a specific task without retraining. Thus, computational and storage needs reduced and effective adaptations can be made with small data sets. The proposed method facilitates the rapid adaptation of large models to different areas, enabling the spread of artificial learning to wider areas of use. In our work, we demonstrate how the task projection network can be used effectively without the need to change a primary model and the practical benefits of this method.
keywords: ["pre-trained language models", "task-specific adaptation", "zero-shot transfer", "fine-tuning alternatives", "memory efficiency", "computational complexity reduction", "small datasets"]

title: MipMap Digital Twin: A Scalable IoT-Based Framework for Smart Cities and Circular Economy
abstract: As cities grow, managing urban infrastructure efficiently becomes a challenge. Digital Twin (DT) technology, combined with IoT, GIS, and AI-driven analytics, enables real-time monitoring, predictive analysis, and automated optimization of urban systems. A DT is a virtual model of a physical system that stays in sync with the real world, providing a deeper understanding of environment operations, supporting smarter decision-making and dynamic infrastructure management. This paper presents the first-stage results of a MipMap digital twin application, integrating a production facility and multiple café locations into a shared digital twin. The study explores bridging urban-scale decision-making with day-to-day operations, utilizing IoT, ESRI’s ArcGIS, and a game engine-based visualization. Results demonstrate improved service quality, resource optimization, and system integration, advancing smart urban ecosystems.
keywords: ["digital twin", "Internet of Things", "smart cities", "circular economy", "urban infrastructure management", "production facilities", "ArcGIS", "resource optimization", "service quality"]

title: EK-LIME: Balancing Local Fidelity and Stability in Imbalanced Classification
abstract: This study investigates the trade-off between local fidelity and stability in LIME explanations, particularly under imbalanced data conditions. To improve the balance between local fidelity and stability, the Ensemble Kernel LIME approach, which combines narrow and wide kernels, is proposed. The method is compared with LIME, DLIME, GLIME, and Opti-LIME across 20 datasets with varying imbalance ratios; performance is evaluated in terms of local fidelity, Variable Stability Index, and Coefficient Stability Index. The results show that EK-LIME improves the fidelity–stability balance in both classes, achieving 0.98 for the majority class and 0.99 for the minority class, with Variable Stability Index values of 0.82 and 0.80, respectively.
keywords: ["lime", "explainable AI", "imbalanced classification", "explanation stability"]

title: TFT-Flood for Nationwide Flood Prediction in Turkey: A Three-Branch Hybrid Deep Learning Architecture
abstract: This paper proposes TFT-Flood, a novel hybrid deep learning model that provides flood forecasting at the district level for Turkey. TFT-Flood uses the Temporal Fusion Transformer and consists of three separate modules: Static Enrichment, Temporal Processing and Risk Quantification that serve individual responsibilities. TFT-Flood is evaluated under a strict no leakage protocol for 6372 eight-day sequences for all 973 districts of the TUCBS open-data flood database with NASA POWER backfill, where the date of prediction is masked and cumulative engineered features are calculated on the basis of the observation period only. Although the marginal distribution of each meteorological feature is very similar for flood and non-flood data, TFT-Flood can successfully exploit temporal knowledge embedded in the dataset multivariate structure. The TFT-Flood ensemble (8 random seeds) achieves 0.909 AUC. In a chronology-based time split, the model exhibits performance degradation but is still better than a random predictor at a statistical level, implying a limited potential for cross-period generalization.
keywords: ["flood forecasting", "Temporal Fusion Transformer", "hybrid deep learning model", "Turkey", "risk quantification", "meteorological features"]

title: Comparative Reliability Analysis of Open-Source Large Language Models in Subjective Text Evaluation
abstract: This study systematically examines the consistency and reliability of large language models (LLMs) in generating numerical scores for subjective text evaluation. Fifteen open-source and one closed-source model (16 total) were tested across 7 datasets–including sentiment analysis, offensive language detection, essay scoring, and response quality assessment–using zero-shot and rubric-based prompting strategies, three temperature values (0, 0.2, 1.0), and two scoring modes (discrete/continuous). Results from 23,780 evaluations show that open-source models (Command-A, NMAE: 0.140) can match or surpass the cost-effective GPT-4o-mini reference (NMAE: 0.159). Discrete scoring consistently outperforms continuous scoring by 10%, temperature has minimal effect, and Turkish datasets achieve performance comparable to English.
keywords: ["large language models", "automated essay scoring", "open-source LLMs", "model reliability", "consistency", "sentiment analysis", "offensive language detection", "zero-shot prompting", "temperature effects", "GPT-4o-mini"]

title: Dual-Port Antenna and Intermediate Frequency Stage Design for SNR Enhancement in Portable Doppler Radars
abstract: This study presents the design and implementation of a portable Doppler radar system focused on compactness, low cost, and field usability. To overcome the portability limitations of traditional systems caused by bulky RF front-end components, a compact hardware architecture is proposed, featuring a dual-port microstrip patch antenna operating at 2.45 GHz and a specialized Intermediate Frequency (IF) stage PCB. The dual-port antenna integrates transmission and reception functions into a single structure, providing sufficient isolation without the need for external circulators, thereby significantly reducing system size and complexity. The accompanying IF stage is designed to amplify weak Doppler signals, enabling reliable motion detection in a fully portable setup. The proposed system was validated through simulations, hardware fabrication, and real-time experiments. Frequency spectrum analyses of the measurements taken demonstrated that they yielded successful results.
keywords: ["dual-port antenna", "microstrip patch antenna", "signal-to-noise ratio improvement", "2.45 GHz", "motion detection"]

title: Drug–Drug Interaction Classification using Graph-Based and Text-Based Drug Representations
abstract: Drug-drug interactions (DDI) are important to detect in clinical practice because they can cause side effects and a decrease in treatment effectiveness. This study presents a DDI classification approach that combines graph and text-based drug representations. GraphBERT is used to obtain graph-based drug representations from drugs in the interaction network, while the textual features of the drugs, namely Description, Mechanism, Indication, and Pharmacodynamics, are represented with the BioSentVec model. These representations are used as input to the model for DDI classification separately or in a combined manner. The results show that the combined use of graph and text-based representations provides the highest performance and reaches an F-score of 91.45%. This result was obtained as 0.64% higher than the text-based model and 0.87% higher than the graph-based model. The findings reveal that both representation types provide higher performance when used together.
keywords: ["drug-drug interactions", "drug interaction networks", "pharmacodynamics", "drug mechanisms", "drug indications", "drug descriptions"]

title: OFDM vs. SC-FDMA for Monostatic THz ISAC Sensing Under Beam Misalignment Fading
abstract: Terahertz (THz) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems rely on highly directional beams that are sensitive to platform-induced misalignment. While beam misalignment (BM) fading models have been developed for THz channels, the impact of waveform selection on sensing performance under these conditions remains unclear. This paper compares OFDM and SC-FDMA for monostatic THz sensing at 0.85 THz with 20 GHz bandwidth, using a statistical BM fading model that distinguishes spot-filling and spot-limited target regimes. Monte Carlo simulations across several misalignment angles show that both waveforms achieve nearly identical range and velocity estimation accuracy. The performance gap between aligned and misaligned scenarios is substantial, while waveform choice has a negligible effect. These findings indicate that beam alignment is the critical design factor for THz ISAC, and waveform selection can be based on other system requirements.
keywords: ["OFDM", "SC-FDMA", "monostatic sensing", "waveform selection", "range and velocity estimation", "beam alignment"]

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Cross-Dataset Face Anti-Spoofing
abstract: Domain shift, induced by diverse sensor characteristics and environmental illuminations, remains a fundamental bottleneck limiting the generalization capacity of deep learning models in face presentation attack detection (PAD). This study proposes a lightweight ResNet-18-based domain generalization framework designed for robustness against such variations and real-time deployment on edge devices. To mitigate the limitations of vanilla convolutions in capturing local texture distortions, Central Difference Convolution (CDC) blocks are integrated into the network’s front-end to extract fine-grained gradient cues and intrinsic spoofing patterns. During the training phase, a MixStyle module is utilized to dynamically blend feature-level statistics from different source domains to simulate domain diversity, while a Supervised Contrastive Learning (SupCon) strategy is employed to maximize the inter-class margin in the feature embedding space. The proposed architecture achieved a 95.48% AUC and 12.08% ACER in cross-dataset evaluations on OULU-NPU and MSU-MFSD, demonstrating a competitive generalization performance against the existing approaches in the literature. With a compact footprint of 45.94 MB and an inference rate of 68.02 FPS, this framework provides an optimized and scalable countermeasure for high-security biometric authentication systems.
keywords: ["face anti-spoofing", "anti-spoofing", "domain generalization", "domain shift", "cross-dataset generalization", "supervised contrastive learning", "lightweight neural networks", "edge deployment", "biometric authentication"]

title: Fragmentation Aware Training for Turkish Named Entity Recognition
abstract: This paper compares five loss variants for Turkish named entity recognition (NER) under the same controlled experimental framework. In the experiments, the Transformer architecture, training schedule, data splits, and tokenizer set are kept fixed, and only the supervision objective is changed. On the WikiANN-tr test split, the mean entity-level F1 score increases from 0.6788 with standard token cross-entropy (CE) to 0.7277 with conditional random field (CRF) and 0.7276 with the combination of word-normalized CE and CRF. The best structured variant outperforms token CE by 0.044-0.054 points across all tokenizer families. The findings show that tokenizer performance differences in Turkish NER arise not only from segmentation design, but also from how fragmented words are supervised in the loss function.
keywords: ["loss functions", "conditional random fields", "word normalization", "tokenization", "structured prediction"]

title: Performance Evaluation of Deep Learning-Based Feature Detection and Matching Algorithms in GNSS/Visual-Inertial Navigation Systems
abstract: This study presents a comparative performance analysis of GNSS-aided visual-inertial navigation systems, namely GVINS with the conventional VINS-Mono visual frontend and GVINS integrated with the deep learning-based SuperVINS visual frontend. Experimental results obtained using the proposed software framework show that the high distinctiveness and trackability of deep learning-based features improve the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) and standard deviation (STD) by 3% and 7%, respectively, in a sports field scenario. In the urban driving scenario, the conventional approach fails in GNSS-challenged areas and in the presence of dynamic objects, whereas the deep learning-based approach maintains a continuous positioning solution and reduces RMSE and STD by 14% and 28%, respectively. The results demonstrate that deep learning-based visual features can enhance system robustness and positioning performance, particularly in challenging urban navigation environments.
keywords: ["GNSS/INS integration", "visual-inertial navigation", "feature detection", "feature matching", "deep features", "VINS-Mono", "positioning accuracy", "urban navigation", "GNSS-denied environments", "dynamic objects"]

title: Tango Scanning Mamba Model for Radar Pulse Repetition Interval Type Classification
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach based on the Mamba state space model for automatic classification of Pulse Repetition Interval (PRI) types in radar electronic intelligence (ELINT) systems. In noisy environments, missing and spurious pulses hinder accurate PRI type identification, and classification is performed using only pulse time of arrival information. The proposed approach is evaluated in two configurations: forward-only and tango scanning, adapted from the TSCMamba architecture. Experiments compare the proposed approach against Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) baselines across two window sizes (32, 64). Leveraging its bidirectional context capturing capability, tango scanning Mamba achieves 93.0 percent macro F1 at window size 64, obtaining the highest performance across both window sizes. This performance is achieved with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost compared to LSTM baselines.
keywords: ["Mamba", "bidirectional context", "LSTM comparison"]

title: Safety Oriented Hybrid Specialist-Generalist Perception Framework for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Reliable perception in autonomous driving is critical under corner cases and distribution shifts. This study proposes a hybrid perception framework that combines a CODA-trained specialist model with a COCO-pretrained generalist model. Predictions from both models are fused at inference time, and overlapping boxes are refined using non-maximum suppression. Experimental results show that the proposed framework reduces missed detections, especially for medium and large objects, and offers a practical solution for safety-critical autonomous driving scenarios.
keywords: ["autonomous driving perception", "coda", "non-maximum suppression", "object detection", "missed detection reduction", "distribution shift", "corner cases", "safety-critical scenarios"]

title: Assessing the Impact of Foundation Model Features and MIL Aggregators for HER2 Status Prediction from Whole-Slide Images
abstract: This study investigates HER2 status prediction from hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained whole-slide images using weakly supervised learning. Patch-level features extracted by two histopathology-specific foundation models, CTransPath and UNI2, were evaluated with multiple instance learning architectures across internal and external test settings. Models were trained on the Yale HER2 and HEROHE cohorts; Yale-trained models were further evaluated on the independent TCGA-BRCA cohort to assess cross-dataset generalization. Internal evaluations showed that several MIL architectures achieved competitive accuracy, whereas on the external TCGA-BRCA test set, UNI2-based models consistently preserved higher performance. In contrast, CTransPath-based models showed a marked drop. These findings suggest that, for HER2 prediction from whole-slide images, robustness of the feature representation under domain shift is more critical than increasing model complexity.
keywords: ["HER2 status prediction", "whole slide images", "multiple instance learning", "foundation models", "H&E staining", "weakly supervised learning", "cross-dataset generalization", "domain shift", "breast cancer", "histopathology image analysis"]

title: Hate Speech Detection on Social Media: A Case Study on the Sports Domain
abstract: Event-specific hate speech monitoring is difficult because social media data are noisy, context dependent, and training datasets may contain inconsistent labels. This paper investigates how an encoder-based classifier can be adapted for detecting hate speech particularly in sports domain. We benchmark encoder models on the MetaHate and HateCheck corpora using stratified cross validation, analyze dataset quality, apply preprocessing and language filtering to reduce noise. We build event-focused Bluesky and YouTube datasets using context-aware collection, topic filtering, and manually annotate a subset to assess agreement. Results show modest gains from data cleaning and reveal systematic failure modes such as negated hate and obfuscated slurs. The Bluesky case study with only a small number of hateful posts highlights platform differences and the need for stronger event-driven retrieval and annotation strategies.
keywords: ["hate speech detection", "social media", "dataset quality", "data cleaning", "annotation agreement", "platform differences", "Bluesky", "YouTube"]

title: Hardware-Aware Federated Learning for Speech Emotion Recognition
abstract: Federated learning (FL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative training across distributed edge devices, but real deployments involve heterogeneous clients with different processing power, memory capacity, and communication latency, which often increase round duration and system cost. This paper proposes a hardware-aware federated learning framework for emotion recognition on session-partitioned IEMOCAP that integrates hardware profiling, top-K client selection, and adaptive local epochs within a unified training loop. We compare the method against FedAvg, FedProx, and random top-K selection under a non-IID setup and show that, across 50 federated rounds and 5 independent trials, the proposed approach achieves competitive validation accuracy (0.352±0.019), reduces total training time by about 36.5% compared to FedAvg, and lowers cumulative communication cost by 40%.
keywords: ["federated learning", "speech emotion recognition", "hardware-aware training", "heterogeneous clients", "non-IID data", "communication cost reduction", "IEMOCAP", "edge devices", "training time reduction"]

title: Deep Learning–Based Image Segmentation for Quality Inspection of Industrial Cable Terminal Crimp Connections
abstract: This study proposes a deep learning-based segmentation approach for the automatic quality control of industrial crimp cross-section images. The method aims to achieve pixel-level separation of critical structural components such as conductive wires, insulation regions, and structural contours. In this context, a unique dataset consisting of 265 samples was constructed, and multi-class annotations were performed. U-Net, U-Net++, Attention U-Net, and G-CASCADE models were comparatively evaluated. Experimental results demonstrate that all models achieved successful segmentation performance, while the G-CASCADE model provided the highest accuracy in terms of Dice and IoU metrics. The findings indicate that the proposed approach offers a fast, objective, and repeatable solution for quality control.
keywords: ["image segmentation", "quality inspection", "manufacturing quality control", "conductive wires", "U-Net", "Attention U-Net", "dataset construction"]

title: Stability of Machine Learning Algorithms in Attack Detection
abstract: Machine learning has become one of the fundamental components of attack detection systems. The performance of machine learning models is affected by class imbalance in datasets and interactions among features. In particular, different proportions of benign and malicious samples may lead to misclassifications. In this study, the stability of five machine learning algorithms (Random forest, naïve Bayes, logistic regression, support vector machine with sequential minimal optimization and J48 decision tree) using three feature selection methods (all features, information gain, principal component analysis) are evaluated on two (UNSW-NB15 and CIC-MalMem2022) data sets with five distinct sample distributions. Experimental results show that Random Forest demonstrates the most stable and performing behavior.

title: A Lightweight Industrial Image Anomaly Detection Using Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
abstract: This study proposes a lightweight and unsupervised method for industrial image anomaly detection using multi scale feature fusion. The method learns a one class embedding from multi level features extracted by a pretrained ResNet-18 and is trained only with normal samples. The architecture is designed for applications requiring low computational cost, low memory usage, and high inference speed. During training, a Deep SVDD based loss is used. The method achieves AUROC scores of 93.5% and 83.2% on the MVTec AD and VisA datasets, respectively. In addition, the proposed model provides a balanced tradeoff between accuracy and efficiency with 15 million parameters, 0.2 GB memory usage, and 26.2 FPS inference speed.

title: mmWave Radar-Based Human Motion Detection for Airports
abstract: Real-time human tracking is crucial for the management of operational processes and security in high-density areas such as airport terminals. However, traditional camera systems face challenges including privacy constraints and dependence on environmental lighting conditions. In this study, a privacy-focused, end-to-end mmWave radar-based human detection and tracking architecture is proposed for airport passenger monitoring. The developed system processes raw radar data in a 5-dimensional feature space—incorporating spatial coordinates, intensity, and Doppler velocity—to effectively filter multipath noise. To preserve the integrity of sparse point clouds at longer distances, an adaptive DBSCAN clustering algorithm with a range-dependent search radius is utilized. Temporal target continuity is ensured through a lifecycle-based Multi-Object Tracking framework, supported by a Kalman filter and the Hungarian algorithm. Field tests conducted demonstrate that incorporating velocity-weighted clustering and shifting the velocity thresholding mechanism to the ID assignment stage prevent track fragmentation and significantly reduce false positive rates. Ensuring complete anonymity without generating visual data, the system exhibits stable real-time performance at an operating frequency of 10 Hz.
