title: Optimizing Visualizations of Congestive Heart Failure Patients Telemonitored Data
abstract: Access to hospital care for congestive heart failure (CHF) patients is often costly and delayed, worsening outcomes. Remote patient monitoring provides a solution by continuously tracking health indicators and supporting timely clinical decisions. For this approach to be effective, data must be presented in a clear, actionable format rather than raw streams that disrupt workflow. This study applies a User-Centered Design methodology to develop intuitive visualizations of daily blood pressure and weight data for CHF patients. Through three iterative cycles of requirement definition, visualization development, and evaluation, the design was refined to meet clinicians’ needs. The final visualizations proved highly effective, enhancing efficiency, usability, and clinical decision-making.
keywords: ["congestive heart failure", "remote patient monitoring", "user-centered design", "blood pressure monitoring", "weight monitoring", "clinical decision support"]

title: Functional Sentence Classification in Legal Decision Summaries: Inter-Task Dependency and Label Derivation
abstract: This study addresses sentence-level functional classification in Constitutional Court decision summaries. A dataset of 10,213 sentences compiled from 876 decision summaries was used. Each sentence was evaluated in terms of its function within the summary, its content type, and a composite label derived from the combination of these two tasks. Relevant sentence segments were also annotated with linguistic markers that make the surface traces of legal reasoning visible. Methodologically, a TF-IDF-based SVM and single-task, multi-task, and two-task label-deriving BERT models were compared. The findings show that the marker layer improves classification performance, that the TF-IDF SVM provides a strong but more overfitting-prone baseline, and that BERT-based models achieve higher macro-F1 scores under the marked main-data setting. The two-task BERT approach reaches the highest 128-token test macro-F1 for the composite task and shows a limited train-test gap at the derived-output level.
keywords: ["constitutional courts", "multi-task learning", "BERT", "linguistic markers", "legal reasoning"]

title: Comprehensive Comparison of YOLOv26-Based RGB, Thermal and 4-Channel Early-Fusion RGBT Models on the KAIST Dataset
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive YOLOv26-based comparison of RGB, Thermal and 4-channel early-fusion RGBT modalities on the KAIST benchmark. Shared dataset splits, identical training hyperparameters, and a common evaluation protocol are used for all modalities. On the test set, the RGBT model achieves the lowest log-average miss rate (MR) of 6.94%, followed by the Thermal model with 8.18% and the RGB model with 10.32%. These results show that the multimodal RGBT approach yields a lower miss rate than single-modality detectors. In addition, the RGBT model also provides the best performance in terms of FPPI@0.25 and MissRate@0.25. Overfitting analysis indicates that no significant overfitting is observed in the final models.
keywords: ["YOLOv2", "infrared thermography", "feature-level fusion", "multimodal fusion", "person re-identification"]

title: Adaptive Hybrid Filtering for Outlier Suppression in Echosounder Measurements
abstract: Echosounder sensors used on submarine platforms play a critical role, particularly in navigation and obstacle detection applications. However, the depth data obtained from these systems may contain a high proportion of outliers due to the noise characteristics and measurement errors inherent to the underwater environment. In this study, a hybrid filtering approach based on the sequential use of the Hampel filter and an adaptive Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA) was employed to suppress outliers observed in echosounder data. This approach was evaluated using real field data. In the first stage, outliers were identified using the Hampel filter and replaced with the local median, while in the second stage, signal smoothing was performed using an adaptively adjusted EWMA according to the measurement error. The employed approach was comparatively examined against conventional mean – fixed-parameter filtering method. The results demonstrate that this hybrid filtering approach is effective in both suppressing outliers and preserving actual depth variations. Furthermore, owing to its low computational cost, the approach was found to be applicable to real-time submarine operations
keywords: ["outlier suppression", "Hampel filter", "exponential moving average", "adaptive filtering", "hybrid filtering", "underwater navigation", "obstacle detection", "signal smoothing", "real-time processing"]

title: A Hardware-Aware Edge-Constrained Region Verification Network for Two-Stage UAV Detection
abstract: Autonomous detection of Low-Slow-Small UAVs on edge devices necessitates two-stage pipelines due to memory bandwidth constraints. However, forcing general-purpose full-frame detectors into region of interest verification tasks yields sub-optimal results. In this study, it is empirically demonstrated that edge-constrained verification is not merely a scaled-down detection problem, and the hardware-aware EMA-Det architecture is proposed as a system demonstrator. Equipped with Laplacian kernel initialization and dynamic early-exit mechanisms, the model empirically shows that global pooling-based attention modules degrade target features at constrained resolutions. Under fair comparison at 128x128 input, pre-trained YOLOv8n in verification-mode achieved 88.7 percent recall, while EMA-Det reached 99.2 percent recall with 10 times fewer operations and 3 times lower peak activation memory.
keywords: ["drone detection", "edge devices", "two-stage detection", "hardware-aware design", "attention modules", "YOLOv8n"]

title: RSC-MPC-Based Motion Planning Framework for Unmanned Surface Vehicles
abstract: In this work, a motion planning and control approach for an unmanned surface vehicle (USV) is introduced. The proposed method generates a sparse graph structure by creating safe regions in obstacle environments, and then navigates the vehicle between these regions using a model predictive control algorithm. The main motivation of this solution is to develop a computationally efficient and robust motion planning algorithm for USVs. Simulations conducted on an underactuated USV model with two thrusters demonstrate the success of the method in obstacle avoidance and goal reaching.
keywords: ["unmanned surface vehicles", "motion planning", "model predictive control", "safe zones", "obstacle avoidance", "underactuated vehicles", "goal achievement"]

title: G-AdaKV: Cross-Layer Dynamic KV Cache Management for Efficient Large Language Model Inference
abstract: The Key-Value (KV) cache constitutes the primary GPU memory bottleneck during long-context inference in Large Language Models. Existing eviction methods either confine budget optimization to a single attention layer or resort to indirect statistical metrics for cross-layer allocation. We propose G-AdaKV, a simple framework that distributes the cache budget across all layers and attention heads through a single global Top-k selection. Unlike multi-stage baselines, G-AdaKV relies on a single mechanism yet achieves the highest overall average on the LongBench benchmark across all three tested budget levels. At the most constrained budget (B = 128), G-AdaKV attains the best score on 12 out of 16 tasks.
keywords: ["large language model inference", "long-context inference", "cache eviction", "attention heads", "top-k selection", "LongBench"]

title: A Structured Signal Processing Application for EtCO 2 Measurement in NDIR-Based Capnography Systems
abstract: In NDIR (Non-Dispersive Infrared)-based capnography systems, raw signals obtained from sensors are typically low in amplitude and are affected by noise caused by light source modulation, making it difficult to achieve stable determination of end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) values. In this study, a structured digital signal processing pipeline was developed to ensure reliable EtCO2measurement. Analog signals were digitized using a high-resolution analog-to-digital converter, followed by the application of high-pass and low-pass filters. Moving average and α-trimmed mean methods were applied to the EtCO2signal obtained from the filtered data using different parameter settings, and their performances were comparatively evaluated. Comparisons conducted using a CO2–carrier gas mixture controlled by a digital mass flow controller demonstrated that the proposed method improves waveform stability and enhances the accuracy of EtCO2measurements.
keywords: ["end-tidal carbon dioxide", "capnography", "moving average", "signal denoising"]

title: Analysis of RCS Reduction in a 1-Bit Coding Metasurface Under Temperature Variations
abstract: This study presents the design of a 1-bit coding metasurface for radar cross section reduction. The structure, formed by unit cells providing an approximate 180-degree phase difference, is optimized using a simulated annealing algorithm. The resulting metasurface suppresses specular reflection, redistributes electromagnetic energy into different directions, and achieves a significant reduction in radar cross section over a wide bandwidth. In this respect, the study provides a basis for investigating the electromagnetic characteristics of coding metasurfaces under temperature variations.
keywords: ["radar cross section reduction", "temperature variation", "simulated annealing", "unit cell design", "specular reflection suppression", "broadband RCS reduction"]

title: Comparing Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning Approaches for Stress Detection on Wearable Devices
abstract: Federated learning is a promising approach in privacy-focused wearable healthcare because it processes data on the user’s device rather than on a central server. However, model updates may still leak sensitive information, necessitating additional privacy-preserving mechanisms such as Secure Aggregation and Differential Privacy. This study compares combinations of Secure Aggregation and Local Differential Privacy with Federated Learning using Multilayer Perceptron and Logistic Regression models for stress detection in wearable devices using the WESAD dataset. The results showed that Secure Aggregation maintained its core benefit with a higher runtime overhead, while Local Differential Privacy offered a cost-competitive stance but reduced model performance depending on noise levels. These findings highlight the privacy-benefit-cost balance in privacy-preserving federated learning for wearable stress detection.
keywords: ["privacy-preserving federated learning", "stress detection", "wearable devices", "secure aggregation", "local differential privacy", "WESAD dataset", "runtime overhead", "multilayer perceptron", "logistic regression", "wearable healthcare"]

title: A Novel Approach Mitigating the Doppler Effect in UAV-LoRa Networks: DQN-Based Dynamic Resource Management
abstract: This study proposes a novel Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based resource allocation architecture that dynamically mitigates physical layer impairments in Long Range (LoRa) communication networks established with Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) operating at tactical speeds. Traditional Adaptive Data Rate (ADR) algorithms used in LoRaWAN networks misinterpret the Doppler shift under high mobility as path loss, leading to an unwarranted increase in the spreading factor and subsequent communication link failures. In this work, a cross-layer Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent is designed to incorporate UAV velocity into the state space, autonomously selecting the optimal spreading factor and transmission power by predicting frequency shifts at the physical layer. Simulations conducted in a realistic Rayleigh fading channel model demonstrate that the proposed method increases the Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) to over 85% at high speeds, significantly outperforming conventional algorithms.
keywords: ["LoRaWAN", "deep Q-network", "dynamic resource allocation", "transmission power control", "UAV mobility", "rate adaptation", "Rayleigh fading", "packet delivery ratio", "cross-layer optimization"]

title: Kronecker Product for Interaction Modeling
abstract: We propose a Kronecker product-based interaction model that provides a unified and expressive framework for feature–embedding interactions. We present multiple variants, including full learned, multi-head learned, and low-rank projection models, and provide efficient implementations using tensor operations. On large-scale industrial CTR prediction data, the proposed model achieves relative improvements of up to 0.05% in AUC and significant gains of 5.5% in logloss and 0.46% in PRAUC over a strong MaskNet baseline. Online A/B testing further shows substantial gains, with increases of 32.1% in RPM and 19.7% in eCPM, outperforming quadratic neural networks by a large margin. These results validate the effectiveness of the Kronecker product as a general and scalable solution for interaction modeling.
keywords: ["Kronecker product", "interaction modeling", "click-through rate prediction", "low-rank projection", "tensor operations", "online A/B testing"]

title: The Context Tax of General-Purpose Tokenization
abstract: This paper quantifies the context tax imposed by general-purpose tokenization in agglutinative languages. Using the same local Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) recipe, we train 64k native tokenizers for Turkish, Finnish, and Hungarian and compare them with tokenizers of GPT-4, mBERT, and XLM-R models. Each native tokenizer is trained on 30,000 Wiki40B texts and evaluated on a disjoint 500-text test set. The main metric is fertility, the average number of subword tokens per word; we also convert it into approximate word coverage under a fixed 512-token budget. In all three languages, the native tokenizer produces the shortest sequences. Native-vs-GPT-4 fertility gains are 77.63% for Turkish, 64.42% for Finnish, and 79.21% for Hungarian. The results show that tokenizer choice is a first-order context-efficiency decision in agglutinative languages.
keywords: ["tokenization", "agglutinative languages", "subword tokenization", "byte pair encoding", "Turkish language", "Finnish language", "Hungarian language", "GPT-4", "multilingual BERT", "XLM-R"]

title: Outage Probability of NTN-Based DF-Relayed FSO Systems Under the Nth Best HAPS Selection
abstract: This paper investigates the end-to-end outage probability of a non-terrestrial network-based, relay-assisted free-space optical communication system operating under the decode-and-forward relaying scheme. In the considered architecture, a satellite transmits data to a ground station via high-altitude platform stations (HAPS). The channel model accounts for the combined effect of path loss, Exponentiated Weibull turbulence, and pointing errors. Within the scope of the analysis, the statistical expressions of the composite channel coefficient and the end-to-end outage probability are first derived for the single-HAPS configuration, which represents a special case of the multi-HAPS architecture. The analysis is then extended to the multi-HAPS scenario based on end-to-end link quality using the Nth best selection scheme. Numerical results demonstrate the impact of turbulence, pointing error, and selection order on the outage performance, and the derived analytical expressions are validated through Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Benchmarking AI Agents for End-to-End Wildfire Intensity Classification and Risk Scoring
abstract: This study evaluates end-to-end machine learning solutions generated by six advanced AI agents for wildfire severity classification and operational risk scoring. The benchmark uses a multi-regional dataset combining NASA FIRMS and Open-Meteo observations (35 countries, 15,500 events, 4 severity classes). Each agent was tested across three independent runs with a shared prompt. Results show uniformly high classification performance, while run-to-run consistency, calibration, and risk score quality differ more clearly across agents. The study contributes an agent-centric benchmarking perspective by evaluating AI systems as workflow-generating entities on an operational disaster prediction task.
keywords: ["AI agents", "benchmarking", "end-to-end machine learning", "calibration", "disaster prediction", "Open-Meteo"]

title: Automated Myocardial Infarction Detection from 3-Lead ECG via Temporal Convolutional Networks
abstract: Myocardial Infarction (MI), commonly known as a heart attack, is a cardiovascular disease with the highest mortality rate worldwide. Early diagnosis has been proven to significantly improve patient survival rates. Therefore, research is being conducted on rapid and reliable automated MI detection methods. Although studies using electrocardiography (ECG) signal analysis frequently utilize 12-lead, current technologies prefer a smaller number of channels to reduce spatial and computational costs. In this study, an automated MI detection approach is proposed using a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) deep learning model based on 3-lead ECG signals II, V5, and V6 from the Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) Diagnostic Database. Classification was conducted using both class-based and subject-based data splitting strategies. The experimental results demonstrated that the proposed model achieved 99.47% accuracy, 99.65% sensitivity, 98.72% specificity, 99.71% precision, and a 99.68% F1-score for class-based detection. For subject-based detection, the model achieved 88.49% accuracy, 89.13% sensitivity, 85.71% specificity, 96.44% precision, and a 92.64% F1-score.
keywords: ["myocardial infarction detection", "3-lead ECG", "temporal convolutional network", "automated diagnosis", "ECG classification"]

title: A Spatially Based Cost Function Approach for Scattering Center Extraction from Near-Field ISAR Data
abstract: Accurately matching near-field ISAR data with a scattering center model is important for reliable far-field radar cross-section (RCS) estimation. In this study, instead of using a direct spectral-domain difference norm, a spatially based cost function is defined using nearest-neighbor distances between pseudo-scattering center locations. The resulting cost profile has a single V-shaped minimum, which enables derivative-free simplex optimization to refine scattering center locations. The method is evaluated using both synthetic examples and real measurement data.
keywords: ["scattering center extraction", "nearest neighbor distance", "simplex optimization", "radar cross section estimation"]

title: Effect of Dimensionality Reduction on Cross-Domain Performance in Person Re-Identification
abstract: In image-based person reidentification systems, the identification process relies on the similarity computation between feature vectors extracted from query images and existing vectors in large galleries. As the size of the feature vector increases, the amount of data that needs to be kept in memory and the computational cost increase linearly. In this study the compressibility of high-dimensional vectors obtained from vision transformer-based feature extraction models trained on the person reidentification task using principal component analysis and the effects of this process on model performance are investigated. Experimental results show that compressing the feature vectors at rates exceeding 80% causes only a minimal loss in training domain performance. A more remarkable finding is that in cross-domain tests, despite the domain shift problem, the performance drop exhibits a similar behavior to the training domain.
keywords: ["person re-identification", "dimensionality reduction", "principal component analysis", "vision transformer", "domain shift", "high-dimensional feature vectors"]

title: Resource and Location Optimization with GA in UAV-Supported Multicellular Networks: A Comparison of Greedy and Local Search
abstract: In this study, subband assignment to base stations (BS) and simultaneous optimization of the three-dimensional positions of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in a multi-cell network supported by UAVs were performed using a genetic algorithm (GA). The aim of the optimization is to maximize a total speed metric that prioritizes edge users (UEs) (based on max-min fairness) at the cell edge. The proposed GA was compared with improved greedy and greedy+local lookup methods. Simulations for different cell radii show that the GA outperforms both methods in terms of total speed and max-min fairness; it improves service quality, especially in large cells, by more effectively directing edge users to UAVs.
keywords: ["base station placement", "genetic algorithm", "greedy algorithm", "local search", "max-min fairness", "edge users", "cell edge coverage"]

title: Night-Time Robustness Analysis of 3D Lane Detection Methods on the OpenLane Dataset
abstract: Lane detection is a critical problem for both autonomous driving systems (ADS) and advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). The accurate identification of lanes within ADS provides important inputs to the control and decision-making modules. In the literature, lane detection methods are categorized into two classes: 2D and 3D. 2D methods have been commonly used in ADS and ADAS and have yielded successful results. However, the performance of these methods can decrease significantly, especially under complex road conditions or challenging environmental situations, such as at night. Recently, 3D methods, which have gained attention owing to their ability to model 3D spatial relationships, can significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of lane detection. In this study, the performances of the Persformer and Anchor3DLane architectures were analyzed using only nighttime driving data from the OpenLane dataset. Both quantitative and visual results are presented in the analysis, and the findings are discussed in detail.
keywords: ["3D lane detection", "night driving", "robustness analysis", "autonomous driving", "driver assistance systems", "3D spatial modeling"]

title: Semi-Supervised Classification of Building Facade Materials Using Satellite Imagery
abstract: The classification of building facade materials from satellite imagery is critical for large-scale remote sensing applications such as urban heat island analysis, energy efficiency modeling, and socio-economic condition prediction. This study primarily investigates a semi-supervised learning framework based on the FixMatch paradigm to address the limited labeled data problem, while also conducting supervised experiments for performance comparison. The DINOv2 and YOLO26 architectures are evaluated under both training settings. Experimental results show that semi-supervised training improves performance in both models compared to supervised learning, with the DINOv2 model demonstrating the highest performance. The DINOv2 model achieved F1-scores of 0.91, 0.78, and 0.75 for the Concrete, Metal, and Glass classes. These results underscore the effectiveness of global semantic representations in discriminating urban facade materials and demonstrate that high classification accuracy can be achieved even with a limited amount of labeled data.
keywords: ["building facade materials", "semi-supervised classification", "satellite imagery", "FixMatch", "DINOv2", "YOLO26", "limited labeled data", "urban heat island", "concrete", "metals", "glass"]

title: Alzheimer-OCT Dataset and Detection of Alzheimer’s Disease using Deep Learning
abstract: This study introduces a new clinical dataset for the detection of Alzheimer’s disease (AD), the Alzheimer-OCT (AOCT) Set, and presents deep learning-based analyses. The dataset includes optical coherence tomography (OCT), angiography (OCTA) and fundus images from 31 volunteer participants. To overcome the limited data constraint, transfer learning strategies were employed; 2D slice-based deep learning architectures were compared with the 3D PointNet++ approach, which directly models spatial relationships by converting OCT volumes into point clouds. The results show that the developed 2D and 3D models are able to distinguish retinal structural changes associated with AD and that clinical OCT data may be a potential biomarker for AD diagnosis.

title: Dual-Polarized Index Modulation in Terrestrial THz Communication Systems
abstract: Terahertz (THz) communication offers extreme data rates for next generation communication systems, yet it suffers from severe path loss. Though multiple-input multiple-output communication technology is a promising solution to overcome this, it may bring an excessive hardware complexity. Hence, index modulation stands as an alternative to exploit the multiple antenna structure and to reduce the hardware complexity. In this paper, a THz system employing dual-polarized variable generalized spatial modulation (DP-VGSM) is proposed, and its performance is examined in terms of bit error rate under free space loss, absorption loss, α-μ fading, and pointing errors. The performance of DP-VGSM is compared to spatial modulation (SM), generalized SM (GSM), variable GSM (VGSM), and DP-GSM. Computer simulations demonstrate that dual-polarized systems provide a significant advantage over single-polarized systems by reducing the correlation between channels and that DP-VGSM outperforms others.

title: A BiLSTM-Based Approach for Detecting Broken and Cracked Porcelain Insulators from Leakage Current Signals
abstract: Insulators exposed to environmental conditions can develop structural defects such as breakages and cracks over time. Early detection of such defects is critical for ensuring the continuity of energy transmission systems. In this study, an original leakage current dataset was constructed by applying 60 kV voltage to a three-element U100 BL (K3) porcelain insulator under intact, broken, and cracked scenarios. A total of 35 features were extracted and restructured into a 5×7 sequential representation as input to a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) model. The proposed model achieved 93.95% accuracy, outperforming a standard LSTM by approximately 2%. The results confirm the significant potential of the proposed approach for reliable and effective insulator fault diagnosis.
keywords: ["porcelain insulators", "insulator defect detection", "bidirectional LSTM", "power transmission lines"]

title: Epileptic Seizure Detection via Dynamic Graph Learning in EEG Signals
abstract: Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder affecting approximately 50 million people worldwide. This study proposes an end-to-end Dynamic Unrolled TVGL (DUTVGL) architecture capable of simultaneously modeling spatial and temporal dependencies in EEG signals. The architecture comprises 1D-CNN feature extraction, Variational Graph Structure Learning (V-GSL) for dynamic connectivity estimation, and GCN classification. Class imbalance is addressed through Focal Loss, while Evidential Deep Learning (EDL) provides prediction-level uncertainty estimation and a patient-specific self-calibration mechanism controls false alarm rates at the individual level. The model was evaluated on both CHB-MIT and Siena Scalp EEG datasets, achieving 96.4% accuracy with 98.0% sensitivity on CHB-MIT and 91.2% accuracy with 85.4% sensitivity on Siena via LOPO cross-validation. With only 116,040 parameters and an inference time of 24 ms, the model demonstrates suitability for real-time applications.

title: Design And Implementation of a High Power VHF Radio Frequency Power Combiner for Wireless Communication Networks
abstract: In this paper, the design, analysis, and implementation of a three-input single-output coaxial power combiner for wireless communication networks have been performed for use in high-power very high frequency (VHF) applications. A coaxial structure was preferred to enhance the power handling capacity and system reliability under high-power conditions. To eliminate thermal issues and constraints related to power capacity, conventional Wilkinson isolation resistors were removed; instead, a circulator-based structure is proposed to direct reflected power to a matched load. 'CST Microwave Studio' software was utilized for simulation studies at a center frequency of 260 MHz. The objective of this study is to achieve an efficient power combining structure with low insertion loss and high power durability for fields such as military communications, radar systems, and industrial plasma technologies.
keywords: ["power combiner", "VHF", "high power RF", "insertion loss", "power handling", "wireless networks", "military communications", "radar systems", "plasma technology"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Age and Gender Classification from ECG Signal
abstract: This study presents the prediction of demographic information, specifically age and gender, from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals using a 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN) deep learning model. The Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt (PTB) Diagnostic Database, comprising both healthy subjects and patients diagnosed with arrhythmia, was utilized. Classification procedures were performed on 3-lead ECG signals (II, V1, and V6) across three experimental groups: a healthy control group, an arrhythmic group and a combined group of both. Based on predefined age thresholds, three age categories (young, middle-aged, and elderly) and two gender categories (male and female) were established. The classification procedures were conducted using class-based and subject-based approaches, and the outcomes were comparatively analyzed. Ultimately, the study demonstrates that while ECG signals carry common morphological traces regarding age and gender, they fundamentally constitute a strong, subject-specific biometric signature due to high inter-subject physiological variability and the impact of pathological structures.
keywords: ["age estimation", "gender classification", "electrocardiogram", "1D convolutional neural network", "ECG biometrics", "cardiac arrhythmias", "ECG morphological features"]

title: LLM Based Code Generation and Code Integration with Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: Contemporary large language models can generate syntactically correct code from natural language specifications. However, integrating the generated code into existing software projects remains a largely manual, error-prone process that severely limits practical utility. This paper proposes a novel four-agent multi-agent system architecture to bridge the gap between code generation and code integration. The system comprises a Context Retrieval Agent, Code Generation Agent, Code Integration Agent, and Orchestration Agent. Evaluated through 270 experiments across three software projects of varying complexity, six language models, and three code generation styles, the AST-based integration architecture achieved a 100% success rate. Syntax validity averaged 69.2%, and the best model configuration reached a normalized score of 0.795.
keywords: ["large language models", "code generation", "code integration", "multi-agent systems", "context retrieval", "natural language specifications"]

title: Analysis of Loop Free Alternates for Fault-Tolerant IEEE 802.1 TSN
abstract: Providing real-time and deterministic communication capabilities to IEEE 802.3 Ethernet, IEEE 802.1 Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) allows traffic with different priority levels to be transmitted over a single physical network. One of these traffic classes, Audio-Video Bridging (AVB), is widely used for traffic requiring bounded end-to-end latency. IP Fast Re-Route (IPFRR) is a mechanism aimed at rapidly redirecting packets to a pre-calculated alternative path to prevent traffic disruption during link and node failures within a network. In this paper, IPFRR methods are investigated for the proactive recovery of single link failures in a TSN network. The impact of IPFRR on the failure coverage percentage in networks and the worst-case delay values on traffic flows is examined.
keywords: ["Audio Video Bridging", "fault tolerance", "link failure recovery", "worst-case delay", "deterministic networking", "real-time communication"]

title: Diagnostic Model Based on Efect Size Across Phases of Respiratory Sounds
abstract: The diagnostic accuracy of stethoscopes and pulmonary function tests used to detect respiratory diseases may be inadequate. This poses a significant limitation to early and accurate diagnosis. This study proposes an approach based on the effect size between the sub-phases of the respiratory cycle. As part of the study, 14-channel respiratory sounds from 135 participants (75 healthy individuals and 60 asthma patients) were divided into sub-phases of the respiratory cycle. Cohen's d effect size was then calculated between sub-phases based on their power spectral density estimates and used as a feature. The features were used as input for five different classifiers. The results demonstrated that the feature composed of effect sizes calculated between consecutive sub-phases achieved successful performance with an F1 score of 0.878, accuracy of 0.889, precision of 0.900, and specificity of 0.880.
keywords: ["lung sounds", "asthma diagnosis", "effect size", "power spectral density", "acoustic biomarkers", "Cohen's d", "lung disease detection"]

title: Statistical Comparison of Denoising Algorithms in Dielectric Characterization by Cavity Perturbation Method
abstract: This paper addresses a practical yet overlooked challenge in cavity perturbation measurements, namely the degradation of parameter extraction accuracy under noisy conditions. Although denoising techniques are widely used in many signal processing applications, their performance in cavity perturbation–based parameter extraction has not been systematically studied. To address this gap, four methods, wavelet thresholding, Savitzky–Golay, moving average, and Gaussian filtering, are evaluated on CST-simulated S-parameter data from microwave cavity resonators using a Monte Carlo framework with 2500 trials per SNR level. Resonant frequency shift and Q-factor are extracted for five dielectric materials and benchmarked against clean simulation data via mean absolute error. Moving average filtering yields the lowest overall error, while wavelet thresholding performs worse at low SNR and for high-loss materials due to peak distortion. All methods converge above 20 dB SNR.

title: Spiking Neural Networks for Efficient Effect Prediction in Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Predicting the effects of actions on objects in robotic manipulation plays an important role in making effective action plans. Performing this prediction with low computational cost is important for the efficient usage of these systems. Although conventional deep learning architectures such as Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) are successful in effect prediction, they require high computational cost due to their structures that rely on a large number of multiplication operations. In this study, a Spiking Neural Network (SNN) model based on Leaky Integrate-and-Fire neurons is proposed to perform an efficient effect prediction. Both event-based SNN and MLP are trained on data collected from a simulation environment, and the impact of different numbers of time steps on accuracy and computational cost is examined for the SNN. Experiments show that the proposed SNN model with 5 time steps achieves a similar effect prediction performance to the MLP, and reduces the total number of operations.

title: Energy- and Hardware-Efficient Phase-Shifter Sharing Architecture for HAPS–RIS Assisted Communication Systems
abstract: High-Altitude Platform Stations (HAPS) have emerged as a promising solution for 6G and beyond communication systems due to their wide coverage capability and strong line-of-sight characteristics. Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS), on the other hand, represent a promising technology capable of extending coverage by controlling the phase of electromagnetic waves. However, employing a dedicated phase shifter for each element in large-scale RIS systems significantly increases hardware complexity, computational burden, and power consumption. In this work, a low-complexity architecture based on phase-shifter sharing is proposed for HAPS–RIS assisted communication systems. In the proposed structure, multiple RIS elements are controlled by a single phase shifter, thereby reducing hardware complexity, computational load, and circuit power consumption. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed architecture can effectively reduce hardware complexity while preserving system performance.

title: Comparative Analysis of Deep Learning Models for Speech Enhancement in Noisy Environments
abstract: Speech enhancement (SE) is a fundamental signal processing task aimed at recovering clean speech components from signals corrupted by environmental noise. While various architectures operating in time and time-frequency domains have been proposed in recent deep learning literature, the generalization capability of these models under acoustic conditions differing from the training data remains a critical area of investigation. In this study, the performances of four pioneering architectures-DCCRN, CMGAN, Attention U-Net, and Demucsare comparatively analyzed in a cross-corpus scenario using an extensive training set and the standard VoiceBank-DEMAND test suite. The evaluation is conducted through objective metrics, including Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI) for speech intelligibility, Scale-Invariant Signal-to-Distortion Ratio (SI-SDR) for noise suppression capacity, and Log-Spectral Distance (LSD) for spectral fidelity and provides technical framework for model selection.

title: FedCRA: Federated Representation Alignment for Label-Skewed Video HAR
abstract: Federated learning (FL) degrades under non-IID data, and label skew can severely affect large models. Video transformers such as TimeSformer are particularly sensitive in this setting, since client-specific CLS representations may drift across heterogeneous clients. We propose FedCRA, a class-conditional representation alignment method that models projected CLS embeddings as diagonal Gaussian distributions and aligns them through a closed-form KL regularizer using communicated sufficient statistics. Experiments on federated UCF101 show that the proposed approach improves robustness over FedAvg under Dirichlet label skew.

title: Comparative Analysis of Hyperparameter Optimization Techniques in Obesity Classification
abstract: The Body Mass Index (BMI), traditionally used in obesity diagnosis, is insufficient to reflect the true metabolic risk profile of individuals. This study aims to overcome the limitations of BMI by presenting a comparative analysis of a six-class metabolic phenotype framework, including overweight subgroups, and machine learning algorithms that utilize hyperparameter optimization to differentiate these classes with high accuracy. In this context, five different classification algorithms (Random Forest, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbour, XGBoost, LightGBM) were integrated with three different optimization techniques (GridSearch, Optuna, and Particle Swarm Optimization - PSO) and analyzed comparatively. According to experimental results, the combination of LightGBM and PSO achieved a test accuracy of 92.56%. Furthermore, the study found that the defined waist-to-height ratio characteristic is more effective than BMI in diagnosing obesity.

title: Learning-based Adaptive Parameter Selection Framework for Navigation in Mobile Robots
abstract: Navigation in autonomous mobile robots depends on complex parameter tuning that often lacks generalizability. This study proposes a context-aware, learning-based adaptive parameter selection framework for local planners. Focusing on a differential-drive mobile robot simulated with ROS 2 Humble and Gazebo, the method enables dynamic switching between predefined configurations (time-optimal, balanced, and safety-optimal) during navigation. A Random Forest model was trained using features such as obstacle density, proximity, and goal distance. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms fixed configurations, achieving a 97.5% success rate and an average task completion time of 18.0 s while maintaining low computational overhead.
keywords: ["adaptive parameter selection", "mobile robot navigation", "local planner", "differential drive robot", "context-aware learning", "random forest", "ROS2", "Gazebo simulation"]

title: Vehicle Speed Estimation Using Quantum Variational Regression: A Comparison with Classical ML and Kalman Filters
abstract: Within intelligent transportation systems, precise prediction of vehicle speeds plays a vital role in traffic management and law enforcement. This work integrates YOLOv8 for object detection, ByteTrack for object tracking, and Bird’s Eye View (BEV) perspective transformation with Kalman filtering. A Variational Quantum Regressor (VQR) model trained with reference vehicle crossings has been developed. The VQR was tested with the Qiskit simulator using a hybrid quantum-classical architecture created with the ZZFeatureMap layer and ansatz circuit. The VQR model was compared with classical machine learning alternatives such as Ridge Regression and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The results show that SVR (99.26%) exhibited the best performance, while VQR (96.90%) offered competitive performance with limited training data. The findings demonstrate the learning potential of the QVR model with small datasets on transportation problems, providing strong motivation for further quantum studies with expanded datasets.

title: A Scalable Dual-Representation Deep Learning Architecture for Specific Emitter Identification
abstract: In electronic warfare and spectrum security applications, distinguishing transmitting devices through their unintentional modulation on pulse (UMOP) attributes originating from the physical layer is a critical requirement. In this study, a dual-branch deep learning-based architecture is proposed for specific emitter identification (SEI) on real-world RF data. In the proposed structure, raw I/Q time-domain representations are processed in one branch via CNN-assisted Transformer blocks, while spectrograms obtained through STFT are processed in the other branch via a Vision Transformer-based structure; the two representations are fused using a multi-head cross-attention mechanism. Experiments conducted on open-source real-world ADS-B raw IQ data demonstrate that the proposed method achieves 96.97% accuracy in a challenging 30-class scenario and offers more stable and superior discriminative performance compared to baseline models in the literature as the number of classes increases. Ablation analyses confirm the contribution of each component employed in the architecture.
keywords: ["specific emitter identification", "vision transformer", "spectrogram", "multi-head cross-attention", "ADS-B", "electronic warfare", "emitter classification"]

title: Local Stationarity in Time-Varying Graph Signals
abstract: Graph signal processing provides a powerful framework for analyzing data defined over irregular network structures. Estimation of effective models from a set of timevarying graph signals requires capturing both temporal dynamics and graph-dependent statistical structures. Existing approaches that model time-vertex signals as stochastic processes typically assume a globally stationary model, which often fails to represent local variations that naturally arise across both temporal and graph dimensions. In this work, we address the problem of learning parametric models for graph signals exhibiting locally stationary behavior over time and graph. We propose a locally stationary time-vertex signal model that extends stationarity to a locally adaptive setting and develop an algorithm to learn the model parameters. Experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate improved estimation accuracy over existing time-vertex methods.
keywords: ["graph signal processing", "time-varying graph signals", "local stationarity", "temporal dynamics"]

title: Image Steganography in the Wavelet Domain: An Analysis of Payload Capacity vs Imperceptibility
abstract: Digital image steganography enables secure communication by embedding data into a cover medium without raising suspicion. Spatial domain methods (e.g., LSB) offer high capacity but are weak against statistical analyses due to distortions in smooth regions. Transform domain approaches (especially DWT), on the other hand, provide better imperceptibility through frequency coefficients. This study proposes a method that selects high-frequency regions using DWT and embeds the data only into the LSBs of these pixels. In this way, smooth regions are preserved. Experiments conducted on 85 grayscale images show that there is a capacity–size trade-off: Level 1 decomposition is suitable for practical payloads (0.01–0.10 bpp), while deeper levels are impractical due to decreasing spatial support. In comparisons, the proposed method achieves similar PSNR to plain LSB (61.14 dB at 0.10 bpp), while showing a clear advantage over direct DWT embedding ( 48.03 dB). RS steganalysis confirms the security of the method with anomaly scores below 3.1% even at high payloads. In addition, the Python-based implementation is suitable for resource-constrained systems with low CPU and memory usage.
keywords: ["image steganography", "wavelet transform", "discrete wavelet transform", "least significant bit embedding", "payload capacity", "imperceptibility", "steganalysis", "grayscale images", "resource-constrained systems"]

title: Optical Flow-Based Video Analysis for the Estimation of Dry Matter Content of Wastewater Treatment Sludge
abstract: Sludge generated in wastewater treatment plants is subjected to a dewatering process prior to disposal or reuse due to its high water content. The determination of the sludge’s dry matter content is generally carried out in laboratory environments using gravimetric methods; however, these methods are time-consuming and labor-intensive processes. In this study, videos of the sludge loading process into trucks were recorded through a camera system integrated into the treatment plant, and the behavior exhibited by the sludge at different dry matter levels was analyzed using image processing techniques.
keywords: ["optical flow", "video analysis", "sewage sludge", "sludge dewatering", "sludge loading", "image processing", "non-destructive measurement", "sludge moisture content"]

title: Performance Analysis of Vision-Language-Action Models: Evaluating Turkish Command Understanding in OpenVLA
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models unify visual perception, language comprehension, and action generation under a single architecture, yet they are trained almost exclusively on English data. We evaluated the OpenVLA-7B model by issuing the same 50 manipulation commands in both Turkish and English and comparing the resulting action vectors. The paired measurements revealed substantial cross-lingual divergence: the mean L2 error reached 0.501 and cosine similarity dropped to 0.372, both statistically significant. No linear relationship between command complexity and performance degradation was observed. Although Turkish commands incurred a 30.8% token overhead, no meaningful latency difference was recorded. Our findings highlight a deep-seated deficiency in multilingual action generation within current VLA architectures.
keywords: ["vision-language-action models", "OpenVLA", "Turkish language", "cross-lingual performance", "action generation"]

title: Parameter Estimation and Detection of Frequency Hopping 915 MHz Narrowband UAV Telemetry
abstract: Frequency hopping spread spectrum (FHSS) is widely employed in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) telemetry systems. The detection of FHSS signals and accurate estimation of their parameters are of critical importance for spectrum monitoring, parameter analysis, and target identification. Existing studies predominantly focus on the 2.4 GHz band, while research addressing the 915 MHz ISM band remains considerably limited. This study aims to achieve high-accuracy detection of UAVs employing FHSS in the 915 MHz band. To this end, the real-world field performance of a narrowband FHSS detection algorithm based on the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT), previously validated only with synthetic data, is evaluated. The algorithm estimates hopping channel center frequency, bandwidth, dwell time, guard time, and hopping rate through threshold-based spectrogram binarization and iterative refinement steps. The results demonstrate that the proposed method constitutes a viable approach under real-world field conditions.
keywords: ["frequency hopping spread spectrum", "UAV telemetry", "915 MHz ISM band", "signal detection", "parameter estimation", "short-time Fourier transform", "dwell time", "guard time", "hopping rate", "spectrum monitoring"]

title: Robustness Comparison of Classical and Deep Learning-Based Methods for q-Space Interpolation in Diffusion MRI
abstract: Accurate characterization of white matter microstructure via diffusion MRI requires dense sampling of q-space, causing prolonged scan times. Recent work has proposed using q-space undersampling followed by classical spherical harmonic or spherical polar Fourier (SPF) interpolation, as well as deep learning-based interpolation approaches such as QUCCI. In this work, we evaluate the robustness of these interpolation methods against the choice of q-space undersampling scheme. Using multi-shell dMRI data from Human Connectome Project dataset, we compare SPF and QUCCI under four different undersampling schemes and on four different downstream diffusion metrics. The results highlight the importance of both the undersampling scheme and the q-space interpolation method. Accordingly, QUCCI provides improved robustness against the choice of undersampling scheme, with undersampling via spherical codes yielding the highest-fidelity diffusion metrics.
keywords: ["diffusion MRI", "spherical codes", "white matter microstructure", "diffusion metrics", "robustness"]

title: Implementation of an ASCON-Based Cryptographic Hardware Core on FPGA and Open-Source ASIC Design Flow
abstract: In this study, an ASCON (Authenticated Encryption and Hashing) based cryptographic hardware core has been designed and implemented for resource-constrained secure embedded systems. The proposed architecture has been developed with a modular approach based on the ASCON permutation structure. The AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) core, permutation engine, round unit, S-box layer, and linear diffusion layer are organized as separate functional blocks. The design has been implemented using the register-transfer level approach and first verified functionally in a simulation environment. Subsequently, the design has been implemented on the Artix-7 XC7A100T FPGA (Field-Programmable Gate Array) platform on the Nexys A7 board and tested at the hardware level. According to the obtained results, the proposed structure uses 846 LUTs (Look-Up Tables) and 985 FFs (Flip-Flops), provides approximately 625 Mbps throughput at a 160 MHz operating frequency, and consumes a total of 133 mW of power. These results demonstrate that the design offers a balanced solution between low resource utilization and achievable performance. In addition to FPGA validation, the physical feasibility of the architecture has also been examined within the scope of an open-source ASIC (Application-Specific Integrated Circuit) design flow. Upon observing congestion in the placement and routing stages of the initially used parallel structure, a serialized architecture with lower area cost was preferred and the OpenLane flow was successfully completed. The physical design results yielded a die area of 0.49 mm2, a placement density of 33.7%, and violation-free verification outputs. As a result, this study presents an area-efficient and physically realizable solution for ASCON-based hardware cores, both within the scope of FPGA validation and open-source ASIC design flow.
keywords: ["Ascon", "authenticated encryption with associated data", "FPGA implementation", "OpenLane", "resource-constrained embedded systems", "S-box", "area-efficient hardware"]

title: Dynamic Beta-Weighted Stacking for Blunder Prediction in Blitz Chess
abstract: This study proposes Dynamic Beta-Weighted Stacking (DBWS) for blunder prediction in blitz chess. DBWS enables the ensemble meta-model to dynamically adjust base learner weights according to remaining clock time and positional uncertainty. Experiments on 93,625 moves from 1,749 blitz games obtained from the Lichess open database show that DBWS matches static stacking in AUC while outperforming soft voting. Analysis of learned coefficients reveals beta-shifting and gradient boosting dominates when time is abundant, while the neural network becomes relatively more influential under time pressure.
keywords: ["position uncertainty", "gradient boosting", "artificial neural networks", "soft voting", "Lichess"]

title: A Blind, Coherent, Reliability-Based ADS-B Decoder for Low-SNR Environments
abstract: Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) relies on 1090 MHz Pulse Position Modulation (PPM). Standard receivers utilize non-coherent hard-decision decoding and strict preamble synchronization, which fail catastrophically in low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) and high-interference environments. This paper presents a novel preamble-bypassing coherent decoder architecture. Utilizing continuous sliding-window Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) phase tracking, spatial selection diversity, and a reliability-based Chase-2 soft-decision algorithm, the proposed architecture corrects multi-bit payload errors and breaks through the strict bounds of standard non-coherent methods. Approaching the coherent orthogonal bound, it successfully recovers packets even at 0 dB SNR.
keywords: ["ADS-B", "pulse position modulation", "low signal-to-noise ratio", "constant false alarm rate", "phase tracking", "spatial diversity", "reliability-based decoding", "1090 MHz"]

title: BEAM: Energy-Aware Adaptive Modality Routing for Beam Prediction in 6G V2I Networks
abstract: This paper proposes BEAM, an energy-aware adaptive modality routing framework for multimodal beam prediction in 6G vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) communications. Unlike conventional static fusion approaches that activate a fixed set of sensing modalities for all samples, BEAM learns a sample-dependent routing policy and selectively activates high-cost modalities only when low-cost contextual information is insufficient. The proposed framework integrates a context extractor, a differentiable router, modality-specific encoders, and a selective fusion mechanism under a joint optimization objective that considers beam prediction accuracy, normalized sensing cost, sparsity, and routing stability. Experimental results on DeepSense 6G Scenarios 31–34 demonstrate that BEAM achieves 82.3% Top-1 and 94.4% Top-3 beam prediction accuracy while reducing the normalized average sensing cost from 7.6 to 2.4 compared with the Static All-Fusion baseline. These findings highlight the effectiveness of adaptive modality routing in enabling cost-efficient and energy-aware multimodal beam prediction for future 6G intelligent transportation systems.
keywords: ["vehicle-to-infrastructure communication", "6G", "selective fusion", "intelligent transportation systems"]

title: Compression and Client Importance with Stragglers in Vertical Federated Learning
abstract: Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) enables collaborative, privacy-preserving model training across multiple parties holding different feature subsets of the same data samples, without sharing raw data. However, VFL is particularly vulnerable to the straggler problem, as slow clients inevitably delay training since they cannot be excluded. In this paper, we investigate the effect of compressing model updates on convergence time and model performance in heterogeneous VFL scenarios. We evaluate Top-K sparsification and 8-bit quantization techniques under different configurations. We also analyze how compression of different clients affects model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that 8-bit quantization compression resulted in the best model performance to communication delay ratio, and that different straggling clients may have varying impacts on model performance. These observations aid in the selection of compression methods for practical VFL systems, where relevant features are often unevenly distributed across clients in real-world datasets.
keywords: ["vertical federated learning", "straggler clients", "model compression", "top-k sparsification", "8-bit quantization", "convergence time", "communication delay", "data heterogeneity", "privacy-preserving machine learning", "client importance"]

title: Implementation and Performance Evaluation of Elliptic Curve Cryptography over SECP256R1 on STM32 Microprocessor
abstract: The use of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in embedded systems has become increasingly popular with advancing technologies. These devices become vulnerable to cyber attacks as they gain popularity. The cryptographic operations performed for the purpose of protection against cyber attacks are crucial to yield fast results in open networks and not slow down network traffic. Therefore, to enhance communication security, studies have been conducted in the literature on using asymmetric encryption and symmetric encryption together in IoT devices for activities such as key sharing, encryption, decryption, data signing, and verifying signed data. In this study, we first propose a cryptographic system engaging of IoT devices operated from a server. Then we do performance analysis of our proposal. In particular, we evaluate the elliptic curve Diffie-Hellman key exchange and elliptic curve digital signature algorithms on the Secp256r1 elliptic curve and AES symmetric encryption via the Micro uECC library conducted with the 32-bit STM32F410RB Nucleo development board microprocessor running at 48 MHz.
keywords: ["elliptic curve cryptography", "Internet of Things security", "ECDSA"]

title: Classification of Turkish Lira Coins from Images Using Deep Learning
abstract: Manual counting of coins, widely used in commercial processes, may lead to time loss and human errors. This study aims to automatically recognize Turkish lira coins from photographs using an object detection-based approach. YOLOv8, YOLO11, and the recent YOLO26 architectures were employed and their performances were compared. A dedicated dataset was created for training and testing, consisting of heterogeneous arrangements of single and multiple Turkish lira and foreign coins captured with cameras having different optical properties. Experimental results show that the YOLO11n-seg model achieved the best overall performance with 93% mAP50, 89.60% precision, 87.70% recall, and an 88.70% F1-score, while the YOLOv8n-seg model was the fastest with the lowest inference time. In addition, a PyQt-based graphical user interface (GUI) was developed to provide a practical solution that reduces errors caused by manual counting in commercial processes. The dataset and GUI developed in this study are publicly available as open access.
keywords: ["coin identification", "coin counting", "object detection", "YOLOv8", "YOLOv11", "YOLO26"]

title: Wide-Beam Optical Beacon-Based UAV Self-Positioning
abstract: We propose an optical beacon-based 3D self-positioning method for uncrewed aerial vehicles (UAVs) operating in GPS-denied environments. Following a GPS outage, the UAV flies a pre-programmed circular holding pattern at approximately constant altitude. At the same time, a high-power ground optical beacon transmitter illuminates the expected region with a wide beam. The UAV samples the received signal strength (RSS) at azimuth-uniform waypoints determined from the onboard heading estimate. The resulting RSS sequence is used to estimate the orbit center position, providing a reliable reference for self-positioning during GPS outages. We formulate this task as a nonlinear weighted least-squares (NWLS) problem and solve it using Gauss–Newton (GN) iterations. We also derive the corresponding Cramér–Rao lower bound (CRLB) as a performance benchmark. Simulation results show that the proposed estimator closely follows the CRLB.
keywords: ["optical beacon", "GPS-denied navigation", "received signal strength", "3D localization", "weighted nonlinear least squares", "Gauss-Newton optimization", "Cramer-Rao lower bound", "holding patterns"]

title: Geometry-Consistent Safety Shaping for PPO-Based Multi-UAV Formation Assembly
abstract: Reward shaping is widely used to discourage close approaches in multi-agent reinforcement learning, but its geometry is often chosen independently of the target formation. This paper studies a 4-UAV 2 × 2 square formation-assembly task in 3D using parameter-sharing PPO. Three controllers from one development line are compared: baseline, safety-intensified, and geometry-aligned. The main finding is that a 5 m warning radius creates a reward–task mismatch when the minimum inter-slot spacing is 7 m, destabilizing training. Reverting the radius to 4 m restores stable learning and reduces violations per episode from 2.64 to 2.11 in the controlled ablation. Under domain randomization, success drops to 94.5 percent, indicating a robustness tradeoff.
keywords: ["reward shaping", "multi-agent reinforcement learning", "collision avoidance", "domain randomization"]

title: Landing of Autonomous UAVs on Maritime Platforms Using LSTM Layered Neural Network-Based Motion Predictor and Energy-Efficient Landing Trajectory Optimization
abstract: This study analyzes the short-term motion prediction of a ship platform operating under irregular sea wave conditions and evaluates the energy efficiency of landing algorithms for a quadrotor unmanned aerial vehicle. A synthetic dataset is generated using a response amplitude operator based irregular wave simulation. Spectral features obtained via the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) are incorporated into the artificial neural network feature vector, and the use of a one-frame STFT is shown to significantly improve position prediction accuracy. In addition, energy-optimal and two-stage landing algorithms are compared based on a quadratic cost function. The results demonstrate that the energy-optimal algorithm is more efficient in terms of actual energy consumption than the two-stage approach.
keywords: ["UAV landing", "quadrotor", "motion prediction", "LSTM neural network", "response amplitude operators", "short-time Fourier transform", "landing trajectory", "energy consumption"]

title: Automated Medical Information Retrieval via Agentic Filter-and-Refine Pipeline
abstract: In clinical decision support systems, finding the suitable medical literature for complex patient scenarios is critical. Although dense vector-based models offer high accuracy, the global vector index requirement creates scalability problems, while word-based search engines remain insufficient due to vocabulary mismatch. In this study, an Autonomous Filter-and-Refine structure operating on standard text search infrastructures is proposed. The developed architecture overcomes the vocabulary mismatch by applying entity extraction and Hypothetical Document Embedding with a large language model, and then determines the most relevant articles with a context-aware ranker. In the experiments conducted on the PMC-Patients dataset; the proposed Autonomous Doctor Agent architecture exhibited equivalent results with vector-based models in top-ten level performance metrics; whereas in the top-three article band, it achieved superiority by leaving existing systems behind.
keywords: ["medical information retrieval", "clinical decision support", "vocabulary mismatch", "named entity recognition", "large language models", "literature searching"]

title: Real-Time Control for Hand Rehabilitation using Beckhoff IPC and Simulink-to-TwinCAT Workflow
abstract: Robotic hand rehabilitation systems are essential for motor learning and functional recovery following stroke. Safe physical human-robot interaction (pHRI) demands a deterministic, low-latency control loop. This paper presents a real-time control architecture for a four-DOF two-finger exoskeleton paired with a pinch-force manipulandum. The architecture centres on a Beckhoff Industrial PC (IPC) executing a 1 ms control cycle under TwinCAT 3, communicating with four BLDC servo drives via CANopen over CAN bus. Compared to a conventional PWM-and-encoder approach, the CANopen topology consolidates velocity commands, position feedback, and torque sensing onto a single bus, reducing wiring complexity, EMI susceptibility, and hardware failure points. Control logic - admittance control, inverse kinematics, and torque estimation - is designed in MATLAB/Simulink and compiled into TwinCAT C++ modules via the TE1400 toolchain, eliminating manual coding and accelerating deployment to hardware.
keywords: ["real-time control", "physical human-robot interaction", "exoskeleton", "CANopen", "TwinCAT", "admittance control", "inverse kinematics", "torque estimation", "stroke recovery", "low-latency control"]

title: Sample-Efficient Autonomous Surface Vehicle Navigation with Enhanced Experience Replay
abstract: This paper proposes a sample-efficient reinforcement learning framework for navigation of Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) in complex, obstacle-dense environments. Learning reliable navigation policies in such settings is challenging due to unsafe early exploration and high sample complexity. To address these issues, we integrate Distributional Reinforcement Learning with Deep Q-learning from Demonstrations (DQfD) and Count-Based Experience Replay (CbER), enabling effective learning from both expert priors and prioritized recent experiences. Furthermore, we critically evaluate the integration of Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) in navigational setups that already employ dense shaping rewards. Extensive simulations demonstrate that while HER offers limited marginal utility in the presence of strong shaping signals, the combined framework accelerates convergence by up to 6.3× compared to baselines.
keywords: ["unmanned surface vehicles", "navigation", "sample efficiency", "experience replay", "distributional reinforcement learning", "hindsight experience replay", "reward shaping", "obstacle avoidance", "exploration safety"]

title: Localization in Wireless Sensor Network
abstract: In some wireless sensor networks, the accurate determination of the physical locations of nodes is crucial for the overall functionality of the network. In this study, the range-free DV-Hop localization algorithm is utilized, and a hybrid approach based on Minimum Mean Square Error (MMSE) and a Genetic Algorithm is proposed for the solution phase. In the proposed method, the communication range is initially divided in two to apply a dual-radius model, thereby resolving the distance ambiguity in close neighborhoods. Subsequently, the average hop sizes between anchor nodes are calculated using the MMSE approach with weighted hop counts and actual distances, and the locations of unknown nodes are estimated by the Genetic Algorithm through a weighted fitness function. Simulation tests were designed to reveal the impact of the locations and number of anchor nodes on the node localization error for various applications. Scenarios were created considering narrow environments like caves, where nodes are randomly distributed, and wide areas like greenhouses, where nodes can be deployed systematically. According to the obtained simulation results, the developed hybrid algorithm reduces the average localization error to the level of one meter in narrow areas (20m x 10m) and to below four meters in wide areas (100m x 100m) in scenarios utilizing six anchor nodes, thereby achieving high accuracy.
keywords: ["wireless sensor networks", "node localization", "range-free localization", "DV-Hop", "anchor nodes", "localization error"]

title: Detection of Sub-Hourly Extreme Shear and Veer Events in Offshore Wind Profiles Using Open LiDAR and Met-ocean Data
abstract: Standard offshore wind turbine design load calculations assume simplified power-law vertical shear (α = 1/7) and negligible directional veer across the rotor, as codified in IEC 61400-1/3. Using 157,680 ten-minute records from the Martha's Vineyard WindCube LiDAR campaign (≈3 years, 40–200 m MSL) with collocated metocean and ERA5 reanalysis stability data, a percentile-threshold event-detection framework is applied. The site-mean shear exponent (α = 0.129) confirms IEC assumptions are conservative on average; however the 95th-percentile value (α = 0.248) substantially exceeds the IEC reference, with exceedances in 37.7% of records. Approximately 438 h/yr of extreme shear and veer events are detected annually; simultaneous exceedance reaches 24 h/yr. Extreme shear is strongly linked to stable stratification; extreme veer to frontal passages. The framework is fully reproducible from open data.
keywords: ["offshore wind energy", "veer", "stable stratification", "frontal passages", "LiDAR", "ERA5 reanalysis", "Martha's Vineyard"]

title: Sum of Costs Guided Diffusion for Motion Planning
abstract: The motion planning problem for robotic manipulation can be addressed through classical or deep learning approaches. Existing methods face significant challenges in generalizing to diverse test environments. In this study, we present a method with high generalization capability that generates collision-free trajectories using diffusion models. Each denoising step of the diffusion model is guided by the gradient of the total collision cost. Experimental results demonstrate that guiding the diffusion model with the sum of costs offers more robust performance by overcoming the generalization issues faced by competing methods. The proposed model demonstrates its effectiveness by achieving the highest performance on diverse test settings in Mπnets dataset among the compared methods.
keywords: ["motion planning", "robotic manipulation", "diffusion models", "collision-free paths", "generalization", "noise reduction"]

title: ML-Assisted HARQ Performance Analysis in 5G NR Toward 6G Reliability and Low Latency
abstract: Hybrid Automatic Repeat reQuest (HARQ) is a key reliability mechanism in 5G New Radio (NR); however, its retransmission-based operation introduces an inherent reliability–latency tradeoff that becomes increasingly critical for emerging 6G systems. This paper presents a 3GPP-compliant, MATLAB 5G Toolbox–based link-level evaluation of HARQ under realistic TDL-C channel conditions. A joint analysis is conducted to examine the impact of signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), modulation order, and HARQ process on block error rate (BLER), retransmission behavior and throughput efficiency. The results demonstrate that HARQ significantly improves link reliability by reducing BLER; however, the resulting retransmissions increase latency and reduce throughput efficiency, particularly for higher-order modulation schemes operating under unfavorable channel conditions. The presented analysis further reveals threshold SNR regions where retransmission rates decrease rapidly while throughput efficiency increases significantly. Motivated by these observations, a machine learning (ML)-based adaptive modulation framework is incorporated to dynamically select optimum modulation schemes according to channel conditions. Our ML-assisted approach significantly reduces retransmission rates while improving throughput performance across a wide SNR range by adaptively balancing reliability and spectral efficiency.
keywords: ["hybrid ARQ", "5G NR", "6G", "block error rate", "retransmission", "throughput efficiency", "adaptive modulation", "machine learning", "signal-to-noise ratio", "modulation order", "link-level simulation"]

title: Accelerated Sparse Deconvolution-Based CFAR for Dense Radar Target Detection
abstract: In radar scenes containing densely spaced targets, classical constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detectors suffer from performance degradation due to target energy leakage into reference cells. To mitigate this problem, the Majorization–Minimization (MM-CFAR) algorithm exploits the sparse structure of the range profile and improves detection performance in dense target environments. In this study, an accelerated approach based on the Fast Iterative Shrinkage-Thresholding Algorithm (FISTA) is proposed as an alternative to the MM solution used in the sparse deconvolution step. The proposed detector is referred to as FISTA-MM-CFAR. MM-CFAR, and the other CFAR algorithms in the literature and proposed FISTA-MM-CFAR methods are comprehensively compared under both sparse and dense target scenarios. In addition, computational complexity analysis is conducted to evaluate their suitability for real-time radar applications. Simulation results demonstrate that proposed method achieves significantly higher detection probabilities than others in both scenarios. Furthermore, the FISTA-based approach provides comparable detection performance while substantially reducing computational time.
keywords: ["constant false alarm rate detection", "dense target detection", "sparse deconvolution", "majorization-minimization", "FISTA", "radar target detection", "computational complexity", "real-time radar processing"]

title: The Effect of Data Interventions on Local Explanations in Credit Risk Models
abstract: Credit risk assessment is widely used to evaluate repayment capacity in financial decision systems. Although modern machine learning models can provide strong predictive performance, similarly performing models may produce different local explanations for the same instance. This study investigates the stability and consistency of explanations within Rashomon sets and analyzes how data interventions affect these properties. We train multiple models with H2O AutoML and construct Rashomon sets under two tolerance levels. Disagreement observations are defined as training instances on which at least two Rashomon models produce different class predictions. Two interventions are then applied to these observations: removal and label flipping. After retraining, local explanations are generated with LIME and compared using Kendall's W coefficient and sign-consistency ratio. Experiments on CreditCard, German_credit, and Loan_data show that near-optimal models do not always produce identical explanations and that intervention effects are dataset-dependent, with stronger shifts on datasets containing more disagreement observations.
keywords: ["credit risk assessment", "local explanations", "Rashomon set", "explanation stability", "explanation consistency", "label flipping", "lime", "model disagreement", "credit card data"]

title: SMOTE Variants in Pneumonia Detection: Comparative Model Analysis
abstract: This study analyzes the effects of SMOTE-based data augmentation techniques on different machine learning algorithms for a dataset of imbalanced X-ray images. For a dataset consisting of two classes (healthy and pneumonia), five different feature families commonly used in the literature were calculated after a preprocessing step involving basic standardization. Three different SMOTE methods were used to address the imbalance problem between the classes, and their effects on different machine learning algorithms were examined. Based on the models performance, the best results were achieved using the SMOTE-TOMEK and Borderline-SMOTE algorithms. When the generated data was analyzed statistically, the Borderline-SMOTE algorithm obtained the most accurate results.
keywords: ["SMOTE", "SMOTE-Tomek", "Borderline-SMOTE", "class imbalance", "pneumonia detection", "X-ray images", "data augmentation", "feature extraction", "model comparison"]

title: Depth-Based Metric Tree Height Estimation from Satellite Imagery
abstract: Accurate estimation of tree heights from aerial and satellite imagery plays a critical role in environmental and urban applications, including ecosystem monitoring, carbon stock assessment, biodiversity management, and city planning. With the increasing availability of high-resolution remote sensing data, detailed characterization of vegetation structure at regional and global scales has become increasingly feasible. This paper presents a study on metric tree height estimation using RGB imagery by fine-tuning the Depth Any Canopy (DAC) model. The model was trained using the FLAIR, IEEE Data Fusion Contest 2019, and GeoTiles datasets and subsequently evaluated across 14 geographically diverse test regions. The fine-tuned model achieved an RMSE below 3 m in all evaluated regions, demonstrating strong generalization performance and the effectiveness of the proposed training strategy for large-scale tree height estimation.
keywords: ["tree height estimation", "depth estimation", "RGB images", "fine-tuning", "canopy depth", "vegetation structure", "carbon stock estimation"]

title: Deep Learning Architectures for Brain Tumor Classification in 2D MRI
abstract: Brain tumor classification from MRI scans is a clinically critical task, and deep learning approaches have shown strong potential in accurately detecting various types of brain tumors (BTs). This paper presents a comparative evaluation of seven deep learning architectures for BT detection: VGG-16, ResNet-18, ResNet-50, DenseNet-121, EfficientNet-B0, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ViT-Base/16. The models are assessed using two publicly available datasets: the Kaggle brain tumor dataset (7,023 images across four classes) and the Figshare dataset (3,064 images across three classes). To ensure robust and unbiased evaluation, a leakage-aware experimental protocol is adopted, incorporating an 80/20 development–test set split along with three-fold cross-validation. When trained exclusively on the Figshare dataset, ViT-Base/16 and VGG-16 achieve relatively low accuracies of 56.12% and 46.49%, respectively. However, the application of transfer learning substantially improves their performance, increasing accuracy to 98.21% and 97.88%. On the Kaggle dataset, EfficientNet-B0 achieves the best overall performance, reaching 99.07% accuracy and 99.70% specificity. Furthermore, an analysis of model accuracy versus parameter size demonstrates that DenseNet-121 and EfficientNet-B0 require approximately four and six times fewer parameters than ConvNeXt-Tiny and ResNet-50, while maintaining competitive performance. These findings suggest that compact architectures can provide an effective balance between classification accuracy and computational efficiency.
