title: Explainable IMU Anomaly Detection: Impact of Window Size on Machine Learning Performance under Noise Injection
abstract: In this study, anomaly detection is investigated under controlled noise injection using IMU sensor data collected from a mobile robot. The collected time-series data is processed using a windowing approach, and machine learning models are developed based on extracted features. Logistic regression and random forest algorithms are employed for anomaly detection, and SHAP is used to enhance model interpretability. In addition, the impact of different window sizes on model performance is analyzed. Experimental results indicate that window size has a significant impact on model performance.
keywords: ["anomaly detection", "inertial measurement unit", "window size", "noise injection", "explainable machine learning", "SHAP", "logistic regression", "random forest", "mobile robots", "time series", "model interpretability"]

title: High-Efficiency Confinement Loss Prediction via Support Vector Regression
abstract: The design of Photonic Crystal Fiber based Surface Plasmon Resonance sensors relies on computationally expensive simulations. While recent studies propose Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) for data augmentation, we demonstrate an Augmentation Paradox where GAN generated samples introduce non physical noise that degrades rigorous kernel models. Instead, we propose a lightweight Bayesian optimized Support Vector Regression model. Achieving a Mean Squared Error of 0.121, our Support Vector Regression outperforms GAN augmented neural networks by over 60 percent without requiring synthetic data. Utilizing SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) values, we identify the outer cladding geometry as the primary driver of confinement loss. Furthermore, Monte Carlo robustness analysis reveals the sensor pitch is most critical for spectral stability, causing a 1.23 nm resonance jitter at a 3 percent manufacturing tolerance.
keywords: ["photonic crystal fiber", "surface plasmon resonance biosensor", "confinement loss", "support vector regression", "generative adversarial networks", "data augmentation", "Bayesian optimization", "SHAP", "manufacturing tolerances", "Monte Carlo robustness analysis"]

title: Evaluating the Impact of CSI Preprocessing on WiFi-Based Human Activity Recognition
abstract: Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) is a robust, privacy-preserving modality for Human Activity Recognition (HAR). Since raw CSI suffers from hardware desynchronizations and noise, preprocessing is vital. This study conducts an empirical ablation of CSI preprocessing using a fixed Two-Stream 2D CNN(Convolutional Neural Network) to quantify its impact on classification accuracy and latency. Results reveal that preprocessing, apart from architectural complexity, is the primary driver of the accuracy-latency trade-off. Computationally heavy methods like Hampel filtering introduce massive latency (>162 ms) without accuracy gains. In contrast, lightweight frequency-domain filtering consistently yields superior results. Specifically, dual-stream Butterworth bandpass filtering achieves 96.43% accuracy with only 49.08 ms latency. These findings demonstrate that isolating motion-relevant frequencies enables efficient, high-performance HAR suitable for real-time edge deployment.
keywords: ["WiFi channel state information", "human activity recognition", "accuracy-latency trade-off", "frequency-domain filtering", "edge deployment", "real-time recognition", "privacy-preserving sensing"]

title: Dynamic Task-Based Urban Routing with IoT Telemetry
abstract: This study addresses multi-stop urban routing using internet of things (IoT)-based container telemetry and focuses on generating feasible routes on directed road networks. It proposes a flow-aware A-star search operating on a graph derived from OpenStreetMap (OSM) data, incorporating directional continuity and turn feasibility. The system generates dynamic task points from fill-level and weight data and constructs a continuous route geometry via deterministic validation and correction steps. A free-ordering mode is also used to optimize visit sequences, with its effects analyzed comparatively. Experiments show that free ordering reduces route distance, while flow-aware cost modeling produces kinematically feasible, continuous routes. The findings indicate that distance-only classical approaches are insufficient for urban service vehicles and that directional constraints must be explicitly integrated into the decision process.
keywords: ["Internet of Things", "A* algorithm", "OpenStreetMap", "service vehicles"]

title: WaveBlock: Hybrid Discrete Wavelet Transform and Block Truncation Coding Based Video Compression Architecture for Resource-Constrained Embedded Systems
abstract: This study presents WaveBlock, a hybrid video compression architecture for resource-constrained IoT devices such as the ESP32. The method applies Integer Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) to smooth regions and Block Truncation Coding (BTC) to textured regions, achieving content-adaptive compression. Bitrate is optimized via motion-adaptive quantization and BTC entropy coding; an IOTAV container format and VLC plugin complete the end-to-end pipeline. Experiments show that WaveBlock achieves efficient bitrate reduction over MJPEG on static surveillance footage, maintaining high visual quality with minimal internal SRAM usage, while providing significantly higher frame rates than MJPEG on the ESP32-S3.
keywords: ["video compression", "block truncation coding", "hybrid compression", "entropy coding", "IoT devices", "ESP32 microcontroller", "resource-constrained embedded systems", "surveillance video", "bit rate reduction"]

title: Self-Supervised SimCLR-Based Solid Waste Classification Using RGB-NIR Images
abstract: With the advancement of technology and the increasing population, consumption is increasing day by day. The waste generated as a result of consumption causes serious damage to the environment and the economy. In this study, a special dataset consisting of 5 classes of solid wastes glass, paper, fabric, metal, and plastic was collected to contribute to the recycling of solid wastes. This collected dataset consists of RGB and NIR images for each class. A SimCLR model using RGB + NIR is proposed for the classification of solid wastes. Accuracy rates of 98% for RGB alone, 98% for NIR alone, and 99.33% for the proposed RGB + NIR method were obtained, showing that combining different spectral information allows the model to learn distinguishing features more effectively and improves classification performance.
keywords: ["solid waste classification", "SimCLR", "self-supervised learning", "near-infrared imaging", "waste recycling"]

title: ICA-Based Analysis and Separation of Eye-Blink Artifacts in EEG Signals
abstract: This study investigates the effect of frontal reference definition on independent component selection in ICA-based artifact removal using an EEG-only dataset. Analyses were conducted on 109 subjects from the PhysioNet EEG Motor Movement/Imagery dataset, where reference signals constructed from different electrode combinations were evaluated in terms of IC selection, stability, and signal preservation. The results indicate that frontal references are associated with more stable IC selection by consistently representing low-frequency components. Analyses further show that artifacts can generally be suppressed (77.1%) while preserving spectral structure and alpha activity (100% PSD correlation, 97–98% alpha preservation). However, sensorimotor mu–beta band preservation remains limited (~50%). These findings suggest that not only IC selection, but also reference definition and suppression strategy may influence EEG signal preservation.
keywords: ["eye blink artifact removal", "independent component analysis", "motor imagery"]

title: Presence-Constrained Optimal Decision Trees with Domain-Knowledge Constraints
abstract: Optimal decision trees are interpretable, yet they may be insufficiently flexible when domain experts require specific features and thresholds to appear in the learned tree. We propose a three-tier threshold-aware presence-constraint family that incorporates domain knowledge into the learned tree: feature presence (Tier I), feature-and-threshold presence (Tier II), and feature-threshold-class presence (Tier III). While existing frameworks can only enforce feature-level presence, the proposed tiers extend expert knowledge to threshold- and class-level specifications on continuous splits. Experiments on six datasets show that the effect of these constraints is dataset-dependent. Threshold-aware tiers can improve test performance over the unconstrained model in some datasets, whereas feature presence alone is not always sufficient. Notably, threshold-aware constraints may act as implicit regularisers when the unconstrained model tends to overfit. The results highlight the need to balance interpretability, feasibility, and solver behaviour.
keywords: ["optimal decision trees", "domain knowledge constraints", "model interpretability", "constraint satisfaction", "overfitting", "implicit regularization"]

title: Comparative Analysis of 700 MHz and 2600 MHz Frequency Bands in Mobile Private LTE Networks in Terms of Performance Parameters
abstract: This study examines a comparison of the 700 MHz and 2600 MHz frequency bands in terms of performance parameters in private LTE mobile networks. To evaluate network performance, RSRP (Received Signal Strength Indicator), RSRQ (Received Signal Quality), and SINR (Signal-to-Interference-and-Noise Ratio) values were measured during the tests. The measurement results were analyzed to reveal the effects of the 700 MHz and 2600 MHz frequency bands on coverage area, signal quality and data transmission performance. It was observed that the 700 MHz frequency provides wider coverage compared to the 2600 MHz band, while the 2600 MHz band offers higher performance in terms of capacity compared to the 700 MHz band.The originality of this study lies in the fact that these tests were conducted on a mobile private LTE network in a completely isolated environment, rather than on commercial mobile networks, and that two different frequency bands were evaluated comparatively on the same infrastructure. The findings are intended to provide technical contributions to private LTE usage scenarios in industry, defense, and critical communications infrastructures.
keywords: ["700 MHz band", "frequency band comparison", "network coverage", "signal quality", "RSRP", "RSRQ", "SINR", "network capacity", "data transfer performance", "critical communication"]

title: Particle Tracking and Velocity Estimation in Solid Propellant Combustion Using Infrared Imaging
abstract: Tracking the particles formed during combustion in solid propellant systems and estimating their velocities are important to understand combustion dynamics. In this study, particle tracking using infrared images is performed without relying on measurement systems specially designed for tracking. For this purpose, the combustion process of a solid propellant sample was simultaneously recorded using two cameras operating in the mid-wave and long-wave infrared bands, and preprocessing methods were applied to the acquired images. Inter-frame particle matching was carried out based on geometric constraints and a constant velocity assumption, enabling the estimation of particle trajectories and velocities. The proposed method was validated using velocity values obtained from manually generated reference trajectories, and the results show that, in both bands, the spatial distribution of particle trajectories, their orientations, and velocities are consistent with the reference data.
keywords: ["particle tracking", "particle velocity estimation", "solid propellant combustion", "infrared imaging", "mid-wave infrared", "long-wave infrared", "geometric constraints", "combustion dynamics", "particle trajectories"]

title: CNN-TA-Based Buy and Sell Signal Generation via Fusion of Technical Analysis Images and News Sentiment
abstract: This study combines the CNN-TA architecture, which converts technical indicators into two-dimensional images, with sentiment signals extracted from GDELT news headlines using FinBERT. News headlines are clustered per stock with K-means, where the number of clusters is selected by the Silhouette score. Four representations are then produced: daily average sentiment, topic presence, topic count, and topic-wise sentiment. These representations are evaluated on CNN, MLP, LSTM, Transformer, and ViT architectures with five-seed ensembles. The results show that the most consistent gain is obtained by CNN with daily average sentiment, increasing annualized return from 10.46 percent to 16.13 percent and the Sharpe ratio from 0.606 to 0.847. Grad-CAM and gradient contribution analyses indicate that successful settings use the sentiment channel meaningfully, whereas weaker modes largely ignore it.
keywords: ["technical indicators", "news sentiment", "GDELT", "FinBERT", "K-means clustering", "stock trading", "ensemble learning", "Grad-CAM", "Sharpe ratio"]

title: Output Steering for Latent Diffusion-Based MRI-to-CT Synthesis
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) and Computed Tomography (CT) are fundamental imaging modalities that provide complementary information for clinical assessment. However, CT acquisition may not always be preferred or available due to additional cost, workflow burden, and exposure to ionizing radiation. Therefore, reliably synthesizing a corresponding CT image from an available MRI scan is an important medical imaging problem. In this work, we present a conditional latent diffusion framework for MRI-to-CT synthesis. To improve the reliability of stochastic generation, the proposed framework incorporates a modular output steering mechanism that favors candidates better matched to target-domain characteristics. In this way, the diversity of diffusion-based synthesis is preserved while output consistency and realism are improved. Experimental results indicate that the proposed approach yields improved quantitative and qualitative performance over a baseline latent diffusion model. The proposed method achieved 26.49±2.19 dB PSNR and 87.89±2.59% SSIM, outperforming the baseline latent diffusion model.
keywords: ["latent diffusion models", "conditional image generation", "photorealism", "cross-modal image translation"]

title: Attention-based Operation-aware Neural Networks
abstract: Operation-aware Neural Networks (ONN) model feature interactions by learning operation-specific embeddings for pairs of input features. However, ONN considers all possible feature pair combinations, which leads to high computational complexity and may include many irrelevant interactions. In this work, we propose Attentional ONN (AttnONN), which incorporate an attention mechanism to selectively identify the most informative feature pairs. Instead of computing interactions for all feature combinations, AttnONN estimates pairwise importance scores using attention and selects the top-k feature pairs to construct cross-embeddings. Experimental results demonstrate that AttnONN improves efficiency and prediction performance with 0.17 relative improvement in AUC and 2.5% and 2.94% improvements in logloss and PRAUC respectively by avoiding unnecessary feature interactions while preserving the most informative ones. Online A/B testing results indicate improvements of 1.86% in TAV, 1.79% in RPM, and 2.17% in eCPM.
keywords: ["attention mechanism", "feature interaction", "computational efficiency", "online A/B testing", "targeted advertising"]

title: Private and Public Law Classification in Turkish Legal Texts Using Large Language Models
abstract: In Turkish legal texts, especially theses, terminology and writing style vary markedly across subfields, making it difficult for general-purpose language models to consistently and reliably distinguish private law from public law. In this study, domain-adaptive pretraining was performed on the BERTurk model using a large-scale legal text corpus compiled from open-access Turkish theses and journal articles. An MLP-based classification head was added on top of the adapted language model, and the resulting model was trained on a labeled dataset of theses in private and public law. In the experimental evaluations, models before (vanilla BERTurk) and after domain adaptation were compared using precision and macro-F1 scores. The results indicate that domain adaptation on legal texts improves the model’s contextual representations, yielding higher and more stable classification performance for distinguishing private law and public law.
keywords: ["private law", "public law", "legal text classification", "domain adaptation", "BERTurk", "large language models", "legal terminology", "Turkish theses", "MLP classifier"]

title: Class Token Fusion in Vision Transformers for Brain Cancer Classification
abstract: Accurate image classification plays a vital role in reliable brain cancer diagnosis. This study proposes a multi-scale class token fusion approach by integrating Vision Transformer models of different sizes, namely TinyViT, SmallViT, and BaseViT. Due to architectural differences, each model captures complementary feature representations. The extracted class tokens are projected into a shared feature space and fused to obtain a more discriminative representation. The fused features are then classified using a classifier aligned with the selected reference model, rather than relying on a single fixed architecture. This strategy effectively exploits complementary information across model scales, improving both feature diversity and generalization performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms individual models, achieving 98.70% accuracy, 99.89% AUC, and 98.65% F1-score.
keywords: ["vision transformer", "shared feature space", "medical image classification"]

title: Iris, Sclera, and Pupil Recognition in Low-Resource Settings: Zero-Shot Adaptation, Fine-Tuning, and Error Analysis of Pre-trained Models
abstract: Artificial intelligence has played a transformative role in recent years across many fields, particularly in medical disciplines. In this study, the performance of the pre-trained semantic segmentation architectures CLIPSeg and SAM3 was investigated in low-resource settings. Ocular images from the OpenEDS (Open Eye Dataset) dataset were utilized to comparatively evaluate the models in terms of both their zero-shot capabilities and their performance after fine-tuning for iris, sclera, and pupil segmentation. Furthermore, the sensitivity of the models to training dataset size was examined through an error analysis framework. The results demonstrated that neither pre-trained model achieved satisfactory performance under zero-shot conditions. However, model performance improved progressively with increasing amounts of training data and the application of fine-tuning.
keywords: ["iris segmentation", "sclera segmentation", "pupil segmentation", "zero-shot transfer", "fine-tuning", "SAM3", "resource-limited settings", "training data size", "error analysis"]

title: Computer Vision-Based Automatic Bookshelf Organization
abstract: Automated library inventory management faces a fundamental High-Noise, Low-Signal challenge, where complex book spine artwork disrupts traditional computer vision algorithms attempting full spine segmentation. To overcome the high computational overhead and feature hallucination inherent in these contemporary approaches, this paper introduces a lightweight, edge-ready Sticker-Centric vision pipeline. By isolating the high-contrast call number label rather than the entire physical book boundary, the proposed architecture employs a YOLOv11 Medium backbone for precise region-of-interest detection. Post-detection, a two-step Spatial Geometric Verification algorithm sequences the physical arrangement of volumes. To optimize optical character recognition (OCR), the pipeline utilizes an Image Super-Resolution module featuring 15-pixel adaptive padding, bicubic upscaling, and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE). Final text extraction is executed via a constraint-based EasyOCR configuration to reject non-alphanumeric noise. The proposed model achieves a highly robust 99.5 percent mean Average Precision at 50, 0.997 precision, and 0.999 recall on a segregated validation set, significantly outperforming current state-of-the-art methodologies.
keywords: ["library inventory management", "YOLOv11", "edge computing", "image super-resolution", "optical character recognition", "CLAHE", "EasyOCR"]

title: Detecting Breaking Changes in PROFINET GSDML Files Using Hybrid LLM and Deterministic Analysis
abstract: Detecting breaking changes in PROFINET device description files (GSDML) after firmware updates is an important but often manual task that may lead to compatibility issues in existing engineering projects. In this study, four different automated change detection approaches are compared using pairs of GSDML files belonging to 15 real industrial Ethernet switch device families. Deterministic methods (SHA256 based fingerprinting and XML difference analysis) can rapidly detect structural changes but cannot assess the breaking impact of changes on engineering projects. A large language model used alone was able to discover various types of breaking changes but produced inconsistent results in severity classification. Therefore, a hybrid architecture combining deterministic analysis with multi agent large language model evaluation is proposed, achieving reliable change detection.
keywords: ["PROFINET", "firmware updates", "large language models", "compatibility"]

title: Explainable Bad Check Risk Using Hybrid Machine Learning and Large Language Models in Natural Language
abstract: An explainable hybrid system model is proposed for detecting non-sufficient funds (NSF) check risks. Data leakage cleaning and feature engineering were applied to create a derived feature set. Multiple ensemble machine learning models were compared using stratified k-fold cross-validation, with LightGBM achieving the highest performance (F1-Makro: 0.7333; ROC-EAA: 0.9212). The best model’s predictions were presented to open-source large language models using zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting strategies to generate natural language risk explanations. Asymmetric score ranges and strategy-specific thresholds were designed to mitigate central tendency bias. A rule-based scoring system was developed as a baseline. With appropriate prompting strategies, large language models provided competitive results compared to both rule-based systems and direct classification; the best performance was achieved by Qwen 32B with chain-of-thought prompting (F1-Makro: 0.8670; Dengeli Doğruluk: 0.8776).
keywords: ["explainable AI", "hybrid machine learning", "large language models", "chain-of-thought prompting", "natural language explanations", "ensemble learning", "LightGBM", "feature engineering", "central tendency bias", "rule-based scoring", "Qwen"]

title: Detectability and Detection Characterization of Pseudorange Drift Anomalies in Commercial Multi-GNSS Receivers
abstract: The positioning integrity of GNSS receivers is threatened by slowly growing drift-type faults that gradually permeate the navigation solution. This paper presents an experimental characterization of the positioning and monitoring capabilities of three commercial-off-the-shelf multi-GNSS receivers against pseudorange drift anomalies. Under controlled laboratory conditions, single and double fault scenarios were evaluated based on detection latency and positioning error growth. Experimental results reveal distinct performance disparities among the internal integrity monitoring strategies; while some receivers exhibited significant positioning biases prior to detection, others maintained high accuracy through more stringent monitoring. The findings highlight a consistent lack of robust integrity monitoring for non-GPS constellations, revealing critical vulnerabilities in modern multi-GNSS positioning environments and emphasizing the need for resilient, constellation-agnostic navigation algorithms.
keywords: ["GNSS integrity monitoring", "multi-GNSS receivers", "positioning integrity"]

title: Design and ASIC Implementation of a RISC-V-Based SoC with an Active Hardware Shield
abstract: In invasive hardware attacks, adversaries aim to analyze the internal structures of integrated circuits to reveal the architecture of the circuit and extract critical information. Microprobing stations and Focused Ion Beam (FIB) devices, which are widely available in ASIC design laboratories, have significantly facilitated the execution of such invasive hardware attacks. To meet the increasing integration demands of the electronics industry, the System-on-Chip (SoC) design approach has become prominent, and these systems also require protection against similar security threats. This study presents the design and ASIC (Application-Specific Integrated Circuit) implementation of a dynamic hardware security shield integrated into a RISC-V-based SoC. The shield generates continuously refreshed bit patterns using randomness derived from a Simon 32/64-based random number generator and ring oscillators, enabling the detection of physical tampering attempts. A dedicated controller manages the generation, comparison, and alarm mechanisms of these patterns. The SoC is implemented in 65 nm TSMC technology targeting a clock frequency of 100 MHz and is verified to be free of DRC (Design Rule Check) violations. The shield module occupies approximately twelve percent of the core area. The results demonstrate that the proposed architecture provides an effective and compact protection mechanism against replay and bypass attacks.
keywords: ["hardware security", "RISC-V", "system-on-chip", "ring oscillator", "random number generators", "replay attacks", "focused ion beam", "65 nm CMOS"]

title: The Impact of Data Leakage on Brain Tumor Classification
abstract: Automatic classification of brain tumors from Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is important for early diagnosis and treatment planning. However, in widely used public datasets, improper data splitting strategies can lead to data leakage, resulting in performance estimates that are higher than the true generalization ability. Although this risk has been generally discussed in the literature, studies that systematically compare patient-independent splitting and slice-based splitting on the Figshare-based brain tumor dataset within the same experimental framework remain limited. In this study, eight deep learning models are evaluated on a Figshare-based dataset using 5-fold cross-validation. The findings show that patient-based independent splitting provides more realistic and reliable results, whereas slice-based splitting can overestimate the true generalization performance of the model.
keywords: ["data leakage", "brain tumor classification", "magnetic resonance imaging", "cross-validation", "generalization performance", "deep learning"]

title: Glucose Sensing Performance of a Realistic NKT Photonics LMA-10 Photonic Crystal Fiber Based Surface Plasmon Resonance Sensor
abstract: The aim of this study is to design a production-oriented photonic crystal fiber (PCF) based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) glucose sensor by modifying a commercially available PCF. Modifying a commercially available PCF removes the largest obstacle in front of commercial deployment of an SPR sensor. We have selected NKT Photonic LMA-10 PCF and modelled it in COMSOL Multiphysics for simulating the proposed modifications using full-vectorial finite element method. We have carved upper part of the original PCF structure until the top air holes disappear and a 40 nm gold layer is deposited to the flat surface to excite surface plasmon waves. Rather than pursuing the theoretical sensitivity of highly idealized and complex structures, this study achieves competitive sensitivity while ensuring the design remains optimized for practical, cost-effective manufacturing. The spectral sensitivity for the 1.338–1.341 refractive-index interval is reported as 1333 nm/RIU, for the 1.341–1.346 interval as 1600 nm/RIU and for the 1.346–1.358 interval as 2000nm/RIU with resolutions 7.5×10−5RIU, 6.0 × 10−5RIU, and 5.0 × 10−5RIU, respectively. For the same intervals the amplitude sensitivities of −118.18 RIU−1, −146.18 RIU−1, and −282.55 RIU−1are obtained.
keywords: ["glucose detection", "surface plasmon resonance biosensor", "photonic crystal fiber", "gold layer", "refractive index sensitivity", "amplitude sensitivity", "finite element method simulation", "sensor fabrication"]

title: Comparative Analysis of Rule-Based Image Filtering and Diffusion-Based Generative Inpainting for Controlled Hotel Room Manipulation
abstract: Online user reviews are an important source of information in the tourism and hospitality industry. This study proposes a region-based image manipulation framework for visualizing hotel user reviews. Object regions are detected using GroundingDINO and the Segment Anything Model (SAM), and are subsequently manipulated using rule-based filtering and Stable Diffusion inpainting. The generated images are evaluated through SSIM, PSNR, LPIPS, and a user study. Results indicate that rule-based filtering preserves structural similarity, whereas diffusion-based editing produces more realistic visual outcomes.
keywords: ["image inpainting", "diffusion models", "Stable Diffusion", "Grounding DINO", "Segment Anything Model", "image quality assessment", "user study"]

title: Face Frontalization Using Vision Transformers
abstract: This study proposes a novel Transformer-based framework for synthesizing high-quality frontal face images from profile views. Unlike conventional methods, the proposed approach FaceFrontViT leverages the self-attention mechanism to adaptively focus on sparse facial regions—such as the eyes, nose, and mouth—effectively modeling pose variations and long- range pixel dependencies based on structural symmetry. Within the framework, input images are transformed into patch-based representations incorporating linear embedding and positional encoding, which are subsequently processed through a Transformer encoder architecture. The encoder outputs are further refined by a convolutional reconstruction module to generate the final frontal images. Experimental results on Honda/UCSD recognition datasets demonstrate that our methodology outperforms existing GAN-based approaches and consistently produces high-fidelity frontal results.
keywords: ["vision transformer", "self-attention", "facial pose variation", "positional encoding", "face synthesis"]

title: Explainable AI-Based Credit Default Risk Modeling on Multi-Table Data
abstract: This study addresses the prediction of credit default risk using the Home Credit Default Risk dataset. Due to the approximately eight percent imbalanced class distribution in the data structure, an intensive feature engineering pipeline that reduces multiple tables to the customer level was applied before modeling. The implementation was designed to include behavioral summaries generated from external credit history, previous applications, installment behavior, credit card transactions, and POS cash records. Missing value handling, encoding, and multicollinearity reduction steps were performed on the obtained features. LightGBM was selected as the classification model, and the hyperparameters were optimized with Optuna under cross validation. In the best configuration, the mean AUC value was observed as 0.78682 and the mean PR AUC value as 0.28015. In order for the probabilities to be used more reliably in decision making processes, Platt scaling and SHAP based explainability analysis were applied.
keywords: ["explainable AI", "SHAP", "class imbalance", "feature engineering", "LightGBM", "Optuna hyperparameter optimization", "Platt scaling", "credit history", "multicollinearity"]

title: Input Quality Validation for Clinical NLP Tradeoffs Between Accuracy and Latency
abstract: Clinical NLP is challenging because medical text is often noisy, abbreviated, and inconsistent. This study evaluates machine learning and deep learning models, together with different text representations, including sparse features and dense embeddings, to validate free text entered by clinicians as a preprocessing step before downstream clinical NLP. We report both best overall models (high invalid recall) and deployment-oriented models (balancing recall with latency and throughput). We also test multilingual behavior using a Turkish dataset. Overall, XGBoost provides the best balance between detection quality and deployment speed, and FastText embeddings perform well, suggesting that subword-based representations help under typos and abbreviations.
keywords: ["clinical natural language processing", "accuracy-latency trade-off", "XGBoost", "FastText embeddings"]

title: Dynamic Clustering-Based Clinical Decision Support Approach for Patient Phenotyping in Mechanical Ventilation
abstract: Mechanical ventilation management in intensive care units is a complex clinical decision-making process due to patient heterogeneity and physiological variability. In this study, a multi-stage machine learning approach was developed to model patient states during the mechanical ventilation process using data-driven phenotypes. Ventilator and physiological parameters obtained from the MIMIC-III intensive care database were used in the analyses. Time-series data were transformed into feature vectors, missing values were completed using median imputation, and variables were standardized. Following autoencoder-based dimensionality reduction, the latent representations were clustered using a Gaussian Mixture Model, and eight ventilation phenotypes were identified. Phenotype transition analysis showed that patients progressed over time from unstable ventilation states to more stable conditions suitable for ventilator weaning. The proposed approach provides an interpretable clinical decision support framework that may assist ventilator weaning decisions in intensive care units.
keywords: ["mechanical ventilation", "patient phenotyping", "clinical decision support", "weaning from mechanical ventilation", "Gaussian mixture model clustering", "autoencoder dimensionality reduction", "time series feature extraction", "MIMIC-III", "intensive care", "model interpretability"]

title: Integration of Legacy PLC Systems into 5G Networks: An OAI-Based UE Interface Design
abstract: Although Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), which are widely used in conventional industrial automation systems, they do not inherently possess a 3GPP-compliant 5G UE architecture. This limitation results in architectural incompatibilities when PLC-based operational data is integrated into digital twin platforms over 5G infrastructures. This study proposes a UE-hosted operational technology (OT) gateway architecture that integrates S7-1200 PLCs into the 5G network via a Linux-based application running on 5G UE. In the proposed system, telemetry data collected from the PLC via Ethernet is processed in user space and transmitted to the data network through an IP-based PDU session that is established by the OAI UE. Validation experiments conducted in an industrial test environment demonstrate that PLC data streams can be reliably transported over the 5G PDU session. The proposed approach offers a practical way to integrate existing OT components into 5G-enabled digital twin systems, eliminating the need for hardware redesign.
keywords: ["programmable logic controller", "5G", "OAI", "industrial automation", "digital twin", "S7-1200 PLC", "telemetry data transmission", "Linux applications", "Industrial Internet of Things"]

title: LiDAR-Based Human Detection for Airports
abstract: Monitoring passenger flow in high-density areas such as airport terminals is critical for operational efficiency and security. Traditional camera-based systems pose challenges including privacy violations and dependence on lighting conditions. In this study, a privacy-focused, real-time, and end-to-end LiDAR-based 3D human detection and tracking system is proposed for airport passenger tracking. The developed architecture utilizes the VoxelNeXt model to process sparse point cloud data, and a 9-dimensional Kalman filter coupled with the Hungarian algorithm to ensure temporal continuity. Experimental analyses conducted using field data collected at study environment demonstrate that incorporating intensity information into the spatial point cloud data significantly improves detection performance, achieving a score of 95.9 in the APR40−50metric. The system, running on the Robot Operating System infrastructure, exhibits stable real-time performance on edge devices with limited hardware resources, achieving a processing speed of 10-11 frames per second with less than 50 MB of graphic memory consumption.
keywords: ["LiDAR", "human detection", "human tracking", "airport passenger flow", "point cloud processing", "Kalman filter", "Hungarian algorithm", "privacy-preserving monitoring", "sparse point clouds", "intensity data"]

title: Canary-Based Privacy Estimation for Federated MRI Generation
abstract: Federated learning (FL) offers a promising framework for collaborative medical imaging by enabling multiple institutions to train shared models without centralizing patient data. However, sharing model parameters may still cause leakage of sensitive information. Existing privacy auditing methods typically require repeated model retraining, limiting their practicality in high-cost medical imaging systems. To address this, this work presents a one-shot privacy auditing framework for federated MRI generation that estimates privacy leakage in a single training run. In the proposed approach, synthetic canary contributions that mimic client updates are introduced in model space, and membership-style privacy leakage is estimated via their alignment with the trained global model. Experiments on multi-site federated MRI generation show that the proposed framework provides practical and computationally efficient privacy estimates while offering meaningful insight into privacy–utility trade-offs.

title: REAL-CSI: Benchmarking DL Architectures for Wi-Fi CSI Human Activity Recognition
abstract: This paper presents the REAL-LAB CSI HAR Dataset, a publicly available Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) dataset for human activity recognition (HAR), together with a controlled deep learning benchmark. We contribute to two key gaps in prior work: the lack of synchronized, balanced datasets and the limited understanding of how architecture and model capacity influence performance. Using a microsecond-synchronized acquisition pipeline, we collect a multi-class dataset and evaluate seven neural architectures across four parameter scales under a multi-seed protocol. The results show that architectural inductive bias dominates model capacity: 2D convolutional networks achieve the best accuracy-efficiency trade-off (96.40%), while larger models often yield diminishing or negative returns. These findings highlight that effective CSI-HAR design depends more on architecture than scale. The dataset and benchmark provide a reproducible foundation for future research.
keywords: ["WiFi channel state information", "human activity recognition", "deep learning benchmark", "model capacity", "inductive bias", "accuracy-efficiency trade-off"]

title: A Polygon-Based Aircraft and Component Dataset: Studies on Classification, Context Prediction, and Component Detection
abstract: In the aviation industry, maintenance and repair operations are still often carried out manually. To contribute to the automation of these processes, this study proposes a new dataset that covers 19 different military aircraft types and 28 part categories, and is designed for multi-purpose use with polygon-based annotations. Unlike traditional bounding box approaches in the literature, 926 high-resolution images are annotated with over 10,000 polygons for the precise analysis of complex aircraft components, and enriched with contextual metadata such as viewport, assembly, and airborne status. The validity and challenging nature of the proposed dataset are demonstrated through comprehensive experiments using lightweight classification architectures suitable for local hardware (ConvNeXtV2, MobileOne), DINOv3-based multi-task context prediction resilient to class imbalance, and state-of-the-art YOLOv11/YOLO26 models for polygon segmentation.

title: Autonomous Food Quality Control Using Edge Computing and Centralized Server-Based Vision-Language Models
abstract: Autonomous quality control is of considerable importance in terms of maintaining production standards and reducing costs. This study proposes a system that monitors bakery products in real-time on the production line using an edge device and an artificial intelligence system located on a central server. Thanks to the optimized YOLO model on the edge device, the system detects food products, human hands, and cutting tools, and transmits the cleanest frames, free of obstructing elements, to the Vision Language Model (VLM) running on the central computer via the local network. The VLM model analyzes and presents to the user features such as burntness, uniformity, symmetry ratio, etc., on the food product. Experimental results show that the YOLO model can perform high-speed object tracking despite hardware limitations, and the VLM model can perform analysis with a high success rate. The architecture is configured to be scalable and can be integrated into a cloud infrastructure.
keywords: ["bakery products", "edge computing", "vision-language models", "YOLO", "object tracking", "central server", "burn detection", "cloud integration"]

title: Spectrogram-Based Analysis of Through-Wall Respiratory Micro-Doppler Using IF Data
abstract: In this study, intermediate frequency (IF) data obtained from continuous wave (CW) radar systems operating in the midfrequency bands were used to extract respiration-induced micro-Doppler signatures of targets located behind obstacles (e.g., a 15 cm brick wall, particleboard, etc.). The IF signals were downconverted to baseband through digital down conversion (DDC) and downsampling processes, followed by band-pass filtering in the respiration band defined as 0.3 Hz–1.5 Hz. Time– frequency analysis was performed using a spectrogram-based short-time Fourier transform, and respiratory frequency estimation was conducted using a maximum spectral energy tracking approach. The findings obtained from real experimental data demonstrate that low-amplitude micro-Doppler components can be reliably separated and indicate that the proposed method, with its low computational complexity, provides a feasible approach for real-time life detection in post-disaster search-andrescue and defense applications.
keywords: ["through-wall radar", "continuous wave radar", "spectrogram", "short-time Fourier transform", "life detection", "search and rescue", "digital down conversion", "bandpass filtering"]

title: QoS-Driven Snapshot Policy Modeling for Dynamic Network Slicing
abstract: This study presents a comparative machine learning analysis for modeling decision-making processes in dynamic network slicing within 6G networks. Experiments use the 6G Network Slicing QoS Dataset containing network telemetry and Quality of Service (QoS) indicators. Two tasks are considered: (i) prediction of the resource allocation decision and (ii) multi-class classification of the operational network state. Several models, including Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTrees, Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Support Vector Machines (SVM), are evaluated under a unified experimental protocol. Performance is measured using accuracy, precision, recall, and macro-F1 metrics. Results indicate that tree-based ensemble methods achieve strong predictive performance for both resource allocation decisions and QoS-driven network state modeling. While several ensemble learning methods achieved near-perfect performance in the resource allocation task, LightGBM achieved the best results in the network state classification task with 0.99 accuracy and 0.98 macro-F1.
keywords: ["dynamic network slicing", "6G", "quality of service", "network telemetry", "tree-based ensemble models", "LightGBM", "XGBoost", "CatBoost"]

title: Noise-guided Masking for Image-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures
abstract: In masked image modeling methods, both data-adaptive and data-independent masking strategies are employed. While noise-guided masking strategies that are data-independent have been observed to improve generative models such as Masked Autoencoders (MAE), their impact on non-generative frameworks remains unexplored. This work fills this gap by adapting noise-guided masking to the Image-based Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (I-JEPA). Our method, which guides the selection of regions to mask using spectrally filtered noise improves training efficiency by 25–30% while matching or exceeding multi-block masking performance in linear probing on ImageNet-1K.
keywords: ["masked image modeling", "training efficiency", "linear probing", "ImageNet-1K", "image representation learning"]

title: Analysis and Optimization of Machine Unlearning Approaches: A Hybrid Perspective
abstract: Legal regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation in Europe and the Personal Data Protection Law in Turkey now allow individuals to request that their personal data be removed from relevant models. The resulting concept of Machine Unlearning enables the elimination of the effect of specific data samples or classes on the relevant model, as requested. This study evaluates and compares important methods in the literature of Machine Unlearning field. As a result of these tests, the weaknesses of these methods were identified, and a hybrid Machine Unlearning method that minimizes these weaknesses was presented. Considering the comparisons and tests performed, it was observed that it almost completely removed the effect of a specific data class on the model, while slightly affecting the accuracy rate of the remaining data.
keywords: ["machine unlearning", "personal data protection", "GDPR", "personal data protection law", "model retraining", "data privacy"]

title: Analysis of the Diagnostic Value of Standard Webcam-Based Eye Tracking and Dynamic Video Distractors in ADHD
abstract: In the digital age, the intensification of visual stimuli places significant pressure on individuals' attention mechanisms and focusing capacities. This study analyzes the potential of fast-paced, dynamic videos (e.g., YouTube), which increasingly shorten attention spans, to trigger ADHD symptoms using a cost-effective eye-tracking system with a standard webcam. In a preliminary study with twenty participants, fluctuations in task disengagement and commission error were analyzed using the Continuous Performance Test (CPT) with and without video. The results showed that despite behavioral similarity in the baseline condition, the dynamic video CPT condition visually captivated the ADHD group, dramatically disengaging them from the task and potentially separating the groups. This innovative paradigm transforms modern distractors into an objective and accessible diagnostic tool.
keywords: ["attention deficit hyperactivity disorder", "eye tracking", "webcam-based eye tracking", "visual attention", "task disengagement", "commission errors", "continuous performance test", "attention span", "ADHD diagnosis", "visual distraction"]

title: ADMM-Based Phase Retrieval
abstract: Phase retrieval is a fundamental inverse problem that aims to reconstruct an image from Fourier magnitude measurements. In this paper, an alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) based phase retrieval method is developed, which can be interpreted as a generalized alternating projection framework. The developed method has closed-form and efficient update steps. In addition, the tolerance parameter for data consistency is updated during iterations by relating it to the measurement noise. The results obtained for different image sizes and SNR levels show that the proposed method provides promising reconstruction performance.
keywords: ["phase retrieval", "alternating direction method of multipliers", "image reconstruction", "data consistency", "measurement noise", "inverse problems"]

title: Detection of Incorrect Named Entities in Automatic Speech Recognition Outputs Using a Multi-Task Transformer-Based Approach
abstract: In recent years, automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems developed have been able to produce highly accurate results in converting speech into text. However, especially in open-source ASR systems, error rates in recognizing named entities remain relatively high, and this situation makes the use of ASR outputs for different purposes difficult. In this study, a transformer-based approach is proposed to detect named entities that are incorrectly translated from speech to text within ASR outputs. A multi-task transformer-based model was fine-tuned to detect incorrect named entities and to predict their types. The results show that a token classification language model integrated with the conditional random fields approach can detect incorrectly translated named entities with 86% accuracy and an F1-score of 0.81, and can also identify the types of these incorrectly translated named entities with a high accuracy rate.
keywords: ["named entity recognition", "speech recognition errors", "multi-task transformer", "conditional random fields", "token classification", "speech-to-text"]

title: Improved Blind Video Super-resolution with Degradation-Aware Reconstruction
abstract: Video super-resolution (VSR) aims to reconstruct high-resolution frames from low-resolution sequences. However, many existing methods rely on non-blind assumptions where the degradation process is known. In real-world videos, degradation processes are often unknown and complex. In this work, a degradation-aware reconstruction approach is proposed to adapt a strong non-blind (VSR) architecture to blind scenarios. The method includes a degradation estimator and a degradation-guided weighted residual refinement mechanism, trained via a progressive multi-phase strategy. Evaluated on the Vid4 dataset, the proposed approach achieves up to 3.59 dB improvement in PSNR compared to the baseline MIA-VSR.
keywords: ["degradation estimation", "unknown degradation"]

title: ISL-Based NTN for Industrial IoT (IIoT) Applications: A Wind Turbine Monitoring Case Study in Türkiye
abstract: The widespread adoption of renewable energy sources globally has highlighted the critical need for sophisticated monitoring and control systems tailored to these infrastructures. In this regard, an Industrial IoT (IIoT)-based hybrid communication architecture has been developed, based on a comprehensive testbed utilizing real telemetry data from wind turbines across Türkiye. This architecture integrates a three-tier hybrid communication network, operationally connecting the wind turbines to Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites at an altitude of 600 km, a Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) satellite and a terrestrial ground station in one structure. The end-to-end satellite simulation analyses have demonstrated that the integrated structure ensures operational continuity despite meteorological or atmospheric disruptions. It successfully meets the stringent 10−5Bit Error Rate (BER) requirement, maintains robust link margins of 6.7 dB and 10.0 dB even under challenging conditions, and keeps end-to-end latency below 300 ms.

title: Comparative Analysis of 5 Different Aggregation Methods in Federated Learning for Breast Cancer Diagnosis
abstract: Privacy of data in machine learning studies constitutes one of the most critical challenges, particularly in domains involving sensitive information such as healthcare. In this study, a Federated Learning approach, enabling model training on edge devices without transferring data to a central server is investigated in the context of breast cancer. A heterogeneous data distribution simulation environment is constructed using breast cancer MR images derived from the MIAS and INbreast datasets. Within this setting, a medium-depth Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model is designed to evaluate the performance of five different Federated Learning aggregation methods, and a comparative analysis is conducted.
keywords: ["federated learning", "aggregation methods", "breast cancer diagnosis", "data privacy", "edge devices", "heterogeneous data distributions", "breast MRI", "convolutional neural networks", "MIAS dataset", "INbreast dataset"]

title: Anomaly Detection on Resource-Constrained IoT Devices Using an Energy-Efficient Dynamic Artificial Intelligence Architecture
abstract: Despite their ubiquity, IoT devices often lack robust security. Deploying standard AI security software to edge devices is challenging due to hardware constraints. This study proposes a low-cost solution by adapting the ADEPOS architecture to cybersecurity. Tested on an ESP32, the hybrid architecture uses a lightweight Decision Tree to filter normal traffic and an expert Fast Artificial Neural Network for suspicious data. The system achieved 96.50% accuracy, providing 23.3% net energy savings with a 94-microsecond average processing time compared to the baseline.
keywords: ["anomaly detection", "Internet of Things security", "resource-constrained devices", "edge computing", "energy efficiency", "ESP32 microcontroller", "lightweight AI", "network traffic classification"]

title: Spectral–Spatial Feature Learning in Multispectral Plant Detection: A Comparison of 2D+ and 3D CNN Architectures
abstract: Plant detection in multispectral images is an important process requiring effective analysis of spectral signatures and spatial patterns. In this study, the detection of horsetail (Equisetum telmateia), a plant species valuable for both medicinal and agricultural purposes, is addressed using multispectral aerial imagery. A detection system focused on achieving a high recall rate is proposed, and the images are subjected to binary classification through local patches. For performance analysis, a 3D convolutional neural network (3D CNN) that processes spectral and spatial dimensions simultaneously is compared with a 2D+ hybrid CNN architecture that handles these dimensions sequentially. Experiments conducted on approximately 300 multispectral images obtained from the Black Sea region show that the 3D model achieves higher recall in plant detection, but its precision is lower than that of the 2D+ model. In addition, it was observed that the 2D+ model has a shorter inference time.
keywords: ["plant detection", "multispectral imagery", "Equisetaceae", "Equisetum telmateia", "3D convolutional neural networks", "aerial imagery", "binary classification", "local patches", "inference latency", "Black Sea region"]

title: The Effect of Morphological Normalization on Retrieval Performance and Answer Accuracy in Turkish RAG Systems
abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique that enables large language models to leverage external knowledge sources to improve response quality. This study investigates the effect of morphological normalization on document retrieval and answer quality in Turkish RAG systems. Three indexes were constructed on the RAGTURK dataset: (i) RAW, using surface-form text, (ii) LEMMA, applying full lemmatization, and (iii) HYBRID, combining both representations. Retrieval performance was measured using Recall and MRR, while RAG answer quality was evaluated with ROUGE and BERTScore metrics. Results show that lemmatization does not improve dense retrieval performance for the multilingual embedding model used in this study, and leads to consistent degradation across all query categories. Similarly, RAG answer quality declined under normalization, with RAW indexing achieving the highest performance throughout. These findings suggest that modern multilingual models are capable of implicitly capturing Turkish morphological variation, and that additional normalization is not always necessary.
keywords: ["retrieval-augmented generation", "lemmatization", "Turkish language", "document retrieval", "answer quality", "dense retrieval", "morphological variation"]

title: A Channel Modeling and Estimation Study for Sub-THz Ultra-Massive MIMO UAV Links
abstract: Sub-Terahertz (sub-THz) 6G networks promise high-capacity unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications; however, rapid mobility and high-frequency propagation complicate ultra-massive MIMO (UM-MIMO) channel estimation. This paper presents a ray-tracing-aided channel modeling and machine learning-based estimation study for sub-THz UAV communications. Realistic channel realizations are generated from ray-tracing-based propagation paths and extended to UM-MIMO representations. To capture channel variability in UAV scenarios, stochastic fading and controlled angular perturbations are incorporated. Estimation is performed using a model-driven deep learning architecture based on a fixed-point network with orthogonal approximate message passing (FPN-OAMP). Results show stable convergence and consistent accuracy improvement with increasing signal-to-noise ratio, highlighting the effectiveness of combining physics-based channel generation with model-driven learning for sub-THz UAV systems.
keywords: ["sub-terahertz communication", "ultra-massive MIMO", "UAV communication", "channel modeling", "channel estimation", "ray tracing", "6G"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Emotion Recognition from EEG Signals: A Hybrid Architecture with EEGNet and Transformer
abstract: Automated recognition of human emotions has be-come a significant research area in fields such as brain-computer interfaces, human-computer interaction, and affective computing. Emotion recognition from electroencephalography (EEG) signals is considered a vital approach as it provides direct access to emotional states through brain activity. However, the high dimensionality, low signal-to-noise ratio, and complex spatio-temporal structure of EEG data pose challenges for developing effective and generalizable models. In this study, we propose a hybrid deep learning architecture for the EEG-based emotion classification problem that integrates domain-specific information directly into the model. Using the widely recognized SEED dataset, raw EEG signals are processed through end-to-end learnable layers instead of predefined feature extraction methods. The proposed architecture combines an EEGNet-based feature extraction block with a Transformer encoder. While EEGNet generates representations suitable for the temporal and spatial structure of EEG signals, the Transformer models long-term temporal dependencies using its multi-head attention mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed EEGNet + Transformer approach achieves an accuracy of approximately 96.31% on the SEED dataset, offering a competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in the literature.
keywords: ["EEG-based emotion recognition", "EEGNet", "Transformer encoder", "hybrid deep learning model", "SEED dataset", "EEG feature extraction", "multi-head attention", "affective computing", "brain-computer interface", "emotion classification"]

title: The Dual Effect of Cholesterol in Photoacoustic Imaging: Structural Deviation and Acoustic Damping Analysis in Hydrophilic and Hydrophobic Liposomal Agents
abstract: Photoacoustic imaging (PAI) provides tumor detection in theranostic approaches. Success depends on stable contrast agents. Cholesterol is added to enhance liposome stability; however, its signal damping effect remains poorly understood. In this study, hydrophilic gold nanoparticles (AuNP) and hydrophobic BODIPY dye were encapsulated in liposomes with varying cholesterol ratios (0%, 25%, 35%). During the 14-day monitoring, BODIPY produced significantly stronger photoacoustic signals compared to AuNP. Chemical structure directly affects encapsulation stability. Hydrophobic BODIPY integrates into the lipid bilayer, exhibiting low deviation. In contrast, hydrophilic AuNP, trapped in the aqueous core, showed heterogeneous distribution and high variance in cholesterol-free environments. In liposomes with 35% cholesterol, increased membrane rigidity restricted thermoelastic expansion, resulting in signal damping.A linear signal loss was observed in both agents after 14 days, with the strongest signal maintained in the BODIPY formulation. In summary, cholesterol optimization in carrier liposome design is as critical as the choice of contrast agent.
keywords: ["cholesterol", "liposomes", "photoacoustic imaging", "contrast media", "BODIPY dyes", "gold nanoparticles", "liposome stability", "structural deviation", "acoustic damping", "membrane rigidity", "thermoelastic expansion", "theranostics", "encapsulation stability"]

title: Optimization Algorithm for Sidelobe Suppression in FDA Radar with Hamming Frequency Window
abstract: In the literature on Frequency Diverse Array (FDA) radar systems, frequency offset strategies and amplitude weight optimization approaches are addressed independently. This study demonstrates that sidelobe levels can be suppressed by applying amplitude weight optimization to a Hamming-based frequency offset scheme that produces high Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR). The proposed method is based on solving a generalized Rayleigh quotient problem, which aims to maximize the energy within the joint range-angle region. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed optimization algorithm for the Hamming frequency-windowed FDA radar system provides an SINR gain of 12.69 dB and a 23 dB improvement in sidelobe levels compared to uniformly weighted FDA systems, while introducing only a limited increase in beamwidth of 0.54° in the angular domain and 0.5 km in the range domain.
keywords: ["frequency diverse array radar", "sidelobe suppression", "generalized Rayleigh quotient", "SINR", "beamwidth"]

title: MiniROCKET-2D for Fast Image Classification
abstract: We present MiniROCKET-2D, a deterministic and training-efficient image classification pipeline designed for CPU-only settings. Instead of learning convolution kernels with backpropagation, the method applies fixed sparse 3x3 kernel patterns with multi-scale dilations and summarizes responses by Proportion of Positive Values (PPV). This design eliminates convolution weight learning and keeps computation lightweight while preserving spatial structure. We evaluate the method on diverse benchmarks (MNIST, Fashion-MNIST, KMNIST, USPS, CIFAR10-gray, EMNIST, EuroSAT, and Blood-Cells) against raw pixels, HOG, LBP, PCA, random projection, and MiniROCKET-1D features using Ridge, SVM, and Random Forest classifiers. Results show that MiniROCKET-2D is consistently competitive and often superior under linear classifiers, with strong gains on structurally rich datasets such as Blood-Cells and EMNIST. The framework offers an effective speed–accuracy balance for resource-limited experiments and embedded/edge-oriented workflows.
keywords: ["image classification", "training efficiency", "linear classifiers", "edge computing", "embedded systems", "blood cell classification", "EMNIST"]

title: FUSE-RAG: A Unified Architecture for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Large language models may suffer from insufficient context use and unsupported generation in question answering tasks that require external knowledge. This study compares the main strategies affecting retrieval and generation performance in retrieval-augmented generation systems within a common experimental setting. In addition to a standard dense retrieval baseline, we evaluate multi-query, hypothetical document, hypothetical question, sparse-dense hybrid retrieval, and chunk compression, and we also propose an integrated method (FUSERAG) that combines these components. Experiments are conducted on a dataset containing 223 documents, 7933 chunks, and 1488 question-answer instances. Results show that the proposed method achieves the highest Mean Reciprocal Rank, nDCG at 5, and recall at 5 at the retrieval level, while the sparse-dense hybrid approach yields the best generation results.
keywords: ["retrieval-augmented generation", "question answering", "dense retrieval", "sparse retrieval", "large language models", "external knowledge retrieval"]

title: Federated Learning-Based Counterfactual Explanations for Resolving the Privacy-Explainability Dilemma in IoT Intrusion Detection
abstract: Makine öğrenmesi tabanlı saldırı tespit sistemleri, IoT ağlarının güvenliğinde kritik bir rol üstlenmektedir; ancak sistemlerin kara kutu yapısı, kararların analistler tarafından yorumlanmasını güçleştirmektedir. Öte yandan, merkezi eğitim yaklaşımlarının gerektirdiği veri toplama süreci gizlilik riskleri taşımaktadır. Bu çalışma, iki soruna birlikte çözüm sunan FedCF-IoT çerçevesini tanıtmaktadır. FedCF-IoT, diferansiyel gizlilik mekanizmalarıyla güçlendirilmiş federe öğrenme ortamında karşıolgusal açıklamalar üreterek ham veri paylaşımı olmadan açıklanabilir tahminler sağlamaktadır. Edge-IIoTset veri kümesi ile 15 sınıflı saldırı tespitinde %99,38 doğruluk (%93,21 makro F1-skoru) elde edilmiş ve karşıolgusal geçerlilik %98,8’e ulaşmıştır. Çalışmada bulgu olarak, diferansiyel gizlilik gürültüsü karşıolgusal geçerliliği düşürmek yerine %93,2’den %98,8’e yükseltmiştir. Federe öğrenme, merkezi eğitime kıyasla yalnızca %0,11–0,17'lik doğruluk kaybıyla gizliliğin korunabildiğini göstermektedir.
keywords: ["federated learning", "counterfactual explanations", "privacy-preserving machine learning", "differential privacy", "IoT intrusion detection", "explainability", "Edge-IIoT dataset", "attack classification"]

title: Prediction of Climate Change-Induced Floods Using Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: Increasing intense and localized rainfall due to climate change significantly elevates the risk of floods, causing severe human and economic losses. In this study, 24-hour time series–based models were developed using discharge and precipitation data from selected hydrological stations to forecast flood risk. To ensure comparability among models, the input window was fixed at 168 hours (1 week) across all architectures. Initially, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, commonly used in time series forecasting, were applied; however, due to the rarity of flood events (less than 1%), these models were observed to inadequately represent extreme events. Consequently, a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) architecture was employed as a baseline for comparison. Finally, a Seq2Seq model enhanced with an attention mechanism was developed, and experimental results demonstrated that this approach achieved superior predictive performance compared to the other models.
keywords: ["flood forecasting", "climate change", "extreme rainfall", "discharge time series", "LSTM", "multilayer perceptron", "flood risk prediction", "hydrological stations", "rare event prediction"]

title: Performance Analysis of SMOTE and Feature Selection Methods in Traumatic Brain Injury Stage Classification
abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a medical condition requiring urgent intervention to preserve vital functions and prevent permanent damage. Machine learning approaches make it possible to classify the severity of TBI more quickly and objectively than with current methods. In this study, two datasets comprising 3 and 4 classes were created using data from 1,228 patients collected by the Department of Neurosurgery at Trakya University. The SMOTE method was used to address class imbalance in the dataset, and feature selection algorithms were employed to identify subsets of features that were more discriminatory. For model development, k-Nearest Neighbor (kNN), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) models were run and their performances were compared. It was observed that the SVM model achieved the highest accuracy success rate of %90.65 with feature selection.
keywords: ["traumatic brain injury", "SMOTE", "class imbalance", "feature selection", "support vector machine", "k-nearest neighbors", "random forest", "multilayer perceptron", "medical data classification"]

title: Latent Diffusion-Based Image Generation from WiFi Channel State Information
abstract: Reconstructing images from WiFi channel state information (CSI) is a privacy-preserving sensing paradigm that eliminates cameras. LatentCSI maps CSI into the latent space of a pretrained diffusion model via a CNN, but this single-frame approach ignores temporal dependencies. This work improves LatentCSI in three directions: a BiLSTM encoder capturing temporal dependencies across consecutive CSI frames, a multi-task activity head structuring the latent representation, and transfer learning accelerating convergence. On the MM-Fi dataset, the proposed multi-task BiLSTM achieves a 50.1% improvement in FID over the original LatentCSI. Controlled experiments show that the BiLSTM learns genuine temporal patterns rather than acting as a simple moving average.
keywords: ["WiFi channel state information", "latent diffusion models", "privacy-preserving sensing", "temporal dependencies", "multi-task learning", "transfer learning"]

title: Edge AI Integration Architecture for the Internet of Things
abstract: The rapid development and current productive use of artificial intelligence models have introduced new integration scenarios and potential. In light of these developments, various opportunities have arisen for the use of generative models in industrial environments, including their potential contributions to automation. However, these opportunities raise questions about the usability and adaptability of generative models in industrial settings with limited device capabilities. This study proposes an intelligent system design for human-operator and artificial intelligence interaction. The necessary models for this system were evaluated using zero-shot and few-shot settings. As a main contribution, the industrial uses and interoperability of language models such as Gemma and Llama were evaluated. Our study contributes to the evaluation of dynamic assistants, such as generative artificial intelligence, as an industrial agent.
keywords: ["edge AI", "Internet of Things", "generative AI", "industrial automation", "human-AI interaction", "language models", "Gemma", "llamas", "zero-shot learning", "few-shot learning", "industrial agents", "interoperability", "resource-constrained devices"]

title: Non-invasive Glucose Sensing Using a Patch Antenna for Biomedical Applications
abstract: Microwave-based glucose sensing has attracted significant attention for non-invasive glucose monitoring. This study proposes a slotted patch antenna operating in the ISM band to detect variations in the dielectric properties of biological tissues associated with changes in blood glucose levels. The antenna incorporates strategically designed slots to enhance electromagnetic field interaction with the sensing region. When a human finger is placed on the antenna surface, the electromagnetic field penetrates the underlying tissues, enabling sensitivity to permittivity variations in blood. These variations lead to measurable shifts in the antenna’s characteristics, particularly its resonant frequency. Electromagnetic simulations are performed using CST Microwave Studio.A three-layer biological model consisting of skin, fat, and blood is developed to realistically represent human tissue. Additionally, the Cole–Cole model is employed to accurately characterize the frequency-dependent dielectric properties of blood. The proposed approach is experimentally validated using glucose solutions.

title: Impact of Normalization Techniques on Mitosis Detection in H&E Stained Histopathology Images
abstract: The aim of this study is to investigate the impact of stain normalization approaches on mitosis detection in histopathology images. Variations in staining and imaging conditions can significantly affect model performance, yet normalization is often applied without a clear understanding of its contribution. To address this, seven widely used stain normalization methods are applied to the ICPR12 and ICPR14 datasets, and their effects are evaluated using YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 models. The results show that stain normalization generally improves detection performance in many cases; however, no single approach consistently outperforms others, and its effectiveness depends on the dataset, model, and normalization method.
keywords: ["stain normalization", "mitosis detection", "YOLOv5", "YOLOv8", "object detection", "staining variability"]

title: Design Of Low Noise - High Gain Tri-Band LNA For Wi-Fi 7 Applications
abstract: This paper presents a low-noise amplifier operating in compliance with the Wi-Fi 7 standard, which has been developed in recent years and is also known as IEEE 802.11be. A differential and inductively degenerated cascode structure is selected as the topology. A 65 nm process and a 1.2 V supply voltage is used. For multi-link operation, which is a target for Wi-Fi 7, three different amplifiers are designed with appropriate values for 2.4 GHz, 5 GHz, and 6 GHz. The main objective of this study is to achieve higher gain and a lower noise figure compared to existing amplifiers. At the 2.4 GHz resonance frequency, a gain of 21.4 dB and a noise figure of 1.6 dB is achieved. An IIP3 value of -1.44 dBm and a bandwidth of 672 MHz is obtained.
