title: Comparison of Real and Imagined Movements in EEG Signals: Feature and Channel Based Analysis
abstract: In this study, cortical activation differences between real and imagined movements were investigated using EEG data. Statistical, model-based, and frequency-domain features were extracted, and significance analyses were performed using a Paired-sample t-test. The results showed that MLE_b, CRB_mu, CRB_b, RMS, Peak-to-Peak, Variance, and DeltaP features provided the highest discriminative power. Significant differences were observed in the frontal, central, parietal, and occipital regions, while Delta, Theta, and Alpha band powers were found to be significant across broad cortical areas. The findings indicate that real movements generate stronger cortical activation than imagined movements and may contribute to the identification of important channels and features for EEG-based motor imagery applications.
keywords: ["motor imagery", "cortical activation", "EEG feature extraction", "EEG channel selection", "maximum likelihood estimation", "Cramer-Rao lower bound", "frequency-domain features", "EEG band power", "motor imagery classification"]

title: A Multi-Objective Association for Post-Disaster UAVs with ISAC-Enabled UAV Swarms
abstract: Natural disasters severely damage terrestrial communication infrastructure, hindering timely rescue coordination. This paper proposes an integrated sensing and communication-enabled non-terrestrial network architecture that repurposes existing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms for post-disaster emergency management. Upon disaster occurrence, UAV swarms are dynamically retasked to provide aerial sensing and rescue coordination, while post-disaster UAVs are deployed to deliver aid. A multi-objective post-disaster UAV association framework is proposed to optimally associate post-disaster UAVs with existing swarms by jointly optimizing disaster intensity, air-to-air communication reliability, and rescue travel time. Simulation results confirm up to 36 percent reduction in rescue delay, lower bit-error-rate, and reduced energy consumption over baseline strategies, validating the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
keywords: ["UAV swarms", "integrated sensing and communication", "disaster response", "rescue coordination", "non-terrestrial networks", "air-to-air communication", "disaster intensity", "energy consumption", "multi-objective optimization"]

title: Data Saturation in Low-Resource TTS Fine-Tuning
abstract: When fine-tuning large language models, the assumption is that more data means better results. This principle is often extended to text-to-speech (TTS) fine-tuning, yet remains underexplored, particularly for low-resource languages where high-quality data is difficult to obtain. In this work, the "more data is better" phenomenon is investigated for Turkish TTS using XTTS v2 by incrementally increasing training data. Speech quality is evaluated using multiple metrics, including UTMOS, NISQA, and an LLM-based TTS evaluation framework. For the LLM-based evaluation, a multimodal language model (Gemini) was prompted to assess Turkish-specific pronunciation, naturalness, and synthesis artifacts on a calibrated 1-10 scale. Results suggest that for TTS fine-tuning on non-mainstream languages, modest data investments may achieve near-optimal quality.
keywords: ["data saturation", "low-resource languages", "training data size", "speech quality assessment", "LLM-based evaluation", "multimodal language models", "pronunciation"]

title: An Anomaly Detection Method Augmented by Domain Knowledge and Predictive Residuals
abstract: Predictive maintenance in industrial systems requires early and reliable detection of anomalous behavior from highdimensional sensor data. In railway air production units, failures often emerge gradually due to complex interactions between physical variables. In this paper, we propose a physics-informed early warning framework combining domain-driven feature engineering with forecasting-based residual analysis. The proposed approach integrates efficiency-based degradation metrics and LSTM residuals into a stacked attention autoencoder. Experiments on the MetroPT-3 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves detection lead time and event-level recall compared to baseline models.
keywords: ["anomaly detection", "predictive maintenance", "physics-informed machine learning", "domain knowledge", "feature engineering", "sensor data", "early warning"]

title: PID Controlled False Alarm Probability Stabilization in Radar Systems
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) detection environment that regulates the false alarm probability (PFA) using a closed-loop PID controller. Unlike classical Cell Average CFAR (CA-CFAR) schemes with fixed threshold scaling factors, the proposed approach dynamically adjusts the scaling parameter based on real-time PFA measurements under non-stationary noise conditions. A dynamic radar environment with time-varying clutter statistics is simulated to evaluate system performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method successfully stabilizes the false alarm probability around a predefined target value while preserving reliable target detection performance. The study highlights the limitations of fixed-parameter CFAR and illustrates the benefits of feedback-based adaptive detection architectures.
keywords: ["constant false alarm rate detection", "PID control", "non-stationary clutter", "radar target detection"]

title: Time Series Classification via Enriched Visibility Graph Feature Extraction
abstract: Deep learning models for time series classification can learn powerful temporal representations directly from raw signals; however, they do not explicitly encode structural information about the series' topological properties. In this work, we propose the Visibility Graph Dual-Branch Temporal Encoder (VG-DBTE) to address this limitation. The proposed architecture augments any temporal encoder with a plug-in branch that integrates a structural feature vector, extracted from the degree sequences of the Natural and Horizontal Visibility Graphs, via a residual connection and an input-dependent gating mechanism. The feature set comprises global degree statistics, peak-anchored asymmetry descriptors, valley degree, and run-length descriptors. Experiments conducted on four UCR datasets across five encoder architectures — MLP, RNN, LSTM, Bidirectional LSTM, and Transformer — demonstrate that the proposed method consistently improves classification accuracy over the baseline encoders.
keywords: ["time series classification", "visibility graph", "horizontal visibility graph", "degree sequences", "structural features", "UCR time series archive"]

title: Illumination-Aware Local Texture and Edge Preservation for Visible-Infrared Image Fusion
abstract: This study proposes a luminance-guided texture edge analysis for quality assessment in visible (RGB) and infrared (IR) image fusion. Existing metrics mostly rely on global evaluation and fail to capture local detail preservation. The proposed method utilizes a luminance map to perform locally weighted gradient-based similarity analysis. In addition, the metric is incorporated as a loss function component and evaluated on SwinFusion and TCDGNet models. Experimental results on LLVIP and RoadScene datasets demonstrate that the proposed approach provides more discriminative evaluation and improves fusion performance.
keywords: ["infrared and visible image fusion", "fusion quality assessment", "texture preservation", "edge preservation", "loss function design", "multimodal image fusion"]

title: IMU-Assisted Blind Calibration for the Blue-Shift Effect-based MC-VLC/P Systems
abstract: Although multi-color visible light communication and positioning (MC-VLC/P) systems offer high accuracy, existing methods require prior and exact knowledge of the spectral characteristics of the hardware. This study proposes inertial measurement unit (IMU) assisted blind calibration method that eliminates this prior knowledge requirement. In the proposed architecture, the non-linear relationship between the optical channel eigenvalues and the angle of incidence (AoI) is learned using IMU data obtained by randomly tilting the receiver at a single unknown location. Simulation studies demonstrate that the proposed system provides cm-level positioning accuracy for different filter sets. This developed structure offers hardware independence, which significantly enhances practical application flexibility.
keywords: ["visible light positioning", "inertial measurement unit", "blind calibration", "angle of incidence", "hardware independence"]

title: Comparative Analysis of Chunking Strategies for Turkish Multimodal RAG Systems
abstract: Geleneksel İçerik Erişimine Dayalı Üretim (RAG) sistemleri; tablo, grafik ve düzensiz yerleşimler içeren karmaşık belgelerle çalışırken bilgi bütünlüğünü korumada genellikle yetersiz kalmaktadır. Bu yapısal sorunların üstesinden gelmek amacıyla bu çalışma, dört farklı parçalama stratejisinin karşılaştırmalı bir analizini sunmaktadır: Basit (Naive), Dinamik, Görsel ve Hibrit RAG. Hibrit mimari; tablo hiyerarşisini koruyan yapıya duyarlı akıllı metin işleme ile hedef odaklı görsel vektör üretimini entegre eden çok aşamalı bir iş akışına dayanmaktadır. Bu stratejilerin performansı; 46 kurumsal entegre rapordan ve 1.380 soru-cevap çiftinden oluşan bir veri seti üzerinde, "LLM-as-a-Judge" yaklaşımı kullanılarak Bağlam Kapsama (Context Recall), Hassasiyet (Precision) ve Doğruluk (Accuracy) metrikleri üzerinden değerlendirilmiştir. Sonuçlar, Hibrit RAG’ın tek modlu sistemlerin sınırlamalarını etkili bir şekilde aştığını göstermektedir. En iyi tek modlu temel yönteme kıyasla Bağlam Kapsama’da 0,82’ye, Hassasiyet’te 0,82’ye ve Cevap Doğruluğu’nda 0,71’e ulaşılmıştır.
keywords: ["retrieval-augmented generation", "chunking strategies", "LLM-as-a-judge", "precision", "answer accuracy", "Turkish language", "corporate reporting", "question answering"]

title: CBAM-RFTOA: Channel–Spatial Attention Based RF Type Classification of Radar System from RF–TOA Patterns
abstract: Radio Frequency (RF) and Time of Arrival (TOA) are fundamental pulse descriptor parameters used for radar RF type identification. Accurate classification of RF–TOA patterns is essential for reliable frequency pattern of threat discrimination in Electronic Support (ESM) systems, yet noise, frequency shifts, and missing/spurious pulses make this task challenging. This study proposes a deep learning–based method that converts RF–TOA scatter data into a single-channel visual representation for classification. The data generation process considers two simulation modes: without noise/dropout and with noise/dropout. A neural architecture enhanced with dilated convolutional blocks and the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is used for classification. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively classifies the frequency patterns of radar emissions based on RF–TOA graphs.
keywords: ["time of arrival", "electronic support systems", "threat discrimination", "channel and spatial attention", "CBAM"]

title: Adaptive Waveform Selection Based on Model Predictive Control for Resource-Constrained Cognitive Radar
abstract: In this study, an adaptive waveform selection strategy based on model predictive control (MPC) is proposed for energy-constrained cognitive radar systems. The developed approach integrates the expected Bayesian surprise metric into an energy-aware cost function, jointly optimizing tracking accuracy and radar resource utilization. Monte Carlo simulations based on a vehicle tracking scenario show that the proposed MPC-based structure reduces position RMSE by 48% relative to fixed waveform usage and by 23% relative to standard greedy selection. This performance gain is achieved with lower total resource consumption compared to alternative methods. Horizon length analyses indicate that a single-step prediction horizon is sufficient, confirming the algorithm’s suitability for real-time applications.
keywords: ["cognitive radar", "model predictive control", "target tracking", "radar resource allocation", "prediction horizon", "vehicle tracking"]

title: Identification of Antibody Patterns in Immunofluorescence Antibody Tests Using a YOLO26-Based Architecture
abstract: Immunofluorescence Antibody (IFA) tests are methods used to detect specific antigens in tissue or cell samples and are traditionally performed manually in clinical laboratories. This makes it susceptible to human error and observer-dependent variability. This study presents a deep learning approach based on the YOLO architecture, supported by image processing techniques, for the automated detection and classification of IFA antibody patterns. Within the proposed method, 15 different antibody patterns were classified in the dataset, and the results were obtained according to the YOLO26 architecture with an F1 score of 0.887 and an average precision of (mAP50) 0.937. These results demonstrate that the model exhibits stable performance at different detection thresholds.
keywords: ["immunofluorescence assay", "YOLO26", "automated image analysis", "object detection", "observer variability", "clinical laboratory automation", "image processing"]

title: Morphology-Based Hybrid Hierarchical Classification of Peripheral Blood Cells
abstract: Periferik kan hücrelerinin otomatik sınıflandırılmasında, morfolojik olarak birbirine benzeyen alt türlerin doğru ayırt edilmesi temel bir zorluktur. Bu çalışmada, bu sınıfların hassas analizi için öznitelik gömme tabanlı hibrit bir hiyerarşik derin öğrenme mimarisi önerilmiştir. Önerilen sistem, ana bir DenseNet121 modelini takiben, hücrelerin çekirdek ve sitoplazma detaylarındaki morfolojik varyasyonları inceleyen özelleşmiş uzman modellerden oluşmaktadır. Elde edilen özniteliklerin bir makine öğrenmesi katmanında birleştirilmesiyle %98,07 doğruluk oranına ulaşılmıştır. Özellikle standart modellerin yetersiz kaldığı Bant Nötrofil sınıfında F1 skoru 0,339’dan 0,886’ya, Miyelosit sınıfında ise 0,138’den 0,737’ye yükseltilmiştir. Sonuçlar, hiyerarşik morfolojik analizin karmaşık hücre gruplarının ayırıcı tanısında yüksek performans sağladığını göstermektedir.
keywords: ["DenseNet121", "feature embedding", "myelocytes", "cell morphology"]

title: Hybrid Centrality for Influence Maximization in Spatial Networks: An Entropy-AHP Case Study on a Large-Scale Road Network
abstract: Selecting influential nodes to maximize information and epidemic spreading in large-scale networks is a critical problem. However, in spatial and planar topologies such as road networks, singular centrality metrics like Degree and PageRank fall short in comprehensively reflecting both the local and global features of the network. This study proposes a hybrid centrality approach based on Multi-Criteria Decision Making (MCDM). In the proposed model, Shannon Entropy is used for objective weighting, while the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) provides hierarchical balancing to determine the optimal centrality combination. The method is evaluated on the roadNet-CA dataset using the SIR model. Results indicate that the Entropy-AHP based Degree+PageRank model steadily enhances spreading performance across various network topologies. Additionally, a notable computational cost advantage is obtained while preserving high stability at reduced simulation repetitions.
keywords: ["influence maximization", "spatial networks", "road network", "Shannon entropy", "analytic hierarchy process", "multi-criteria decision making", "degree centrality", "PageRank", "SIR model", "information dissemination"]

title: MindMate: BERT and Semantics in Turkish Texts Lexico-Based Hybrid Sentiment Analysis with Acoustics Content Recommendation Model
abstract: This study proposes a hybrid digital assistant architecture named MindMate, which combines the deep learning-based BERT model with rule-based semantic lexicon analysis to analyze emotional states expressed in natural language and provide personalized content recommendations. Training and testing were conducted on 7,439 Turkish sentences obtained by translating the ISEAR dataset using the NLLB-200 neural machine translation model. Experimental results show that the BERTurk model achieves 70.43% accuracy, while the hybrid lexicon layer increases the average prediction confidence to 75.24%. The model maps seven fundamental emotions to Spotify audio features (valence, energy) based on Russell’s Circumplex Model of Affect to deliver mood-congruent music recommendations.
keywords: ["sentiment analysis", "Turkish language", "BERT", "lexicon-based sentiment analysis", "BERTurk", "NLLB-200", "music recommendation", "circumplex model of affect", "virtual assistants", "personalized content recommendation"]

title: Self-Attention Transformer-Based Detector for Faster-than-Nyquist Signaling
abstract: In this study, a novel encoder-only Transformer-based receiver architecture is presented for BPSK signals transmitted over Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) signaling channels that introduce intentional inter-symbol interference (ISI) with a compression factor of τ=0.8. A complete end-to-end communication chain encompassing BPSK modulation, RRC pulse shaping, and the ISI coefficients arising from matched filtering was constructed and evaluated. The proposed Transformer receiver was benchmarked against the optimal BCJR detector over an Eb/N0range of 0–8 dB. To systematically close the BER gap to the BCJR, a two-stage training strategy combining multi-SNR pretraining and per-SNR curriculum fine-tuning was developed. The computational complexity and inference latency of the Transformer receiver were analyzed in comparison with a GRU based receiver. Attention map visualizations revealed that the Transformer autonomously identifies the FTN-induced ISI memory structure without requiring any prior channel knowledge; as the SNR increases, the attention weights become significantly concentrated around the center token and its nearest neighbors.
keywords: ["faster-than-Nyquist signaling", "encoder-only transformer", "BPSK", "intersymbol interference", "curriculum learning", "pre-training and fine-tuning", "attention maps", "matched filter", "bit error rate", "inference latency"]

title: Synthetic Generation of SAS Raw Data from 3D Underwater Targets
abstract: This work presents a mesh-based synthetic data generation framework for Synthetic Aperture Sonar (SAS) imaging of extended underwater targets. Starting from a triangulated three-dimensional scene model, the proposed approach converts the surface into discrete scatterers, determines visible scatterers through ray-based occlusion analysis, and assigns their amplitudes using a Lambertian-type angular scattering model. SAS raw data are then synthesized by coherently summing the delayed contributions of the visible scatterers over the synthetic aperture. One of the distinctive aspects of the proposed framework is its ability to support raw data generation under perturbed platform trajectories beyond ideal straight-line acquisition. These trajectories may include deviations from the nominal linear path as well as roll, pitch, and yaw variations that change from ping to ping, which distinguishes the simulator from existing approaches that assume idealized acquisition geometry. This capability enables controlled modeling of motion effects and supports the development and evaluation of motion compensation algorithms. The framework enables realistic synthetic data generation for the development and evaluation of SAS reconstruction, motion compensation, image formation, automatic target detection, and classification algorithms under controlled conditions.
keywords: ["synthetic aperture sonar", "synthetic data generation", "underwater targets", "3D scene modeling", "mesh-based simulation", "coherent summation", "motion compensation", "automatic target detection"]

title: Improving Training Performance on Violence Videos with Mixup Data Augmentation
abstract: Due to the increase in crime and violence, it is important to develop technology to automatically detect the presence of violence in security camera images. While law enforcement agencies may have sufficient footage, they may not have the human resources to analyze it and detect violence in a timely manner. Video clips containing violence are often unevenly distributed, which causes deep learning-based models to suffer from overfitting and undergeneralization problems. In this study, unlike classical and modern data augmentation methods, we aim to preserve temporal integrity by applying Mixup to each frame separately. The CNN+LSTM model with Mixup at the frame level achieved a training performance of approximately 96%. The study also provides a comparison of which data augmentation strategy is suitable for which tasks and emphasizes the importance of task-specific data augmentation.
keywords: ["violence detection", "mixup augmentation", "temporal integrity", "CNN-LSTM", "overfitting", "class imbalance", "training performance"]

title: Radar Intrapulse Modulation Classification via PELT-Based Change Point Detection
abstract: Modern radar systems utilize complex intra-pulse modulation techniques to maintain their survivability in electronic warfare environments. Rapid and accurate recognition of these modulations is a critical necessity for both threat library generation and signal identification processes. In this study, a two-stage classification approach based on the Pruned Exact Linear Time (PELT) algorithm is proposed for signal segmentation. Under the proposed method, the first stage involves isolating modulation classes that do not contain change points. In the second stage, for complex signals falling outside these classes, the change points on the instantaneous phase series are detected using the PELT algorithm to segment the signal. Subsequently, the final modulation type is determined through statistical features extracted from each segment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach offers high accuracy and low computational complexity, even at low signal-to-noise ratios (SNR).
keywords: ["automatic modulation classification", "PELT algorithm", "change point detection", "signal segmentation", "instantaneous phase", "statistical features", "electronic warfare", "low signal-to-noise ratio"]

title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of the Resonance Frequency of a Microstrip Patch Antenna Operating in the 5G Band
abstract: In this study, a machine-learning-based approach is presented to predict the resonance frequency of an inset-fed microstrip patch antenna operating in the 28 GHz 5G millimeter-wave band. A parametric data set comprising 216 samples of the antenna geometry was generated through full-wave electromagnetic simulations. In the dataset, substrate thickness, patch length, patch width, and the S11magnitude at the resonance point were used as input parameters, while the resonance frequency was defined as the target variable. Six different machine learning algorithms, namely Support Vector Regression, Gradient Boosting Regression, Random Forest Regression, Decision Tree Regression, Ridge Regression, and Lasso Regression, were applied to the dataset, and the performances of the models were comparatively evaluated. The best performance was achieved using the Gradient Boosting Regression model. For this model, the mean absolute error (MAE) and coefficient of determination (R2) were calculated as 0.1190 GHz and 0.9919, respectively, on the test dataset. The target resonance frequency of 28.0 GHz was predicted with an error of 0.05%, and the corresponding parameter combination was used for antenna fabrication. The measured S11spectrum of the fabricated antenna shows agreement with the results obtained from full-wave electromagnetic simulations and equivalent circuit model.
keywords: ["microstrip patch antenna", "resonant frequency prediction", "5G millimeter-wave", "28 GHz", "inset feed", "gradient boosting regression", "support vector regression", "random forest regression", "S11 reflection coefficient", "equivalent circuit model", "antenna fabrication"]

title: Credit Risk Modeling Using Unsupervised Graph Representation Learning
abstract: Banks’ credit lending decisions are usually managed through the outputs of machine learning models. These models generally work with high precision, and novel approaches are needed for performance improvement. In this work, we aim to improve a bank’s credit scoring model by passing small and medium sized enterprises through graph representation learning algorithms. For this reason, enterprises are represented as nodes, and their money transfers are represented as weighted edges in a graph. Feature extraction was performed using GraphSAGE. A significant potential savings amount is calculated based on the improvements in predictions.
keywords: ["credit risk modeling", "credit scoring", "graph representation learning", "GraphSAGE", "small and medium-sized enterprises", "bank lending decisions", "feature extraction", "unsupervised learning"]

title: Solving The One Epoch Phenomenon
abstract: The one-epoch phenomenon (OEP) is a pervasive challenge in industrial click-through rate (CTR) prediction, where model performance peaks within the first epoch and declines sharply thereafter due to the high sparsity of feature sets and the rapid memorization capacity of deep neural networks. This study investigates techniques to overcome OEP using large-scale industrial datasets, evaluating the impact of learning rate adjustments, optimization algorithms, and feature filtering. While decreasing the learning rate improved performance, it did not prevent the onset of OEP. However, filtering out highly sparse features improved model accuracy and extended the training duration to four epochs. Offline best results demonstrated significant improvements with RelaImp of 0.57 in AUC and improvements in logloss and PRAUC reaching 16.2% and 10.4% respectively, while online deployment led to a 1.88% increase in total advertiser value (TAV) and a 3.39% increase in conversion rate (CVR). Feature value filtering improves the performance as well with RelaImp of 0.29 in AUC and 0.88 in GAUC and with 0.67% in PRAUC.
keywords: ["click-through rate prediction", "feature sparsity", "adaptive learning rate", "feature filtering", "deep neural network", "memorization", "online advertising", "conversion rate"]

title: FACTurk: Insights into the Turkish Fact-Checking Ecosystem via a New Dataset
abstract: False and misleading information has become a major societal challenge, increasing the importance of fact-checking activities. In this study, we present FACTurk, a dataset comprising 15,766 fact-checking reports published between 2009 and 2026 and collected from six Turkish fact-checking platforms. In addition, a range of statistical analyses has been conducted on the dataset, and the distribution of persons and organisations mentioned in the claims has been examined using a named entity recognition model. The dataset is intended to support future research aimed at understanding the dynamics of disinformation in Türkiye and advancing fact-checking practices. FACTurk and its accompanying source code have been made publicly available as open source at https://github.com/altuncu/FACTurk.
keywords: ["fact-checking", "disinformation", "named entity recognition", "misinformation", "Turkey"]

title: Generative AI Use in Financial Reporting and Analytical Workflows with Anthropic Economic Index Data: Automation, Autonomy, and Relative Time Ratio
abstract: This study examines generative AI use in financial reporting and analytical workflows at the task level by using the 2026 release of the Anthropic Economic Index dataset. The analysis is based on raw Claude.ai and 1P API records for the period from 13 to 20 November 2025. Financial tasks are defined through a narrowed manual filter built from the open task list. Task-level measures include usage share, collaboration mode, relative time ratio, AI autonomy, human education years, and task success rate. Descriptive findings show that the share of financial tasks is higher on Claude.ai, whereas the automation share is markedly higher on 1P API. Claude.ai displays higher augmentation and higher task success. A weighted least squares model estimated at the task level indicates that the relative time ratio is positively and significantly associated with AI autonomy, human education years, and API use. The results indicate that the effect of generative AI in finance cannot be reduced to a single automation pattern and instead varies with the interface used and the nature of the task.
keywords: ["generative AI", "financial reporting", "data analysis pipeline", "Claude AI", "AI autonomy", "task automation", "human-AI collaboration", "task success rate"]

title: Effect of Stain Normalization on Cross-Dataset Performance in Liquid-Based Pap Smear Images
abstract: Cervical cell classification from liquid-based Pap smear images is vital for the early diagnosis of cervical cancer. However, the most significant barrier to deploying artificial intelligence models in real-world clinical settings is the severe staining variations in images obtained from different laboratories. This "domain shift" problem dramatically degrades the performance of deep learning models, hindering their generalizability. In this study, we investigate the critical role of stain normalization techniques in resolving this issue and their direct impact on cross-dataset performance. Using the CRIC and Comparison Detector datasets, we trained and evaluated ResNet50, EfficientNet, and Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures. The findings prove that stain normalization prevents models from memorizing misleading color artifacts, forcing them to focus on true cellular morphology, thereby massively improving cross-dataset performance, classification accuracy, and overall model robustness.
keywords: ["stain normalization", "cervical cell classification", "domain shift", "cross-dataset generalization", "cervical cancer diagnosis", "color artifacts", "ResNet50", "EfficientNet", "vision transformer"]

title: Comparative Analysis of Adaptive and Extended Kalman Filter Variations for IMU and GNSS Data Fusion in Railway Vehicles
abstract: This study presents a performance analysis of five different Kalman Filter (KF)-based algorithms that integrate Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) and Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) data to enhance the navigation accuracy of railway vehicles. Within the scope of the study, five distinct Kalman filters (KF, Sage-Husa Adaptive Kalman Filter (SH-AKF), Strong Tracking Adaptive Kalman Filter (ST-AKF), Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), and Sage-Husa Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter (SH-EAKF)) were compared using real-time data in the MATLAB environment, based on the criteria of positioning error and computational cost.
keywords: ["adaptive Kalman filter", "extended Kalman filter", "positioning error", "computational cost", "sensor fusion"]

title: Using Weighted Loss in Bilingual Model Training
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance largely due to the availability of high-quality and large-scale training data. However, this reliance creates a significant performance disparity between high-resource languages such as English and low-resource languages like Arabic. The imbalance in data exposure during the pre-training phase persists into the bilingual supervised fine-tuning (SFT) stage, limiting the models’ semantic depth and reasoning capabilities in low-resource languages.To address the aforementioned imbalance, we depart from traditional approaches by computing the optimal learning rates for each language in the dataset separately and transforming these learning rates into language-specific weighting coefficients used in the loss function. Experimental results obtained on the XQuAD test set after training on the MURI dataset demonstrate that the proposed method preserves performance in English while significantly improving Arabic performance, achieving 56.36 F1 and 40.27 Exact Match (EM) scores.
keywords: ["bilingual language models", "loss weighting", "low-resource languages", "Arabic language", "large language models", "supervised fine-tuning", "class imbalance", "XQuAD"]

title: Waste Sorting for Recycling: An Approach Using Deep Learning and Multimodal Large Language Models
abstract: Accurate waste sorting is vital for sustainability and energy conservation. This study treats sorting as a two-stage task—object detection and classification—comparing traditional deep learning with Large Language Models (LLMs). YOLOv11n and Faster R-CNN were trained on a custom 4-class dataset (plastic, metal, glass, paper). For classification, the Gemini LLM was integrated to create four distinct model pairs. Results from 5-fold cross-validation indicated that the end-to-end YOLOv11n model achieved the highest overall performance. However, LLM-integrated approaches outperformed the traditional Faster R-CNN for classification, offering a promising and innovative alternative. A notable error in LLM-based pairs was the misclassification of backgrounds as "plastic," which slightly impacted performance. Overall, LLMs show significant potential for improving waste management processes.
keywords: ["waste sorting", "recycling", "object detection", "image classification", "multimodal large language models", "YOLOv11n", "Faster R-CNN", "waste management"]

title: Beyond Application Identification: Fine-Grained Activity Classification in Encrypted Mobile Traffic
abstract: Fine-grained activity-level classification is essential for precise network management and security monitoring. However, it faces challenges due to transport-layer encryption and the complexity of simultaneous user actions in applications. In this paper, we first investigate the performance of user activity classification in nine realistic activity classes, including classes with concurrent actions (e.g., simultaneous calling and messaging). We then explore multi-task learning (MTL) for the joint prediction of application identity and user activity. While the multi-task model achieved high application classification accuracy (90.08%), it did not improve the activity classification accuracy. To our knowledge, this work represents the first study to employ MTL for activity-level analysis on the MIRAGEAPP×ACT-2024 dataset.
keywords: ["user activity classification", "application identification", "multi-task learning", "network management", "network security monitoring"]

title: Brainwave Entrainment Rhythms Detection with Frequency Bands Classification in Hybrid Deep Networks
abstract: The proliferation of digital content consumption has risen exposure to acoustic stimuli that can influence cognitive processes and temper. This study proposes a transfer learning-based classification approach to detect patterns in these acoustic elements, which are known as brainwave entrainment rhythms and can stimulate specific frequency bands. MobileNetV4 model was trained by converting multi-class audio data into Mel-spectrograms, and an LSTM layer was integrated into the architecture to capture temporal dependencies. Furthermore, data augmentation was performed by utilizing the channel differences of dual-channel audio signals. Comparative experiments demonstrated that the standalone MobileNetV4 model achieved 88.28% accuracy, while the MobileNetV4+LSTM model reached 92.34%. The MobileNetV4+LSTM model that was trained after data augmentation attained a peak accuracy of 92.53%. The competence of the LSTM layer in learning temporal dependencies significantly enhanced classification performance, hence the proposed hybrid deep learning architecture was indicated to be effective in detecting relevant rhythms.
keywords: ["brainwave entrainment", "transfer learning", "MobileNetV4", "LSTM", "Mel spectrogram", "data augmentation", "temporal dependencies"]

title: Double-Threshold sEMG Onset Detection with Median–MAD Baseline Estimation
abstract: Surface electromyography (sEMG) onset detection is a fundamental task in biomechanical analysis, motor control research, and human–machine interfacing. Although threshold-based detection methods are widely used due to their simplicity and computational efficiency, their reliability critically depends on accurate statistical modelling of baseline EMG activity. Conventional estimators based on the mean and standard deviation are highly sensitive to outliers and non-Gaussian noise components frequently present in baseline EMG segments, resulting in unstable threshold placement and reduced detection accuracy. This study proposes a robust statistical baseline modelling approach for a classical double-threshold EMG onset detection framework. Baseline central tendency and dispersion are estimated using the median and median absolute deviation (MAD), which are inherently resistant to outliers. To ensure comparability with the standard deviation under Gaussian assumptions, the MAD is scaled using a consistency factor of 1.4826. The detection pipeline further incorporates Teager-Kaiser energy conditioning, RMS envelope extraction, and temporal validation constraints to improve detection stability. Comparative evaluation against a conventional mean-standard deviation baseline model demonstrates that the proposed robust estimation significantly reduces threshold sensitivity to transient artifacts and improves temporal onset detection accuracy. The proposed approach preserves the simplicity and real-time feasibility of classical amplitude thresholding while substantially enhancing robustness under realistic noise conditions.
keywords: ["surface electromyography", "double threshold detection", "baseline estimation", "median absolute deviation", "robust estimation", "outlier robustness", "temporal validation", "amplitude thresholding", "non-Gaussian noise"]

title: Hybrid Channel Access Protocol for Ultra-Wideband Swarm Networks
abstract: In this study, a novel hybrid channel access protocol (HCAP) designed for high-density and mobile ultra-wideband (UWB) swarm networks is presented. Standard IEEE 802.15.4 and alternative channel access protocols proposed in the literature suffer from high collision rates and scalability issues in dynamic three-dimensional environments with high node density. HCAP integrates deterministic distributed channel access with a flexible contention-based mechanism, eliminating the need for centralized coordination while delivering stable performance under high mobility.
keywords: ["ultra-wideband", "IEEE 802.15.4", "collision avoidance", "contention-based access", "mobile nodes", "scalability"]

title: Cross-Modal Temporal Attention Network for Continuous Authentication in Mobile Behavioral Biometrics
abstract: In this study, a novel deep learning architecture called Cross-Modal Temporal Attention Network (CMTA-Net) is proposed for the problem of continuous authentication based on mobile behavioral biometrics. The model represents user behavior by processing touch, accelerometer, and gyroscope data through separate branches using cross-modal attention and temporal attention mechanisms. In experiments conducted on the HMOG dataset under the leakage-free Leave-One-Session-Out (LOSO) protocol, an EER of 8.17% was achieved at the instant decision level, which was reduced to 5.97% with 20-second decision fusion. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides effective and competitive performance for continuous authentication using multimodal mobile sensor data.
keywords: ["continuous authentication", "cross-modal attention", "temporal attention", "multimodal sensor fusion", "accelerometer", "gyroscope", "decision fusion"]

title: Frequency-Based Gait Synthesis for Humanoid Robots: Extension from 2D to 3D
abstract: Bipedal walking remains a challenging problem due to hybrid dynamics and terrain variability. In this work, we propose a walking controller system that combines a gait generator network learned from human motion capture data with a Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based torque controller. Results show that combining spectral motion priors with deep reinforcement learning offers a practical path toward natural and robust bipedal locomotion. Experiments on a 2D robot demonstrate human-like walking performance, and subsequent experiments on a 3D humanoid robot confirm that a similarly trained gait generator network generalizes to 3D robots as well.
keywords: ["gait synthesis", "humanoid robots", "bipedalism", "motion capture data", "proximal policy optimization", "torque control", "deep reinforcement learning"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Activity and Posture Recognition Using mmWave Radar Data
abstract: Activity and posture recognition is an important observation tool for health monitoring, elderly care systems, and smart environment applications. However, the privacy and environmental dependency issues of camera-based and wearable systems used for this purpose have increased the need for alternative solutions. In this study, a mmWave radar-based activity and posture recognition system is proposed. In this method, temporal features are extracted by processing point cloud data obtained from the radar sensor, and these data are classified using LSTM and Temporal CNN models. As a result of experiments conducted on a dataset collected in a real indoor environment, it was observed that the proposed system reached an accuracy rate of 93% across four different activity classes. The obtained results demonstrate that mmWave radar-based systems offer an effective alternative for human activity and posture recognition problems, thanks to their privacy-friendly nature and their ability to operate under different environmental conditions.
keywords: ["human activity recognition", "posture recognition", "millimeter-wave radar", "radar point clouds", "temporal feature extraction", "LSTM", "temporal convolutional network", "privacy-preserving sensing", "elderly care", "health monitoring", "indoor sensing"]

title: Investigating the Relationship Between Workload and Performance Using Time-Frequency Analysis: An HRV-Based Approach
abstract: This study focuses on examining the relationship between task difficulty and performance through physiological indicators. In this context, analyses were conducted using Heart Rate Variability (HRV) time series derived from heart rate data. The obtained data were segmented according to the task process, and changes in task difficulty and performance were evaluated together in each segment. To examine the time-dependent changes in HRV signals in detail, in addition to basic statistical measures in the time domain, time-frequency based methods were used to reveal the dynamic nature of physiological responses. In this context, a scalogram was obtained with Continous Wavelet transform (CWT) in the time-frequency domain, and frequency-time analysis was examined on a task difficulty/performance basis. The analysis results revealed that the frequency components are not constant and that the spectral energy distributions show significant fluctuations over time.
keywords: ["workload", "task difficulty", "task performance", "heart rate variability", "time-frequency analysis", "continuous wavelet transform", "scalogram", "physiological parameters", "spectral energy distribution"]

title: Supersonic Target Detection with OMP and Blind Range Analysis in Random Pulse Interval Radar
abstract: Range ambiguity is a consequence of constant pulse repetition frequency (PRF) in pulsed Doppler radar systems. Determining pulse intervals according to a random variable in a burst is known to increase the maximum unambiguous range, but it increases the computational complexity associated with 2D matched filtering (2D MF). Furthermore implementational limitations introduce blind regions. In this study a simulation of a pulsed Doppler radar was developed, and tested for preliminaries that would lead to a characterization of blind range behaviour.
keywords: ["orthogonal matching pursuit", "range ambiguity", "pulse Doppler radar", "pulse repetition rate", "computational complexity"]

title: Real-Time Video Transmission over an SDR Platform with Rotator-Based Doppler Compensation
abstract: In non-geostationary satellite communication systems, the relative motion between the transmitter and receiver leads to Doppler-induced carrier frequency offsets, which can degrade receiver synchronization and disrupt transmission continuity In this study, the impact of this effect on real-time video transmission is investigated using an accessible software-defined radio (SDR) platform based on ADALM-Pluto and a DVB-S2 signal processing chain implemented in GNU Radio. A channel model incorporating time-varying carrier frequency offsets is integrated into the system, and a rotator-based frequency correction mechanism driven by synchronization estimates at the receiver is applied to mitigate these effects. System performance is evaluated in terms of the temporal behavior of the carrier frequency offset, receiver lock stability, BBFrame drop ratio, and the continuity of real-time video transmission. The results show that, under channel impairments, frequency offsets lead to loss of lock and increased data loss, whereas the proposed correction method improves lock stability, reduces BBFrame drop ratio, and enhances video transmission continuity. These findings demonstrate that low-cost SDR platforms can effectively be used for experimental modeling and compensation of Doppler effects.
keywords: ["Doppler compensation", "carrier frequency offset", "live streaming", "receiver synchronization", "DVB-S2", "ADALM-PLUTO", "GNU Radio", "frame loss"]

title: Modeling Multipath Propagation with Ray Tracing in Underwater Acoustic Communication
abstract: Underwater acoustic communication systems face significant challenges due to limited bandwidth at low frequencies, high ambient noise, and multipath propagation. In this study, the BELLHOP module of the Acoustic Toolbox is employed for ray tracing to model these effects. Sound speed profiles derived from EMODnet bathymetry and oceanographic databases are used to compute ray paths and transmission loss matrices for transceiver pairs. The resulting delay and amplitude coefficients are converted into channel impulse responses. Thus, the multipath propagation behavior of the underwater acoustic channel has been visualized in a two-dimensional environment, and the response of communication signals under channel effects has been observed in a simulation environment through the obtained channel impulse response.
keywords: ["underwater acoustic communication", "multipath propagation", "ray tracing", "Bellhop", "sound speed profile", "transmission loss", "channel impulse response", "underwater acoustic channel modeling"]

title: Synthetic Data Generation with Generative Models for Interference Classification in HetNets
abstract: Interference continuity and uncertain transitions between low and high levels in heterogeneous cellular networks complicate classification. Different base station types and environmental variability introduce high variance in measurement data, making it harder to learn underrepresented interference classes. This study addresses interference detection using KPI-based data from a nationwide mobile operator. To mitigate class imbalance, statistical (SMOTE), GAN-based, and diffusion-based synthetic data generation methods are applied and compared. Results show that the diffusion-based method improves performance in minority class. Compared to the original dataset, Random Forest achieves a 4% increase in overall F1 score and an 11% increase in the minority class, indicating that the generated data closely approximates real data and improves class separability by sharpening inter-class boundaries.
keywords: ["interference classification", "heterogeneous cellular networks", "synthetic data generation", "generative adversarial networks", "diffusion models", "SMOTE", "class imbalance", "key performance indicators", "base station interference"]

title: IGA Based Anti-ISRJ Waveform Design
abstract: This study presents an Immune Genetic Algorithm (IGA)-based orthogonal waveform design against the Intermittent Sampling Repetitive Jamming (ISRJ) threat. Optimized waveforms, utilizing a quad-DNA coding design that reduces computational load and a cubic penalty function that guarantees orthogonality, suppress spurious targets at the 12–12 dB level through paired filtering and maintain cross-correlation peaks around the 0.2 threshold. Monte Carlo stress tests performed under high Jammer-to-Signal Ratios (JSR) confirm that the method provides symmetrical protection and maintains operational robustness under challenging electronic warfare conditions. The proposed architecture provides a robust decision engine infrastructure for Cognitive Radar systems capable of generating autonomous ECCM reactions against DRFM jammers.
keywords: ["immune genetic algorithm", "waveform design", "orthogonal waveforms", "cross correlation function", "jammer suppression", "cognitive radar", "electronic counter-countermeasures"]

title: Comparative Analysis of CNN and CNN+Transformer Based Arrhythmia Classification on One-Dimensional ECG Signals
abstract: Early and accurate detection of cardiac arrhythmias is crucial for preventing life-threatening cardiovascular events. In this study, five-class arrhythmia classification was performed using single-beat ECG segments derived from the MIT-BIH arrhythmia database. The main objective was to compare a pure convolutional approach, namely CNN, with a hybrid CNN+Transformer architecture on one-dimensional ECG signals. Each ECG beat was represented by 256 samples and normalized using sample-wise z-score normalization. The evaluation was carried out using stratified 5-fold cross-validation, where 10% of the training data in each fold was reserved for validation. To reduce the effect of class imbalance, class-weighted loss was employed during training. Experimental results were evaluated using accuracy, macro F1-score, weighted F1-score, balanced accuracy, and class-wise precision-recall-F1 metrics. The findings indicate that the CNN model provides a strong balance between classification performance and computational efficiency, while the CNN+Transformer model offers competitive results on certain classes along with potential interpretability advantages.
keywords: ["arrhythmia classification", "convolutional neural networks", "CNN-Transformer hybrid", "MIT-BIH arrhythmia database", "arrhythmia detection", "class imbalance", "class-weighted loss", "computational efficiency"]

title: CSAC-Based GNSS Spoofing Detection and Timing Integrity
abstract: Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) serve as the primary reference for time synchronization in critical infrastructures but are vulnerable to spoofing attacks. These attacks can induce sudden time jumps or gradual drifts that compromise system integrity. This paper proposes a monitoring architecture based on a Chip-Scale Atomic Clock (CSAC) to detect and mitigate spoofing-induced timing anomalies. The proposed method maintains an autonomous local timescale using the high stability of the atomic clock and validates incoming signals through a dynamic thresholding mechanism based on aging and thermal fluctuations. Experimental results demonstrate that the method successfully identifies timing offsets as small as one hundred two nanoseconds within a single cycle and transitions the system into a secure holdover mode.
keywords: ["GNSS spoofing detection", "chip-scale atomic clock", "clock synchronization", "critical infrastructure", "thermal fluctuations", "dynamic thresholding"]

title: Cross Model Knowledge Distillation: Enhancing Whisper Small via Teacher Generated Pseudo Labels
abstract: This study examines the Cross-Model Knowledge Distillation method to enhance the performance of the Whisper Small model on TBMM general assembly records. Within the scope of the research, the Whisper Large-v3 model was used as the "teacher" to generate pseudo-labels for the dataset, and these labels served as the primary data source in the fine-tuning process of the Whisper Small model. Experimental results indicate that the base model's WER decreased from 27.07% to 15.97% with the pseudo-labeling strategy, while the CER dropped from 7.68% to 3.89%. The achieved 15.97% WER value exhibits a success quite close to the 15.55% results from manual corrections. These findings demonstrate that teacher model-supported derived labels provide an effective and sustainable alternative to high-cost and time-consuming manual labeling processes in low-resource and technical domains such as parliamentary terminology.
keywords: ["pseudo-labeling", "teacher model", "speech recognition", "word error rate", "character error rate"]

title: Comparative Analysis of UNet, SwinUNet, and SwinUNETR Models for Skin Lesion Segmentation
abstract: Skin lesion segmentation is a key component of computer-aided diagnosis systems for the early detection of skin diseases. However, this task remains challenging due to irregular lesion boundaries, low contrast between lesions and surrounding skin, and the presence of imaging artifacts. In this study, the segmentation performance of the UNet, SwinUNet, and SwinUNETR models was compared using the ISIC2018 dataset. The models were evaluated using different color channels and loss functions. The results show that UNet and SwinUNETR achieved the highest performance, reaching Dice scores of 0.893 and IoU values of 0.824. However, UNet offers more computationally efficient performance compared to SwinUNETR due to its lower number of parameters and shorter training time. SwinUNet, on the other hand, was observed to exhibit lower performance compared to the other models. Overall, UNet provides a strong and efficient baseline for skin lesion segmentation, whereas transformer-based models offer potential advantages in more complex scenarios.
keywords: ["skin lesion segmentation", "U-Net", "Swin-Unet", "Swin UNETR", "transformer-based segmentation", "ISIC 2018", "computer-aided diagnosis", "skin disease detection", "loss function comparison", "computational efficiency"]

title: Semantic Relevance Detection of Visual Content in Corporate Reports Using Layout-Aware Vision-Language Models
abstract: Bu çalışma, kurumsal sürdürülebilirlik raporlarındaki görsel içeriğin çevreleyen metinle anlamsal tutarlılığını otomatik olarak değerlendiren bir sistem sunmaktadır. Önerilen sistem dört aşamadan oluşmaktadır: (1) PDF belgelerinden sayfa düzeni bilgisiyle birlikte içerik çıkaran MinerU Ayrıştırıcı, (2) çıkarılan verileri sorgulanabilir tablolara dönüştüren Parquet Normalleştirici, (3) her görseli çevreleyen sayfa metniyle birlikte bir Görme-Dil Modeline (VLM) sunarak uygunluk puanı üreten İyimser Tarayıcı (Optimistic Scanner) ve (4) yalnızca ilgili sayfa metnini kullanarak bu puanları doğrulayan Bağımsız Denetçi (Independent Auditor). Sistem 30 rapor üzerinde test edilmiş; %83,3 kesinlik (precision) ve 0,79 F1 skoru elde edilmiştir.
keywords: ["visual content", "corporate sustainability reports", "page layout", "image-text matching"]

title: Temperature-Induced Carrier Frequency Offset Variability in LoRa Devices: An Experimental Study
abstract: Long Range (LoRa) has emerged as an enabling technology for Internet of Things (IoT) due to its long-range capability and cost-effectiveness whilst entailing cybersecurity challenges, motivating complementary mechanisms. Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) is a novel Physical Layer Security (PLS) mechanism exploiting inherent device-level impairments whose sensitivity to operating conditions remains insufficiently characterized in the literature. Carrier Frequency Offset (CFO) affects baseband signal integrity in LoRa systems. Uncompensated CFO causes phase rotation and frequency misalignment, degrading impairment-sensitive features and RFF performance. This work presents an empirical investigation of CFO dynamics under controlled temperature conditions to quantify CFO variability across thermal regimes. The results reveal temperature-dependent CFO instability, highlighting a fundamental challenge for data-driven RFF systems operating under realistic environmental conditions.
keywords: ["LoRa", "carrier frequency offset", "temperature dependence", "radio frequency fingerprinting", "physical layer security", "Internet of Things", "thermal effects", "phase rotation"]

title: S-Interleaving: A Deterministic Matrix-Based Separation-Optimized Interleaving Method
abstract: This work presents a deterministic matrix-based interleaving method that achieves near-theoretical maximum symbol separation through adaptive dimensioning and structured swapping. The method operates with minimal overhead and O(N) complexity without any length limitations. The separation limits determined through theoretical analysis have been empirically validated across 9,993 different lengths. Comparative evaluation of 19 known methods in single and multiple burst scenarios under Reed-Solomon coding shows that the proposed method consistently ranks higher in all key performance indicators. The proposed multi-metric evaluation framework captures structural, distributional, and error correction aware features while also mitigating survival bias. Statistical validation results, including ANOVA, power analysis, and robustness checks performed on 1.19 million observations for each regime, support the method's performance.
keywords: ["interleaving", "Reed-Solomon codes", "burst error correction", "survivorship bias", "error correction performance"]

title: Performance of RIS-Based Transmission with Maximal Ratio Combining
abstract: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) can significantly enhance system performance when integrated with multiple-antenna systems. However, the phase-shifting capability of RISs remains limited for achieving maximum performance in such systems. Many studies in the literature do not consider the practical phase-shifting capability of RIS and instead analyze systems under idealized RIS models. In this study, the performance of idealized and practical phase-shifting models is theoretically analyzed over Rayleigh fading channel, and closed-form expressions for the outage probability are derived. The obtained analytical results are validated through Monte Carlo simulations.
keywords: ["reconfigurable intelligent surface", "maximum ratio combining", "multiple antennas", "Rayleigh fading", "outage probability", "closed-form expressions"]

title: CEMA Memory Fabric: Benchmarking Hierarchical Memory for Long-Context Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: This study presents the contribution of the CEMA Memory Fabric approach along three main axes: (i) a State/Story/Relation memory representation for long-horizon knowledge continuity, (ii) an integrated retrieval pipeline that activates this representation at retrieval time, and (iii) preliminary long-context findings reported on LoCoMo and RULER. Unlike static RAG, the proposed memory design organizes past interactions into three layers: State (atemporal topic containers), Story (time-indexed episodic sessions), and Relation (graph-based logical links). In this study, Blackboard-based orchestration and a Reviewer-guided Auto-Repair loop are positioned as architectural components that support the main contribution.
keywords: ["hierarchical memory", "retrieval-augmented generation", "LoCoMo", "rulers"]

title: AI-Based Detection, Analysis, and Classification of Aircraft Surface Defects Using Deep Learning
abstract: Early detection of aircraft surface defects is important for maintenance reliability. This study proposes an AI-based system for the automatic detection and classification of five defect types - dents, cracks, paint peeling, scratches, and missing-head - using 4,557 images. The system employs a hybrid architecture combining EfficientNet-based CNN feature extraction with K-means clustering. Comparative results show that the supervised approach achieves higher performance across all metrics. Accuracy and recall improve by approximately %76, F1-score by %68, and precision by %48, while the F1-score increases from 0.5492 to 0.9266. The proposed system serves as a decision-support tool aimed at reducing error rates and accelerating inspection processes.
keywords: ["defect detection", "defect classification", "dents", "cracks", "paint peeling", "Scratch", "EfficientNet", "K-means clustering", "automated inspection", "aircraft maintenance", "decision support"]

title: Analysis of Regenerative Braking Performance in Electric Vehicles Using Fuzzy Logic-Based Model
abstract: Regenerative braking systems, one of the critical technologies for enhancing energy efficiency in electric vehicles (EVs), enable the conversion of kinetic energy into electrical energy to recharge the battery system. This study presents a fuzzy logic model that analyzes four fundamental inputs—speed, State of Charge (SoC), braking intensity, and road gradient—affecting regenerative braking system (RBS) performance. Simulation results demonstrate that the base model achieves a range extension of up to 8.17 km, particularly under varying road gradients and low battery levels, with a processing time of 63.27 ms, confirming its suitability for real-time control.
keywords: ["regenerative braking", "electric vehicles", "fuzzy logic control", "energy recovery", "state of charge", "road slope", "vehicle speed", "range extension", "real-time control", "battery charging"]

title: A Multi-Agent Reasoning Reliability Framework for Autonomous Decision Support and Its Preliminary Evaluation on StrategyQA
abstract: High accuracy alone is not sufficient in autonomous decision support; the underlying reasoning must also be reliable, explainable, and auditable. This study proposes a safety-oriented auditing framework combining multi-agent reasoning, Theory-of-Mind-based critique, and symbolic verification, and presents a preliminary evaluation on the StrategyQA dataset. StrategyQA is utilized as a structural proxy for the multi-step reasoning processes involved in autonomous network control decisions. In the framework, an agent produces an answer and rationale, a critic agent questions hidden beliefs and conflicting assumptions, and a symbolic verifier checks logical consistency before the final decision. This structure enables measurable and reproducible evaluation of safety-oriented decision support. In experiments on 100 samples, the full pipeline achieved the highest accepted accuracy of 0.96, with an abstention rate of 0.50.
keywords: ["multi-agent reasoning", "reasoning reliability", "autonomous decision support", "symbolic verification", "logical consistency checking", "explainable AI", "auditable AI", "StrategyQA", "multi-step reasoning"]

title: Optimal Neural Network Hyperparameter Consideration through Digital Predistortion in RF Power Amplifiers
abstract: This study introduces an effective optimization technique for identifying the optimal hyperparameters of a deep neural network (DNN) designed to model the behavior of power amplifiers (PAs). Hence, an innovative and efficient yield-analysis-based approach is proposed to improve both the modeling accuracy and the digital predistortion (DPD) performance of PAs. The method leverages a long short-term memory (LSTM) DNN architecture to capture the nonlinear and memory effects inherent in PA systems, thereby enhancing overall performance and linearization capability. To achieve optimal training, multiple optimization strategies are systematically applied to determine the most suitable hyperparameters, such as learning rate, network depth, and neuron configuration. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a PA operating in the 1.8 GHz to 2.2 GHz frequency range is considered, for which extensive simulations and evaluations demonstrate that the optimized DNN achieves minimal modeling error while significantly improving DPD performance. The results confirm that the proposed framework offers a reliable and efficient solution for PA modeling and linearization, outperforming conventional techniques in terms of accuracy and consistency.
keywords: ["digital predistortion", "RF power amplifier", "LSTM", "power amplifier modeling", "yield analysis", "nonlinear memory effects", "power amplifier linearization", "learning rate optimization", "network depth"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Prediction of Whiting (Merlangius merlangus) Length, Weight, and Catch Amount Using Satellite and Meteorological Data
abstract: Satellite and meteorological data are increasingly used resources in marine and fisheries management. Combined with deep learning methods, these data have been utilized to predict the length, weight, and catch amount of whiting, a heavily caught species in the Black Sea. Within the scope of the study, Landsat 8/9 and Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite images along with meteorological time series such as sea surface temperature, wind, precipitation, and wind direction were integrated to construct a multidimensional dataset. This dataset was analyzed using an LSTM and a CNN+LSTM hybrid model. Results revealed that while the LSTM model showed limited performance in predicting length, weight, and catch amount, the CNN+LSTM model achieved higher accuracy in all three predictions when satellite imagery were included. The findings demonstrate that incorporating spatial information together with meteorological time series improves prediction performance in fisheries data modeling.
keywords: ["whiting", "Merlangius merlangus", "satellite remote sensing", "Landsat 8/9", "Sentinel-2", "meteorological time series", "sea surface temperature", "CNN-LSTM hybrid model", "LSTM", "fisheries management", "Black Sea"]

title: SBL-SIC for Grant-Free Random Access Under Near-Far Conditions
abstract: This paper proposes a Sparse Bayesian Learning with Successive Interference Cancellation (SBL-SIC) method for blind user activity detection in grant-free random access (GFRA) under near-far conditions. SBL is used to estimate the sparse active-user support, while SIC improves the detection of weak users by iteratively removing strong-user interference. Simulation results show that the proposed method improves the detection probability, the average error rate, and the normalized mean square error compared with standalone SBL, especially in the more challenging scenario.
keywords: ["grant-free access", "sparse Bayesian learning", "successive interference cancellation"]

title: Feature-Level Comparison of Static and Dynamic Analysis for Malware Detection and Family Classification
abstract: The number and diversity of malware targeting information systems are steadily increasing, making the effective detection and classification of such threats critical. In this context, understanding the impact of different feature types on malware detection and family classification is of great importance. In this study, static features based on file structure and opcode sequences, as well as dynamic features reflecting runtime behaviors, were evaluated separately, and their performance on both problems was compared using various machine learning algorithms. The results demonstrate that features provide varying levels of discriminative power and that proper feature selection is crucial for model performance. Furthermore, it was shown that static analysis-based features can achieve high performance compared to dynamic features when combined with appropriate algorithms.
keywords: ["malware detection", "malware family classification", "static analysis", "dynamic analysis", "feature extraction", "opcode sequences", "feature selection", "machine learning classification"]

title: Decoupled Dual-Regularization for Phase-Wise Identification of Linear Time-Periodic Systems
abstract: This paper considers the phase-wise identification problem of linear time-periodic (LTP) systems. In conventional single-coefficient regularization approaches, the phase-to-phase variations of the state matrix (A) and the input matrix (B) are modeled under the same smoothness assumption. However, this assumption may limit estimation performance in hybrid dynamical systems where these two parameter groups exhibit physically different variation characteristics. To address this issue, a decoupled dual-regularization approach using independent penalty coefficients for the state and input matrices is proposed. The proposed method is evaluated on a synthetic system excited by a chirp signal, using separate datasets of 10 cycles each for training, validation, and testing. Numerical results show that the proposed approach provides a clear improvement over unregularized least-squares estimation and a consistent improvement over standard Tikhonov regularization.
keywords: ["linear time-periodic systems", "hybrid dynamical systems", "Tikhonov regularization"]

title: Impedance-Controlled Tendon-Driven Robotic Finger
abstract: In this study, the modeling, path planning, and controller design of a three-degree-of-freedom tendon-driven robotic finger, inspired by the anatomical structure of the human hand, are presented. By analyzing the workspace of the system, deterministic and safe path planning compliant with mechanical constraints is achieved using KD-Tree data structure and Breadth-First Search algorithms. The inherent nonlinear dynamics of the robotic finger are compensated via the feedback linearization method. An impedance-based control strategy is adopted, providing a flexible and stable trajectory tracking performance in the closed-loop system. Furthermore, the calculated joint torques are converted into antagonist tendon forces using a synchronized push-pull principle, ensuring the mechanical safety and motion continuity of the system.
keywords: ["impedance control", "path planning", "feedback linearization", "nonlinear dynamics compensation", "workspace analysis", "k-d tree", "breadth-first search", "trajectory tracking", "joint torque control"]

title: Structured CT Imaging Artefact Assessment using Vision-Language Models
abstract: X-ray bilgisayarlı tomografi (BT), tıbbi tanıdan endüstriyel uygulamalara kadar geniş bir kullanım alanıyla günümüzün en kritik görüntüleme yöntemlerinden biridir. BT görüntüleri; düşük doz gürültüsü ve ışın sertleşmesi gibi fiziksel kaynaklı bozulmalardan ciddi ölçüde etkilenebilmekte, bu durum görüntü kalitesini ve tanısal doğruluğu olumsuz yönde etkilemektedir. Mevcut yapay zekâ tabanlı yaklaşımlar bu sorunu yalnızca bir sınıflandırma görevi olarak ele almakta; artefaktın fiziksel mekanizmasını açıklayan ve kullanıcıya somut eylem önerisi sunan bir sistem ise literatürde oldukça sınırlı kalmaktadır. Bu çalışmada, BT artefaktlarını tespit eden, fiziksel mekanizmalarını doğal dille açıklayan ve yapılandırılmış eylem önerisi üreten bir görsel-dil modeli (VLM) tabanlı boru hattı (pipeline) önerilmektedir. LLaVA-1.5-7B ve Qwen2-VL-7B modelleri QLoRA ince ayarıyla 2DeteCT veri seti üzerinde eğitilmiş; ince ayar sonrasında LLaVA-1.5-7B %99,8, Qwen2-VL-7B ise %86,9 doğruluk elde etmiştir. Elde edilen sonuçlar, alan uyarlamasının yapılandırılmış artefakt değerlendirmesindeki etkinliğini ortaya koymaktadır.
keywords: ["computed tomography", "vision-language models", "action recommendations", "beam hardening", "QLoRA fine-tuning", "LLaVA-1.5", "Qwen2-VL"]

title: SEMBO: Semantic Memory-Based Warm-Starting for Hyperparameter Optimization with Local Large Language Models
abstract: In this paper, the SEMBO framework, which accelerates hyperparameter optimization using a large language model-based agent architecture, is proposed. The system is composed of a meta-learning component that stores past experiences in a FAISS vector memory, a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) module, and a locally running Llama 3.1:8B model. Rather than a fixed point injection, a trust region based on semantic similarities is defined to narrow the search space, and Optuna continues Bayesian optimization within these boundaries. The proposed system is evaluated on three models spanning the gradient boosting and bagging families, using 12 training and 5 test datasets with multiple seeds. It is shown that convergence speedup is model-dependent. On LightGBM and Random Forest, statistically significant speedup is achieved as confirmed by the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, with median speedups determined as 1.40 and 2.02-fold, respectively.
keywords: ["hyperparameter optimization", "large language models", "semantic memory", "warm start", "retrieval-augmented generation", "meta-learning", "trust region", "Bayesian optimization", "Optuna", "Llama 3.1", "LightGBM", "random forest", "gradient boosting", "bagging", "search space reduction"]

title: LooM: Self-Organizing Graph Autoencoders via Hebbian Learning
abstract: Most deep learning models rely on static, feedforward architectures defined prior to training, contrasting with the adaptive self-organization of biological systems. We introduce LooM, a self-organizing autoencoder where latent connectivity emerges through Hebbian plasticity. While traditional autoencoders treat latent variables as isolated vectors, LooM extracts feature maps from convolutional layers and organizes them into a dynamically evolving graph. By utilizing feature co-activation statistics as a teacher, the model learns adjacencies that reflect relationships between extracted features. Message passing over this learned graph generates a topologically-informed latent space. The resulting unified model integrates biologically inspired plasticity with neural networks, offering a novel approach to unsupervised feature orchestration and explainable latent representations.
keywords: ["Hebbian plasticity", "message passing", "biologically inspired learning", "unsupervised feature learning"]

title: Transfer Learning-Based Low-Cost Object Detection in Real-Time UAV Image Analysis
abstract: Real-time object detection in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery remains a challenging task due to small target sizes, varying viewpoints, and class imbalance. This study presents a YOLOv11n-based Transfer Learning (TL) approach capable of operating under low hardware costs. During the process, data integrity and label consistency were verified, and the pre-trained model was adapted to a four-class target problem (Vehicle, UAP, UAI, Human). The model, trained for 100 epochs, was analyzed using precision, recall, mAP@50, and mAP@50–95 metrics, as well as confusion matrices and confidence threshold curves. Experimental findings demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach for real-time UAV scenarios, while indicating that class imbalance limits performance, particularly in underrepresented classes. The results highlight the critical role of data augmentation, class balancing, and label refinement in enhancing the performance of lightweight models.

title: Wavelet-Based Loss Function Approach for Synthetic IHC Generation from H&E in Breast Cancer Histopathology Images
abstract: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) is vital for breast cancer diagnosis but costly and time-consuming compared to Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) staining. This study explores synthetic IHC generation (virtual staining) from H&E using deep learning. We analyze the impact of a Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT)-based loss function on the texture and spectral consistency of synthesized images. Experiments on BCI, MIST, and HER2match datasets using Pyramid Pix2Pix, Pix2Pix, and CycleGAN show DWT loss significantly improves perceptual metrics like FID and KID. Specifically, applying DWT loss to the Pyramid Pix2Pix model on the BCI dataset increased PSNR by 3.04% (22.55 dB) and improved FID by 20.4% (118.83) compared to the baseline. These findings prove that frequency-based losses effectively mitigate the perception-distortion trade-off and preserve high-frequency texture details in virtual staining.
keywords: ["virtual staining", "breast cancer histopathology", "image-to-image translation", "perceptual image quality", "texture preservation", "Pix2Pix", "CycleGAN"]

title: Hybrid Efficient-KAN: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework for Choroidal Tumor Classification
abstract: In this study, a novel multimodal deep learning approach is proposed to address the challenges of missing modalities and class imbalance in the classification of rare choroidal tumors. In the proposed Hybrid Efficient-KAN model, the parameter-efficient EfficientNet-B0 architecture is employed for feature extraction, while Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks (KAN) with learnable activation functions are utilized in the classification stage. A multimodal dataset consisting of angiography and ultrasonography images is used, and the model performance is evaluated through comprehensive ablation studies under various data processing strategies. It is demonstrated by the experimental results that an accuracy of 94.73% is achieved and superior performance is obtained compared to conventional CNN-based methods. It is further shown that diagnostic accuracy is enhanced through multimodal KAN-based classification, and an effective solution to the problem of missing data is provided.
