title: Low-Frequency Anchored Diffusion Transition Process for MRI Reconstruction
abstract: Accelerated MRI reconstruction is vital for reducing scan times, but high-fidelity recovery from undersampled data remains challenging. Standard diffusion models often underperform because their isotropic Gaussian noise-based processes focus on denoising rather than the primary hurdle which is suppressing aliasing artifacts. Alternative methods, such as cold diffusion or diffusion bridges, use progressive undersampling but often remove critical low-frequency k-space components, making the inverse problem harder to solve. To address this, we propose the Low-Frequency Anchored (LFA) transition process. LFA performs progressive undersampling while explicitly preserving a central low-frequency "anchor" throughout the diffusion process. This creates a better-posed recovery problem where missing high-frequency details are reconstructed from a reliable baseline. Our results demonstrate that LFA significantly improves reconstruction performance over existing techniques.
keywords: ["accelerated MRI reconstruction", "diffusion models", "k-space undersampling", "inverse problems", "scan time reduction"]

title: Comparison of 2D Temporal and 3D CNN Approaches on the UCF101 Dataset
abstract: This study presents a comparative analysis of 2D temporal modeling and 3D CNN approaches for video-based human action classification on the UCF101 dataset. Frame-level features extracted using pretrained 2D CNN backbones are temporally aggregated using average pooling, LSTM, and BiLSTM structures, and the results are compared with a 3D CNN-based r3d_18 model. Experimental findings demonstrate the impact of temporal modeling under limited data conditions. The results indicate that the 2D CNN combined with BiLSTM provides a competitive balance between classification accuracy and computational cost.
keywords: ["human action recognition", "video classification", "UCF101", "3D convolutional neural networks", "BiLSTM", "average pooling", "frame-level features", "computational cost", "limited training data"]

title: RAG-Powered Financial Trend Analysis System Using Borsa Istanbul Indices
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive capabilities in general-purpose text generation although they face serious reliability challenges in financial analysis-a domain where precision and currency are non-negotiable. The knowledge cutoff inherent in training data, coupled with a tendency towards hallucination, presents unacceptable risks for systems intended to support investment decisions. This study introduces a novel hybrid Question-Answering architecture designed specifically for Borsa Istanbul (BIST) data, fusing LLM-based generation with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and an Intent Classification layer. To support this, we constructed a proprietary dataset comprising approximately 9,000 documents sourced from recent financial news and BIST100 reports. A key innovation involves the handling of structured tabular data, such as Public Disclosure Platform (KAP) filings; these were integrated into the vector space using a specialized preprocessing pipeline to maintain semantic integrity. The resulting system utilizes a GPT-4o-mini powered intent layer to refine queries and a FAISS-based vector search engine to construct context within milliseconds. To evaluate the efficacy of the proposed architecture, three open-source models with distinct parameter structures (Zephyr-7B, Turkish-Llama-8B, OpenR1-Qwen-7B) and GPT-4o-mini as a reference model were subjected to comparative analysis in both context-free (LLM Only) and retrieval-augmented (LLM + RAG) scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that RAG integration reduced hallucination rates from approximately 70% to the 10% range and improved accuracy metrics by nearly threefold. Furthermore, the Turkish-Llama 8B model outperformed the commercial GPT-4o-mini model in the retrieval-augmented scenario, achieving the highest performance, thereby experimentally validating the effectiveness of localized models in financial analysis.
keywords: ["retrieval-augmented generation", "financial trend analysis", "large language models", "hallucination mitigation", "intent classification", "business news", "vector search", "FAISS", "GPT-4o-mini", "BIST 100", "hybrid question answering"]

title: High-Performance GPU Acceleration of FMCW Radar Signal Processing and 2D CA-CFAR Detection
abstract: Modern FMCW radar systems require computationally intensive FFT and 2D CA-CFAR processing on high-resolution data. CPU-based implementations introduce significant latency. This paper presents a unified GPU-accelerated pipeline integrating range-Doppler generation and adaptive CFAR detection. Naive and SIMD-optimized CPU versions are compared against shared-memory and SAT-based CUDA implementations. Experimental results demonstrate a significant speedup over baseline CPU approaches while preserving numerical accuracy. Bandwidth analysis reveals PCIe transfer as the dominant bottleneck once computation is accelerated.
keywords: ["FMCW radar", "GPU acceleration", "fast Fourier transform", "CUDA", "SIMD optimization", "shared-memory parallelism", "radar signal processing"]

title: A Simulation-Driven Dataset for Anomaly Detection Targeting RISC-V ML Accelerators
abstract: With the growing adoption of the software-defined vehicle (SDV) approach in automotive systems, RISC-V-based ML accelerators are increasingly used in latency-sensitive and reliability-critical settings. This makes early run-time anomaly detection critical. However, under conditions where access to hardware is limited and large-scale telemetry collection is difficult, obtaining reproducible and labeled anomaly data is challenging. In this work, we present a simulation-based dataset that combines window-level statistics from a gem5 RISC-V simulator with power and energy metrics estimated using McPAT. The dataset covers 6 ML-like workloads, 5 anomaly types, and multiple hardware configurations; for each window, it provides telemetry and anomaly labels. The dataset aims to provide a reproducible basis for training and evaluating anomaly detection models targeting RISC-V-based ML accelerators and to support analysis of how different telemetry feature groups respond to controlled run-time anomalies.
keywords: ["anomaly detection", "RISC-V", "software-defined vehicles", "gem5"]

title: Multidimensional EMG Assessment of Post-Stroke Upper Limb Impairment Across Functional Tasks
abstract: Post-stroke motor impairment involves neuromus-cular adaptations that amplitude-based EMG assessment alone cannot fully characterize. This study applied a multidimensional framework integrating RMS, Hjorth parameters, and Higuchi Fractal Dimension to a 12-channel surface EMG dataset from 10 stroke survivors and 10 healthy controls across six functional upper limb tasks. The intensity domain revealed proximal amplitude excesses, with the triceps and flexor digitorum superficialis recording increases of +226% and +213%, respectively. The complexity domain demonstrated reductions in neural drive quality proximally, alongside task-dependent compensatory gains distally. The highest effect size was recorded for flexor digitorum superficialis during the small cube task (d = 1.41). These findings confirm that amplitude and complexity features capture distinct dimensions of post-stroke motor disorganization, supporting their integration as multidimensional biomarkers for rehabilitation assessment.
keywords: ["post-stroke motor impairment", "upper limb", "surface electromyography", "Hjorth parameters", "Higuchi fractal dimension", "RMS amplitude", "flexor digitorum superficialis", "triceps brachii", "functional tasks", "stroke rehabilitation assessment"]

title: Fine-Tuning Text-to-Speech Models with Turkish Speech Data
abstract: Developing text-to-speech (TTS) systems for a language with limited accessible speech data such as Turkish remains a challenge. This study describes a process for creating a Turkish text-to-speech system using web-scraping data to train deep learning models. The data collection approach is based on transcribing Turkish audiobook content from YouTube and converting it into a usable dataset using normalization, piece segmentation, and human annotation methods. In this study, the performances of fine-tuning KaniTTS and Dia voice models are compared with the performance of Elevenlabs voice clone. It has been observed that fine-tuned voice models with limited resources gained the ability to synthesize at the level of commercial based API voice model.
keywords: ["text-to-speech", "Turkish language", "fine-tuning", "low-resource speech data", "speech normalization", "manual annotation", "speech synthesis"]

title: Performance Analysis of Distributed Hybrid RIS-Assisted SSK Systems over THz Channels with Pointing Errors
abstract: This study presents a statistical performance analysis of distributed hybrid reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted space shift keying (SSK) systems operating in the terahertz (THz) band. The considered system model integrates the joint effects of α-μ fading, pointing errors, hardware impairments (HWI) and the thermal noise of active RIS elements within a unified signal framework. By employing the Moschopoulos series expansion for the statistical characterization of the cascaded effective channel amplitude and a Gamma distribution representation based on moment matching for the noise power of active RIS elements, analytical expressions for the outage probability (OP) and average bit error rate (ABER) of the system are derived. The accuracy of the obtained analytical expressions is verified by Monte Carlo simulations.
keywords: ["reconfigurable intelligent surface", "space shift keying", "terahertz communication", "pointing errors", "alpha-mu fading", "hardware impairments", "outage probability", "average bit error rate", "moment matching"]

title: Real-Time Non-Invasive Vein Imaging System with Autofocus Near-Infrared Camera
abstract: Phlebotomy can be a disadvantageous procedure due to factors such as inadequate equipment sterilization and the time-consuming nature of the process for healthcare personnel. Furthermore, it is challenging to perform interventions with invasive tools like needles in certain patient groups, such as those with obesity, which can also lead to patient trauma. In this study, a non-invasive vein imaging system was developed. The system is designed to visualize subcutaneous veins in real-time. Utilizing the principle that hemoglobin in the blood absorbs infrared light at a wavelength of 850 nanometers, a setup was established to emit these rays onto the skin and capture the reflections. The light rays are captured by a Near-Infrared (NIR) camera. The captured images are processed using image processing algorithms developed on an embedded processing unit, converted into vein visuals, and transferred to the target area. Experimental trials have proven that veins in a limb can be successfully isolated and visualized.
keywords: ["near-infrared camera", "autofocus", "phlebotomy", "hemoglobin absorption", "real-time imaging", "embedded image processing", "obesity"]

title: Strategic University Quota Prediction: A Multi-Stage Hurdle Architecture and Explainable AI Approach
abstract: This study presents a two-stage Hurdle architecture for predicting annual enrollment quota changes in Turkish university programs. Approximately 46 percent of the more than 12,000 programs tracked by the Council of Higher Education (YÖK) retain identical quotas year over year, creating a zero-inflated target distribution that standard regression models handle poorly. The proposed pipeline first classifies whether a program’s quota will change, then estimates the signed magnitude of change for those that do. Both stages employ CatBoost gradient boosting, jointly optimized via Optuna, and are validated through leak-free Temporal Rolling Validation on three held-out years. The model achieves a mean absolute error of 6.70 (plus or minus 2.30) seats and a median absolute error of 2.0 seats, representing a 33.8 percent reduction over linear baselines and a 23.0 percent reduction over a single-stage CatBoost multiclass baseline, confirming that architectural decomposition rather than the gradient boosting algorithm drives the improvement. SHAP-based global and local explanations translate predictions into auditable signals for institutional planning.
keywords: ["hurdle models", "CatBoost", "Optuna hyperparameter optimization", "SHAP", "YÖK"]

title: SpatioCoo: Spatiotemporal Gait Analysis of Cows for Lameness Detection Using Radar
abstract: Lameness in dairy cattle is a major welfare issue that affects animal productivity and farm profitability, making early detection essential for effective management. Radar sensing has recently been explored as a non contact approach for monitoring animal movement and behaviour. This paper presents a radar based pathway for spatiotemporal gait analysis of cows aimed at supporting automated lameness detection. The proposed approach focuses on capturing micro-Doppler signatures and extracting gait related characteristics that reflect changes in locomotion. The study highlights the potential of radar sensing as an objective and scalable tool for continuous livestock monitoring and early identification of mobility impairments.
keywords: ["lameness detection", "dairy cattle", "radar sensing", "spatiotemporal gait analysis", "micro-Doppler signatures", "livestock monitoring", "gait analysis", "locomotor impairment"]

title: ADS-B Signal Separation with a Dual-Path Convolutional-Recurrent Neural Network
abstract: In this study, a Dual-Path Convolutional-Recurrent Neural Network architecture is proposed for the separation of garbled signals observed in single-antenna ADS-B receivers. In addition, a new loss function is employed to better preserve the structural characteristics of ADS-B signals. Test results show that the proposed approach provides higher separation performance than the baseline model and methods in literature and it indicates that the proposed method constitutes an effective alternative for addressing the ADS-B garbling problem.
keywords: ["ADS-B", "signal separation", "dual-path network", "convolutional recurrent neural network", "single-antenna receiver", "loss function design"]

title: Evolutionary Optimization of Gait Stability for Three Spoke Wheg Rovers via Discrete Element Method
abstract: This paper presents an evolutionary approach to enhance the gait stability and mobility efficiency of quadrupedal micro-rovers on granular lunar terrains. Standard heuristic fixed gait phases often cause instabilities (Z-hop, roll, pitch, and yaw) due to complex granular soil mechanics. In this study, the phase offset defining a single leg's ground contact and the crossover speed coefficient are optimized on a level lunar soil analog using the Differential Evolution algorithm. To ensure physical accuracy, a Multi-Body Dynamics (MBD) and Discrete Element Method (DEM) co-simulation framework is developed. The terrain is modeled with asymmetric multi-sphere particles to capture realistic interlocking behavior. The optimization algorithm systematically identifies configurations that minimize orientational instabilities while maximizing forward distance, achieving significantly more stable mobility than standard strategies.
keywords: ["gait stability", "lunar terrain", "granular soil mechanics", "differential evolution", "discrete element method", "locomotion optimization"]

title: Compression Analysis of Automotive Radar Raw Data Using Video-Codecs
abstract: Automotive radars are essential sensors in advanced driver assistance systems due to their robustness against challenging environmental conditions and their capability of providing accurate range and velocity measurements. The use of multiple radar sensors in modern vehicles enables high-resolution detection in both near and far ranges, significantly increasing the total volume of generated data. Centralized processing of these multi-source radar raw data streams is necessary for data fusion, joint processing, and enhanced target detection performance. However, the growing data volume introduces severe bandwidth limitations, particularly for real-time transmission and storage. This study investigates the adaptability of the HEVC (High Efficiency Video Coding) codec to radar raw data compression, as an alternative to traditional JPEG-2000 based image compression approaches. The experimental analysis was conducted using the HM (HEVC Test Model) software (HM-master), which is the official and widely accepted reference implementation of the HEVC standard for scientific research. By utilizing this reference software, which is considered a standard benchmark in scientific research, the temporal correlations of HEVC were exploited. It was observed that at compression ratios reaching up to 99%, the error in radar detection performance remained below 1%. This enhanced compression efficiency offers a crucial advantage for high-bandwidth radar data streams. Within this scope, the effects of various compression ratios on Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Mean Squared Error (MSE), and the accuracy of radar range-velocity estimation have been thoroughly analyzed.
keywords: ["automotive radar", "HEVC", "driver assistance systems", "bandwidth constraints", "range and velocity estimation", "compression ratio", "temporal correlation"]

title: Measuring Statutory Citation Hallucinations of LLMs in Turkish Law: A Multi-Agent Based Novel Benchmark Dataset and Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Framework
abstract: Although large language models show potential in legal reasoning, hallucinated statutory citations undermine their reliability. This study presents the first benchmark for measuring citation hallucinations in Turkish law, a generator–verifier–evaluator multi-agent architecture for dataset construction, and a multi-dimensional evaluation framework introducing Norm Content Fabrication and Weighted Hallucination Severity metrics. Seven models were evaluated across 72 scenarios spanning six legal domains, yielding 504 inferences. The judge model approach was validated through agreement analysis with two expert jurists. Findings reveal that statutory fabrication is exceedingly rare, whereas the dominant error types are real-yet-misapplied citation and inconsistent legal reasoning over correctly identified provisions.
keywords: ["large language models", "hallucinations", "Turkish law", "legal reasoning", "benchmark dataset", "multi-agent architecture"]

title: A Review of Electronic Nose (E-Nose) Systems
abstract: This study provides a comparative analysis of electronic nose (e-nose) systems and odor sensors. Metal oxide semiconductor (MOS), surface acoustic wave (SAW), conductive polymer (CP), and optical sensor types were examined in terms of their technical characteristics and application areas. In this experimental study, six different models LDA, SVM, Random Forest, XGBoost, MLP, and 1D-CNN were trained using the UCI Gas Sensor Array Drift dataset, and their results were compared. As a result of the comparison, the 1D-CNN model showed the highest performance with a test accuracy of 99.38%. In addition, the nature of sensor drift issues and their impact on model training were also investigated. In the drift analysis covering an approximate 36-month measurement period, it was observed that the model did not fall below the 98.98% accuracy threshold in any of the time periods.
keywords: ["electronic nose", "odor sensors", "gas sensor arrays", "metal oxide semiconductor sensors", "surface acoustic wave sensors", "conductive polymer sensors", "optical sensors", "sensor drift", "gas classification", "1D convolutional neural network", "classifier comparison"]

title: Track-Aligned Interaction Modeling for Group Activity Recognition
abstract: Understanding group activities in video requires reasoning about individual actions and their contextual relationships over time. We present a context-aware interaction modeling approach that represents each clip as temporally consistent person trajectories and constructs a dynamic graph where nodes correspond to persons and edges encode spatial and motion relations. The graph is refined through stacked message-passing stages, and the resulting person states are propagated over time using recurrent modeling to obtain a clip-level representation. In addition, we introduce track-aligned sequence supervision for individual actions, where auxiliary labels are applied along person trajectories across the clip. This supervision stabilizes role representations and improves interaction reasoning. The method achieves strong performance on benchmark datasets, highlighting the importance of dynamic interaction modeling and temporally consistent supervision.
keywords: ["group activity recognition", "interaction modeling", "human tracking", "dynamic graphs", "message passing", "role representation", "video understanding"]

title: Brand Logo Detection in Social Media Images
abstract: Although logos in social media images are often not the focal in the post, they provide critical signals for measuring brand visibility. Existing open logo benchmarks partially reflect social-media-specific challenges such as highly diverse contexts, cluttered backgrounds, and small or partially occluded logos, which can limit model generalization in real deployments. In this work, we present a social-media-focused logo detection dataset covering 25 widely used brands in Türkiye. The data collection and annotation pipeline was designed with quality assurance, including analyses of annotator behavior, session dynamics, and label consistency. The resulting dataset contains 5,087 images and 9,731 logo instances. Our main objective is to quantify the impact of training data source on detection performance. We therefore compare a model trained on our social media dataset against a model trained on a Flickr dataset, and evaluate each model on the other dataset’s evaluation split. Cross-dataset results show that the social-media-trained model achieves stronger in-domain performance and better out-of-domain generalization, indicating higher robustness for social media logo detection.
keywords: ["logo detection", "social media images", "brand visibility", "background clutter", "cross-dataset generalization", "annotation quality", "brand recognition"]

title: Accelerating Lanczos- and DCT-Based Realistic Sparse Matrix Generation Using CUDA and OpenMP
abstract: The discrete cosine transform (DCT) and Lanczos resampling are fundamental signal processing techniques known for preserving spectral and structural characteristics. Sparse matrices are widely used in evaluating numerical algorithms and data-driven methods; however, existing collections are limited, and synthetic generators often fail to capture real-world structural patterns. This need has led to signal processing–based approaches such as MatGen, whose sequential Python implementation incurs significant computational overhead. In this work, we present a high-performance C implementation of Lanczos- and DCT-based sparse matrix generation methods in MatGen, accelerated using OpenMP and CUDA. The proposed approach operates directly on sparse representations, improving efficiency while avoiding dense expansions. Experimental results demonstrate substantial performance gains and strong scalability for large-scale sparse matrices.
keywords: ["discrete cosine transform", "GPU acceleration", "CUDA", "OpenMP", "parallel computing"]

title: Normalized Least Mean Square Based Optimization Algorithms for Deep Learning
abstract: In deep learning, various optimization algorithms have been proposed to improve performance and training efficiency. In this paper, we introduce two optimizers, Input Normalized Adam (INAdam) and Loss and Input Normalized SGD (LINSGD), which are built upon the Adam and SGD algorithms, respectively, by incorporating the input normalization concept from the Normalized Least Mean Square (NLMS) algorithm. We evaluate our optimizers using CIFAR-10 dataset with Res-Net 20 model, and CIFAR-100 dataset with Wide Res-Net 18 model. Our experimental results show that INAdam optimizer achieves higher accuracy than that of both Adam and SGD optimizers in CIFAR-10, and provides better results than Adam optimizer in CIFAR-100.
keywords: ["normalized least mean square", "input normalization", "Adam optimizer", "stochastic gradient descent", "deep learning optimization", "ResNet", "WideResNet", "image classification"]

title: Structure-Aware Filtering for Real-Time Separation of Active-Sensing and Tracking Motions
abstract: Animals that rely on active sensing often generate high-frequency movements superimposed on slower task-related behaviors, making their functional role difficult to quantify in real time. We propose a structure-aware adaptive finite impulse response filter that separates the longitudinal motion of weakly electric fish into low-frequency refuge-tracking movements and high-frequency active-sensing oscillations. The filter is analytically derived and operates causally at the behavioral sampling rate. Simulation and ROS2-based real-time experiments show that the method selectively suppresses targeted frequency components while remaining stable under hardware constraints. Closed-loop experiments with freely swimming fish further demonstrate that manipulating the filtered high-frequency component systematically alters movement variability.
keywords: ["active sensing", "weakly electric fish", "high-frequency oscillations", "real-time filtering", "causal filtering", "movement variability", "animal behavior", "ROS2"]

title: RGB2HSI Spectral Reconstruction on NEON Tree Canopy Data
abstract: Spectral reconstruction aims to generate dense-band hyperspectral data from low-cost RGB images. While existing methods are mostly evaluated on controlled datasets, preserving spectral signatures under high natural texture diversity remains a fundamental challenge. This study systematically investigates spectral reconstruction performance and the resolution mismatch problem using the NEON dataset, which features diverse forest and plant covers. Various methods are compared, and the state-of-the-art GMSR-Net state-space model is proposed with an L1 and SAM-based hybrid loss function for reconstruction. Evaluated via PSNR, RMSE, and SAM metrics, the proposed approach ensures consistent spectral signature preservation, with generalization validated via an external dataset. The findings demonstrate that RGB-based reconstruction offers a practical, cost-effective approximate solution when hyperspectral data is limited.
keywords: ["resolution mismatch", "state-space model", "L1 loss", "forest canopy"]

title: Identity-Preserved Portrait Generation for Fictional Worlds via Visual Reference Guidance
abstract: Identity-preserving portrait generation has gained significant popularity in recent years due to its success in realistic face synthesis; however, it still struggles to balance biometric fidelity and stylistic integrity within fictional world applications. Furthermore, the heavy reliance on text prompts remains a critical limitation for generating unique artistic styles. This study proposes a hybrid approach that ensures identity preservation via the InstantID model while simultaneously learning stylistic features directly from visual references by disentangling content and style through B-LoRA. Experimental findings and quantitative metrics demonstrate that the developed approach achieves high CLIP-I (0.739) and CLIP-T (0.270) scores in fictional world scenarios, while maintaining a competitive level of identity preservation performance compared to current state-of-the-art models in the literature.
keywords: ["fictional worlds", "content-style disentanglement", "face synthesis", "CLIP score"]

title: Cross-Lingual Adaptation of Phoneme–Motion Memory for Turkish Talking Head Generation
abstract: Speech-driven 3D facial animation is largely developed on English datasets, leaving cross-lingual generalization underexplored. We study the transferability of memory-based motion representations to Turkish using MemoryTalker, a two-stage architecture with a Facial Motion Memory and audio-guided stylization. The model is trained on VOCASET and evaluated zero-shot on TDV, a Turkish 3D facial motion dataset. Results reveal a significant cross-lingual gap, especially in lip articulation, while fine-tuning with limited Turkish data effectively adapts the motion memory, achieving near in-domain performance without sacrificing temporal consistency. These findings show that memory-based motion representations enable efficient cross-lingual transfer and rapid adaptation to language-specific articulation.
keywords: ["talking head generation", "cross-lingual transfer", "Turkish speech", "zero-shot transfer", "fine-tuning", "temporal coherence"]

title: Credit Assessment Integrated with Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Large Language Models
abstract: Financial institutions utilise complex machine learning algorithms when evaluating credit applications. However, the vast majority of these algorithms are characterised as "black box" models due to their complex structures, and their decision-making mechanisms cannot be explained transparently. To address this problem, this study integrates machine learning algorithms with Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) tools such as SHAP and LIME and Large Language Models (LLMs) to increase the transparency and reliability of credit assessment processes. This integration ensures that the complex decisions of machine learning models are communicated in an understandable manner not only to technical experts but also to non-technical stakeholders such as business analysts, managers, and customers. To this end, a web-based application has also been developed that presents credit assessment decisions transparently with both verbal and visual explanations that anyone can easily understand.
keywords: ["creditworthiness assessment", "explainable AI", "large language models", "SHAP", "lime", "model interpretability", "black-box models"]

title: OFDM-based Semantic Communication with UAV-Assisted Connectivity in Disastrous Mountainous Regions
abstract: In this study, an OFDM-based digital semantic communication system is proposed to provide UAV-assisted connectivity in mountainous regions where terrestrial infrastructure is damaged after an earthquake. Information is represented by a triplet-based knowledge base (KB) consistent with the knowledge graph (KG) paradigm and transformed into low-dimensional semantic vectors by a deep neural network (DNN) based semantic encoder. The resulting vectors are mapped onto data subcarriers using fixed 16-QAM, while BPSK-modulated channel pilots, semantic identity (ID) pilots, and an additional semantic hash/checksum pilot are used for reliable recovery. The proposed system is evaluated over Doppler-impaired Rayleigh and Rician multipath fading channels.
keywords: ["semantic communication", "OFDM", "disaster communication", "mountainous terrain", "earthquake damage", "knowledge graphs", "semantic encoder", "16-QAM", "Rician fading"]

title: Sobel-Guided Feature Reweighting for Robust MRI Translation
abstract: This work proposes a CycleGAN framework with Sobel-based structural guidance for unpaired brain MRI translation between proton density (PD) and T2-weighted images. Although CycleGAN offers an effective solution for unpaired image translation, it often struggles to preserve fine anatomical boundaries and local structural detail. However, contrasts such as PD and T2 differ in intensity appearance while still sharing the same underlying anatomy in multi-contrast MRI. This makes edge information a potentially valuable structural prior for cross-contrast translation, yet the most effective way to integrate such information into the generator remains unclear. To address this, we developed three Sobel-assisted generators: residual-correction, FiLM-guided, and attention-guided multi-channel models. Results demonstrate that Sobel guidance consistently improves synthesis quality, with the attention-guided multi-channel design achieving the best overall performance in both translation directions.
keywords: ["unpaired image-to-image translation", "CycleGAN", "structural priors", "edge preservation", "cinema"]

title: Fusion-Guided Distillation for Lightweight Landscape Segmentation Using DINOv3
abstract: Accurate urban landscape segmentation is essential for applications such as environmental planning and infrastructure management, including base station deployment. In this study, high-resolution satellite images were segmented into four classes—open land, village, forest, and water. While a Fusion model combining three binary segmentation models achieved strong performance, it suffered from high inference time. To address this limitation, a DINOv3-based student model was trained using knowledge distillation, with the Fusion model as the teacher. The proposed Student-DINOv3 model improves the average F1 score from approximately 70% to over 85% while reducing inference time by nearly 50%, offering a more accurate and computationally efficient solution for large-scale landscape segmentation.
keywords: ["landscape segmentation", "urban landscape", "satellite imagery", "knowledge distillation", "DINOv3", "lightweight segmentation model", "inference latency reduction", "base station placement", "open land", "forests", "water", "village"]

title: HTS-PTO: A Novel Hierarchical Two-Stage Machine Learning Framework for Predicting Patient Transfer Outcomes from Intensive Care Units in Secondary-Care Hospitals
abstract: This Predicting patient transfer outcomes in intensive care units (ICUs) is critical for optimizing resource allocation and improving patient care, particularly in secondary-care hospitals. However, existing predictive models often fail to handle the complex, multi-class nature of ICU discharge outcomes, particularly under conditions of class imbalance. This study proposes a novel Hierarchical Two-Stage Patient Transfer Outcomes (HTS-PTO) framework to accurately classify ICU patient discharge types, distinguishing between critical and noncritical outcomes and further refining multi-class predictions. HTS-PTO incorporates a two-stage machine learning hierarchy, where the first stage predicts whether a patient’s outcome is critical or non-critical, and the second stage further classifies critical cases as either death or transfer outside the hospital. The framework leverages Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) as the base classifier and incorporates carefully engineered clinical features, including vital signs, laboratory results, and comorbidities. The model is trained and validated on a real-world ICU dataset comprising 15,728 patient records, utilizing stratified training and testing splits. The hierarchical model achieved an overall accuracy of 90%, with a precision of 0.91, recall of 0.79, and F1-score of 0.84 for multi-class ICU outcome predictions. Confusion matrix analysis demonstrates high predictive performance for both common and clinically important critical outcomes. HTS-PTO offers a robust framework for predicting ICU patient outcomes, facilitating improved resource allocation and patient management in secondary-care hospitals.

title: Contrastive Representation Learning for Stock Trading Classification: A TS2Vec Approach with Technical Indicators
abstract: We present a self-supervised contrastive learning approach for stock trading classification using TS2Vec. The problem is formulated as a three-class task (BUY, HOLD, SELL) based on future price movements. Our approach combines TS2Vec’s hierarchical contrastive learning with 22 engineered features including technical indicators and trend analysis. Evaluated on Turkish BIST stocks, our best configuration—TS2Vec with enhanced PatchTST—achieves 74.24% gross portfolio returns on the MGROS 2025 test set, exceeding the MLP baseline (36.78%).

title: Simple Dynamic Fusion For RGB-T Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Multi-modal sensor fusion is important for semantic segmentation under poor visibility and varying illumination. However, most existing methods rely on fixed fusion rules or heavily fine-tuned backbones. In this work, we present a framework based on dual FasterViT backbones for RGB-Thermal semantic segmentation. The RGB and thermal branches are initialized from pretrained models without task-specific fine-tuning and are connected through lightweight multi-scale adapters and a dynamic fusion module. The proposed mechanism adaptively weights RGB and thermal features according to scene conditions. Experiments on the MFNet and PST900 datasets show that the proposed method achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art RGB-Thermal segmentation approaches even without fine-tuning. The results indicate that FasterViT is an effective backbone for multi-modal perception.

title: Detection of Neonatal Jaundice with Hybrid Models of ViT and Machine Learning
abstract: This study proposes a hybrid approach combining Vision Transformer (ViT)-based deep feature extraction with classical machine learning classifiers for the detection of neonatal jaundice in images. The high-dimensional feature vector obtained from the developed ViT model was classified using SVM, MLP, Logistic Regression, KNN, RF, XGBoost, Naive Bayes, and SVM-MLP-based Soft-Ensemble models, and the model performances were comparatively analyzed. According to the results, it was observed that the MLP and Ensemble models, in particular, offered more balanced and reliable performance compared to the others in terms of accuracy, F1, and AUC metrics. These results demonstrate that hybrid approaches combining deep feature extraction with classical classifiers can be used as an effective jaundice detection decision support tool in small datasets.

title: A Turkish Biology Dataset and LLM Model
abstract: General-purpose, low-parameterized language models often produce imprecise or shallow explanations when handling specialized scientific subjects, particularly in non-English contexts like Turkish, where training data is limited. In this paper, an original Turkish biology dataset within the scope of the high school curriculum has been developed; and subsequently, large natural language model studies conducted on this dataset are presented. To synthesize high-quality question-answer pairs, video transcripts and written content were first scraped from public Khan Academy resources. In the two-stage synthesis strategy, by using the GPT-4 API, firstly questions depending on the content and then answers were generated. Data diversity was ensured by producing more than one answer for a single question. The Gemma-3 1B model was fine-tuned on this specialized dataset using the Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) method. To measure model performance, LLM-as-a-judge, standard n-gram metrics such as ROUGE, and human evaluation were used. The best-performing configuration, Gemma-3 1B trained on standard-length answers, achieved superior results across all dimensions, reaching M-Prometheus scores of 3.8 for coherence and 3.0 for both correctness and completeness. Additionally, it has been shown that LLM-as-a-judge metrics are closer to human evaluation compared to the ROUGE metric.

title: A Comparative Analysis of the Perturbation Stability of Grad CAM and SHAP Explanations in CNN Architectures
abstract: Explainability of deep learning models is a fundamental requirement for the development of trustworthy artificial intelligence systems. This study presents an experimental analysis comparing the perturbation stability of Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad CAM) and Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) across two convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures under identical conditions. ResNet18 and EfficientNet B0 models were evaluated on the CIFAR10 dataset. The key finding is that Grad CAM stability thresholds are architecture dependent. SHAP provides more consistent minimum stability across both models, and all comparisons satisfy statistical significance criteria.
keywords: ["Grad-CAM", "SHAP", "perturbation stability", "explainable AI", "CNN interpretability", "ResNet-18", "EfficientNetB0", "CIFAR-10", "model architecture comparison"]

title: Minimal EOG ile Ne Kadarı Mümkün? Tek Diferansiyel Kanal ile Göz Hareketi Sınıflandırması
abstract: Elektrookülografi (EOG), göz hareketlerinin analizi ve insan-makine arayüzü uygulamaları için düşük maliyetli ve pratik bir yöntemdir. Bu çalışmada, gözün üstü ve altına yerleştirilen elektrotlar arasındaki potansiyel farktan elde edilen tek diferansiyel dikey EOG kanalının, farklı göz hareketlerini ayırt etme kapasitesi incelenmiştir. Deneklerin bakış yönlerini center (merkez), up (yukarı), down (aşağı), right (sağ) ve left (sol) arasında değiştirdiği kontrollü bir protokol uygulanmış, sinyaller video tabanlı anotasyonlarla segmentlere ayrılmıştır. Üç sınıflandırma problemi ele alınmıştır: fiksasyon–geçiş, center–up–down ve center–left–right. Zaman alanı özellikleri çıkarılmış ve sınıflandırma performansı leave-one-subject-out yaklaşımı ile değerlendirilmiştir. Sonuçlar, fiksasyon–geçiş ayrımının çok yüksek doğrulukla gerçekleştirilebildiğini (0.993), dikey yönlerin orta düzeyde (0.636) ve yatay yönlerin daha düşük doğrulukla (0.527) ayırt edilebildiğini göstermiştir. Bu bulgular, tek diferansiyel dikey EOG kanalının özellikle dinamik değişimleri güçlü biçimde temsil ettiğini, ancak yön ayrımında sınırlı kaldığını ortaya koymaktadır.

title: Scalable Truncated Kleene Star on Maze Graphs
abstract: This paper studies the scalability of the Kleene-star operator for path planning on maze graphs. Computing the full explicit matrix form of Kleene star becomes impractical on large graphs due to rapid densification. We therefore focus on truncated star and operator-form star, and compare two realizations: explicit sparse-matrix accumulation and implicit sparse matrix-vector iteration. Across grid sizes, obstacle ratios, and truncation depths, we measure densification, connectivity growth and runtime behavior. The study provides a practical regime map that identifies when each realization is preferable while keeping the contribution centered on Kleene-star computation.
keywords: ["path planning", "scalability", "regime map"]

title: A Hybrid Architecture Based on Diffusion and Residual GAN for RGB Generation from Infrared Images
abstract: This study presents a two-stage hybrid architecture for RGB generation from infrared (IR) images. In the first stage, a conditional diffusion model produces an RGB prior carrying the overall scene structure and coarse color distribution; in the second stage, a residual GAN applies bounded residual correction to refine local boundaries, contrast, and details. The diffusion model is trained with a velocity-prediction objective. On a KAIST-based validation set of 9,150 samples, the Hybrid v3 model reaches 17.533 PSNR, 0.574 SSIM, 0.349 LPIPS, and 52.64 clean-FID, outperforming the stabilized Pix2Pix-v2 on all metrics. The lowest clean-FID and LPIPS are obtained by the diffusion prior alone, while the residual stage improves pixel fidelity (PSNR, SSIM) in exchange for a controlled trade-off in these distributional metrics. Coarse prior generation combined with controlled residual correction improves pixel fidelity and structural similarity in IR-to-RGB translation.
keywords: ["conditional diffusion models", "image super-resolution", "boundary refinement"]

title: Spectral-Spatial Open-Set Recognition with Adaptive Contrastive Semantic Reconstruction for Hyperspectral Image Classification
abstract: Open-set recognition in hyperspectral imagery requires classifying known land-cover classes while rejecting samples from unseen categories. Existing reconstruction-based approaches often discard cross-band spectral correlations, provide insufficient per-class separation, and rely on fixed thresholds that limit adaptability. This paper proposes a unified framework that addresses all three limitations. A lightweight pointwise convolution restores spectral correlations after grouped embedding. A hinge-based contrastive loss separates bottleneck representations across class autoencoders, reducing inter-class confusion. The global mean reconstruction error provides a complementary detection signal, and fusion weights are calibrated using the Fisher discriminability ratio. An adaptive threshold anchors the decision boundary to the training score distribution, eliminating manual tuning. Experiments on the Houston benchmark demonstrate improved overall accuracy, kappa coefficient, and unknown-class detection compared with state-of-the-art methods.

title: An On-Premises RAG Framework for Turkish Financial Documents with Structure-Aware Chunking and Hybrid Retrieval
abstract: Financial institutions operate under strict regulatory requirements that prohibit external exposure of sensitive data. This paper presents an on premise Retrieval Augmented Generation architecture designed for secure enterprise use in the financial domain. Standard RAG systems often struggle with hierarchical report structures and specialized terminology, which may reduce retrieval quality and increase hallucinated responses. We combine section aware chunking based on Docling, metadata rich grouping, and a Turkish compatible embedding model fine tuned through contrastive learning. The retrieval layer uses hybrid search on Milvus and fuses dense and sparse channels with Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Results show that the proposed architecture improves both retrieval performance and end to end answer quality.

title: Generating Synthetic Brain Signals of Parkinson's Disease Using a Conditional Diffusion-Based Approach
abstract: Subcortical local field potentials (LFPs) are signals that play an important role in investigating pathological neural oscillations associated with Parkinson's disease. In particular, beta band activity in the 13-35 Hz range is considered one of the main electrophysiological biomarkers of the disease. However, the invasive surgical procedures required for LFP recordings and the limited accessibility of clinical data restrict data-driven machine learning studies. In this study, a conditional diffusion-based generative framework is proposed for synthesizing LFP signals of Parkinson's disease patients. Raw signals were transformed into time-frequency representations using the Short-Time Fourier Transform, and magnitude and phase components were used as model inputs. The model was conditioned on clinical variables including medication state, dominant hemisphere, akinetic-rigid (AR) score, and tremor score. The proposed method was evaluated using an open-access dataset containing recordings from 18 Parkinson's disease patients. Results show significant correlations between beta band power and clinical scores in the generated signals (Spearman ρ = 0.43-0.57). Furthermore, the Wilcoxon test confirmed that dopaminergic medication suppresses beta-band activity (p < 0.01). Pearson similarity analysis indicated moderate similarity (~0.5-0.6) between synthetic and real signals.
keywords: ["Parkinson's disease", "local field potentials", "synthetic signal generation", "conditional diffusion models", "beta activity", "dopaminergic therapy", "clinical biomarkers", "short-time Fourier transform", "generative models"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Analysis of RGB and NIR Images for Classification of Recyclable Waste
abstract: In this study, RGB and near-infrared (NIR) image-based methods were developed for the sorting of waste in recycling facilities. A dataset was collected on five different waste classes: glass, paper, fabric, metal, and plastic, on a conveyor belt. A total of 8789 RGB images and 8210 NIR images were used. These images were analyzed using various deep learning models previously trained on the ImageNet dataset. For RGB images, the best result was calculated with the MobileNetV2 model with 93.5% accuracy. For NIR images, the best result was obtained with the MobileNetV2 model with 91.2% accuracy. It is observed that high classification accuracy is achieved with both RGB and NIR images for this collected dataset. Since RGB images are affected by environmental conditions, it is seen that NIR images can also be preferred.

title: GPS-Aided Scale Estimation for Visual SLAM-Based Point Cloud Mapping
abstract: Visual SLAM (VSLAM) systems can perform mapping and localization using a monocular camera; however, due to scale ambiguity, they cannot produce results consistent with the real-world metric scale. In this study, surface mapping is performed using data collected from a monocular camera, a 2D LiDAR, and a GPS sensor mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Camera data are processed using the ORB-SLAM algorithm to obtain pose estimates and sparse map outputs. The VSLAM scale is determined using GPS data through Procrustes analysis. Using the scale-corrected pose estimates, a surface point cloud map is generated from 2D LiDAR measurements. The resulting map is compared with satellite imagery to validate the scale. Field experiments demonstrate that the estimated scale factors align the SLAM-based trajectory and point cloud maps with the real-world coordinate frame.

title: Domain-Adapted Language Models for English-Turkish Medical Text Translation: An Evaluation of Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, and Fine-Tuning Strategies
abstract: This study investigates the English-to-Turkish clinical translation performance of three large language models (Aya-23, Seed-X-Instruct, Gemma-3) using zero/few-shot prompting and QLoRA fine-tuning. Our three-stage setup evaluates: (1) general translation after FLORES-devtest training, (2) medical domain adaptation on i2b2 via a mixed dataset, and (3) generalization capacity on the independent FLORES-test set after mixed-data fine-tuning, using SacreBLEU, chrF, and COMET. Results show that Seed-X-Instruct achieves the strongest fine-tuned performance, reaching 32.70 BLEU, 64.34 chrF, and 90.65 COMET on the general FLORES test set, and 22.40 BLEU, 54.61 chrF, and 79.70 COMET on the medical i2b2 set. After mixed-data training, Seed-X improves from 11.48 to 32.39 BLEU on the unseen FLORES test set, whereas Aya-23 drops from 19.23 to 10.83 and Gemma-3 largely preserves its strong zero-shot baseline. These findings indicate that QLoRA effects are model-dependent and that domain adaptation does not yield the same generalization behavior across models.

title: LiDAR-Based Multi-Object Pedestrian Tracking Using an Extended Kalman Filter for Autonomous Driving
abstract: For autonomous driving systems, reliable pedestrian tracking is a critical requirement, especially in safety-critical urban environments where sensor measurements are noisy and intermittent. While object detection methods provide location information, they do not provide temporal consistency and velocity information. This study aims to implement LiDAR-based multi-object pedestrian tracking using an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF). Pedestrian candidates are primarily detected through the clustering of 3D LiDAR point clouds, and the resulting cluster centers are used as location measurements. Each detected pedestrian is tracked by an independent EKF based on a constant velocity motion model, providing robust state estimation and temporal consistency under measurement uncertainty. A data association mechanism based on Mahalanobis distance is used to match incoming measurements with existing tracks, while an adaptive track management strategy is implemented to prevent false obstacle persistence when the number of detected pedestrians decreases. The proposed system has been implemented in ROS2 and visualized in real-time using RViz. Tracking performance was evaluated using the root mean square error (RMSE) metric, and it was shown that EKF significantly reduced measurement noise and improved tracking stability compared to raw cluster observations. The results confirm that EKF-based multi-object tracking provides an effective and computationally efficient solution for pedestrian tracking in autonomous vehicle applications.
keywords: ["pedestrian tracking", "multi-target tracking", "LiDAR", "extended Kalman filter", "autonomous driving", "data association", "Mahalanobis distance", "constant velocity model"]

title: A New Turkish Speech Emotion Recognition Database with a Novel Construction Approach
abstract: This study presents TGU-SER, a novel database developed to address gaps in Turkish speech emotion recognition research. TGU-SER is designed for speaker-independent evaluation with controlled sentence content, with sentences kept structurally identical within classes but expressed in different emotion categories. Experiments employed Wav2Vec2, eGeMAPS based SVM, and MFCC-based CNN methods, evaluated using 5-fold speaker-independent cross-validation and macro-F1 metrics. The highest test macro-F1 score on the trials recorded 0.7870 using the Wav2Vec2 model. Cross-database generalization was also assessed by training on TGU-SER and testing on EmoDB, yielding a macro-F1 of 0.6867. Results demonstrate that TGU-SER provides a reliable resource for speech emotion recognition studies.

title: Intent Classification Under Label Noise: A Comparative Analysis of Fine-Tuned Transformers and Large Language Models
abstract: Label noise, which is frequently encountered in real-world data, is a critical problem that can directly degrade model performance. In this study, we systematically investigated the impact of label noise on intent classification by comparing the in-context learning (ICL) approach of large language models (LLMs) with fine-tuned transformer models. In the experiments conducted on the Banking77 dataset, we evaluated four LLMs and two transformer models under three different noise types and three different noise levels. We also tested the LLMs with different prompting strategies to examine the effect of taking precautions against potential noise on different LLMs. Our findings show that strong LLMs experience less than 2 percent loss in accuracy and F1 score even under the heaviest noise conditions, whereas in fine-tuned transformer models and relatively weaker LLMs, the drop can reach the 15-20 percent range.

title: Practical Performance Analysis of Distributed MIMO in Realistic Urban Environments Using Ray Tracing
abstract: In this study, the downlink performance of distributed MIMO systems in urban environments is investigated through a deterministic ray-tracing-based approach using the Sionna library. Simulations conducted on a Munich city scene evaluate the effects of the number of active access points (APs), user location, and different multiple access techniques on the bit error rate (BER). Numerical results demonstrate that the spatial diversity gain provided by the distributed architecture minimizes deep shadowing effects and offers wider coverage compared to centralized systems.

title: Digit Recognition for Mobile Robots Using Convolutional and Spiking Neural Networks
abstract: In mobile robot systems, image-based detection methods play a critical role in perceiving the environment. In this study, the problem of image-based digit recognition in mobile robot systems has been addressed, and convolutional neural networks and stroke-generating neural networks have been implemented under the same system architecture. The robot freely navigates a maze with MNIST labels on its walls to recognize patterns. The proposed system has been implemented on a ROS2-based structure, where images obtained from the camera are processed through target detection and preprocessing steps before being input into recognition models. Initially, the system was validated with convolutional neural networks, and then it was replaced with an unsupervised trained spiking neural network. The study demonstrates the applicability of different neural network approaches in mobile robot systems. It is considered that it will contribute to the development of real-time and energy-efficient neuromorphic robotic perception systems in the future.

title: Learnable Piecewise-Linear Model for Susceptibility Artifact Modeling in Echo Planar Imaging
abstract: Echo planar imaging (EPI) is an essential imaging technique for functional and diffusion MRI but suffers from geometric distortions due to magnetic susceptibility differences. Existing methods to correct geometric distortions rely on field mapping or reversed phase-encoded acquisitions, yet assume rigid voxel-wise displacement and struggle in case of large deformations and signal pile-up. In this work, we propose a learnable continuous piecewise-linear (CPWL) forward model that represents image intensity and displacement fields via simplex interpolants, enabling physically grounded sub-voxel distortion synthesis. Using four physically interpretable learnable parameters, CPWL adaptively subdivides mesh elements under high stretch and preserves signal energy through conservative remapping. CPWL improves performance over piece-wise constant methods and generalizes well across subjects. This enables end-to-end differentiable optimization for physics-informed EPI artifact characterization.

title: Effect of Representation Format on LLM-Based Analytics Copilots: Accuracy, Latency, and Cost
abstract: This study investigates the impact of how SQL query results are presented to the model on accuracy, latency, and token consumption in large language model (LLM)-based analytical assistant systems. The evaluation is kept independent of SQL generation quality, focusing solely on the result serialization stage. Four representation formats are compared: raw JSON, normalized JSON, minimal projection, and schema-first compact representation. A total of 288 experiments were conducted on industrial sensor data across four data scales, six question families, and three models. Results show that raw JSON yields the highest cost and lowest accuracy, while minimal projection improves accuracy by up to 36.9% and reduces token consumption by 32%. Although the schema-first compact representation achieves the lowest token cost, it may cause context window overflows in large datasets. The findings indicate that query result representation can be as critical as model selection in the design of analytical assistants.

title: MoAUXNet: An Attention-Enhanced Mixture-of-Experts Approach for Low-SNR Modulation Classification
abstract: Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC) is a key component of modern wireless communication systems, yet its performance significantly degrades under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. In this study, a novel attention-enhanced Mixture-of-Experts deep learning model, termed MoAUXNet, is proposed to improve classification performance in low-SNR environments. The model combines LSTM and GRU-based temporal experts with a convolutional attention-based expert and employs a gating mechanism for adaptive expert selection. Experimental results show that MoAUXNet achieves %59.78 accuracy, outperforming DAE (%53.66) and MCNet (%56.42). The improvements are particularly notable in low-SNR regions, demonstrating the model’s ability to learn more discriminative features under noisy conditions.

title: A Two-Stage CLIP–DINOv2 Framework for Zero-Shot Industrial Visual Anomaly Detection
abstract: In industrial visual anomaly detection, computational cost is as important as detection accuracy. CLIP-based approaches can provide fast image-level discrimination, but they remain limited in directly localizing defect regions. DINOv2-based patch analysis offers strong localization capability, yet applying it to every image increases inference cost. In this study, we propose a zero-shot two-stage CLIP-DINOv2 hybrid approach that does not require additional training, prompt learning, or auxiliary anomaly data. In the first stage, CLIP is used for low-cost prescreening, and only suspicious images are forwarded to the second stage. In the second stage, defect regions are identified through DINOv2-based patch analysis. The method is evaluated on the MVTec AD dataset. Results show that the proposed structure reduces total runtime by approximately 33.5% compared with full DINOv2-based analysis while achieving a conditional pixel AUROC of 94.35 on suspicious samples. These findings indicate that the approach offers an efficient and practical solution for zero-shot industrial quality control applications.

title: CT Image Reconstruction with Vision Mamba
abstract: Sparse-view CT reconstruction aims to recover high-quality images from a limited number of projections. This requires suppressing spatially extended artifacts while preserving the underlying anatomy. Convolutional architectures capture local correlations but are limited in modeling long-range context, whereas transformers incur high computational cost. Recently, state-space models have shown promise in data-driven architectures for CT reconstruction. Yet, coupling data consistency mechanisms in unrolled architectures have shown potential for improving reconstruction performance in other modalities. Here we propose an unrolled vision Mamba architecture which consists of an encoder, an SS2D block that performs cross-scanning in four spatial directions, a decoder, and a data-consistency projection in cascades. Experiments show that the proposed method consistently outperforms convolutional, transformer, and Mamba-based baselines under both standard and cross-rate generalization settings.

title: Dilated-CNN Based Jammer Detection for FFH Communications
abstract: In this paper, a method for jammer detection and mitigation in fast frequency hopping (FFH) communication systems with noncoherent demodulation is presented. In such systems, the short dwell time per frequency and the absence of pilot symbols prevent reliable signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) estimation, leading to degraded performance under jamming. To address this challenge, a dilated convolutional neural network (dilated-CNN) based jammer detection approach is proposed. The proposed method effectively identifies jammed frequency bands by using features such as frequency index, received signal strength (RSSI), and blind estimated SINR. Based on the detection results, jammer effects are mitigated at the receiver by zeroing out the corresponding log-likelihood ratio (LLR) values. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method provides a significant improvement in communication performance under jamming conditions.

title: Attention-Guided Deep Learning for Brain Tumor Biopsy
abstract: Accurate tumor localization is critical for improving the precision of robot-assisted biopsy in brain cancer diagnosis. This study proposes an end-to-end MRI-to-robot framework that integrates deep learning–based brain tumor segmentation with transformer-based attention localization to automatically determine biopsy target coordinates. A U-Net model with a pretrained ResNet-34 encoder segments tumor regions from brain MRI images. The predicted mask extracts a tumor region of interest, which is analyzed using a Vision Transformer to generate a spatial attention map highlighting the most relevant tumor area. The biopsy target is determined by selecting the highest attention response and mapping it back to the original MRI to obtain tumor coordinates. Experimental results achieve a Dice score of 0.8426, IoU of 0.7685, and Point-in-Mask Accuracy of 0.9277. Robotic validation in CoppeliaSim using a Franka Emika Panda robot achieves a mean targeting error of 0.389 ± 0.159 mm.

title: Deep Learning Based Acoustic Drone Detection
abstract: In this study, a deep learning-based drone detection system was developed using acoustic data. Within the scope of the research, a comprehensive hybrid dataset was obtained by combining three different open-source datasets commonly used in the literature (DroneAudioDataset, DADS, DroneThesis) with a custom ITU ARIS Lab. dataset collected in the field using various drone models. For training, (i) solely open-source and (ii) hybrid datasets were used; for testing, (i) solely open-source and (ii) ITU ARIS Lab. datasets were utilized. Models were trained with CNN, ResNet-18, CRNN, and EfficientNet-B0 architectures using Mel-Spectrogram features extracted from the audio signals, and their performances were compared. Experimental results revealed that models trained exclusively on open-source data remained at a low accuracy rate of 55–58% on the ITU ARIS Lab. test data. In contrast, training conducted with the hybrid dataset increased the generalization capacity of the models, raising the detection accuracy up to 98.05%.

title: Synthetic Data Generation and Validation Framework for Synthetic-to-Real Transfer
abstract: This paper proposes a synthetic data generation framework to address the limitations of small datasets in rotating machinery fault. The framework combines a convolutional autoencoder (CAE) with a Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) to generate vibration and current signals. The CAE compresses raw time-series signals into a compact latent representation, while the WGAN-GP learns the latent distribution to generate realistic signal representations, which later decoded to produce synthetic time-domain signals. Statistical, time-domain, and frequency-domain analyses demonstrate a strong similarity between real and synthetic signals. Furthermore, synthetic-to-real experiments achieve performance comparable to models trained on real signals. These results indicate that the proposed framework can effectively augment limited datasets and support robust fault detection.
