title: Text Classification for Foreign Trade Documents
abstract: Financial institutions must process a large volume of written customer instructions submitted in various formats. However, these instructions - often provided as free text or semi-structured templates - may contain several sources of noise, such as spelling errors, missing information, and terminological inconsistencies. In this study, we address a multi-class text classification problem using real customer instructions obtained from the foreign trade and foreign exchange transfer operations of a financial institution. The dataset consists of five financial payment categories annotated by domain experts and contains a total of 1,195 documents. Following OCR-based text extraction, we compare Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Large Language Models, and Vision-Language Models. The results show that the Logistic Regression model with a Bag-of-Words (BoW) representation achieves the highest performance with a weighted F1 score of 88.8%, while vision-language models remain around 76.2% weighted F1.
keywords: ["text classification", "OCR text extraction", "multi-class classification", "large language models", "vision-language models", "logistic regression", "bag-of-words", "financial institutions"]

title: Deep Visual Localization for UAVs in GNSS-Denied Environments Using Satellite Imagery
abstract: Accurate absolute localization is essential for the reliable and autonomous mission execution of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). However, GNSS-based navigation may be disabled under electronic warfare, physical obstruction, or spoofing. In this study, absolute position is estimated in GNSS-denied environments by matching UAV camera images with open-source satellite imagery. The proposed visual localization pipeline combines deep matching with SuperPoint–LightGlue, satellite–camera alignment via homography, Efficient Perspective-n-Point (EPnP)-based absolute pose estimation, and Kalman fusion with an optical-flow backup. Compared with SIFT and ORB, it achieves higher matching success (mAP) and lower horizontal error. In real flights validated against RTK GNSS, a positioning error of 10 m (MAE) and 14 m (RMSE) in the X–Y plane is obtained at approximately 500 m altitude, running at approximately 5 Hz on a Jetson Orin Nano.
keywords: ["GNSS-denied navigation", "visual localization", "Kalman filter fusion", "autonomous UAV navigation"]

title: Spatio-Temporal Time Series Forecasting with Graph-Enhanced Embeddings
abstract: Spatio-temporal time series forecasting is an important task in many areas such as traffic networks, environmental monitoring, and social networks. The goal is to predict future values of signals on the nodes of a graph using past observations. Current temporal encoding methods assume that temporal patterns are the same for all nodes. In practice, however, different nodes can show different temporal behavior depending on where they are in the graph and what their neighbors look like. In this work, we propose Graph-Enhanced Embeddings, a method that produces temporal embeddings based on the node's own signal and its neighbors' signals. The method uses learnable sinusoidal bases and a linear trend term together with a gating mechanism that controls which temporal bases are active for each node. We test the method on three benchmark datasets and show that it consistently outperforms standard baselines including fixed positional encodings, linear features, and Time2Vec.
keywords: ["temporal embeddings", "gating mechanism", "graph neural networks", "traffic networks", "environmental monitoring", "social networks"]

title: Precoding-Based Multi-User Coded OFDM-IM With Physical Layer Security
abstract: We propose a precoding-based multi-user coded orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing with index modulation (MU coded-OFDM-IM) framework with physical layer security (PLS). In the considered downlink system, the base station serves multiple legitimate users (Bobs) in the presence of a passive eavesdropper (Eve). A blockwise linear precoder is designed to eliminate multi-user interference (MUI) at the Bobs. The resulting effective jamming signal inherently corrupts Eve’s received signal without requiring dedicated artificial noise (AN). In addition, a structured linear index encoder and decoder are developed for reliable active-subcarrier index selection with single-bit error correction capability. Simulation results confirm interference-free detection at the Bobs and a bit error rate (BER) approaching 0.5 at Eve, validating the effectiveness of the proposed PLS scheme.
keywords: ["physical layer security", "index modulation", "OFDM", "linear precoding", "multiple access interference cancellation", "passive eavesdropper", "artificial noise", "jamming", "error correction", "downlink"]

title: Block-Based Autoregressive Approach for Long Horizon Time Series Forecasting
abstract: Long Horizon Time Series Forecasting (LHTSF) remains a challenging research problem due to the difficulty of producing reliable predictions over long forecasting horizons. Existing approaches mainly rely on recursive forecasting or multi-input multi-output (MIMO) strategies. Recursive methods are prone to error accumulation, while MIMO approaches may fail to adequately preserve temporal dependencies across forecast steps. In this study, we propose BlockMIMO, a block-based forecasting framework that provides a balance between these approaches. BlockMIMO divides the forecasting horizon into discrete blocks and predicts each segment sequentially while updating the input window with the generated blocks. This structure aims to preserve local temporal dependencies while mitigating error propagation in long-term forecasting. The proposed framework can be applied to different neural network architectures, and demonstrates superior performance on widely used multivariate time series datasets.
keywords: ["autoregressive models", "error propagation", "temporal dependencies", "multivariate time series", "recursive forecasting"]

title: Channel Tracking in Mobile RIS-Assisted Systems: KF Scaling Equivalence and Adaptive Noise Estimation
abstract: This paper addresses the channel tracking problem under mobility in RIS-assisted wireless communication systems. We analytically show that a scaling factor common to all covariance terms cancels in the Kalman gain, and demonstrate through ablation experiments that consistent scaling yields results equivalent to the baseline whereas inconsistent (partial) scaling noticeably degrades performance. An innovation-covariance-matching-based adaptive noise variance estimator is proposed for scenarios where the true noise power is unknown. Simulation results show that the proposed adaptive mechanism largely compensates for noise mismatch and achieves results close to the baseline.
keywords: ["channel tracking", "reconfigurable intelligent surface", "Kalman filter", "Kalman gain", "adaptive noise estimation", "noise variance estimation"]

title: Limit Management in Network Traffic Forecasting via Asymmetric Loss Function
abstract: This study focuses on the unpredictability of capacity expansion requirements driven by usage growth in telecommunication networks. In contrast to reactive methods, an end-to-end forecasting approach is proposed to enable intervention before bottlenecks occur. Anomalies in the dataset were mitigated using a rolling Z-score, and the current network characteristics were identified via the PELT algorithm. The NeuralProphet architecture was employed for the forecasting process, integrating an asymmetric loss function that heavily penalizes undershoots to ensure proactive capacity management. Evaluations conducted on real-world network traffic scenarios demonstrate that the proposed method increases the success rate of forecasting future capacity needs within a safety margin while maintaining the overall low error margin.
keywords: ["network traffic prediction", "asymmetric loss functions", "capacity planning", "telecommunications networks", "anomaly detection", "PELT algorithm", "NeuralProphet", "bottleneck prediction"]

title: Instruction-Tuned Translation Language Model Focused On Turkish
abstract: Large language models have high computation and inference costs. Recently, Small Language Models (SLMs) have become more important because they require fewer resources and offer high efficiency. Different training approaches can be used for SLMs to achieve high performance, even on resource-constrained hardware.In this study, we present our MT-270M translation model. It was trained using instruction fine-tuning to provide high efficiency and success for bidirectional translation between Turkish and English. We observe how we selected the datasets for the training phase and how data selection affects translation quality. Then, we explain how we prepared our high-quality training data. Finally, we examine the effects of data quality changes and including different tasks in the training process on the success of the small language model.
keywords: ["small language models", "instruction tuning", "machine translation", "Turkish-English translation", "bidirectional translation", "training data selection", "data quality"]

title: Do We Still Need Fine Tuning? Turkish Sentiment Analysis in the Era of Large Language Models
abstract: This study examines whether supervised fine-tuning remains necessary for Turkish sentiment analysis in the era of large language models. We compare classical machine learning methods, fine-tuned pretrained language models, and prompted large language models on a Turkish e-commerce review dataset with negative, neutral, and positive labels. Fine-tuned BERTurk models perform best overall and outperform all prompted large language models in the full three-class task. The neutral class emerges as the main difficulty: while several large language models are much more competitive in binary positive–negative classification, they degrade substantially in the three-class setting by collapsing neutral reviews into polarized categories. The findings suggest that, in realistic Turkish sentiment classification, prompted large language models do not yet match supervised fine-tuning in the zero-shot setting, and that including the neutral class is crucial for robust evaluation.
keywords: ["large language models", "supervised fine-tuning", "BERTurk", "prompt-based classification", "zero-shot learning", "online customer reviews", "neutral sentiment", "Turkish language"]

title: Decoding Chronological Age from the Retinal Fundus Images: A Deep Learning-based Analysis with Vision Transformers
abstract: This paper presents a Vision Transformer (ViT) based analysis study for chronological age prediction using retinal fundus images. In the scope of the study, four distinct ViT models with different parameters were trained and tested by using retinal images pre-processed through various stages. Experimental tests were carried out on a recent data set in this field, including both regression-based age prediction and age category classification, and the observed results were reported. The observed experimental results demonstrate that the ViT based approach shows competitive performance in the task of chronological age prediction from retinal fundus images. In the performance evaluation tests, a mean absolute error (MAE) of 4.86 was measured for the chronological age prediction. In the age category classification using the predicted age values, an accuracy of 0.8497, a precision of 0.7287, a recall of 0.7196, and an F-measure of 0.7219 were observed, respectively.
keywords: ["chronological age estimation", "fundus images", "vision transformer", "age regression", "deep learning", "retinal image preprocessing"]

title: Multi-Metric Analysis of Structural Divergences in the Midlatitude Ionospheric Base Trend
abstract: In this study, the base ionospheric trend of lower and upper mid-latitude bands is statistically and morphologically investigated using Global Ionosphere Maps spanning the years 2000-2025. Signal mismatches between the two bands are determined using Root Mean Square Difference and Modified Hausdorff Distance for absolute amplitude differences, alongside Symmetric Kullback-Leibler Distance and Dissimilarity Measure for structural and shape divergences. Analyses conducted across four Solar Activity (SA) phases reveal that while amplitude-based deviations are directly proportional to SA, structural divergences—especially during low SA phases—reflect the dominant impact of local magnetic and atmospheric anomalies within the signal space.
keywords: ["mid-latitude ionosphere", "signal divergence", "Hausdorff distance", "Kullback-Leibler divergence", "magnetic anomalies", "atmospheric anomalies", "global ionospheric maps"]

title: HAPS for Maritime Communications: Performance Comparison of Relaying Techniques
abstract: Cellular communication systems in maritime environments face challenging conditions due to the considerably long signal transmission distances in open sea scenarios and the shadowing effects encountered in regions with dense infrastructure and structural elements such as ports. Next-generation communication technologies, such as sixth-generation (6G) systems, aim to address these challenging connectivity conditions in maritime environments. In this context, high-altitude platform stations (HAPS), considered within the scope of non-terrestrial networks (NTN), have the payload capacity to host relay systems for maritime communications. In this study, the performances of relay approaches deployed on HAPS, namely decode-and-forward (DF) and reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) relaying, are compared under challenging maritime communication conditions including shadowing and long path loss effects. The obtained results provide important insights into the performance of DF and RIS relay systems and reveal that the use of relays in maritime cellular communication mechanisms provides approximately 8% performance improvement.
keywords: ["high-altitude platforms", "maritime communication", "decode-and-forward relaying", "reconfigurable intelligent surface", "non-terrestrial networks", "shadowing", "path loss", "6G", "performance comparison"]

title: A Zernike-Based Tool for State-Space Modeling of Atmospheric Turbulence
abstract: Atmospheric turbulence degrades optical wavefront quality and is the primary disturbance in adaptive optics (AO) systems. This study presents a state-space turbulence model based on Zernike polynomial decomposition under the Kolmogorov spectrum. The turbulent phase is a finite sum of orthogonal Zernike modes; each modal coefficient follows an autoregressive structure with parameters from cutoff frequencies tied to radial degree and wind velocity. The system matrix is diagonal, and the input matrix is obtained via a steady-state Lyapunov formulation using the covariance of Zernike coefficients. The model provides a compact spatio-temporal representation and synthesizes statistically consistent phase screens. A MATLAB environment generates, visualizes, and analyzes 3D wavefront distortions for varying Fried parameter, wind speed, and aperture diameter. The formulation is computationally efficient, physically grounded, and suitable for AO performance evaluation and control design.
keywords: ["atmospheric turbulence", "state-space model", "Zernike polynomials", "Kolmogorov spectrum", "adaptive optics", "autoregressive models", "phase screens", "Lyapunov equation", "wavefront distortion", "Fried parameter", "wind speed", "modal coefficients"]

title: Frequency-Aware CNN for Respiratory Sound Classification
abstract: Early detection of respiratory diseases remains an important research area for clinical decision support systems. In this study, a CNN-based deep learning model incorporating a frequency-axis attention mechanism is proposed for respiratory sound classification. The proposed approach employs a lightweight Frequency Attention module operating on Mel spectrogram representations to emphasize discriminative frequency regions. The model is evaluated against a baseline CNN architecture, segment-attention-based approaches, and BiLSTM-based temporal modeling methods. Experiments are conducted on the Asthma Detection Dataset Version 2 using a patient-wise data splitting strategy to prevent data leakage between training, validation, and test sets. Single-run experiments indicate that the proposed approach can improve Macro F1-score under certain experimental settings. However, additional multi-seed evaluations reveal that these performance gains are not consistently preserved across different training initializations. The findings suggest that frequency-aware attention mechanisms have potential for respiratory sound classification, while their effectiveness should be further investigated under different data partitions and training conditions.
keywords: ["respiratory sound classification", "frequency attention", "Mel spectrogram", "convolutional neural networks", "asthma detection", "data leakage", "clinical decision support"]

title: End-to-End Implicit Learning of Logical Constraints from Raw Pixels via CNNs in Shidoku
abstract: This study investigates solving Constraint Satisfaction Problems via end-to-end deep learning using 4 × 4 Shidoku puzzles. While existing approaches use computer vision to recognize inputs and apply rule-based algorithms to solve them, we trained a pure Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to generate solutions directly from pixels without any explicit logical rules. Trained on 80% of a 1,351,300 synthetic image dataset, the model achieved 97.96% perfect puzzle accuracy on the 20% holdout test set (270,260 samples). Analysis shows performance heavily depends on clue density; the perfect solve rate of 99.17% on 6-clue puzzles drops to 86.64% on 4-clue puzzles (the theoretical minimum). Error distributions empirically prove the existence of a "logical gap," demonstrating that statistical models struggle to satisfy hard constraints as information entropy increases.
keywords: ["constraint satisfaction", "end-to-end learning", "convolutional neural networks", "puzzle solving", "Shannon entropy", "synthetic image dataset"]

title: AoA-Based Localization Method for Underwater Wireless Optical Communication Systems
abstract: This paper proposes an integrated angle of arrival (AoA)-based localization method for underwater wireless optical communication (UWOC) systems. The proposed method utilizes the same optical signals used for data transmission for localization purposes as well, without requiring any additional hardware. The transmitter location is estimated from the optical power ratios measured by multiple photodiodes (PDs) at the receiver. The ratioing of the optical powers eliminates the impact of channel parameters on localization, allowing the method to be directly applicable in various underwater environments without the need for parameter reconfiguration. Simulation results validate the proposed method, determine the appropriate number and arrangement of PDs, and demonstrate the localization performance.
keywords: ["angle of arrival", "underwater optical communication", "transmitter localization", "photodiode array"]

title: TDOA-Based Target Localization in Passive Radar Electronic Support Measures: A Hybrid Chan-PSO Approach
abstract: This paper presents a two-stage hybrid approach for three-dimensional target localization in passive radar Electronic Support Measures (ESM) systems. The Chan algorithm’s LS and WLS solutions provide closed-form initial estimates; the resulting adaptive covariance-derived error ellipsoid then constrains the PSO search space. Monte Carlo simulation results demonstrate that the proposed WLS-PSO method provides higher accuracy than the compared closed-form solvers and stochastic optimization methods, while also achieving significant computational time savings through the constrained PSO search space.
keywords: ["time difference of arrival", "passive radar", "electronic support measures", "target localization", "3D localization", "Chan algorithm", "weighted least squares", "particle swarm optimization", "error ellipsoid"]

title: A Layered Control Architecture for Cartesian Teleoperation on 6-Axis Velocity-Driven Manipulators
abstract: This study presents a practical implementation of Cartesian teleoperation on a 6 -degree-of-freedom manipulator equipped with velocity-only motor drivers. Task-space velocity commands are converted to joint-space velocities using differential kinematics through the MoveIt Servo framework. Non-linear behavior and deadband effects in low-speed regions limit the direct application of computed velocities. To address these challenges, a layered architecture is proposed including taskspace conversion, a ROS-embedded interface, and actuator-level command shaping. Velocity commands generated in ROS are normalized and transmitted via a fixed-length serial frame, while per-cycle velocity change limiting is applied at the embedded level. Experimental results demonstrate directionally consistent and stable Cartesian motion despite velocity-only actuation constraints.
keywords: ["6-DOF manipulator", "layered control architecture", "differential kinematics", "input shaping", "serial communication", "embedded control"]

title: Bidirectional Communication for the Hearing Impaired: An Offline Sign Language and Speech Recognition System Based on BiLSTM-Attention and VOSK
abstract: A wearable system prototype consisting of two pairs of smart glasses that convert speech and Turkish Sign Language (TSL) into text has been developed to eliminate face-to-face communication barriers for hearing-impaired individuals. One pair is used by the hearing-impaired individual to convert speech into text, while the other is used by a hearing person who does not know sign language to convert TSL gestures into text. In performance tests of this fully offline system, which ensures hardware-level data privacy, the speech-to-text module achieved 93% sentence accuracy. The TSL model overcame two-hand recognition challenges across 30 words, demonstrating a 90.5% real-time classification success rate. The results demonstrate that the proposed bidirectional architecture can support daily dialogues naturally while preserving data privacy and maintaining eye contact.
keywords: ["Turkish Sign Language", "sign language recognition", "speech-to-text", "hearing-impaired communication", "two-way communication", "BiLSTM-Attention", "Vosk", "offline speech recognition", "data privacy", "assistive technology"]

title: Explainable AI (XAI) for Sentiment Analysis in low-resource languages
abstract: Natural Language Processing has achieved progress for high-resource languages, but low-resource African languages remain underserved. This paper presents an XAI framework for sentiment analysis in Swahili and Hausa. We fine-tune the afro-xlmr-small model and integrate Integrated Gradients, LIME, and SHAP to analyze model decisions. We introduce fidelity metrics to assess explanation quality and investigate biases related to loanwords and entities, alongside cultural validation. Results show that dataset quality and class balance are the primary determinants of performance in these settings.
keywords: ["explainable AI", "sentiment analysis", "low-resource languages", "African languages", "Swahili language", "Hausa language", "integrated gradients", "lime", "SHAP", "loanwords", "cultural validation", "dataset quality", "class imbalance"]

title: Design and Implementation of an Optimized RISC-V Core for SPHINCS+ Post-Quantum Cryptographic Algorithm
abstract: The increasing processing power of quantum computers is leaving currently used classical public-key encryption methods vulnerable. In response to this threat, the SPHINCS+ algorithm stands out in the Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) standardization process initiated by NIST, thanks to its stateless hash-based signature structure. In this study, an open-source RISC-V "Hornet" core has been optimized hardware-wise and software-wise to efficiently run the SPHINCS+ algorithm. Systematic profiling studies resulted in the development of a dedicated hardware accelerator integration and a custom instruction set extension (ISA extension) for bottleneck functions. Tests conducted in a simulation environment revealed that the proposed architecture provides a significant speed increase compared to the standard software solution.
keywords: ["SPHINCS+", "post-quantum cryptography", "RISC-V", "hardware accelerators", "hash-based signatures", "public-key encryption", "NIST PQC standardization", "hardware-software co-optimization"]

title: A 165-GHz Center-Frequency SPDT Switch with 60-GHz Bandwidth Using Reverse-Saturated SiGe HBTs
abstract: This paper presents a 165-GHz single-pole double-throw (SPDT) switch with a 60-GHz bandwidth, designed using reverse-saturated SiGe HBTs in a 0.13-um SiGe BiCMOS process. The switch operates in the 140-200 GHz range, achieving an insertion loss of 2.3-2.9 dB and an isolation of 21.7-22.7 dB when RF pads are excluded. When RF pads are included, insertion loss increases to 2.7-3.7 dB while isolation ranges from 18.9-21.5 dB. The input 1dB compression point (IP1dB) is 15.5 dBm in both cases. The proposed switch leverages a quarter-wave single-shunt topology to minimize insertion loss while maintaining high isolation, confirming its suitability for 6G applications.
keywords: ["SPDT switch", "SiGe HBT", "SiGe BiCMOS", "terahertz switch", "insertion loss", "isolation", "6G applications"]

title: Learning-Assisted Target Localization in Distributed UAV Networks
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a learning-assisted approach for three-dimensional target localization in distributed uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) networks using joint measurements of bistatic range (BR) and space angle (SA). The proposed hybrid method consists of two stages. In the first stage, we employ a physics-informed DeepSets network (PI-DSN) to generate a coarse yet globally reliable estimate in a single forward pass. The second stage then uses this estimate to initialize a Gauss-Newton (GN) solver. Simulation results confirm that our approach achieves Cramér-Rao lower bound (CRLB) accuracy across a broad noise range while outperforming competing methods in both accuracy and execution time.
keywords: ["target localization", "physics-informed neural networks", "Deep Sets", "Cramer-Rao lower bound", "3D localization"]

title: Simulation-Based Analysis of BB84 Decoy-State Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) Protocol on İstanbul Metropolitan Fiber Optic Infrastructure
abstract: The integration of Quantum Key Distribution technologies into existing telecommunications infrastructure, moving beyond laboratory settings, is a critical step for the secure communication networks of the future. However, one of the main obstacles to this transformation is that theoretical models do not fully capture the physical limitations and operational challenges in real-world environments. In this study, the feasibility of a metropolitan-scale link representative of Turkey’s fiber backbone is analyzed based on real-world field data. The simulations were conducted in a Python environment, and the results obtained from Dark fiber over 84,8 km showed quantum bit error rate (QBER) and secret key rate (SKR) of 6,70% and 10,4 bit/s, respectively. For Single-Core fiber, 32,7% QBER and for Multi-Core fiber, 24,1% QBER were achieved.
keywords: ["BB84 protocol", "decoy-state QKD", "quantum key distribution", "dark fiber", "quantum bit error rate", "secret key rate", "multicore fiber", "single-core fiber"]

title: A Lightweight Adaptive Fusion Approach for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis, by integrating diverse information sources like text, audio, and visual cues, yields significantly more accurate outcomes than systems relying on singular data streams. However, a large portion of high-performing models depend on massive networks, resulting in substantial computational overhead. To address this cost dilemma, an adaptive fusion mechanism capable of dynamically measuring and adjusting the influence of different modalities on the model was designed. The primary goal is to achieve effective sentiment detection using a hardware-friendly, lightweight architecture. Upon evaluating this efficient model, it was demonstrated that it attains competitive accuracy rates of 78.28% and 60.58% on the MELD and CMU-MOSEI datasets, respectively, while incurring significantly lower computational costs.
keywords: ["multimodal sentiment analysis", "adaptive fusion", "lightweight models", "computational efficiency", "modality weighting", "audio-visual-text fusion", "MELD dataset", "speech emotion recognition"]

title: Artificial Intelligence for Multi-Hazard Disaster Preparedness and Response
abstract: This paper presents a modular decision support system that infers the primary location of the user or the reported incident and a situation-aware risk level from multi-turn Turkish disaster dialogues between a help-seeking user and an AI-supported emergency assistant. The assistant guides the user with follow-up questions about health status, number of affected people, structural damage, environmental hazards, and known nearby landmarks to complete missing information. The system manages the dialogue with a finite state machine, determines the location by linking user cues to a local GeoJSON point-of-interest database and by landmark verification, and produces explainable risk scores with Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis. The key novelty is treating landmarks as an evidence layer that verifies the current location hypothesis through proximity and clustering instead of directly replacing candidates based on a landmark signal. In a ten-scenario pilot evaluation, accuracy, end-to-end latency, and token usage are reported for three configurations.
keywords: ["disaster response", "decision support system", "location inference", "multi-criteria decision making", "help-seeking", "situational awareness"]

title: Validation of a Radar Signal-Processing Pipeline for 30s Sit-to-Stand Analysis in Older Adults
abstract: The 30-second sit-to-stand test (STS) is a widely used functional assessment in older adults, but routine administration relies on manual observation and yields only a total repetition count. This paper presents a deterministic frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) radar signal-processing pipeline for automated analysis of this test. Twelve participants (mean age 70.3 years, SD 3.7) completed the 30s STS with concurrent but unsynchronised radar and motion-capture acquisition; motioncapture-derived line-of-sight quantities served as the reference for velocity-envelope development and repetition-count evaluation. A gated weighted mean velocity-extraction method was selected for downstream analysis, after which repetition counting was performed using a fixed peak-based detector and a non-personalised adaptive detector. The fixed detector achieved 93.11 percent mean count accuracy; the adaptive detector improved this to 98.21 percent, with all remaining errors within one repetition. These results demonstrate that deterministic FMCW radar can reliably automate STS repetition counting in older adults, supporting its potential as a contactless clinical assessment tool. Future work will target larger cohorts, hardware synchronisation, and richer temporal metrics.
keywords: ["30-second sit-to-stand test", "FMCW radar", "older adults", "functional assessment", "motion capture validation", "radial velocity"]

title: Resolving Color Ambiguity in Image Colorization through Caption Guidance and Probabilistic Decoding
abstract: This paper considers grayscale image colorization as an inherently ambiguous mapping problem in which a single luminance value may correspond to multiple plausible colors. To resolve this ambiguity, two complementary mechanisms are investigated: semantic text conditioning via automatically generated image captions, and probabilistic output modeling via a Mixture Density Network (MDN). Two scenarios are considered depending on whether text guidance is incorporated through cross-attention alone or jointly with feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM). By comparing four model variants on a COCO 2017 subset across multiple perceptual metrics, the trade-offs between pixel-level fidelity and distributional realism are characterized. Although multimodal color distributions are typically difficult to model in a regression framework, the combination of caption-guided conditioning and the MDN output head turns out to be effective in reducing color ambiguity.
keywords: ["image colorization", "image captioning", "mixture density networks", "probabilistic decoding", "cross-attention", "feature-wise linear modulation"]

title: Biyomedikal Sinyallerde Gürültü Giderme İçin Biyolojik Esinli Purkinje Hücre Modeli Tabanlı Uyarlamalı Dijital Filtre
abstract: Bu çalışmada, serebellar Purkinje hücrelerinin sinaptik plastisite dinamiklerinden esinlenen çok kompartmanlı bir uyarlamalı elektroensefalografi (EEG) filtresi sunulmaktadır. Yöntem, proksimal ve distal dendritik işleme kollarını soma bütünleştirme katmanında birleştirerek düşük frekanslı ve geçici bileşenleri birlikte modellemektedir. Öğrenme, tırmanıcı lif (climbing fiber) benzetimli hata sinyali üzerinden eşiksiz ve hataya duyarlı LTD/LTP güncellemesi ile yürütülmekte; uzun dönemli kararlılık için homeostatik ağırlık sınırlama mekanizması kullanılmaktadır. Dört test sinyali (EEG benzetimi, sinüs, chirp ve ECG) üzerinde fs= 160 Hz, 9600 örnek ve n = 20 Monte Carlo koşusuyla yapılan deneyler, önerilen yaklaşımın özellikle değişken bantlı ve geçici bileşen içeren sinyallerde Butterworth ve Kalman filtrelerine göre daha yüksek SNR, daha düşük PRD/MSE, daha iyi korelasyon ve karşılaştırmada genel olarak dengeli bir başarım profili sunduğunu göstermektedir.
keywords: ["adaptive digital filters", "EEG denoising", "synaptic plasticity", "long-term depression", "long-term potentiation", "climbing fibers", "biomedical signal denoising", "transient components"]

title: Comparative Analysis of Learning Rate Strategies in MS Lesion Segmentation with 3D U-Net
abstract: Manual monitoring of lesions in Multiple Sclerosis (MS), which affects the central nervous system, imposes a significant workload on radiologists. In this study, various learning rate (η) scheduling strategies were comparatively analyzed to enhance the performance of a deep learning-based 3D U-Net model in MS lesion segmentation. During the training process, six different LR strategies—Time-Based, Step, Exponential, Adaptive Plateau, Cosine Annealing, and Cyclical—were tested on the MSLesSeg dataset. Model performance was evaluated using Dice Score (DSC), Hausdorff Distance (HD95), TPR, and PPV metrics. Experimental results demonstrated that the Adaptive Plateau (Reduce LR on Plateau) method achieved the highest segmentation success (0.622 DSC) and the lowest geometric error margin (21.695 HD95). The findings confirm the critical importance of hyper-parameter optimization on the generalization capacity and clinical accuracy of models in 3D medical image analysis.
keywords: ["multiple sclerosis", "lesion segmentation", "3D U-Net", "learning rate scheduling", "cosine annealing", "cyclical learning rate", "exponential decay", "hyperparameter optimization", "medical image segmentation"]

title: Clinical Classification-Oriented Ejection Fraction Estimation in Echocardiography
abstract: Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) is the primary clinical parameter for heart failure diagnosis. Existing automatic LVEF estimation methods generally focus on regression accuracy while neglecting classification performance at clinical thresholds. This study presents a pipeline that estimates LVEF from end-diastolic and end-systolic echocardiography frames with an emphasis on clinical classification performance. The proposed approach employs long axis detection based on mask moments, extended geometric features, and a weighted loss function to address class imbalance. The system is evaluated with two segmentation and three EF estimation methods. Results reveal that the lowest regression error does not guarantee the best clinical classification performance.
keywords: ["echocardiography", "heart failure diagnosis", "geometric features", "class imbalance", "weighted loss function", "cardiac image segmentation"]

title: Vision Transformer-Based Cross-Modal Change Detection Method for HD Maps
abstract: In autonomous driving, a high-definition (HD) map is a critical component for lane-level localization and safe self-driving decisions. However, the dynamic nature of urban environments leads to inconsistencies between the real world and pre-built HD maps over time; therefore, changes must be detected reliably in the map maintenance process. In this study, we present a ViT-DeepLabV3+ based change detection framework that detects the change (change/no-change) between a perspective-view camera image and its corresponding egoview projected HD map view, and is robust to domain gap. In our approach, feature maps are generated using DeepLabV3+ based feature extractors specialized for each modality, and these representations are compared with a Vision Transformer to make the change decision. Experimental results show that the proposed method successfully detects changes and achieves better performance than previous studies.
keywords: ["high-definition maps", "autonomous driving", "vision transformer", "map maintenance"]

title: The Schur Complement-Based Covariance Intersection Method
abstract: In distributed data fusion, unknown cross-correlations between estimates are a fundamental issue that limits fusion accuracy. The Covariance Intersection method is frequently used in the literature because it ensures consistency without requiring correlation information; however, it has a high computational cost due to repeated determinant calculations in the optimization process. In this study, a Schur complement-based approach that re-structures the determinant calculation is proposed. The proposed method reduces computational cost by reducing high-dimensional matrix operations to lower-dimensional operations via the Schur complement. This significantly reduces the computational load while preserving the method’s consistency and fusion performance. The results demonstrate that equivalent results are obtained with fewer computations.

title: Optimization of Sub-threshold Bandgap Reference Circuit with Immune Plasma Algorithm
abstract: In this study, the Immune Plasma Algorithm (IPA) is applied to optimize the subthreshold bandgap reference (SBGR) circuit used in low-power analog IC design. The SBGR problem involves multiple analog design constraints, including voltage stability, temperature coefficient, loop gain, phase margin, gain margin, and power consumption, forming a challenging high-dimensional constrained optimization problem.IPA is evaluated across three scenarios—Base, Hard, and High-Dimensional—over 30 independent runs and compared with the Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO) and the Firefly Algorithm (FA). Results show that IPA achieves feasibility rates of 96.7%, 63.3%, and 93.3% in the Base, Hard, and High-Dimensional scenarios, respectively, outperforming GWO (40%, 13.3%, 10%) and FA (53.3%, 23.3%, 13.3%). IPA also provides a higher mean fitness and a stable PSRR around 106.5 dB, confirming its effectiveness.

title: Cross-Domain Video Object Detection
abstract: In this study, a cross-domain video object detector using a DETR-based transformer architecture is presented. The base training of the model is performed as similarity learning using a 1-shot query object. Unlike the common transformer usage that employs only spatial-query-patches, the training utilizes both spatial and temporal information in conjunction. To improve adaptation to the query domain, an online query-example-update layer, which depends on score and overlap criteria, has been added to the inference architecture. During the inference phase, cross-domain object detection performance is examined using VOT-LT2020 videos. In cross-domain video object detection, it is reported that spatio-temporal learning provides improvements of 8.85, 9.79, and 10.79 percent in mAP, AP50, and AP75 scores, respectively, compared to spatial learning alone. With the 1-shot updating, increases of 1.09, 1.67, and 1.58 percent were achieved in mAP, AP50, and AP75 scores, respectively. Comparative performance is reported by utilizing the CNN-based DeFRCN and ViT-based CD-ViTO architectures from the literature for cross-space video object detection.
keywords: ["DETR", "transformer models", "similarity learning", "spatiotemporal learning", "video object tracking"]

title: Performance Analysis of Integrated Sensing and Communication in Tunnel Environments
abstract: ISAC (Integrated Sensing and Communication) technology stands out as a critical approach that enhances bandwidth efficiency and enables next-generation intelligent network applications by combining sensing and communication functions on a common spectrum, waveform, and hardware infrastructure. This study comparatively examines RF-ISAC (Radio Frequency-based ISAC) and O-ISAC (Optical-based ISAC) systems operating in tunnel environments under a unified framework encompassing transmitter, channel, and receiver models. While multi-antenna structures and complex signaling methods are considered in the RF-ISAC model, optical transmission is modeled under the constraints of intensity modulation and direct sensing in the O-ISAC model. Due to the challenging characteristics of tunnel environments, such as limited geometry, multipath propagation, waveguide effects, and direct and off-line-of-sight transitions, physically consistent channel representations have been developed for both systems; thus, it is possible to evaluate sensing and communication performances under the same assumptions. Using simulation parameters consistent with experimental findings in the literature, the relationships between BER (Bit Error Rate) and SNR (Signal to Noise Ratio), detection probability and SNR, range and SNR, and bandwidth and range resolution were analyzed, and the obtained results were evaluated.
keywords: ["integrated sensing and communication", "tunnel environment", "channel modeling", "intensity modulation", "multipath propagation", "waveguide effect", "bit error rate", "detection probability", "multiple antennas"]

title: Comparative Security Framework for Privacy-Preserving Small Language Models
abstract: This study examines privacy-preserving uses of small language models along three axes: on-device inference, parameter-efficient fine-tuning, and retrieval-augmented generation. Our analysis shows that each method introduces distinct security vulnerabilities. For device-centric solutions, physical access and device compromise are primary risks; for fine-tuning, adapter leakage emerges as a key concern; and for retrieval-augmented generation systems, index security is a critical weak point. The literature review further indicates that inconsistent threat-model definitions and heterogeneous evaluation metrics weaken cross-approach comparability. Overall, the findings high-light the need for hybrid security architectures and standardized protocols.
keywords: ["small language models", "privacy preservation", "on-device inference", "parameter-efficient fine-tuning", "retrieval-augmented generation", "threat model", "security vulnerabilities"]

title: A Multi-Cohort Stable Gene Panel for Parkinson's Disease Detection from Blood Genomics
abstract: This study proposes Heterogeneity-Penalized Cross-Cohort Stability Scoring (H-CSP) to distinguish Parkinson's disease (PD) patients from healthy controls using blood. Four GEO microarray datasets (GSE6613, GSE57475, GSE72267, GSE99039; 754 samples, 4 platforms) were used. H-CSP penalizes platform-inconsistent gene expressions via the I2statistic. Under a Leave-One-Dataset-Out (LODO) protocol with cohort-independent normalization, a 37-gene consensus panel reached a cross-platform discrimination of AUC= 0.810±0.074 (sensitivity 0.76, specificity 0.72) with L2-regularized logistic regression. Under a fully nested, leakage-free evaluation H-CSP achieved AUC = 0.626 ± 0.081, within the performance range of recent single-cohort panels (AUC≈ 0.60) assessed under the same protocol. Its distinctive contribution is reducing cross-cohort performance variance, yielding a consistent gene selection. CACNA1D, RGS2, PTGDS and BCL2L2 are linked to PD pathogenesis.

title: An Efficient Technique for Low Rank and Sparse Decomposition of Matrices
abstract: Low-rank and sparse matrix decomposition techniques generally require prior knowledge of matrix properties or rely on computationally expensive convex relaxations. These methods often employ parameters that are sensitive to noise. In this study, an iterative technique utilizing Stiefel manifolds is presented to achieve efficient convergence without requiring prior information on rank or sparsity levels. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed technique achieves superior performance compared to well-known alternatives in terms of both efficiency and robustness.

title: StimBench: A Video Benchmark for Stereotypical Motor Movement Detection in Autism Spectrum Disorder
abstract: Existing video datasets for stereotypical motor movement (stimming) detection in Autism Spectrum Disorder are distributed as YouTube URL lists that degrade over time, limiting reproducibility. We introduce StimBench, a frozen, face-anonymized benchmark of 333 clips across three stimming classes and a normal class, with video-level splits and a gender-balanced test set. Across 27 configurations spanning six architectures and four parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) strategies, V-JEPA 2 with LoRA achieves the best result at over 90 percent accuracy while updating only a small fraction of parameters. PEFT consistently outperforms full fine-tuning under limited clinical data. Gender-stratified analysis shows the largest male–female gaps among fully fine-tuned models (e.g., I3D at 57.1%/41.2%), though gaps remain variable across adapted models as well. The dataset and code are publicly available at https://github.com/UlkuTuncerKucuktas/StimBench.
keywords: ["stimming", "autism spectrum disorder", "video benchmark", "parameter-efficient fine-tuning", "LoRa", "gender gap", "face anonymization", "video action recognition"]

title: Particle Filter-Based Location Tracking with Cellular Network Parameters and Data-Driven Measurement Modeling
abstract: This study proposes a mobile tracking system based on cellular network parameters for scenarios where GPS signals are inadequate in urban environments. In the proposed architecture, the non-linear relationship between physical location and network measurements - namely Reference Signal Received Power (RSRP), Reference Signal Received Quality (RSRQ), and Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) - is first modeled using Random Forest regression. Subsequently, this model is integrated as the measurement model into a Particle Filter framework characterized by irregular sampling intervals. To mitigate the uncertainty arising from irregular sampling steps in field data, an approach incorporating temporal dynamics into the system model has been developed. Experiments conducted with real-world field data verify that the proposed method reduces the localization error to below 20 meters.
keywords: ["location tracking", "particle filter", "GPS-denied environments", "urban localization", "RSRP", "RSRQ", "SINR", "random forest regression", "measurement modeling", "non-uniform sampling", "temporal dynamics", "mobile device tracking"]

title: Vibration-Based Fault Detection in Rotating Machinery: The Effect of Accelerometer Position and Ensemble Learning
abstract: This study investigates fault detection in electric motors using machine learning applied to vibration data collected from a laboratory-based test setup. The dataset comprises five experimental conditions: healthy, slight unbalance, severe unbalance, rotor fault, and bearing fault. The influence of three sensor positions on classification performance was assessed. Machine learning algorithms and an ensemble model were evaluated using statistical features extracted from both time and frequency domains across various motor speeds and load conditions. The findings indicate that sensor position significantly affects classification, with the drive end sensor yielding higher and more consistent performance. The ensemble model achieved the highest accuracy by integrating the strengths of multiple classifiers, although its improvement over individual models was limited.
keywords: ["vibration-based fault detection", "rotating machinery", "electric motors", "ensemble learning", "rotor faults", "bearing defects", "statistical features", "time and frequency domain features"]

title: Three-Dimensional Radar Algorithms for the Detection and Tracking of Drones
abstract: In this study, a three-dimensional detection and tracking approach based on a 24 GHz frequency-modulated continuous-wave radar is presented for drone detection applications. The proposed structure includes an integrated detection and tracking algorithm based on processing radar data in range, velocity, and angle dimensions. In the processing pipeline, detection, clustering, data association, and Kalman-based tracking steps are applied sequentially to obtain stable target tracks. The objective of the study is to examine the performance of the system on real measurement data and to reveal the effect of track continuity and false association behavior on target tracking. Results obtained from drone scenarios show that the proposed approach provides an applicable and effective solution for low-visibility targets with high measurement variability.
keywords: ["drone detection", "drone tracking", "target detection", "data association", "Kalman filter tracking", "clustering", "track continuity", "measurement variability"]

title: AMSEG: Adaptive Multi-Channel STA/LTA Detection of Impulsive Acoustic Events on UAVs
abstract: In this paper, the Adaptive Multichannel STA/LTA Energy Gate (AMSEG) method, based on the STA/LTA (Short-Term Average / Long-Term Average) ratio, is proposed to detect impulsive muzzle-blast-like events in acoustic recordings obtained from a six-element Uniform Circular Array (UCA) on noisy platforms. Instead of applying costly operations such as Wiener filtering or wavelet transform to the entire recording, AMSEG determines the event time interval using adaptive thresholds and thus reduces the data processing load. The windowed signals with high Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) are transferred to the Generalized Cross-Correlation – Phase Transform (GCC-PHAT) algorithm for direction estimation. In addition, it was observed that the combined use of Least Squares (LS) and Exhaustive Search (ES) methods reduces angular error under intense harmonic noise. The results show that this dynamic windowing approach improves Direction of Arrival (DoA) estimation and reduces computational cost.
keywords: ["adaptive thresholding", "uniform circular array", "direction of arrival estimation", "GCC-PHAT", "harmonic noise", "computational complexity reduction"]

title: Performance Analysis of Chebyshev Filters
abstract: Ring resonator-based optical filters are key components in Wavelength Division Multiplexing (WDM) systems due to their frequency selectivity and compact design. Although the designs of Butterworth and Chebyshev optical filters are well-established in the literature, the reliability of their performance under realistic manufacturing constraints remains a challenge. In this study, high-order Chebyshev optical filters designed using step-index fibre couplers have been analysed. Here, the filters were examined using the Unified Error Model, which simultaneously accounts for coupling coefficients, waveguide losses and phase errors. In light of Monte Carlo simulations, quantitative signal integrity metrics such as the maximum Q-factor and eye height have been determined in conjunction with manufacturing tolerances. The results obtained demonstrate that the proposed design maintains a safe margin with a zero error rate up to tolerance levels of 5%, and provides a design guideline for nextgeneration optical networks.
keywords: ["ring resonator", "wavelength division multiplexing", "manufacturing tolerances", "quality factor", "eye height", "signal integrity", "high-order filters", "waveguide loss", "phase error"]

title: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning and Deep Learning Methods for Malware Detection in Portable Executable Files
abstract: Zararlı yazılımlar (malware), Taşınabilir Çalıştırılabilir (PE) dosyalar üzerinden siber güvenliği ciddi şekilde tehdit etmektedir. Bu çalışmada, PE dosyalarından elde edilen statik analiz öznitelikleriyle zararlı yazılım tespiti için makine ögrenmesi ve derin öğrenme modellerinin performansları karşılaştırılmıştır. Toplam 62.485 örnek ve 15 öznitelikten oluşan veri seti üzerinde Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM ve CatBoost gibi ağaç tabanlı topluluk modelleri ile MLP, DNN ve 1D-CNN derin öğrenme mimarileri eğitilmiştir. Deneysel sonuçlar, düşük boyutlu tabular verilerde topluluk algoritmalarının derin öğrenme modellerinden daha üstün performans gösterdiğini kanıtlamıştır. Modeller arasında Random Forest, 99.65% dogruluk (accuracy) ve 99.59% F1-skoru ile en yüksek başarıyı elde etmiştir. Bu akademik çalışma, zararlı yazılım tespitinde donanım maliyeti yüksek derin sinir ağları yerine, hafif ve performanslı ağaç tabanlı modellerin daha verimli bir çözüm sunduğunu göstermektedir.

title: A Wideband High-Gain Antipodal Antenna with Mitre Reflector for SATCOM Applications
abstract: This paper presents the design and characterization of a low-cost antipodal Vivaldi antenna (AVA) featuring a mitre-shaped reflector for various applications, including satellite communication ground terminals. Realized on a low-cost FR-4 substrate, the antenna is designed to provide high-gain wideband operation covering C and X band communications (4–10 GHz). The mitre-shaped reflector is optimized to serve as a gain booster, achieving a maximum realized gain of 10.9 dBi. Cross-validation results using two independent electromagnetic simulation soft-ware packages (CST and CEMS) demonstrate that the antenna exhibits a return loss better than 10 dB from 4 GHz to 20 GHz, while maintaining operational capability beyond 20 GHz with reduced performance. Due to the intrinsic limitations of the FR-4 substrate, experimental measurements on the fabricated prototype were conducted up to 20 GHz.

title: Comparison of the Effectiveness of Semi-Supervised and Self-Supervised Learning in Low Data Regimes in Medical Image Analysis
abstract: This study compares supervised, semi-supervised (EMA-FixMatch), and self-supervised (SimSiam) learning approaches on the TissueMNIST dataset to address the labeled data scarcity in histopathological image analysis. The ConvNeXt-Tiny architecture was used as the common backbone in all experiments; the models were tested under label ratios of 5%, 10%, and 100%. The results show that supervised learning achieved the highest performance with 71.4% accuracy in the fully labeled scenario; in the limited-label scenarios, the EMA-FixMatch method outperformed the SimSiam-based approach (65.1% with 10% labels; 59.5% with 5% labels). The results highlight the effectiveness of semi-supervised learning under data scarcity and the reliability of supervised transfer learning when sufficient data is available.
keywords: ["semi-supervised learning", "self-supervised learning", "supervised learning", "limited labeled data", "histopathology image analysis", "SimSiam", "ConvNeXt-Tiny", "transfer learning", "medical image classification"]

title: Fast and Robust IVIM Parameter Estimation in Breast MRI Using Physics-Informed Deep Learning
abstract: The intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM) model provides a powerful framework for quantifying tissue diffusion and perfusion properties in breast MRI without contrast agents. However, IVIM parameter estimation is an inherently ill-conditioned inverse problem, and its conventional solution via nonlinear least squares (NLLS) fitting is both highly sensitive to noise and computationally slow. In this study, we employ PIA-IVIM, a physics-informed autoencoder architecture designed to solve the IVIM inverse problem in a fast and noise-robust manner. The model integrates the IVIM signal equation into the decoder as a deterministic constraint and is trained through self-supervised learning, enabling parameter estimation in a single forward pass. PIA-IVIM reduces estimation time from minutes to milliseconds —approximately 10,000 times faster than NLLS— enabling real-time analysis of high-resolution breast MRI data. In addition to its computational efficiency, numerical simulations and experiments on 1,000 digital phantom cases demonstrate that PIA-IVIM achieves lower estimation error and higher correlation than NLLS under clinical noise levels.
keywords: ["intravoxel incoherent motion", "breast MRI", "physics-informed deep learning", "self-supervised learning", "noise-robust estimation", "ill-conditioned inverse problems", "real-time image analysis"]

title: Centrality Aware AODV Routing for FANETs
abstract: End-to-end unmanned aerial vehicle networks suffer from overloading of central nodes due to shortest-path routing strategies. This study presents the CA-AODV approach, which integrates distributed eigenvector centrality computation into the AODV routing protocol. The proposed protocol employs a two-phase eigenvector computation mechanism, RREQ (Route Request) buffering for best-path selection, and a centrality-based link cost function to divert traffic away from central nodes. Simulation results conducted with OMNeT++ on a 50-node UAV network demonstrate that CA-AODV achieves up to %3.7 improvement in packet delivery ratio, up to %25.3 reduction in end-to-end delay, and %3.5 increase in sum rate compared to standard AODV under high traffic loads.
keywords: ["AODV routing protocol", "UAV networks", "eigenvector centrality", "link cost function", "traffic load balancing", "packet delivery ratio", "end-to-end delay"]

title: A Deep Learning Approach for SDR-Based Automatic Modulation Classification
abstract: Deep learning has become an indispensable component of next-generation communication systems and stands out with advantages such as automatic feature extraction from high-dimensional data, the ability to model non-linear relationships, and adaptation to changing channel conditions. Although there are numerous studies in the literature specifically addressing problems such as modulation classification, signal detection, and channel estimation, it is observed that real-time applications are still limited. Based on this, in this study, a raw IQ dataset obtained using software-defined radios was processed with a dual-stream residual network-based deep learning model to perform automatic modulation classification. The results obtained were comprehensively analyzed with parameters such as different modulation types, levels, and transmission distance. Experimental findings show that the modulation classification accuracy is over 90.1% at all signal-to-noise ratio levels.
keywords: ["automatic modulation classification", "software-defined radio", "deep learning", "real-time signal processing", "signal-to-noise ratio robustness", "transmission distance"]

title: Image Based Detection of Low Probability of Intercept LoRa Signals
abstract: Low Probability of Intercept (LPI) communication signals, used as an electronic protection method, have special modulations that spread their spectrum across a wide band. In this way, the detectability of the signals becomes more difficult, and their resistance against electronic jamming increases. One example of LPI signals generated in different forms is the Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) modulation technique. LoRa, which falls under the category of Low-Power Wide-Area Networks (LPWAN) in wireless communication technologies, is modulated using the CSS technique. This study proposes a new method based on image processing via spectrogram for automatic LoRa signal detection and parameter extraction. The aim is to extract the bandwidth, center frequency, symbol duration, preamble duration, packet duration, and spreading factor (SF) parameters of the detected LoRa signals. LoRa signals with unknown configurations were passed through various channels by creating spectrum density in a laboratory environment. The performance of the developed method was tested by acquiring IQ (In-phase Quadrature) records via SDR (Software Defined Radio). With the developed algorithm, LoRa signal detection was performed with high accuracy even below the noise level for all configurations.
keywords: ["LoRa", "low probability of intercept", "chirp spread spectrum", "signal detection", "spectrogram", "image processing", "low-power wide-area networks", "parameter extraction", "electronic protection", "software-defined radio"]

title: RF Front-End LNA Design for Radar Receiver Applications
abstract: An LNA MMIC (Monolithic microwave integrated circuit) was designed using a 0.15 μm GaAs pseudomorphic high electron mobility transistor (pHEMT) process for radar receiver applications operating in the 2.7-3.5 GHz frequency band. In the designed cascade topology, the first stage is used to minimize overall noise, while the second stage is designed to increase gain. The circuit exhibits a noise figure (NF) below 0.6 dB and a nearly flat gain greater than 20 dB across the frequency band. The RLC negative-feedback network and the input/output matching networks help achieve control, improve gain flatness, and broaden bandwidth. The design has input/output return-loss values S11and S22better than 15 dB, all within a compact chip size of 1.1×1.1 mm2.

title: Relational Feature Selection and Uncertainty Quantification for Financial Time Series Forecasting
abstract: The contribution of this study is to improve the success of stock forecasting and to perform reliability analysis through uncertainty estimation. In the first stage of the study, a common change matrix was created by examining the directional movement of stocks in the same financial sector, and the most correlated stocks for a selected stock were determined using association rule analysis (ARM). A model was designed to predict the closing prices of the selected main stock from t+1 to t+5 days, and not only its own historical values but also the stocks selected through association analysis were used as input signals. Dual Attention Networks (DAN) were used in time series modeling. In the second stage of the study, uncertainty analysis was performed on the forecasting models using the Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD) method, and the points where uncertainty changes in forward forecasts were marked. The proposed methods were validated with a stock selected from the BIST database.
keywords: ["stock price prediction", "financial time series forecasting", "uncertainty quantification", "association rule mining", "dual attention network", "Monte Carlo dropout"]

title: Can We Trust LLMs? Inter-model Reliability and Geopolitical Bias under Zero-Shot Classification
abstract: This study analyzes the classification consistency of Large Language Models (LLMs) using geopolitical texts collected from social media. Data gathered under the headings of the United States, Russia, and China were classified using a zero-shot prompt with six different state-of-the-art LLMs ranging from 12 to 32 billion parameters. The level of inter-model agreement was measured in a multidimensional manner. The findings reveal that the inter-model split rate exceeded 70% across all topics and that consensus on specific topics, such as Russia, was statistically insignificant. Consequently, it was determined that inter-model inconsistencies are influenced by model size and architecture. Additionally, it was found that models originating from China and the U.S. also exhibited inconsistent labeling among themselves. In conclusion, researchers should not blindly trust LLM models in zero-shot classification tasks; properly designed validity and reliability tests must also be conducted.
keywords: ["large language models", "zero-shot classification", "inter-model agreement", "geopolitical bias", "model reliability", "social media text", "United States", "Russia", "China", "trust in AI"]

title: Intrusion Detection with Random Forest and XGBoost Architecture: A Soft Voting Approach
abstract: With the expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) and cloud computing networks, the volume and complexity of cyberattacks have increased. Traditional signature-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) are insufficient, especially in unstable datasets and complex attack vectors. In this study, a hybrid ensemble learning model combining Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) algorithms is proposed to improve network security. The model makes decisions by weighting the probability scores of the classifiers using a "Soft Voting" mechanism. In experiments conducted on the NSL-KDD dataset, the proposed model achieved a 99.91% accuracy rate, surpassing most current (2024-2025) studies in literature. Furthermore, feature importance analysis is performed to increase the model's transparency, and the 20 most critical features are identified. Finally, the data space is visualized in 3D using the t-SNE algorithm, and it has been observed that the attack classes are separable.

title: Modeling High-Order Systems with Nature-Inspired Optimization Algorithms
abstract: This study analyzes the effectiveness of the Forest Optimization Algorithm (FOA), Grey Wolf Optimizer (GWO), and Wild Geese Algorithm (WGA) in modeling high-order systems. Simulation studies, based on the modeling of eighth and sixth-order systems with a second-order model, evaluate the algorithms in terms of integral squared error (ISE), standard deviation of error, runtime, and convergence criteria. The findings show that all three algorithms yield competitive results in model order reduction compared to the existing literature. The GWO, in particular, stands out by exhibiting high modeling success with the shortest running time; the WGA provides promising ISE results in reasonable timeframes; and the FOA offers effective performance when parameter fit is achieved. Consequently, it is predicted that enhanced versions of these methods have high potential in system modeling.

title: Contrastive Wrong-Label Evaluation of Signal Grounding vs. Template Parroting in LLM-Based Bearing Fault Explainers
abstract: Bearing failures in electric motors make vibration-based early fault detection essential. Deep learning classifiers achieve high accuracy but their black-box nature limits trustworthiness; large language models (LLMs) have been employed to provide natural language explanations for these classifications. However, existing methods measure only linguistic quality and cannot verify whether the model genuinely processes the signal or simply generates template text matching the provided label. A model that confirms any diagnosis regardless of signal content offers no real explainability. A contrastive wrong-label evaluation is proposed: the LLM receives real vibration data (audio waveform + short-time Fourier transform (STFT) spectrogram) with a deliberately incorrect fault label, testing whether it detects the mismatch. Qwen3-Omni is fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) on the Paderborn dataset, and the contrastive ratio is varied from 0% to 100%. The 0% and 100% ratios exhibit template behavior, while 45% achieves the best trade-off.
keywords: ["bearing fault diagnosis", "vibration signal analysis", "large language models", "explainable AI", "low-rank adaptation", "natural language explanations"]

title: Analysis of Fracture-Based Temporal Abstractions in Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the generalization capacity of an automated option discovery framework in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (RL). The targeted method is based on the clustering of fixed-length action sequences, referred to as "Fractures", which are extracted from successful trajectories. The fractures identified as most useful are incorporated into the agent's action space as options. In this study, we systematically analyze how options derived from a simple source task accelerate learning in structurally different and more complex target tasks. Additionally, we analyze the impact of the number of options, a hyperparameter chosen by the experimenter, whose effect on learning performance has not been previously investigated. The findings address existing gaps in the literature and provide critical insights into the scalability and task transfer success of the Fracture framework.
keywords: ["hierarchical reinforcement learning", "option discovery", "temporal abstraction", "generalization", "task transfer", "accelerated learning"]

title: Evaluation of End-to-End RAG Performance in Turkish Legal Texts
abstract: Abstract-Recently, large language models (LLMs) have enabled significant advances across a wide range of domains. However, the training, adaptation, and evaluation of LLMs with a large number of parameters incur substantial computational and financial costs. This limits the ability of researchers with constrained resources to effectively leverage LLM-based approaches. In this study, we examine the performance of relatively small-scale LLMs for question answering and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) on Turkish legal texts under limited computational resources. We investigate several factors affecting Turkish RAG performance and adapt embedding models to the target domain using automatically generated question-context pairs. The findings indicate that relatively small, domain-adapted models can achieve performance levels close to those of larger-scale or commercial models on the target dataset.
keywords: ["retrieval-augmented generation", "question answering", "domain adaptation", "embedding models", "Turkish language"]

title: Risk Sensitive Semantic Flow Management in Capacity Constrained Wireless Systems
abstract: This study addresses the capacity constraints created by increasing device and data density using an adaptive data management approach based on semantic communication. In a fixed-capacity system with multiple data streams, the primary objective is to protect critical data and reduce unnecessary data load. To this end, a risk-sensitive reinforcement learning-based mode adaptation method is proposed. The system consists of three data types: general user traffic, sensor data, and camera streams. While critical sensor data is prioritized for protection, non-critical sensor and camera streams are dynamically scaled through a total of nine modes with three levels of adaptation. The decision-making mechanism selects the most suitable mode based on traffic density and risk level. Simulation results show that, especially under high traffic loads, the proposed method significantly reduces average data loss and increases system efficiency compared to the fixed-mode approach.
keywords: ["semantic communication", "reinforcement learning", "capacity constraints", "traffic density", "data loss reduction", "adaptive resource allocation"]

title: Performance Analysis of Superimposed Pilot Channel Estimation for OTFS in Fractional Doppler Channels
abstract: Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) modulation is a promising technology for 6G and beyond, as it overcomes severe Doppler shifts in high-mobility environments. However, physical channel paths introduce fractional Doppler shifts that cause inter-Doppler interference. Conventional pilot-based channel estimation mitigates this by transmitting pilots in time-multiplexed frames (block pilots), which degrades spectral efficiency. In this study, a Superimposed Pilot (SP) based channel estimation architecture for OTFS is implemented and evaluated against Block Pilot, Pseudo-Noise sequence, and Ideal Channel State Information methods. By overlaying the pilot directly onto the data across the delay-Doppler grid, the need for dedicated pilot time slots is eliminated. Simulation results under 3GPP Extended Vehicular A conditions at 500 km/h show that the SP scheme achieves higher throughput than the Block Pilot scheme while maintaining comparable reliability at high signal-to-noise ratio.
keywords: ["orthogonal time frequency space", "superimposed pilots", "channel estimation", "pseudonoise sequences", "high-speed mobile communication", "6G", "vehicular channel", "throughput"]

title: Sparse Reconstruction for Radar Based Vital Sign Monitoring Using Orthogonal Matching Pursuit
abstract: Radar based vital sign monitoring provides a contactless approach for the continuous estimation of respiration and heart rate, with potential applications in healthcare and assistive living. However, conventional spectral analysis methods may have limited capability in resolving weak cardiac components, particularly in the presence of noise and dominant respiration signals. In this work, a sparse reconstruction approach based on Orthogonal Matching Pursuit is proposed for vital sign estimation. The method operates on the phase signal obtained from a selected range bin and models physiological motion as a sparse representation in the frequency domain. This formulation enables improved separation of respiration and heartbeat components compared to conventional approaches. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide reliable estimation under practical measurement conditions, indicating its suitability for remote and continuous monitoring applications.
