title: A PyCaret-Assisted Comparative Study of AI/ML Models for Anomaly Detection in 5G and 6G Networks
abstract: Early detection of events such as cell outages, base station failures, sudden traffic changes, and service degradations is critical for network resilience and service continuity in 5G and 6G networks. In this study, multiple AI/ML models were comparatively evaluated within a PyCaret-based experimental pipeline for a supervised binary classification problem based on anomaly labels. The results show that K-Nearest Neighbors, CatBoost, and Random Forest emerged as the most prominent models; on the held-out test set, K-Nearest Neighbors achieved the highest overall performance with a macro-F1 score of 0.9246 and an accuracy of 0.9430, while CatBoost provided the highest precision of 0.9216 for the positive class. The findings indicate that the PyCaret-based approach offers a practical and reproducible framework for model selection, comparative analysis, and rapid experimentation in network anomaly detection problems.
keywords: ["network anomaly detection", "5G", "6G", "PyCaret", "model comparison", "k-nearest neighbors", "CatBoost", "random forest", "binary classification", "network resilience", "base station failure", "service degradation"]

title: Design of a Switched Yagi–Uda Patch Antenna Array for Amplitude-Comparison Direction Finding in Aerial Vehicles
abstract: This study presents the design, components, and performance analysis of a multi-directional antenna operating at 2.4 GHz and capable of beam tilting in four directions. The aim is to develop a compact antenna for amplitude-comparison direction finding, offering a more volume-efficient solution than similar work in literature. The antenna is optimized for installation on the underside of aerial platforms. To represent the electromagnetic influence of the aircraft fuselage, a conductive surface is placed at a defined distance from the antenna and included in the simulation to model platform effects. Each antenna element is designed to produce a stable radiation pattern focused on a specific direction. An initial geometry is created, the radiation direction is controlled using a partially reflective surface, the feed structure is optimized, and the system is expanded into a four-antenna switched architecture. Return loss, gain, beam tilt, and mutual coupling are evaluated using full-wave simulations.
keywords: ["Yagi-Uda antenna", "microstrip antenna array", "beam tilt", "aerial vehicles", "2.4 GHz", "partially reflective surface", "mutual coupling", "compact antenna design"]

title: Delta-Sigma Based Signal Shaping and Limit Cycle Analysis in Multi-Stage Series Converter Systems
abstract: This study addresses the mitigation of limit cycle oscillations caused by hardware quantization constraints in an 8-stage Input-Parallel Output-Series (IPOS) Flyback converter architecture using digital signal processing techniques. The coarse-step effect induced by a 10-bit hardware PWM resolution within a 1 mV precision feedback loop causes the system to exhibit unstable oscillations around the target voltage level . To overcome this limitation, a dithering algorithm based on first-order Delta-Sigma modulation is proposed and implemented within a FreeRTOS environment. Experimental findings demonstrate that the proposed dithering method effectively reduces 30 mV quantization jumps to within a 2 mV error band and significantly prevents instability propagation between series-connected stages by stabilizing the dynamic reference points of the stack . The results confirm that software-based noise shaping and temporal averaging can successfully bypass the physical resolution limits of low-cost microcontrollers in high-precision power applications.
keywords: ["sigma-delta modulator", "dithering", "limit cycle oscillations", "quantization error", "flyback converter", "noise shaping", "FreeRTOS"]

title: Analysis of SAR Exposure for Different Age Groups and 6G Perspective
abstract: In this study, the dosimetric effects of the 2.4 GHz frequency band on human head models were comprehensively investigated in terms of age-dependent dielectric changes, antenna position, and distance parameters. Simulations were conducted using Altair Feko software by creating head phantoms representing the 1-80 age range. The findings demonstrated that distance is the most critical parameter determining exposure; moving the device merely 2 cm away from the tissue reduces the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) value by an average of %70, bringing it below safe limits. In the analysis of five different anatomical regions, it was found that 1-year-old models were subjected to %86-%110 higher local exposure compared to the 80-year-old group. Furthermore, while 2.4 GHz signals penetrate deeply into brain tissue, it was established that 6G frequencies are absorbed solely at the skin surface due to the Absorbed Power Density (APD) mechanism, thereby providing a current safety perspective for next-generation communication technologies.
keywords: ["specific absorption rate", "2.4 GHz", "6G", "human head model", "absorbed power density", "head phantom"]

title: Ideal-Based Code Construction and Low-Complexity Hybrid Decoding Over Gaussian Integer Rings
abstract: In this paper, a novel ideal-based linear code family defined over Gaussian integer rings and compatible with restricted error models is proposed. The algebraic construction of the proposed codes allows for the exact correction of specific error patterns. At the receiver side, as an alternative to the computational complexity caused by the traditional Maximum Likelihood (ML) rule at large constellation sizes, an S-Search algorithm that restricts the search space solely to a fixed-element error set is presented. Furthermore, a hybrid decoding architecture utilizing a dynamic reliability threshold has been developed to autonomously adapt to channel quality and preserve error performance for risky symbols near the decision boundaries. Simulation results obtained under the AWGN channel demonstrate that the proposed hybrid algorithm exhibits an error performance close to that of the ML algorithm, while significantly reducing the computational load by making it completely independent of the constellation size.

title: An Artificial Intelligence-Based Hardware Architecture for LDPC Decoding
abstract: This study presents an integrated hardware and learning framework for Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) decoders. The proposed design integrates a fully parallel Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) architecture with a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) that replaces the fixed majority-based Variable Node Unit (VNU) decision mechanism with a trainable Perceptron-VNU structure. The learned VNU employs sigmoid-based neural modules that are trained offline and utilize shared weights. The obtained results demonstrate that the proposed method provides equivalent FER performance to conventional decoders, while maintaining limited hardware overhead. These findings indicate that hard-decision LDPC decoding can be efficiently realized on FPGA platforms and can be further enhanced with a compact and trainable local decision model.

title: Outage Performance of RIS-Assisted LEO Satellite Communication Systems with Alamouti Coding
abstract: In this study, a cooperative Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite communication system is investigated. The system consists of a transmitting LEO satellite operating at a low elevation angle, a reflective LEO satellite equipped with a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), and a ground user (GU). The transmitting LEO satellite employs Alamouti space-time block coding to achieve full diversity gain while reducing channel-state information burden. Communication between the transmitting LEO satellite and GU is established through both the direct and the RIS-LEO satellite links, and all corresponding channels are modeled as shadowed-Rician fading. To demonstrate the system performance, the outage probability is evaluated via Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Comparison of Classical and Cyclic Analysis Methods for Estimating Propeller Features with Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: The fundamental shaft frequency f0and number of blades (NOB) parameters, which are of critical importance in ship acoustic signature analysis, can be determined via DEMON and ICMC analyses of propeller-induced noise. In this study, a model based on one-dimensional convolutional neural networks (1D-CNN) is proposed for the automatic estimation of the f0and NOB parameters. As model inputs, spectral outputs obtained from DEMON and ICMC analyses are used, and the effects of these features on estimation performance are comparatively examined. Analyses performed on simulation data based on realistic target noise models reveal which method achieves higher performance in the deep learning-based estimation process. The findings show that the features derived from ICMC analysis significantly enhance the performance of the 1D-CNN model and provide higher accuracy compared to the DEMON method.

title: Fault Detection on Electronic Boards with MSPRT
abstract: This study presents a real time fault detection system for circuit boards using thermal imaging sequences. The framework uses time varying Gaussian distributions to model the heating profiles of various components over time. Classification is handled by the Multi Hypothesis Sequential Probability Ratio Test (MSPRT) and it makes diagnostic decisions by collecting statistical data across consecutive frames. To ensure the system is not affected by sensor noise or sudden thermal changes, a stability rule are used. This rule requires the decision threshold to be reached for a specific number of frames in a row N before a final result is confirmed. The method reduces inspection time by identifying the correct class as soon as the evidence meets the threshold.

title: VMD and Cortical Region Analysis Based Mental Attention State Detection from EEG Signals
abstract: In this study, a Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD)-based classification method is presented for the detection of mental attention states (focused, unfocused, and drowsy) using EEG signals. EEG signals were analyzed in six cortical regions: prefrontal, frontal, frontocentral, temporal, parietal, and occipital. The five sub-bands extracted using the VMD method were extracted for statistical, entropy, and Hjorth features, as well as band powers derived from the signal itself. In the analysis with 10-fold cross-validation, the highest success rate of 85.21% was achieved in the frontal region using the Ensemble Bagged Trees classification model. Although the number of features was reduced to 20 using Chi-2 feature selection analysis, the Ensemble Bagged Trees model achieved 81.13% accuracy in the prefrontal region, offering the architecture with the lowest computational cost. When the features extracted from all cortical regions were combined and classified using a Quadratic SVM model, the study achieved an accuracy of 88.96%, a specificity of 94.97%, an F1 score of 89.04, and an MCC value of 83.55, demonstrating the highest performance in the study for detecting mental attention states.

title: Interpretable Fall Detection via Scene Graphs: Decision Fusion with Constrained LinUCB
abstract: Falls are a leading cause of serious injuries among older adults; however, vision-based fall detection systems often produce high false alarms due to confusion between support surfaces such as beds or chairs and the floor. This study presents an interpretable fall detection framework in which each video frame is represented as a scene graph encoding person posture, objects, and person–support surface relations. The perception stage integrates object detection, human pose estimation, monocular depth estimation, and segmentation; floor geometry is estimated via RANSAC-based plane fitting, and the most plausible support surface for each person is selected using a scoring function. Changes between consecutive scene graphs are reduced to a 13-dimensional feature vector and evaluated using a constrained LinUCB decision module. Experiments on the URFall and CAUCAFall datasets achieve 0.960 recall and 0.800 F1-score, with alarms reported through humanreadable short explanations.

title: Türevlenebilir Radon Köprüleme ve Çapraz Dikkat Füzyonu ile Çift Alanlı Düşük Doz BT İyileştirme
abstract: Özet-Düşük doz bilgisayarıı tomografi (LDCT), yüksek doz bilgisayarlı tomografiye (HDCT) nazaran radyasyon maruziyetini azaltır ancak projeksiyon ölçümlerinde kuantum gürültüsünü artırır; bu durum, rekonstrüksiyon sonrası benekli dokular ve çizgisel artefaktların ortaya çıkmasına neden olur. Bu çalışmada, türevlenebilir Radon/FBP katmanları aracılığıyla bir sinogram U-Net ile bir görüntü U-Net'i birbirine bağlayan çift katmanlı bir iyileştirme çerçevesi sunuyoruz. Buna ek olarak, alanlar arası özellik aktarımını denetlemek amacıyla, çapraz dikkat (cross-attention) tabanlı bir birleştirme mekanizması kullanmaktayız. Eşleştirilmiş LDCT/HDCT kesitleri üzerindeki deneyler kararlı yakınsama ve tutarı iyileşmeler göstermekte olup, görüntü alanında ortalama PSNR/SSIM değerlerinin 26.48 dB/0.857'ye ve sinogram alanında 29.95 dB/0.977’ye ulaştığımı göstermektedir.

title: Optimizing Firing-Rate Map Spatial Resolution via Position-Decoding Accuracy
abstract: Firing rate maps are used to quantify the dependence of action potential firing rates of hippocampal place cells on location. These maps, which display the firing rates exhibited by cells at different spatial positions, were constructed using two-dimensional histograms in the earliest studies, and this method is still widely used today. In this method, how to set the size of the histogram bins has remained an open problem since the early days. On the other hand, it is known that position can be decoded from neural activity based on the relationship between the population firing rates of place cells and these maps. Moreover, there are studies suggesting that, during free foraging behavior, neural activity encodes the subject’s position δ = 100–200 ms into the future. In the present study, during the same behavior, the histogram bin size and the δ interval that minimize the position decoding error were determined simultaneously on a real dataset. The results show that the optimal bin size is larger than values commonly used in the literature and that the optimal δ lies in the range 66–100 ms.
keywords: ["place cells", "hippocampus", "spatial resolution", "position decoding", "decoding errors", "population firing rate"]

title: Multi-Label Disease Detection in Chest X-Ray Images Using CheXFound: Loss Function Analysis
abstract: Multi-label disease detection in chest radiographs is a challenging task due to class imbalance and cross-institutional distribution shift. Although self-supervised foundation models pretrained on large-scale data provide a strong starting point, the impact of different loss functions and classifier heads during fine-tuning has not been sufficiently explored. In this study, the CheXFound foundation model is fine-tuned with LoRA in six configurations (Linear and GLoRI heads; Masked BCE, Weighted BCE, ArcFace, and ASL+LION loss functions) and evaluated on both internal validation and the previously unseen Stanford CheXpert dataset. The results show that loss function selection has important impact on internal validation, whereas classifier head type and loss function play a decisive role in true out-of-distribution evaluation.
keywords: ["chest radiography", "foundation models", "loss functions", "low-rank adaptation", "class imbalance", "out-of-distribution evaluation", "ArcFace"]

title: LLM Inference Performance Optimization in Limited-Resource Environments
abstract: With the widespread adoption of LLM-based chatbots, cloud-dependent solutions have come to dominate the market. However, open-source pre-trained LLMs are enabling implementation of local solutions. Achieving competitive performance locally requires the ability to run high-parameter models. Here, the primary bottleneck is GPU VRAM capacity, which limits model parameter size. Furthermore, the efficiency of inference optimizations such as kv caching depends directly on the amount of available VRAM remaining after the model is loaded. In such a scenario with hardware constraints, we conduct user tests by applying kv cache quantization. As a result, we identify distinct performance trends in critical metrics such as Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) and Total Generation Time. Additionally, we evaluate model accuracy results using the LLM-as-a-judge paradigm.
keywords: ["large language model inference", "KV cache quantization", "inference optimization", "time-to-first-token", "generation time", "LLM-as-a-judge", "local LLM deployment"]

title: Predicting Polarization Converter Transmittance Performance Using Machine Learning
abstract: Metamaterials are used in many fields, including polarization converter design. In this study, five different machine learning algorithms were used to predict the transmittance performance of polarization converters. The disadvantages created by numerical-based methods have necessitated the use of alternative methods in metamaterial design. In this regard, machine learning methods have provided an opportunity for design. In the current study, predicting polarization converter transmittance performance of Linear Regression (LR), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), and Bagging Regression models are presented. The XGBoost Regression model showed the best performance for both Tyy and Tyx.
keywords: ["polarization converter", "metamaterials", "XGBoost regression", "random forest", "decision tree", "linear regression", "bagging regression"]

title: Self-Supervised Poisson Denoising in Biomedical Imaging: Edge-AI Verification of Deep Unrolling Architectures
abstract: Biomedical imaging systems typically operate under low signal conditions. As a consequence, the acquired measurements are often affected by Poisson noise, which arises from the stochastic nature of photon counting and varies with the underlying signal intensity. Although supervised deep learning approaches have achieved strong performance in image denoising tasks, obtaining clean reference images (ground truth) is rarely feasible in real clinical settings. In this work, we consider the Poisson2Sparse framework, which combines sparse representation theory with a deep algorithm unrolling architecture and enables self-supervised learning directly from noisy observations. While most existing implementations rely on CUDA-based GPU environments, the present study re-implements and evaluates the framework on Apple M4 hardware using the Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) backend. Experiments conducted on the PINCAT dataset show that the proposed implementation attains a PSNR of 31.88dB at a photon intensity level of 20, corresponding to a medium-noise regime and closely aligning with previously reported baseline results. These findings suggest that advanced self-supervised restoration models can be executed reliably on consumer-grade hardware equipped with a unified memory architecture (UMA), making such approaches more accessible for both research and potential clinical deployment.
keywords: ["shot noise", "image denoising", "self-supervised learning", "deep unrolling", "sparse representation", "edge AI", "unified memory architecture", "biomedical imaging"]

title: A Wearable IMU-Based Human-Robot Interaction Framework Configured with Large Language Models
abstract: In this study, a scalable and hardware-independent modular framework is proposed for IMU-based human-robot interaction. The architecture consists of a hardware abstraction layer for sensor integration, a calibration layer for sensor-segment alignment, a kinematic reconstruction layer for estimating human limb poses, and an interaction layer where human motions are interpreted as meaningful actions from the robot's perspective. This layered structure facilitates the integration of different wearable sensor systems while providing a consistent interface for higher-level interaction modules. In addition, the system aims to reduce setup complexity and improve adaptability by enabling high-level information - such as sensor placements and task descriptions - to be interpreted by large language models (LLM), allowing sensor mappings, kinematic model configurations, and calibration procedures to be generated automatically.
keywords: ["human-robot interaction", "wearable inertial sensors", "large language models", "sensor calibration", "kinematic reconstruction", "hardware abstraction layer"]

title: A Hybrid Approach Based on Multiple Feature Selection and Ensemble Learning in the Classification of Gallstone Disease
abstract: Gallstone disease, despite its prevalence, is a significant health problem that can lead to serious complications if not diagnosed early and accurately. This study proposes a two-level hybrid machine learning approach for disease classification using non-invasive clinical and metabolic data. In the first stage, features selected using Boruta, LightGBM, TabNet, Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), and ReliefF methods are combined with a feature set based on majority voting. In the second stage, a model set consisting of random forest, gradient boosting, and support vector machines algorithms is integrated using a soft voting method. The performance of the models is evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, precision, F1 score, Matthews Correlation Coefficient, and ROC-AUC metrics. The findings show that feature selection improves performance, and the proposed hybrid model yielded results with 85.42% accuracy and 0.92 AUC.

title: Turkish Tweet Classification and Critical Information Extraction for Disaster Coordination
abstract: Although social media plays a critical role in disaster management, it is difficult to use resources effectively due to the high volume of posts and the potential spread of unverified information. In this study, we present a module of a developing system designed to analyze Turkish tweets to support search-rescue operations following a disaster. The proposed approach first classifies posts collected in real-time as disaster-related or not and then further categorizes disaster-related posts into intent classes such as help requests and situation updates based on their content. In addition, critical named entities appearing in the posts (such as persons and addresses) are identified to enable the alignment between people in need and potential helpers. The study is conducted on a dataset consisting of 29,346 disaster-related posts, where all labeling and classification tasks are performed by using language models.

title: A Comparative Analysis of MLP and Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) for Faster-than-Nyquist (FTN) Signaling Detection
abstract: Faster-than-Nyquist signaling improves spectral efficiency by deliberately introducing inter-symbol interference. Classical sequence detectors such as BCJR can approach optimal performance, but their computational cost grows rapidly with channel memory. This paper investigates data-driven FTN BPSK detection under AWGN through a direct comparison between multilayer perceptrons and Kolmogorov Arnold Networks. A large-scale Monte Carlo dataset containing nearly four million labeled windows is generated for a time-packing factor of zero point eight and signal-to-noise ratio values from seven to ten decibels. The best MLP obtained from width sweeping uses hidden width thirty two, whereas the selected KAN uses hidden width four with spline grid size five. At ten decibels, the MLP produces a bit error rate of one point three times ten to the minus four, while the KAN reaches seven times ten to the minus six. This corresponds to an eighteen point six times lower bit error rate while using only one eighth of the MLP hidden width. The results show that KAN provides a more effective and more parameter-efficient neural decision model than the MLP baseline for FTN BPSK detection.
keywords: ["faster-than-Nyquist signaling", "multilayer perceptron", "Kolmogorov-Arnold networks", "intersymbol interference", "bit error rate", "AWGN channel"]

title: Anatomy-Aware Routing for Robust Medical Image Segmentation: A Failure-Detectable Alternative to Mixed Models
abstract: Heterogeneous medical segmentation pipelines that use a single shared model lose organ-specific feature learning and degrade silently under distribution shift. We propose an anatomy-aware framework where an upstream classifier routes inputs to dedicated specialist networks, combined with a composite post-hoc failure detector based on MC-Dropout uncertainty, domain-shift detection, and plausibility checking. Using chest X-ray pneumothorax and brain MRI datasets, we show anatomy-aware routing yields higher segmentation accuracy (+8.6-14.4 Dice points) compared to a mixed-organ baseline. Our failure detector achieves flag rates of 1.000 on misrouted pneumothorax cases and 0.963 on brain cases. In contrast, under identical noise, the mixed model produces flag rates of only 0.173 and 0.156. Anatomy-aware pipelines offer superior accuracy and the ability to fail loudly, allowing safer clinical deployment through explicit abstention.
keywords: ["medical image segmentation", "fault detection", "distribution shift", "plausibility checking", "brain MRI segmentation", "model robustness"]

title: Yapay Arı Kolonisi Tabanlı Portföy Optimizasyonu ve Derin Pekiştirmeli Öğrenme ile Hibrit Risk Yönetimi
abstract: Bu çalışmada, stratejik portföy seçimi ile günlük risk yönetimini birleştiren hibrit bir yapı önerilmektedir. Aylık portföy oluşturma süreci, Yapay Arı Kolonisi (ABC) algoritmasının minimum varyans, negatif Sharpe ve negatif Sortino oranına dayalı üç varyantı ile yürütülmektedir. Günlük risk müdahaleleri ise Avantaj Aktör-Eleştirmen (A2C – Advantage Actor-Critic) tabanlı bir ajan tarafindan gerçekleştirilmektedir. Deneyler, NASDAQ-100 üzerinde 2025 değerlendirme dönemi için yürütülmüş ve hibrit yapı statik portföylerle karşılaştırılmıştır. Bulgular, özellikle Sortino tabanlı stratejinin hibrit yapı ile daha yüksek getiri ve daha düşük maksimum düşüş ürettiğini göstermektedir. Sonuç olarak, aşağı yönlü riski dikkate alan stratejik portföy seçiminin dinamik risk yönetimi ile daha uyumlu çalıştığı görülmüştür.

title: Multiplier-Free PoT Block-BiLSTM Channel Equalizer in Tactical Communications
abstract: In this paper, a multiplier-free Block Bidirectional LSTM (Block-BiLSTM) equalizer is proposed to mitigate the combined effects of Power Amplifier (PA) nonlinearity and multipath fading in tactical radio systems. All weights are constrained to a 4-bit Power-of-Two (PoT) set, converting floating-point multiplications into bit-shift and addition operations, thereby completely eliminating DSP block usage on FPGA or ASIC platforms. Trained under Quantization-Aware Training using the Straight-Through Estimator, the proposed PoT Block-BiLSTM exhibits equivalent performance to the floating-point baseline across all SNR points under a PA soft-clipping channel with a 1.2 threshold, 32 hidden units, four-tap multipath, and BPSK modulation. Furthermore, it completely eliminates all 220 DSP48E1 blocks on the xc7z020 capacity, reducing dynamic power consumption from 1.041 W to 0.195 W (a 5.3x reduction) and total power consumption from 1.162 W to 0.300 W, ensuring high energy efficiency for constrained devices.

title: Efficient Optic Disc and Cup Segmentation for Glaucoma Assessment
abstract: The analysis of fundus images plays a critical role in the early diagnosis of glaucoma. Accurate segmentation of anatomical structures within these images forms the foundation of computer-aided diagnosis systems. In this study, the segmentation performance of seven state-of-the-art deep learning architectures (DeepLabv3+, FPN, MA-Net, PAN, PSPNet, SegFormer, and U-Net++) on fundus images for glaucoma diagnosis is comprehensively evaluated. Utilizing the publicly available Glaucoma Fundus Imaging dataset, the models were assessed using accuracy metrics such as Precision, Recall, Dice coefficient, and Intersection over Union (IoU), alongside computational efficiency measures including training time and parameter count. Experimental results demonstrate that all architectures achieve outstanding performance in the anatomically distinct OD region (Dice > 0.96), while producing clinically competitive results in the more challenging OC region. In terms of accuracy, FPN, PAN, and U-Net++ stood out in the OD region, whereas SegFormer and U-Net++ achieved the highest metrics in the OC region. However, these highly accurate models incurred significant computational costs. When evaluating all metrics and regions comprehensively, the PAN architecture provided an optimal balance between accuracy and hardware requirements by delivering high segmentation accuracy in both regions with significantly reduced training time. This study emphasizes that model selection in medical imaging applications should consider computational costs and clinical applicability alongside pure accuracy metrics.
keywords: ["optic disc segmentation", "optic cup segmentation", "glaucoma diagnosis", "fundus images", "semantic segmentation", "deep learning architectures", "computational efficiency", "model selection", "U-Net", "SegFormer"]

title: In-Context Example Selection for Few-Shot Text Classification in 5G Security Text Using LLM
abstract: This study examines a few-shot text classification approach for the classification of technical texts produced in the telecommunications domain. In this context, the examples included in the prompt are selected using different methods, and the impact of these methods on classification performance is analyzed. In this study, the text classification performance of the Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 model was evaluated using the 5GSC dataset, which consists of security-related texts specific to the 5G domain. To examine the effect of the examples included in the prompt on the classification performance of the model, zero-shot, random example selection, and semantic similarity-based example selection approaches were comparatively analyzed. The evaluation based on performance metrics demonstrates that including examples with semantic similarity to the query text improves classification performance.
keywords: ["few-shot text classification", "example selection", "in-context learning", "5G security", "semantic similarity", "Mistral-7B-Instruct", "prompt engineering", "zero-shot learning"]

title: The Inference Compiler: An Automated Pipeline for High-Sparsity Neural Network Deployment
abstract: Deep neural network deployment on edge devices is limited by computational overhead. We present "The Inference Compiler," an automated pipeline transitioning models from Python frameworks into highly optimized C++ executables. It synthesizes Knowledge Distillation, Taylor Expansion Pruning, and Synchronized Post-Training Quantization. For complex architectures, we introduce a Dependency Tracer to maintain residual network symmetry and a parallelized Sensitivity-Aware Recovery (SAR) mechanism to mitigate pruning shockwaves. Evaluated primarily on MLP and ResNet-110 architectures within a strict 2.0% accuracy degradation limit for pruning (with an additional 0.5% tolerance for quantization), the compiler achieved up to 88.08% global sparsity. Physical benchmarks on an AMD Ryzen 5 CPU demonstrate that our SIMD-unrolled C++ generation yields up to an 89.1x end-to-end speedup over Python environments, significantly reducing inference latency on standard mobile hardware.
keywords: ["neural network deployment", "knowledge distillation", "post-training quantization", "C code generation", "edge devices", "inference latency", "MLP"]

title: A Lightweight Method for Multiple Signal Direction Estimation with Adaptive Notch Filters
abstract: For multi-signal detection and direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation, conventional Capon beamforming degrades when there are more transmitters than receive antennas minus one. This paper proposes a lightweight method using adaptive notch filters (ANFs) with only two receive antennas for simultaneous DoA of two or more narrowband signals. Cascaded ANF stages form isolated channels per signal, and Capon estimates direction on each. The method has very low computational cost, and in simulation, for transmitters separable in time, frequency, and angle, performance approaches that of an oracle with prior signal knowledge. As with ANFs themselves, multiple components at closely spaced frequencies are poorly resolved, forming the main limitation of the proposed method. Simulations are complemented by an experimental implementation on a low-cost software-defined radio (ADALM-Pluto).
keywords: ["direction of arrival estimation", "adaptive notch filter", "Capon beamforming", "low computational cost", "software-defined radio"]

title: Kalman Filter-Assisted Localization Using MUSIC-Based Angle of Arrival Measurements in Ray-Tracing Urban Scenarios
abstract: This study investigates Kalman-based temporal refinement of MUSIC-based angle-of-arrival (AoA) measurements in a challenging two-receiver urban scenario generated with Sionna RT. Raw triangulation, azimuth-domain Kalman filtering, position-domain adaptive Kalman filtering, and a two-stage structure are compared. Results show that the position-domain adaptive Kalman filter improves the 95th-percentile (p95) error by 69%, while the lowest mean error is obtained with the twostage structure. The findings indicate a trade-off between outlier suppression and median error.
keywords: ["Kalman filter", "MUSIC algorithm", "angle of arrival", "localization", "urban propagation", "ray tracing", "adaptive Kalman filter", "triangulation", "outlier suppression"]

title: Two-Legged Robot Design and System Identification with Deep Learning
abstract: Today, different artificial neural network applications are being used in various robot systems. Especially in the field of legged robots, important advancements are made in recent years. In this study, data obtained from a two-legged robot system developed in our laboratory are processed by artificial neural networks to be used in robot system identification. Results obtained are presented comparatively for this study, in which different activation functions are used and DELU activation function utilization acquired the lowest test set error rate.
keywords: ["two-legged robot", "legged robots", "artificial neural networks", "activation functions"]

title: Classification of Marine Vessels in the NASTaR Dataset
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data plays a critical role in maritime surveillance applications, enabling vessel monitoring, maritime safety, and prevention of illegal activities regardless of weather conditions or daylight. The diversity of SAR data across different frequency bands (X, C, S, etc.) also has significant implications for their analysis. In this study, the NASTaR dataset, derived from NovaSAR S-band SAR imagery, is used to classify maritime vessels including cargo, passenger, tanker, fishing, and sailing vessels using the SwinV2-B model. Results across six classification scenarios are compared with the baseline study in the literature.
keywords: ["vessel classification", "synthetic aperture radar", "maritime surveillance", "cargo ships", "passenger ships", "tankers", "fishing boats", "sailing ships"]

title: Benign-Malignant Discrimination of Dermoscopic Lesions Using Dermatologist-Informed Quantitative Features
abstract: Early and reliable pre-assessment of skin cancer is critical for patient prioritization and clinical decision support. However, most existing automated classification studies rely primarily on public datasets and remain limited in terms of clinical interpretability. In this study, an explainable classification pipeline leveraging dermatological knowledge is proposed for benign–malignant discrimination of dermoscopic lesions. The dataset was constructed by combining ISIC 2016–2018 data with private clinical images, resulting in a balanced set of 1,400 samples. Following SAM-based lesion extraction, the extracted features were evaluated using machine learning methods, and the best performance was achieved by the Random Forest classifier in the scenario combining texture, histogram, and shape features, yielding an accuracy of 0.919, an F1-score of 0.917, and an AUC of 0.923. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach provides clinically interpretable and effective decision support.
keywords: ["skin cancer", "explainable classification", "lesion segmentation", "Segment Anything Model", "texture features", "histogram features", "shape features", "clinical decision support", "ISIC dataset"]

title: Performance Analysis of Different Channel Coding Techniques Under Turbidity Effects in Underwater Optical Channels
abstract: Underwater Visible Light Communication (UVLC), although it has the potential to overcome the data rate limitations of acoustic and RF systems, suffers from absorption and scattering losses due to water turbidity. In this study, channel effects are modeled using the Beer–Lambert law, and Clear Ocean, Coastal Ocean, and Harbor Water scenarios are investigated. Under OOK modulation, the BER performance of Hamming, BCH, RS, convolutional, and LDPC codes is compared. The results show that coding techniques exhibit distinct behaviors depending on channel severity. In harbor water, due to LLR degradation, LDPC reaches a BER of 10-4only at ~34 dB, while convolutional coding achieves error-free transmission at ~30 dB. In contrast, in clear and coastal waters, LDPC demonstrates superior performance with a pronounced waterfall effect at 8.5 dB and 10.7 dB. These findings highlight the critical importance of channel-adaptive coding selection in UVLC systems.

title: Cell Type Identification in Spatial Transcriptomics Data Using Hybrid Neighborhood Graphs and Contrastive Learning
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics technologies facilitate the understanding of biological tissue organization by providing gene expression profiles alongside their spatial coordinates. However, defining cellular relationships based solely on physical distance hinders the identification of cells that are biologically similar yet spatially distal. In this study, we present a self-supervised graph neural network model that integrates gene expression, spatial coordinates, and histological images. In the proposed method, tissue topology is modeled using a multimodal hybrid adjacency matrix that incorporates physical distances, gene expression similarity, and image-based morphological similarities. During the learning phase, the model utilizes a contrastive learning strategy to extract consistent features across these different views. This architecture enables the model to identify biologically and morphologically coherent cell clusters within complex tissue regions.
keywords: ["cell type annotation", "spatial transcriptomics", "contrastive learning", "graph neural networks", "self-supervised learning", "histological images", "cell clustering", "morphological similarity"]

title: Analysis of Meta-Reinforcement Learning on Transfer Learning for HVAC Control
abstract: Deploying reinforcement learning (RL) agents for heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) control across climatically diverse buildings is challenging, as policies trained in one climate often fail to generalize to others. We investigate transfer and meta-reinforcement learning for building climate control using Sinergym with a custom EnergyPlus model of a real room, comparing Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) and Model-Agnostic Meta Learning DDQN (MAML-DDQN) across three transfer scenarios on a target very hot climate. Fine-tuned DDQN reduces temperature violations by a factor of 35 over the from-scratch baseline and improves reward by 86% over zero-shot transfer, while MAML-DDQN converges in less than half the fine-tuning episodes and exhibits substantially lower variance across seeds. Results highlight a key trade-off: MAML-DDQN is preferable at adaptation-focused deployments, while fine-tuned DDQN is superior when maximum performance is the objective.
keywords: ["meta-reinforcement learning", "transfer learning", "HVAC control", "building climate control", "double deep Q-network", "fine-tuning", "zero-shot transfer", "EnergyPlus"]

title: Semantic Retrieval in Composite Data Structures: Fine-Tuning with LLM-Assisted Synthetic Data
abstract: This study addresses information retrieval challenges in composite data structures such as Network Equipment Identifier (NE ID) in the X-Y-Z format. The modality gap between natural language queries and technical codes, combined with high character-level similarity among records (hard negatives), causes fundamental problems in search system. To overcome these issues, various models are fine-tuned using LLM-generated synthetic queries and hard negative mining, yielding notable improvements in semantic matching over their baseline counterparts.
keywords: ["semantic search", "hard negative mining", "modality gap", "fine-tuning", "semantic matching"]

title: Content-Based Classification of Technical Support Requests via Machine Learning Methods
abstract: Support and request management systems play a critical role in handling customer and staff demands within organizational IT infrastructures. However, mislabeling of requests can lead to delays in routing to the appropriate IT units and cause unnecessary resource consumption. In this study, a natural language processing and machine learning-based classification approach is introduced for automatically routing technical support requests to the correct units based on the content of the requests. To reduce data imbalance of classes and improve model generalizability, data augmentation techniques were employed. Requests were classified using K-Nearest Neighbors, Logistic Regression, Naive Bayes, Random Forest and Support Vector Machine algorithms. Random Forest demonstrated the best performance with an accuracy of 92,92% and a Cohen’s Kappa score of 0,9050.
keywords: ["request classification", "IT service management", "request routing", "content-based classification", "class imbalance", "data augmentation", "random forest", "natural language processing"]

title: The Impact of Trajectory Segmentation on Learning Performance in the C-CNMP Architecture
abstract: Learning from Demonstration enables robots to learn complex motor skills from expert demonstrations without relying on costly trial-and-error procedures. Coupled Conditional Neural Movement Primitives (C-CNMP), a CNMP-based approach, provides a resource-efficient trajectory representation by segmenting trajectories using a divide-and-conquer strategy while preserving inter-segment dependencies. However, the effect of trajectory segmentation on learning performance, particularly for real-world robot trajectories, has not been systematically studied. In this paper, we investigate the impact of segmentation point selection and the number of segments on the learning performance of C-CNMP using a 7-DoF arm movement of Torobo robot. Experimental results show that appropriate segmentation reduces prediction errors and improves overall trajectory learning performance.
keywords: ["trajectory segmentation", "imitation learning", "segment number", "trajectory prediction", "7-DOF robot arm"]

title: Driver Fatigue Estimation Using Multimodal Deep Learning with EEG and EOG Signals
abstract: Driver fatigue is a critical condition that increases accident risk by causing loss of concentration and perceptual limitations. Therefore, researchers have focused on developing systems aimed at the early detection of driver fatigue. In this study, driver fatigue detection was targeted using Differential Entropy–Linear Dynamic System (DE-LDS) based Electroencephalography (EEG) features and Electrooculography (EOG) features provided by the SEED-VIG dataset. The feature pool employed in the study was enriched through feature engineering methods such as band ratios, temporal delta components, hemispheric asymmetry, and moving standard deviation. Moreover, by eliminating the need for raw signal processing, the focus was directed toward the temporal variation patterns of meaningful features. Experimental results demonstrated that predictions based solely on EEG data remained limited, whereas the inclusion of EOG data significantly improved performance.These findings reveal that EEG and EOG signals provide complementary information in the prediction of driver fatigue. The proposed multimodal approach exhibited greater robustness against inter-subject variability compared to unimodal systems and offered a more generalizable monitoring framework.
keywords: ["driver fatigue detection", "EEG", "electrooculography", "multimodal fusion", "differential entropy", "SEED-VIG dataset", "feature engineering", "hemispheric lateralization", "interindividual variability", "driver drowsiness monitoring"]

title: Lightweight Ensemble Deep Learning–Based Device Identification for LoRa RF Fingerprinting in IoT Networks
abstract: Device authentication in LoRa-based IoT networks has become an important research topic, particularly from the perspective of physical-layer security. In this study, a lightweight and effective RF fingerprinting approach is proposed to identify LoRa devices by exploiting hardware-specific signal characteristics. The proposed method relies on a soft voting-based ensemble classification strategy to combine complementary features learned by different architectures. Specifically, ChirpNet-Lite, which models the time-frequency structure of LoRa signals, and Extreme-Lite, which provides a low parameter count and fast inference, are jointly employed. The class probabilities produced by these two models are combined through a soft voting mechanism to obtain a more robust classification. The proposed method is evaluated on the official test split of the LoRa_RFFI dataset. Experimental results show that the method achieves an accuracy of 98.90%, demonstrating competitive performance compared to many existing approaches in literature. Furthermore, the model contains only approximately 57 K parameters and 15.37M FLOPs, highlighting its computational efficiency. This makes the proposed approach particularly suitable for deployment on resource-constrained IoT gateways and edge systems.
keywords: ["LoRa", "radio frequency fingerprinting", "device identification", "device authentication", "physical layer security", "ensemble classification", "soft voting", "lightweight deep learning", "time-frequency analysis", "IoT gateway", "edge deployment"]

title: Performance Evaluation of Different FDA-MIMO Radar Systems in terms of Multi-Target Separation Capability
abstract: This study investigates the performance of frequency diverse array multiple-input multiple-output (FDA-MIMO) radar systems in terms of their multiple target separation capabilities, following fast-time, slow-time, and spatial processing steps. The comparisons and simulation results are presented and compared with the classical phased-array radar systems.
keywords: ["frequency diverse array", "MIMO radar", "spatial processing", "radar performance evaluation"]

title: Facial Alignment and Grid-Based ROI Selection for rPPG-Based Contactless Heart Rate Estimation
abstract: In recent years, cardiovascular diseases have been steadily increasing, making regular and convenient monitoring of heart rate more important. In this study, a lightweight and practical processing pipeline based on remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) was developed to estimate heart rate in a contactless manner. The method was inspired by the Face2PPG approach, and its modular structure was further improved and reorganised. The main stages of the modular structure include face detection using MediaPipe FaceMesh, affine-based alignment, skin masking, and grid-based region of interest (ROI) selection achieved by dividing the facial area into small blocks. The red-green-blue (RGB) time series obtained from the selected ROI regions were used to extract the blood volume pulse (BVP) signal through different methods. The signals were passed through a band-pass filter, and heart rate (HR) was estimated using fast Fourier transform (FFT) based spectral analysis. The proposed modular structure provides a reliable and easily applicable contactless PPG measurement.
keywords: ["remote photoplethysmography", "facial landmark detection", "bandpass filtering", "spectral analysis", "face detection"]

title: Using Hybrid Training Sets in Large Language Models for Detecting Sensitive Data Leakage
abstract: Accidental exposure of secrets such as API keys, access tokens and cryptographic keys in source code repositories poses significant security risks. Traditional regex-based secret detection tools can capture specific patterns but often produce high false positive rates. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have been applied to code security tasks due to their contextual understanding capabilities. However, model performance strongly depends on the characteristics of the training dataset. In this study, a hybrid dataset constructed from SecretBench and CredData is used to analyze cross-dataset generalization in LLM-based secret detection. Experiments conducted on the LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen-2.5-Coder-7B models show that training LLMs with a hybrid dataset significantly improves both the False Positive-False Negative balance and performance across cross-datasets.
keywords: ["secret detection", "sensitive data leakage", "large language models", "cross-dataset generalization", "software repositories", "false positive reduction", "Llama 3.1", "code security"]

title: Harvesting the Unseen: Reject Inference and Temporal Data Integration in Agricultural Risk Scoring
abstract: This study advances the financing of agricultural Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises by addressing critical limitations of traditional machine learning-based credit scoring methods. The main flaw in conventional risk models stems from selection bias caused by training only on approved applications. To mitigate this effect, a deterministic reject inference methodology was applied by integrating historical data from the Credit Bureau and tracking the post-rejection financial behavior of rejected applicants within a specified time-window tolerance. A novel ensemble model architecture combining TabPFN and CatBoost algorithms was proposed. In addition, thin-file applicants with no banking history were segmented and modeled independently. In offline back-testing experiments, the developed model achieved an average ROC-AUC score of 0.904 on test folds consisting solely of real operational labels.
keywords: ["small and medium-sized enterprises", "reject inference", "selection bias", "rejected applicants", "credit bureau data", "TabPFN", "CatBoost", "ensemble learning", "agricultural finance"]

title: Denoising, Multi-Label Classification, and CCA-Based Parameter Extraction for Overlapping Radar Signals
abstract: In dense spectral environments, multiple radar emitters may operate within the same band and produce overlapping signatures in the time-frequency plane. This degrades waveform recognition and parameter estimation performance. This paper presents a modular and end-to-end framework for the spectrogram-based analysis of overlapping radar signals. In the first stage, denoising is performed using a U-Net-like encoder-decoder model based on ResNet-18. Next, a multi-label classifier detects the radar waveforms present in the scene. In the subsequent stage, component-wise separation is carried out through edge extraction and connected component analysis (CCA), enabling the estimation of parameters such as time of arrival, pulse width, PRI, and bandwidth. Experimental results show that the proposed approach provides consistent improvements in denoising, classification, and parameter estimation under different SNR conditions.
keywords: ["multi-label classification", "connected component analysis", "parameter estimation", "time of arrival estimation", "pulse repetition interval", "pulse width estimation", "bandwidth estimation", "U-Net encoder-decoder", "edge detection"]

title: FairCore: Weighted K-Core Based Graph Decomposition for Fair Federated Recommendation Systems
abstract: Federated recommender systems aim to preserve data privacy by performing model training without directly transmitting user data to a central server. However, graph-based federated recommender systems are sensitive to the neighbor selection mechanism and are therefore prone to structural biases inherent in the graph, which may lead to unfair recommendations across different user groups. In this study, to address this problem, a weighted k-core–based graph decomposition approach is proposed. The proposed method aims to improve recommendations for all user groups by enabling a fairer training process. In addition, fairness evaluation is comprehensively conducted by considering different user attributes as well as their intersections. Experiments on the MovieLens dataset show that the proposed model reduces RMSE to 1.107 and lowers disparity to 0.040 (gender) and 0.030 (activity), improving both accuracy and fairness.
keywords: ["federated recommender systems", "graph-based recommendation", "graph decomposition", "fairness", "structural bias", "neighbor selection", "fairness evaluation", "data privacy"]

title: Detection of Blood Cells in Microscopic Images Using YOLOv5
abstract: Microscopic analysis of blood cells is an important component of hematological assessment. The evaluation process increasingly relies on image-based systems. In this study, we evaluate blood cell images and how deep learning can be applied to support analysis processes. Within the proposed framework, the model was evaluated on the blood cell count and detection dataset and an mAP@0.5 value of 0.942 was observed. These results show that the proposed model provides an effective approach for the detection of blood cells.
keywords: ["blood cell detection", "microscopic images", "YOLOv5", "object detection", "hematological analysis", "blood cell count", "deep learning"]

title: PPO-Based JPEG Quantization Table Optimization
abstract: Recent advances in deep learning-based image compression, particularly variational autoencoder (VAE) frameworks, have demonstrated strong rate-distortion performance. However, these models are often computationally expensive and difficult to deploy in resource-constrained or legacy systems. In contrast, classical codecs such as JPEG remain widely used due to their simplicity, standardization, and cross-platform compatibility. This motivates the need for modern optimization techniques that can enhance codec performance without altering their fundamental structure. Reinforcement Learning (RL), particularly Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), offers a promising alternative by enabling optimization in black-box environments without requiring differentiability. In this work, we propose a PPO-based stepwise optimization framework for adapting JPEG quantization tables with respect to rate-distortion performance. Experimental results demonstrate consistent gains over standard JPEG baselines, highlighting the potential of reinforcement learning for enhancing classical compression systems.
keywords: ["proximal policy optimization", "rate-distortion performance", "black-box optimization"]

title: Adaptive IIR Filter Identification Using Artificial Protozoa Optimizer
abstract: Adaptive infinite impulse response (IIR) filter identification remains a challenging problem due to the nonlinear and multimodal nature of the error surface. In this study, the artificial protozoa optimizer (APO) is employed to estimate the coefficients of adaptive IIR filters by minimizing the mean squared error between the plant and model outputs. The proposed method is evaluated under both same-order and reduced-order modelling conditions. The performance of APO is assessed through convergence analysis and comparisons with several reported optimization algorithms. The results indicate that APO achieves improved identification accuracy with stable convergence behaviour and consistent performance across multiple independent runs. These results demonstrate that APO provides an effective and reliable framework for adaptive IIR filter identification and shows potential for more complex system identification tasks.
keywords: ["artificial protozoa optimizer", "filter coefficient estimation", "mean square error minimization", "model reduction", "convergence analysis", "bio-inspired optimization"]

title: Horizon Profile Based Autonomous Positioning for Low-Altitude Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
abstract: Autonomous positioning is a critical requirement for unmanned aerial vehicles operating in environments where satellite navigation is unavailable. This study develops a positioning method based on matching the horizon profile observed by the vehicle against reference profiles generated from a digital elevation model. Algorithm performance is evaluated on synthetic profiles to isolate matching accuracy from sensor and environmental variables. Experiments at different altitudes show that near-ground observations suffer from nearby obstacles degrading the distinctiveness of distant terrain silhouettes, significantly reducing matching accuracy. Above 200 meters, the large-scale terrain structure dominates and consistent positioning becomes achievable. The proposed derivative contour word encoding captures terrain transitions and curvature, achieving 98.5 percent accuracy at 1 km Haversine distance with a median positioning error of 62 meters over an approximately 30,000 square kilometer area containing 3.5 million candidate locations.
keywords: ["autonomous positioning", "unmanned aerial vehicles", "low-altitude UAV", "digital elevation model", "terrain curvature"]

title: Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) Sensor Design for Railway Monitoring Applications
abstract: Railway infrastructures are critical engineering structures exposed to high dynamic strain and wide temperature variations. This study proposes a Fiber Bragg Grating sensor architecture that integrates material characteristics with spectral design parameters for railway monitoring applications. The proposed approach considers grating length, refractive index modulation and apodization parameters within a unified design framework and evaluates the influence of different fiber materials on sensor performance. A dual grating configuration is also employed to reduce temperature strain cross sensitivity. The results indicate that the proposed design improves spectral resolution, reduces side lobe levels and enhances measurement stability. The presented sensor architecture provides a scalable and practical solution for high strain monitoring and multi sensor integration in railway infrastructures.
keywords: ["fiber Bragg grating sensors", "railway infrastructure monitoring", "strain sensing", "temperature compensation", "apodization", "refractive index modulation", "grating length", "spectral resolution", "sidelobe level", "multi-sensor integration"]

title: Mask R-CNN-Based Fracture Segmentation on FracAtlas: Effects of Backbone Architecture and Mosaic Augmentation on Cross-Dataset Generalization
abstract: Bone fracture diagnosis from radiographic images is a critical task in clinical practice that requires expertise and time. Deep learning has enabled decision support systems for fracture detection, localization, and segmentation. In this study, a Mask R-CNN-based instance segmentation approach is evaluated on FracAtlas through a two-stage evaluation protocol. Track A is designed as a positive-only localization ablation that isolates the effects of feature-extracting backbone architecture selection and mosaic augmentation, whereas Track B is structured as a balanced clinical validation protocol with anatomically matched negative images. The threshold is locked on the validation set and the results are examined on the internal test set and independent external datasets. The findings show that balanced training improves internal clinical discrimination, while anatomy and institution shift remain important limitations in external validation.
keywords: ["Mask R-CNN", "instance segmentation", "mosaic augmentation", "cross-dataset generalization", "radiographic images", "fracture localization", "external validation", "clinical decision support"]

title: Interpolation of Multifeature Time-Vertex Signals via Joint Spectral ARMA Model
abstract: Graph signal processing provides effective techniques for the analysis of data structures residing on irregular topologies. Existing time-vertex signal processing approaches in the literature generally focus on single-attribute signals. However, many applications require working with data types where multiple attributes (e.g., temperature, humidity, wind speed) are measured simultaneously at each node. In this study, a novel Multi-feature Joint Spectral ARMA (MF-JS-ARMA) model based on the Joint Wide Sense Stationarity assumption is proposed for modeling multi-attribute time-vertex signals and estimating missing observations in partially observed data. The proposed method simultaneously learns the auto-spectral and cross-spectral densities of attribute pairs within the framework of a joint optimization problem. The developed model has been applied to the LMMSE-based missing data estimation problem on meteorological data, and it has been shown to improve estimation performance compared to reference methods in the literature.
keywords: ["graph signal processing", "wide-sense stationarity", "missing data estimation", "LMMSE estimation", "cross-spectral density", "meteorological observations", "sensor networks"]

title: Heuristic and LLM-Based RoI Extraction for Turkish News Pages
abstract: This study addresses the extraction of news content regions (Region of Interest, RoI) from Turkish news pages using both rule-based and large language model (LLM)-based methods. A heuristic container element is first selected from the HTML DOM; then either this container or the full page body is fed to the LLM under different input types. A 2 × 3 factorial design crossing two scope levels (container/body) with three input types (HTML / Flow-Filtered / Flow-AllText) is evaluated on 100 news samples using weighted token-multiset F1 and ROUGE-L F1. Results show that HTML-based inputs consistently outperform flow-based alternatives across all models, with body + HTML achieving the highest quality and container+HTML offering the best quality-cost trade-off.
keywords: ["region of interest extraction", "large language models", "rule-based extraction", "cost-quality trade-off"]

title: Performance of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces with Multi-Antenna Systems
abstract: In this paper, the performances of two multi-antenna techniques such as Maximal Ratio Combining (MRC) and Transmit Antenna Selection (TAS)-MRC are examined for the systems using Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RIS) in the presence of phase noise. Ideal and imperfect phase alterization cases have been considered. Comparisons are made considering realistic phase compensation and ideal situation. Results show that Single Input Multiple Output (SIMO) and Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) RIS systems with phase noise perform better than the ideal Single Input Single Output (SISO) RIS systems and the number of meta surfaces affects the performance balance.
keywords: ["reconfigurable intelligent surface", "multiple antennas", "maximum ratio combining", "transmit antenna selection", "phase noise", "phase compensation", "SIMO", "MIMO", "SISO systems", "metasurfaces", "wireless communication performance"]

title: Knee Angle Estimation Invariant to Sensor Placement with Magnetometer-Free Inertial Sensors
abstract: We investigate the estimation of knee joint angle using wearable inertial measurement units (IMUs). Magneto-meters are often affected by disturbances in the surrounding magnetic field, therefore, this study focuses on only accelerometer and gyroscope data. Two IMU sensors were attached, some in arbitrary orientations, to the femur and tibia segments to measure the knee angle during knee flexion–extension movements. The collected data were processed using several estimation methods, and the resulting knee angles were compared with reference measurements obtained from a video-based motion analysis system. Results demonstrate that acceptable accuracy can be achieved even when IMU sensors are not aligned with the body axis and magnetometer data is not used.
keywords: ["knee joint angle estimation", "wearable inertial sensors", "accelerometer and gyroscope fusion", "knee flexion and extension", "magnetic disturbances"]

title: A Correlation-Based Adaptive Multimodal Fusion Approach for Continuous Driver Fatigue Monitoring
abstract: This study presents a correlation-based adaptive multimodal fusion approach for continuous monitoring of driver fatigue using physiological signals.The proposed method integrates multiple biosignal-derived features, including heart rate (HR), heart rate variability metrics (SDNN, RMSSD, LF/HF), galvanic skin response components (SCL, SCR), and oxygen saturation (SpO2). Unlike conventional approaches where physiological signals are analyzed independently, this study combines all modalities into a single unified and compact representation, effectively reducing the dimensionality of the multimodal data space.The relationships between physiological parameters are analyzed using Pearson correlation coefficients, and data-driven adaptive weights are computed accordingly. These weights dynamically determine the contribution of each parameter to the driver fatigue, enabling the construction of a continuous Fatigue Trend Score (FTS) over time. This unified score provides a compact and interpretable representation of fatigue dynamics and can be directly utilized in subsequent classification and decision-making stages while significantly reducing model complexity compared to multi-input approaches.Unlike the strategies in the literature, the proposed approach adapts to the intrinsic relationships within the data, allowing a robust and meaningful modeling of fatigue dynamics. The results demonstrate that adaptive weighting effectively balances heterogeneous physiological signals and enhances trend interpretability. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study represents one of the first implementations of a correlation-based adaptive multimodal fusion framework that produces a single continuous fatigue representation for driver monitoring.
keywords: ["driver fatigue monitoring", "multimodal fusion", "adaptive weighting", "Pearson correlation", "heart rate", "heart rate variability", "skin conductance", "oxygen saturation", "physiological signals", "driver monitoring"]

title: A Two-Stage Case-Based Reasoning Architecture for Factoring Decisions
abstract: To address operational bottlenecks in Turkish factoring companies, we present a two stage Case Based Reasoning framework for automated decision making. The system performs coarse vector retrieval via Qdrant and applies fine grained reranking by decoupling feature weights from the embedding space, enabling real time adjustments without re indexing. Evaluated on 12374 industry records, the framework achieves a 72.4 percent overall agreement with experts. By incorporating a class adjusted threshold for imbalanced data and a confidence based routing mechanism that escalates 23.8 percent of uncertain cases to human review, agreement of automated decisions with historical expert decisions increases to 80.8 percent. Demonstrating competitive performance against ML baselines, this scalable system supports over a thousand distinct workflows and is successfully deployed in production.
keywords: ["case-based reasoning", "factoring", "automated decision-making", "vector retrieval", "re-ranking", "embedding space", "class imbalance", "human-in-the-loop"]

title: Hybrid Machine Learning Approaches for Early Diabetes Diagnosis Using Explainable Artificial Intelligence
abstract: Early detection of diabetes is critical, yet many AI models rely on dominant symptoms like Polyuria, leading to data leakage and reduced clinical reliability. This study proposes a hybrid architecture combining FT-Transformer, GRU, and XGBoost to capture complex patterns in patient data. By utilizing a Reduced Feature Set (14 features) that excludes dominant leakage variables, we ensure the model learns subtle clinical indicators. SHAP analysis confirms that our model prioritizes features like Gender, Age, and Sudden Weight Loss, providing a transparent and explainable decision-making process. Our findings demonstrate that high accuracy can be achieved without sacrificing clinical interpretability.
keywords: ["diabetes diagnosis", "early detection", "hybrid machine learning", "explainable AI", "SHAP", "feature leakage", "FT-Transformer", "GRU", "XGBoost", "clinical indicators"]

title: SDR-Based Wideband Signal Detection with Gaussian Mixture Model
abstract: The rapid growth of wireless communication technologies and the increasing number of wireless devices have made monitoring and analyzing the RF spectrum increasingly important. Energy-based methods commonly used in wideband spectrum sensing may exhibit limited performance in real environments due to noise uncertainty and the difficulty of determining an appropriate detection threshold. In this study, power spectral density (PSD) data obtained from wideband spectrum measurements are statistically modeled using a Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM). A two-component mixture model is employed to separate the noise and signal components in the spectrum data, and the probability of signal presence is estimated for each frequency bin. The performance of the proposed approach is evaluated using both Monte Carlo simulations and software-defined radio (SDR)-based RF measurements. The results show that the GMM-based statistical modeling approach can provide more stable and reliable results in identifying active signal regions in wideband spectrum observations compared to the classical energy detector.
keywords: ["wideband spectrum sensing", "Gaussian mixture model", "signal detection", "software-defined radio", "energy detector comparison", "detection threshold"]

title: QTSCH: A Lightweight Reinforcement Learning Based TSCH Scheduling Approach for TSCH Networks
abstract: This paper proposes QTSCH, a lightweight reinforcement learning based scheduling approach for Time Slotted Channel Hopping networks. The method selects between a shared common cell and a neighbor specific unicast cell for DATA packets using a per-node epsilon-greedy Q-learning mechanism. The proposed design preserves an Orchestra-like distributed slotframe architecture while making only the data transmission decision adaptive. In addition, the learning signal is updated using MAC-layer outcomes including successful transmission, collision, link failure, and wrong address events. Simulation results obtained in TSCH-Sim and compared with MSF and Orchestra show that QTSCH achieves lower latency, fewer queue drops, fewer MAC collisions, lower idle listening, and a lower radio duty cycle. The results demonstrate that QTSCH provides multi-metric improvement with low computational complexity.
keywords: ["TSCH", "reinforcement learning", "Q-learning", "epsilon-greedy", "MAC scheduling", "low duty cycle", "low-power wireless networks", "adaptive data transmission"]

title: A Lightweight Hybrid Encryption Architecture for High-Telemetry Constrained IoT Devices
abstract: Constrained IoT devices producing high-frequency telemetry need authenticated encryption and key rotation but lack resources for full session-negotiation. Using static AES-GCM avoids protocol overhead but risks traffic exposure in the event of key compromise. We propose hybrid secure IoT communication (H-SIC) that offers lightweight key rotation without a session-negotiation stack. Bulk payload encryption employs hardware AES-128-GCM, while session-key derivation and key encapsulation operate in CPU software. A dual-tag binding authenticates keys and payloads separately, while a caching mechanism spreads out the cost of key wrapping over each packet epoch. It also prevents contention on the hardware cryptographic peripheral by limiting key management to software. Evaluation on ESP32 reveals 46 to 86 percent per-packet latency reduction via caching, a tunable security-performance trade-off, and a resource cost of only 15 KB flash and 200 B heap over raw AES-GCM.

title: Zero-Shot Cell Tracking and Instance Segmentation in Phase-Contrast Microscopy via Prompt-Optimized Foundation Models
abstract: Cell behavior analysis is essential for biological research, particularly in studying cancer metastasis and wound healing. This paper addresses the challenge of automating cell tracking and segmentation in label-free phase-contrast microscopy (PCM). While PCM allows non-invasive observation, low contrast and noise make manual analysis time-consuming and error-prone. In response, we propose a hybrid framework for zero-shot tracking using prompt-optimized foundation models. Our pipeline integrates Tucker-decomposition-based denoising with YOLO26s detection, SAM2 segmentation, and DeepSORT temporal association. By applying a 1.2x spatial scaling to detection boxes, the system captures complete morphological boundaries without requiring expert mask annotations. Experimental results on the CAMAD dataset demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms U-Net baselines in identity preservation and tracking accuracy.

title: Analysing V2V & V2I Collision Warning Systems at Intersections Under LOS/NLOS Conditions
abstract: Unsignalized intersections pose high collision risks in Intelligent Transportation Systems. This study compares three trajectory prediction methods (mathematical, map-based mathematical, and map-based LSTM/WaleNet) for V2V and V2I collision warning systems (ICRW/CWI). Evaluated under LOS/NLOS conditions, results show the map-based mathematical model provides the best balance of accuracy and real-time efficiency, making it highly suitable for lightweight edge-based warning systems.

title: XAI-Based Analysis of Transformer and XGBoost Models for Diabetes Diagnosis: Assessing Alignment with ADA Clinical Risk Factors
abstract: In this study, XGBoost and FT-Transformer machine learning models developed from structured data for diabetes risk prediction were comparatively analyzed. Model performance was evaluated using metrics that are critical for clinical decision—making-namely Sensitivity, F2-Score, ROC-AUC, and PR-AUC—rather than relying solely on conventional accuracy-based measures. Performance differences between classifiers were statistically examined using the McNemar test and a 1000-iteration bootstrap procedure. To interpret the factors influencing model predictions, explainability analyses were conducted using the XAI-SHAP technique. The findings indicate that the two structurally distinct model architectures learned similar risk patterns. The resulting feature importance rankings showed strong consistency with the risk factors defined by the American Diabetes Association. The McNemar test results revealed no statistically significant difference between the models.

title: Extended State Observer Based Estimation of 2-DOF Gimbal Systems Under Disturbances
abstract: This study presents the modeling, state estimation, and disturbance estimation of a two-degree-of-freedom (2-DOF) gimbal system under external disturbances. To mitigate the effects of unknown and time-varying disturbances, an Extended State Observer (ESO)-based approach is employed, enabling simultaneous estimation of system states and disturbances. The ESO is designed using pole placement, with observer gains derived from a bandwidth parameter. System performance is evaluated under sinusoidal disturbances at various frequencies, including those near the system's natural frequencies. Simulation results indicate that the ESO achieves accurate state and disturbance estimation and maintains stable performance even under resonance-like conditions.

title: Physics-Aware Lightweight Deep Learning Model for Human Breathing Detection via UWB Radar
abstract: A physics-aware deep learning framework for human detection from raw ultra-wideband (UWB) radar signals is proposed in this paper. The proposed framework is based on a lightweight 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture that can be deployed on edge devices with limited computational resources. To better capture spatial-temporal and physiological patterns related to human respiration, physics-inspired features, including the Hilbert Envelope and Breathing Band Energy, are added as additional input channels to direct the network to concentrate on signal variations relevant to the presence of a human. In addition, model quantization methods are employed to drastically reduce the computational load and memory footprint, making it feasible to deploy on low-power embedded platforms. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves high detection accuracy with fast inference and minimal memory requirements.

title: Fusion of Low- and High-Order Functional Connectivity for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection
abstract: Bu çalışmada, dinlenim durumu fonksiyonel manyetik rezonans görüntüleme (rs-fMRI) verileri kullanılarak Alzheimer hastalığının (AH) sınıflandırılmasında düşük mertebeli fonksiyonel bağlantısallık (LOFC), yüksek mertebeli fonksiyonel bağlantısallık (HOFC) ve bu iki yaklaşımın birleşimini içeren füzyon modunun (LOFC+HOFC) performansı karşılaştırılmıştır. Bağlantısallık matrislerine Fisher-z dönüşümü uygulanmış, farklı yoğunluk eşiği oranları kullanılarak ağ temsilleri oluşturulmuş ve bu ağlardan düğüm gücü öznitelikleri çıkarılmıştır. Elde edilen öznitelikler, Top-K (K=10) özellik seçimi ve Destek Vektör Makinesi (SVM) altında değerlendirilmiş; model performansı Leave-One-Out Cross Validation (LOOCV) yöntemi ile analiz edilmiştir. Sonuçlar, füzyon modelinin tüm eşik seviyelerinde tekli modalite yaklaşımlarına kıyasla tutarlı biçimde daha yüksek performans metrikleri ürettiğini ortaya koymuş; en yüksek sınıflandırma performansı %20 eşik değerinde gözlemlenmiş olup, orta düzey eşiklerin güçlü bağlantıları korurken gürültüyü bastırma açısından elverişli bir denge sunabileceğine işaret etmektedir. Bu bulgular, AH’nin yalnızca lokal beyin bölgelerini değil, aynı zamanda beyin ağlarının bütünsel organizasyonunu etkileyen bir bozukluk olduğunu desteklemektedir.
