title: Machine Learning Analysis of Japanese Candlestick Patterns in Financial Data: An Empirical Application Based on 10 Years of Daily Data
abstract: This study examines whether Japanese candlestick patterns provide predictive power in financial time series, either alone or combined with technical indicators, using daily data from eight liquid assets over a ten-year period. Rule-based pattern detection was integrated with returns, volatility, momentum, moving averages, ATR, RSI, MACD, and volume. Logistic regression and random forest models were evaluated using a chronological train-validation-test split. On 20,147 observations, random forest achieved ROC-AUC=0.544 in validation but dropped to 0.486 in testing, while logistic regression reached 0.518. A simple strategy yielded −16.2% return, whereas buy-and-hold achieved 40.0%. Results indicate that candlestick patterns do not provide stable alpha at daily frequency but remain useful as auxiliary features capturing behavioral patterns.

title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Angle Estimation from Beam-Swept Measurements in FR3 Near-Field Environments Using a Low-Cost Phased Array
abstract: This paper presents an experimental framework for near-field angle estimation in the FR3 using a low-cost ADALM-Phaser-based phased array operating at 10.45 GHz. Measurements are collected at 114 transmitter positions within the Fresnel near-field zone using an adaptive two-stage beam sweeping procedure. On clean measurements, heuristic angle estimators achieve a mean absolute error (MAE) between 6.1 and 6.3 degrees, while machine learning models reduce this to 3.2 degrees, providing a 49.3 percent improvement. In addition, this study shows that power-based distance estimation is unreliable under indoor multipath conditions in the FR3 near-field regime, as the power-distance relationship becomes weak and non-monotonic, with a near-zero correlation. The results highlight the limitations of heuristic methods under indoor multipath conditions and demonstrate the effectiveness of data-driven approaches for angle estimation in the FR3 near-field regime.

title: Data Augmentation and Classification of Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy Data Using Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model
abstract: This study proposes a denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) based method for synthetic generation of functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) data. Yes - No stimulus paradigm data collected from 28 participants were processed through a comprehensive signal processing pipeline and synthetic epoch data were generated using a conditional one-dimensional U-Net architecture. With the proposed pipeline, features showed no statistically significant difference from real data. The findings from the classification demonstrate that DDPM based data augmentation yields statistically significant improvements in the performance of deep learning models.

title: Impact of EKF-Based Sensor Fusion of Different Sensors on Position Estimation for Four-Wheeled UGV
abstract: In this study, the effect of different sensors on position estimation in four-wheeled differential drive unmanned ground vehicles was investigated using Extended Kalman Filter-based sensor fusion. Different sensor combinations were compared in simulation, while the hardware behavior of GPS- and IMU-supported position estimation was evaluated on the Kangal UGV platform. Simulation results show that, in estimation based solely on odometry, the loop closure error reaches approximately 108.5 m. The combined use of IMU and odometry significantly reduces this error (0.91 m), and with the inclusion of GPS, the error decreases below 1 m (0.36 m), achieving accurate position estimation. Although mechanical effects such as synchronization losses arising from differential drive and encoder limitations constrain accuracy, sensor fusion has been shown to improve both position estimation accuracy and system stability.

title: A Digital Twin–Based ACT-R Model of Time Perception Under Dynamic Cognitive Load
abstract: The computational modeling of cognitive processes is an important research area for explaining and predicting human behavior. However, in many cognitive modeling studies, experimental data and model outputs are mainly compared using average performance measures, which limits model validation. This study proposes a digital twin–based framework for validating cognitive models. In this approach, a computational representation of the experimental task structure is created and the cognitive model is executed under identical task conditions. As an application scenario, a dual-task paradigm examining time perception under dynamic cognitive load is used. A digital twin of the experimental environment is constructed to compare the performance of human participants with an agent operating within the ACT-R cognitive architecture. The results show that the digital twin approach enables detailed model validation and phase-based analysis of performance trajectories.

title: Vibration Control of a Flexible Space Structure via Reduced Order Finite Element Modeling
abstract: This study presents a hybrid modeling and control approach based on the integration of ANSYS and MATLAB for the active vibration control of flexible space structures. The structural dynamics were obtained through high-degree-of-freedom models via ANSYS APDL and transformed into a reduced-order state-space model (ROSSM) representing the rigid-flexible interaction for controller design. Performance analyses of the designed Pole Placement (PP) controller revealed that a damping ratio of 0.70 rapidly stabilizes oscillations under shock inputs; however, it was observed that this high damping performance significantly increases the control force requirements on the actuator. Sensitivity analyses conducted in the final stage of the study confirmed that the controller maintains its stability despite 10% variations in material properties, demonstrating a robust performance against parametric uncertainties.

title: Predicting PPGL Risk from Clinical Case Reports Using Automated Text Extraction and Machine Learning
abstract: Pheochromocytoma and paraganglioma (PPGL) are rare neuroendocrine tumors with nonspecific symptoms overlapping with common hypertension, making early diagnosis challenging for first stage clinicians who have likely never encountered the disease. This study proposes a machine learning approach to detect PPGL using data extracted from publicly available clinical case reports via a named entity recognition pipeline utilizing the LangExtract library and OpenAI Large Language Models (LLMs). The features chosen for extraction were decided by a medical expert in the field. To prevent overfitting, feature selection was performed to retain only the features representing 95% of total cumulative importance. Three machine learning models, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, and XGBoost, were optimized using grid search and cross-validation. The performance of the models varied greatly prior to feature selection, but results became much more consistent after selection, and the models demonstrated comparable performance.

title: Connected Dominating Set Construction using Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Virtual backbone construction for energy-efficient routing in wireless multi-hop networks is modeled by the Connected Dominating Set (CDS) problem. In this study, a Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based two-stage method is proposed for CDS construction. The approach consists of a "node scoring" component that predicts the backbone candidacy of nodes with continuous scores, and a "score-aware connectivity completion" component that achieves connectivity by utilizing these scores as costs. Experiments conducted on Random Geometric Graphs demonstrated that the proposed architecture produced feasible solutions across all scenarios, and that performance could be evaluated more descriptively by decoupling it into core set and connector node costs. Graph Isomorphism Network and Graph Transformer-based scorers assigned more accurate scores to key nodes, thereby reducing the connectivity completion cost, and produced smaller CDS sizes compared to the expert heuristic reference method under sparse network conditions.

title: Transformer-Based Turkish Keyword Spotting in Noisy Environments
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of transformer-based approach for Turkish keyword spotting under challenging conditions. A baseline transformer was compared against three improved variants: KWTm1, which incorporates increased warm-up duration, added dropout, and decreased label smoothing; KWTm2, which employs a data-driven approach by integrating delta and delta-delta coefficients along with optimized spectral features, including increased Mel-filter bank resolution and refined frequency boundaries to better capture Turkish phonetic characteristics; and KWTm3, a hybrid model combining both parametric and data-driven enhancements. The study also investigates the efficacy of test-time adaptation techniques to mitigate performance degradation in noisy environments. The experimental findings indicate that the proposed models provide improved accuracy in most noisy conditions and reveal that well-tuned hyperparameters may offer benefits comparable to feature engineering.

title: Network-Hardware Co-design Framework for Inference on An MCU
abstract: With the increase in computational power, developments in the field of artificial intelligence, which significantly affect daily life and the economy, continue to progress by shifting towards the point where data is generated, i.e., the edge, in order to reduce the risks associated with data access. Artificial intelligence methods that aim to process data at the edge where it is generated and transform it into economic value are generally categorized under the concept of Edge AI. Microcontrollers, which operate at many points in industry where data is generated, emerge as the primary platforms where Edge AI inference algorithms can be deployed. However, enabling Edge AI inference algorithms to generate value without introducing additional economic costs on such resource-constrained systems remains a current and important research challenge. In this study, an applicable approach is proposed to integrate artificial intelligence solutions that can add value to systems running on microprocessors and microcontrollers not specifically designed for AI applications, without introducing additional hardware costs. For this purpose, a Network–Hardware Co-Design Framework Software (ADOT) has been developed. ADOT can generate a neural network model architecture that complies with the limited and control-application-oriented resources of the selected TMS320F28379D microcontroller while satisfying predefined confidence threshold targets, and it can automatically produce executable code that runs on the selected microcontroller.

title: DeepChequeNet: A Hybrid Ensemble for Default Risk Scoring in Cheque Factoring
abstract: Defaulted cheque prediction in cheque factoring is commonly addressed using tabular machine learning models. However, such models may fail to capture relational fraud patterns such as accommodation cheques, cross cheque structures, and cyclic interactions. Purely graph based approaches, on the other hand, cannot fully exploit classical credit risk signals such as payment performance, risk limits, and historical financial behavior. In this study, we propose a hybrid ensemble that combines tabular data and temporal graph learning for cheque level risk scoring. A CatBoost based tabular model is used for classical credit risk signals, while a Temporal Graph Networks component models each cheque as a directed time stamped edge between transaction parties to capture relational and topological fraud patterns. The resulting tabular and graph scores are fused with a logistic regression meta learner to produce the final cheque risk score.

title: An Updated Language Model for Finance Sector
abstract: Translation models have started to be widely used with advancing technology. Although commercial models like Google Translate and DeepL perform well in low-resource languages such as Turkish, their use is very limited in sectors with high data privacy and strict regulations, such as banking, due to their cloud-based operations. On the other hand, open-source translation models do not perform well in sectors with unique terminologies, like finance, because Turkish is a low-resource language. In this study, the aim is to increase translation performance in a specialized field using an open-source translation model and specially prepared data sets. As a result of the automated and human evaluations performed, an increase in translation performance was observed using several performance metrics compared to the base model.

title: Mental Health Disorder Detection in a Low-Resource Language: A Case Study on Turkish Social Media Text
abstract: Mental health disorders such as suicidal ideation, bipolar disorder, depression, and anxiety pose public health challenges in Turkey. Approximately 20% of the population is estimated to be affected by some form of mental illness. Social media is used for sharing personal experiences and opinions in Turkey. This presents an opportunity to use textual data for detecting mental health disorders. This study aims to examine the predictive performance of various machine learning classifiers for identifying mental health conditions in Turkish language texts from social media. Given the lack of structured and unstructured datasets focused on Turkish mental health, we have mined and processed textual data from the social media platform Reddit. This led to the creation of the Turkish Mental Health Disorder (TMHD) Corpus. The TMHD dataset and the machine learning experiments conducted aim to improve the understanding of predicting mental health issues in Turkey using Artificial Intelligence.

title: Multimodal Large Language Models for Turkish Radiology Report Generation from 3D CT Images
abstract: Writing radiology reports constitutes a significant clinical burden for radiologists. While artificial intelligence research on automatic report generation from medical images has gained momentum in recent years, the existing literature predominantly focuses on English, leaving low-resource clinical languages such as Turkish largely underexplored. In this study, multimodal large language models are comprehensively compared for automatic Turkish radiology report generation from three-dimensional Computed Tomography (CT) volumes. General-purpose (Gemma 3) and medical domain-specific (MedGemma) models are evaluated under slice-based and volumetric representation strategies, as well as zero-shot and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (QLoRA) scenarios, using ROUGE and BERTurk-based BERTScore metrics. Results demonstrate that fine-tuning plays a decisive role in low-resource languages and that slice-based representations outperform volumetric approaches in the current setup.

title: A Probabilistic Model for Noisy Decision Making in Rodent Brains
abstract: Decision-making provides a foundational framework for studying cognition, yet it is an inherently noisy process. Behavioral variability arises from multiple sources, including sensory noise, decision biases, and motor errors, which are often conflated in existing computational models. We introduce a probabilistic framework that explicitly separates these components in a two-alternative forced-choice interval discrimination task. Subjective time is modeled as a Gaussian random variable with variance proportional to interval duration, consistent with scalar variability. The resulting noisy percept is combined with a Win-Stay, Lose-Switch history feature and a static bias to form a decision variable that governs probabilistic action selection with an explicit lapse process. Model parameters are estimated using gradient-based maximum likelihood optimization enabled by the reparameterization trick. The model is fitted to behavioral data from mice and provides a quantitative framework for dissociating sensory uncertainty, history dependence, and motor bias in temporal decision-making. Results demonstrate that the model captures psychometric sensitivity and behavioral performance with high fidelity, showing no statistically significant deviation from empirical behavior. From an engineering perspective, this framework offers a robust method for designing biologically plausible decision-making systems that function under uncertainty and provides a computational tool for quantifying phenotypic deficits in neurological research.

title: Impact of Developer Seniority on the Acceptance of AI-Generated Code Documentation
abstract: This study aims to investigate the correlation between the seniority of the developers and their affiliation towards AI-generated code documentation. The evaluations of junior, senior, and expert-level developers are analyzed using four different key performance indicators (KPIs): acceptance rate, reliability, time cost, and descriptiveness. Based on the results obtained, conclusions were drawn regarding the benefits of AI and the role of human supervision in software documentation processes, with a special focus on differences in developer experience.

title: AI-Based Autonomous, Energy-Efficient and Resilient O-RAN Architecture for 5G and 6G Networks
abstract: Balancing energy efficiency and network resilience have become a major engineering challenge in emerging 5G and 6G systems. This paper proposes an AI-based unified control architecture operating over the O-RAN framework. The openness and programmability advantages of O-RAN architecture may support the solution of this major challenge when integrated with artificial intelligence. Accordingly, the proposed approach will be able to integrate network outage detection, disaster-aware autonomous resource management, and traffic-aware energy saving mechanisms within a closed-loop control structure. Industrial campus network, post-disaster base station management, and load-aware energy optimization scenarios are considered. The architecture leverages O1, E2, and A1 interfaces for data collection and policy enforcement. The study presents a holistic framework towards autonomous and energy-aware 6G networks. Thus, it establishes a theoretical foundation compliant with O-RAN Alliance standards for future experimental testing and proof-of-concept studies.

title: Vision-Language Models for Remote Sensing: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning and Reinforcement Learning Approaches
abstract: In recent years, vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved significant advances in natural language processing and visual understanding. However, their effective use in specialized domains such as remote sensing has been constrained by high computational costs and domain-specific data requirements. This paper summarizes three approaches developed for remote sensing image analysis. First, TinyRS, a compact 2B-parameter VLM, and its reasoning-augmented variant TinyRS-R1 with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning and Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) alignment are presented. Second, the SAMChat model, focusing on military installation detection, outperforms larger general-purpose models through domain-specific fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Finally, a few-shot reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) framework demonstrates that meaningful performance gains can be achieved with as few as a single training example. Experimental results show that 2B-parameter models achieve competitive or superior performance compared to 7B-scale models.

title: The Limits and Fine-Tuning Performance of Open-Source Small Language Models in Turkish NLP Tasks
abstract: Low-resource languages like Turkish suffer from a shortage of high-quality data for AI research. This study investigates the capacity of Small Language Models (SLMs) to automate labeling processes and scale synthetic data generation on local hardware. We evaluate state-of-the-art SLMs across 8 fundamental NLP tasks using zero-shot and 5-shot strategies. Furthermore, we demonstrate the extent to which full fine-tuning of the ultra-small Gemma 3 270M model can surpass pre-trained limits to function as a specialized labeling assistant. Our findings suggest that optimized SLMs provide a cost-effective alternative to larger models for augmenting Turkish datasets.

title: PSD Estimation in Artifact-Contaminated HRV Signals: A Methodological Comparison
abstract: Heart rate variability (HRV) analysis commonly uses power spectral density (PSD) estimation and related band-based metrics, such as LF, HF, and LF/HF. However, the reliability of these metrics may change depending on data quality, recording duration, and the selected estimation method. In this study, the effects of ECG artifacts and recording duration on HRV spectral analysis were examined. R–R intervals obtained from synthetic ECG signals were used to compare different PSD methods. Performance analysis was also carried out under artifact conditions using multiple realizations. The results show that artifacts can affect R-peak detection and disturb the time structure of R–R intervals. They can also cause spectral distortions and deviations in LF/HF metrics. In addition, PSD results may change even in the reference condition depending on the method and duration, especially in short recordings. Therefore, data quality, recording duration, and method selection should be considered together for reliable HRV analysis.

title: Performance, Scalability, and Computational Resource Consumption Analysis of QNN and QSVM Models in Ideal and Noisy Quantum Simulation Environments
abstract: The performance of quantum machine learning algorithms is subject to hardware noise and scalability constraints. In this study, Quantum Neural Networks (QNN) and Quantum Support Vector Machines (QSVM) were comparatively analysed under ideal and IBM noise models. Accuracy, F1-score, CPU/RAM consumption and iteration times were evaluated in 2, 4 and 6-qubit systems. In the ideal simulation, it was observed that an increasing number of qubits enhances the model’s expressive power. Under noisy conditions, decoherence effects generally reduce performance, whilst it was found that noise exerts a regularising effect under specific hyperparameter settings. Furthermore, it was determined that the QNN optimisation process consumes more classical hardware resources compared to the core computations of QSVM. The research empirically establishes the noise tolerance limits of the models and defines the hardware requirements for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) applications.

title: Evaluation of Deep Learning-based Models for ADHD Detection using Electroencephalography Signals
abstract: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is commonly diagnosed through behavioral assessments, which can be subjective and prone to misdiagnosis. Therefore, we aim to develop an objective diagnostic framework for ADHD detection using deep learning (DL) methods and electroencephalography (EEG). To avoid data leakage, the data was first split and then preprocessed. The conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) was used to augment data. DL models, including one-dimensional residual network (ResNet-1D), conditional variational autoencoder (cVAE), long short-term memory (LSTM), and graph convolutional network (GCN), were utilized to train models using original data and 1:1 augmented data. Our results indicate that the LSTM and ResNet-1D had an accuracy of 85.54% and 82.71%, respectively, while GCN had the lowest accuracy of 64.19%. Our results show that a leakage-free LSTM model has the highest potential to effectively detect ADHD using EEG signals.

title: LLM-Assisted Indoor Scene Assembly with Rule-Based Spatial Validation for Emergency Navigation
abstract: In emergency scenarios such as fires or earthquakes, rapid and accurate situational awareness of the scene is critical for decision-making processes. Operators may inaccurately visualize descriptions received from victims under stress. In this study, a web-based system is proposed that instantly converts natural language environment descriptions into three-dimensional (3D) scene visualizations. Although Generative AI approaches produce photorealistic images, they carry the risk of hallucination. Therefore, this study adopts a deterministic Scene Assembly approach that prioritizes spatial consistency. The system converts user text into a structured JSON format via an LLM-based parser, validates physical consistency through a rulebased spatial inference layer, and computes evacuation routes using the A* algorithm. Experimental results on 100 scenarios show that while LLM-only achieves 76.3% overall accuracy, the addition of the spatial constraint layer raises this to 85.7%.

title: Comparative Performance Analysis of Different Machine Learning Models for an X-Band Metamaterial Absorber
abstract: In this study, the maximum absorption of an X-band metamaterial absorber for transverse magnetic polarized waves is predicted using machine learning. The absorber consists of a meander-line structure surrounded by a ring resonator with two splits on a 1.0 mm thick FR-4 substrate backed by a ground plane. The geometrical parameters and the resonance frequency at which the maximum absorption occurs are defined as the input variables, while the absorption value is taken as the output. Eight different regression models are optimized using Bayesian optimization over a dataset consisting of 216 samples. Nested cross-validation and geometry-variation-based GroupKFold data partitioning are employed. The best result is achieved by Support Vector Regression. For this model, the mean absolute error and the coefficient of determination are 0.00891 and 0.98420, respectively. In addition, for the structure with the highest absorption in the test dataset, the absorption is predicted as 0.994, while full-wave electromagnetic simulation gives an absorption of 0.995. The selected structure maintains an absorption above 0.9 even at an incidence angle of 60°.

title: Development of a Turkish Embedding Model for RAG Applications in the Legal Domain
abstract: For RAG applications in the legal domain, existing embedding models were fine-tuned on Turkish legal data, and the effect of domain adaptation on retrieval performance was investigated. Different models were fine-tuned and comparatively evaluated on a Turkish legal dataset. Metrics such as faithfulness and recall were used in the evaluation. The results showed that fine-tuned models outperformed their base versions. In particular, the fine-tuned bge-m3 model achieved the highest performance on retrieval metrics. The findings reveal that fine-tuning with domain-specific data improves the performance of RAG systems in the Turkish legal domain.

title: An Analysis and Improvement Study on the Wasserstein Policy Optimization
abstract: Wasserstein Policy Optimization (WPO) is a recently proposed Reinforcement Learning (RL) algorithm which aims to maximize the expected reward in the action space, independent of its parametrization. This algorithm, which has been tested in limited RL environments, was compared with several other common algorithms in MuJoCo Gymnasium simulation environments. Experiments revealed that while WPO yields competitive results in terms of short-term training stability, a collapse issue related to cumulative exploding gradients was observed during long-term training. Various architectural improvements have been proposed to address this issue and enhance overall performance. The proposed improvements were implemented in PyTorch and compared with the algorithm’s baseline version. Experimental results showed that applying these improvements together have significantly increased training stability and improved the final reward values obtained.
