title: Multi-view Graph Neural Network Guided Transformer for Cell-Type Annotation
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) provide an effective mechanism for enhancing transformer representations by modeling relational structures that sequence-based models cannot directly capture. In this study, a multiview graph neural network enhanced transformer architecture is proposed for cell-type annotation in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. The proposed approach models complementary relationships between cells using multiple graph views constructed from the training expression matrix, allowing the GNN component to refine transformer-derived embeddings through neighborhood-based information propagation. By combining transformer-based contextual representations with relational information from multiple graph structures, the framework exploits both structural and feature-level patterns in scRNA-seq data. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves cell-type annotation performance compared with existing approaches.
keywords: ["cell type annotation", "single-cell RNA sequencing", "graph neural networks", "transformer models", "multi-view learning"]

title: Anomaly Detection in SDR-Based Spectrums Using the SAIFE Method
abstract: This study proposes an anomaly detection system for wireless communication spectrums based on the SAIFE method using software-defined radio (SDR). Raw I/Q samples acquired through a HackRF One SDR are transformed into the frequency domain to compute the power spectral density (PSD), from which skewness and kurtosis statistical features are extracted. An adaptive error metric derived from z-scores of these features is then used as the anomaly decision criterion. MATLAB/Simulink simulations conducted with random-pulse jammer scenarios on OFDM signals demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively distinguishes between normal and anomalous spectrum conditions.
keywords: ["anomaly detection", "software-defined radio", "spectrum monitoring", "power spectral density", "skewness", "kurtosis", "Z-score", "OFDM signals", "IQ samples"]

title: A Mathematical Method for Detecting LPI Signals
abstract: The unique characteristics of Low Probability of Intercept (LPI) waveforms, which are based on wideband specialized modulation techniques, LPI signals not only provide high resistance against electronic jamming but also significantly reduce the detectability of these signals, thereby establishing LPI signals as an effective electronic countermeasure. The Chirp Spread Spectrum (CSS) waveforms used in the LoRa protocol are a current example of signals possessing LPI characteristics. In complex electromagnetic environments where spectral density is high and the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) drops to critical levels, the detection of these signals and the separation of their sub-characteristics remain an ongoing challenge in the literature. This study presents an original time-frequency analysis approach that enables the detection of CSS signals and parameter estimation with high accuracy under the aforementioned challenging environmental conditions. In tests conducted to validate the method’s performance, CSS signals with unknown parameters were subjected to different channel scenarios by generating spectral density in a laboratory environment. The proposed method was tested on IQ (In-Phase Quadrature) signal data recorded on a Software-Defined Radio (SDR) platform; using the developed algorithm, CSS signal parameters are extracted with high accuracy even under low SNR conditions where the signal power fell below the noise floor in some cases.
keywords: ["chirp spread spectrum", "LoRa", "signal detection", "time-frequency analysis", "parameter estimation", "low signal-to-noise ratio", "electronic countermeasures", "electronic jamming", "software-defined radio", "wideband modulation"]

title: Low Earth Orbit-Supported Non-Terrestrial Networks in 6G: Challenges and Future Research Directions
abstract: Sixth-generation (6G) communication systems require new network architectures capable of delivering global coverage, ultra-low latency, high data rates, and high reliability. However, terrestrial infrastructures remain insufficient in rural areas, oceans, mountainous regions, and disaster scenarios. For this reason, Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTNs), particularly those supported by Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite constellations, have emerged as a key enabler for the coverage and accessibility goals of 6G. Nevertheless, LEO-based NTN systems introduce major challenges, including high mobility, dynamic topology, frequent handovers, and complex resource management. This survey reviews LEO-supported NTN architectures, communication characteristics, and network management mechanisms for 6G, comparatively analyzes solutions for mobility, resource, beam, and routing management, and highlights current limitations as well as future research directions.
keywords: ["non-terrestrial networks", "low Earth orbit satellites", "6G", "satellite constellations", "network architecture", "mobility management", "resource management", "beam management", "routing management", "handover", "network management", "disaster communication"]

title: Temperature-Aware Logit-Based Uncertainty Quantification Analysis for Trustworthy Vision-Language Models in Histopathology
abstract: Integration of Visual Language Models (VLMs) into the healthcare field offers supportive potential for disease diagnosis. However, the black-box nature of VLMs presents significant risks in terms of reliability and safety. This study performs uncertainty quantification analysis to evaluate the reliability of general-purpose and domain-specific VLMs in the context of pathology. The models were evaluated at the logit-level with cosine similarity under varying temperature controls. In terms of temperature increase, the general-purpose medical VILA-M3-8B showed maximum sensitivity, while the pathology domain-specific PRISM demonstrated deterministic stability. The findings suggest that general-purpose VLMs can produce inconsistent outputs under small parameter changes, and that domain-specific pre-training can improve reliability. This study highlights the importance of logit-level uncertainty quantification for the use of VLMs in high-risk clinical decision-making processes.
keywords: ["vision-language models", "uncertainty quantification", "temperature scaling", "histopathology", "medical image analysis", "model reliability", "domain-specific pre-training", "PRISM", "cosine similarity", "clinical decision support"]

title: Placement Optimization for IRS-Assisted Indoor Laser Communication
abstract: Indoor laser-based optical wireless communication systems offer high data rates through narrow-beam transmission, but they also introduce significant design challenges due to the requirements of line-of-sight (LoS) continuity, beam steering precision, and accurate focusing. In this study, an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS)-assisted communication system is considered for redirecting the laser beam in obstructed indoor environments. The proposed outage probability model jointly takes into account the LoS condition between the transmitter and the IRS, as well as the beam spread ratio (BSR), which characterizes the angular spread of the reflected beam. Based on this model, IRS placement optimization is performed using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in order to minimize communication outages within the target service area. Numerical results show that, in scenarios with physical obstacles, the optimized IRS placement significantly reduces the outage probability compared to standard placement.
keywords: ["reconfigurable intelligent surface", "optical wireless communication", "outage probability", "lines of sight", "beam steering", "particle swarm optimization", "obstructed environments"]

title: Robot Number-Cost Balance in Warehouse Automation: A Financial and Operational Analysis
abstract: With the increasing adoption of automation in warehouses, determining the number of autonomous mobile robots has become a critical problem directly impacting both operational performance and investment decisions. This study proposes an integrated analysis that considers both operational and financial dimensions for determining the number of robots in warehouse systems. A model fed with real operational data is developed to systematically represent warehouse movements, task flows, and aisle-based traffic rules. Task times and distances are calculated according to order sequence and warehouse layout. The results show that with a properly configured robot fleet, the system can meet the planned workload, and the parallel operation of robots significantly increases system capacity. The return on investment analysis has shown that robot usage is an economically competitive alternative compared to labor-intensive systems.
keywords: ["warehouse automation", "autonomous mobile robots", "return on investment", "warehouse throughput", "order picking", "warehouse layout"]

title: GWO-Based Hybrid Precoding Optimization for Indoor THz-RSMA Systems Under Practical Impairments
abstract: This paper investigates rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) with grey wolf optimization (GWO)-based digital precoder design in indoor terahertz (THz) communication systems operating at 300 GHz. A hybrid architecture with a 32 × 32 uniform planar array and Grid-of-Beams (GoB) analog beamformer is considered. The proposed GWO algorithm directly refines the joint precoder matrix initialized from regularized zero-forcing (RZF) solutions. Results show that RZF-based RSMA achieves up to 39.6% sum-rate gain over space-division multiple access (SDMA), while GWO-based RSMA provides an additional 49.9% gain over RZF-RSMA. Robustness analyses under channel state information (CSI) errors, phase noise, and their combination indicate that the proposed GWO-RSMA system retains 87.2% of ideal performance under combined impairments.
keywords: ["rate-splitting multiple access", "grey wolf optimizer", "hybrid beamforming", "terahertz communication", "analog beamforming", "regularized zero-forcing", "phase noise", "sum rate"]

title: WeatherOcc3D: VLM-Assisted Adverse Weather Aware 3D Occupancy Prediction
abstract: While multi-modal 3D occupancy prediction typically enhances robustness by fusing camera and LiDAR inputs, its effectiveness is fundamentally constrained by environmental variability. Specifically, camera sensors suffer from severe low-light degradation, while LiDAR sensors encounter significant backscatter noise during heavy precipitation. These adverse conditions create a modality trust problem, as static fusion strategies fail to adaptively re-weight inputs when a specific sensor becomes unreliable. To address this, we propose a VLM-assisted framework leveraging the pre-trained CLIP latent space to guide multi-sensor integration via linguistic environmental cues. We utilize a parameter-efficient adapter to align weather-specific text embeddings with sensor features, coupled with a gating strategy that decomposes environmental uncertainty into two factors: visibility and illumination. This enables the model to dynamically modulate the fusion ratio—prioritizing semantic camera features in clear daylight and shifting to geometric LiDAR priors during rainy nights. Evaluations on the nuScenes dataset demonstrate the versatility of our approach, as implementing our proposed framework on the OccMamba and M-CONet architectures achieves mIoU scores of 26.3 and 21.1, respectively, significantly outperforming their traditional baselines.
keywords: ["3D occupancy prediction", "multi-sensor fusion", "LiDAR-camera fusion", "adverse weather", "vision-language models", "environmental uncertainty", "nuScenes"]

title: Task-Oriented Navigation with Semantic Perception for Monocular Camera-Based Mobile Robots
abstract: For mobile robots to execute commands given by humans in environments lacking localization infrastructure, they must be capable of making semantic inferences about the environment. To this end, we present a task-based navigation method for a mobile robot using single monocular camera. The robot’s perception mechanism consists of a SSD-InceptionV2 for target object detection and MiDaS-Small for depth map estimation. By exploiting the geometric advantage of the motion plane of ground robots, metric distances derived from relative depth outputs are used in the obstacle avoidance algorithm, and a Kalman filter is applied to ensure continuity in target object tracking. Tests conducted on a Jetson TX2 platform verified that the system exhibits stable performance at approximately 15 FPS and successfully completes its task. The results demonstrate that mobile robot navigation systems can be developed in infrastructure-free environments using solely camera-based perception.
keywords: ["mobile robots", "monocular camera", "semantic perception", "object detection", "depth estimation", "obstacle avoidance", "target tracking", "Kalman filter", "unmanned ground vehicles", "NVIDIA Jetson TX2"]

title: Unsupervised Predictive Maintenance for Multivariate Pump Sensor Streams Using Isolation Forest: Health Score Calibration and Persistence Filtering
abstract: Predictive maintenance is critical for reducing unplanned downtime in pump-based cyber-physical systems. This study presents an unsupervised approach based on multivariate sensor data for scenarios with limited labeled data. The dataset contains 220,320 observations and 52 sensor channels; one channel with excessive missing values was removed, and the remaining data were completed. Using 51 sensors, a 408-dimensional feature space was constructed from raw values, first-order differences, and multi-scale moving statistics. An Isolation Forest model was trained using only NORMAL data; anomaly scores were transformed into a 0–100 health score via ECDF, and alarms were generated using a 98th percentile threshold with a 4-in-10 persistence rule. Validation achieved AUC=0.9885 and accuracy=0.9769, while the alarm rate in the test set was 1.14%. Results show that unsupervised scores can be converted into reliable health indicators.
keywords: ["predictive maintenance", "pump condition monitoring", "multivariate sensor data", "Isolation Forest", "anomaly detection", "alarm generation", "missing data imputation", "feature construction", "cyber-physical systems"]

title: CityFlow-Based Smart City Transportation Optimization with Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality Open Data
abstract: In this study, a data-driven reinforcement learning-based signal control model for smart city transportation is developed using traffic records obtained from the open data infrastructure of the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality. The proposed framework transforms raw traffic data into an hourly demand profile, from which microsimulation flows and public transit schedules are generated. A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based controller equipped with a future-aware reward function is trained over a two-intersection corridor. The proposed reward structure jointly optimizes waiting time, queue length, and inter-intersection imbalance through a single cost component projected over a lambda-weighted time horizon. Results reported over five independent random seeds indicate that, compared to the fixed-time baseline, the learned policy achieves approximately a 30.72 percent (standard deviation 5.50 percent) reduction in average waiting time, a 17.75 percent (standard deviation 3.48 percent) reduction in queue length, and a 3.36 percent (standard deviation 0.53 percent) increase in network efficiency. On the public transit side, measurements performed on buses physically present in the simulation show that the same policy reduces average bus waiting time by approximately 29.64 percent (standard deviation 7.59 percent). The findings demonstrate that reinforcement learning approaches fed by open municipal data are applicable to holistic optimization frameworks that jointly handle urban traffic control and public transit performance.
keywords: ["traffic signal control", "reinforcement learning", "proximal policy optimization", "Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality", "microscopic traffic simulation", "public transport", "bus waiting time", "queue length", "waiting time reduction", "reward function design", "network efficiency"]

title: Clinical-Aware CNN with 1D Grad-CAM for AFib Detection on Wearable ECG
abstract: We present a lightweight, edge-compatible convolutional neural network with approximately 66 thousand parameters for four-class atrial fibrillation detection on the PhysioNet/CinC 2017 single-lead ECG dataset. A cost-sensitive loss function penalizes false negatives via an asymmetric weight, meeting clinical safety targets. As a result of ten-fold stratified cross-validation, our model achieves a clinically competent atrial fibrillation sensitivity, substantially outperforming a wavelet scattering transform and random forest-based baseline model. 1D Grad-CAM analyses confirm that the model focuses on clinically meaningful markers such as irregular R-R intervals and absent P-waves.
keywords: ["atrial fibrillation detection", "wearable ECG", "single-lead ECG", "convolutional neural networks", "Grad-CAM", "explainable AI"]

title: yEMG-Based 1D Stiffness Modeling and Classification in Fingertip Grasping
abstract: This study models the mechanical interaction at the fingertip during natural pinch grasping using a control-oriented one-dimensional (1D) stiffness representation. In an experimental setup with different spring stiffness conditions, surface electromyography (sEMG) signals acquired from the Flexor Digitorum Superficialis (FDS) and Extensor Digitorum Communis (Extensor Digitorum Communis) muscles were processed, and root mean square (RMS), average amplitude change (AAC), and co-contraction index (CCI)-based features were extracted. These features were associated with mechanically computed stiffness derived from force and displacement measurements and mapped into three discrete classes: soft, medium, and hard. Results show that the hard condition is clearly separated, gönüllü(subject)specific support vector machine (SVM) models achieve strong accuracy, and limited calibration samples significantly improve personalization. The proposed framework provides an interpretable, low-complexity, and real-time feasible control layer for prosthetic hand and tele-impedance applications.
keywords: ["surface electromyography", "flexor digitorum superficialis", "extensor digitorum communis", "co-contraction index", "support vector machine", "subject-specific calibration", "prosthetic hand control"]

title: Comparison of CAF Methods for Radar EW
abstract: This study compares CAF-based methods for time difference of arrival (TDOA) and frequency difference of arrival (FDOA) estimation in wideband radar electronic warfare (EW) signals. The methods considered are brute-force CAF, lag-product + FFT-based CAF, and Stein-based decimated CAF. All methods are evaluated within the same wideband simulation framework, and the comparison is carried out in terms of estimation accuracy and computational cost. Sinusoidal and triangular frequency-modulated signals are used under different signal-to-noise-ratio conditions. The results show that the method selection in wideband radar EW scenarios depends not only on estimation performance but also on processing cost. In this respect, the study provides a practical comparison that makes the trade-off between accuracy and complexity more explicit.
keywords: ["cyclic autocorrelation function", "time difference of arrival estimation", "wideband radar signals", "computational complexity", "estimation accuracy", "frequency-modulated signals", "sinusoidal signals"]

title: Cell-Based Binary Target Detection and Position Refinement in Multistatic Radar Networks
abstract: This paper addresses target detection and localization in multistatic radar networks using a cell-based binary integration framework. The coarse position estimate obtained from binary integration is refined by a weighted least-squares stage that employs SNR-weighted initialization, prescreening, and Gauss–Newton iterations. Simulation results show that this approach reduces localization error and provides more accurate position estimates.
keywords: ["target detection", "target localization", "weighted least squares", "Gauss-Newton iteration"]

title: Explainable Machine Learning for Cross-Sectional Stock Return Prediction and Mean–Variance Portfolio Optimization
abstract: Portfolio construction aims to balance expected return and risk through effective asset allocation. This study proposes a portfolio formation framework that integrates machine learning-based return prediction with Markowitz mean–variance portfolio optimization. Random Forest, XGBoost, Multilayer Perceptron, and Support Vector Regression models are employed to predict the cross-sectional excess returns of stocks using financial indicators derived from technical and macroeconomic variables. These predictions are incorporated into the portfolio optimization process to determine portfolio weights. The resulting strategies are evaluated against benchmark portfolios including an equal-weighted portfolio and the BIST 100 index. Empirical results show that machine learning-based stock selection improves portfolio performance. In particular, the XGBoost-based portfolio achieves the best results with an annual return of 75.30% and a Sharpe ratio of 1.80. SHAP analysis further indicates that momentum and price-based technical indicators play a dominant role in model predictions.
keywords: ["explainable machine learning", "stock return prediction", "mean-variance optimization", "Markowitz portfolio", "portfolio construction", "asset allocation", "XGBoost", "SHAP analysis", "momentum indicators", "technical indicators", "macroeconomic indicators", "BIST 100 index", "Sharpe ratio"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Health Risk Classification Using Lifestyle and Physiological Indicators
abstract: Accurate assessment of metabolic health status is critically important in preventing diabetes and similar diseases. In recent years, data-driven analyses based on lifestyle and physiological indicators have been increasingly used in assessing health risks. Due to their ability to model complex and nonlinear relationships, artificial intelligence methods used as effective tools in predicting health risks. In this study, a new deep learning architecture was developed to classify health status in a dataset consisting of lifestyle and physiological indicators. To validate the architecture's performance, an analysis was conducted using three machine learning methods (K-nearest neighbors, Gaussian naive Bayes, multinomial logistic regression). The architecture performed significantly better than the compared methods in terms of accuracy (93.00%), precision (95.10%), recall (91.70%), and macro F1(93.04%) metrics.
keywords: ["health risk classification", "lifestyle indicators", "physiological parameters", "diabetes prevention", "deep learning architectures", "health risk prediction"]

title: SafeEx: Safe Robot Execution Framework with Failure Prevention Skills
abstract: Ensuring safe robot execution in unstructured environments remains a significant challenge, particularly for learning-based robotic systems. In this work, we propose SafeEx, a safe robot execution framework that maintains task-oriented skills and safety-oriented failure prevention skills within a structured skill library. SafeEx represents failures using learned risk estimation models and enables efficient learning of failure prevention behaviors by generating risky states through aggressor skills for experimentation. During execution, a risk-based skill selection mechanism dynamically switches between base skills and prevention skills. SafeEx is evaluated in a robotic manipulation case study involving a stirring task with spill failures. Simulation results show that SafeEx reduces spill events by up to 87.5% compared to the baseline stirring policy. Overall, SafeEx significantly improves execution safety while maintaining task progression.
keywords: ["robot safety", "failure prevention", "risk estimation", "skill library", "robotic manipulation", "spill prevention", "unstructured environments"]

title: FMU-Based Residual Decomposition and Dual LSTM Autoencoder Fusion for Anomaly Detection in Collaborative Robots
abstract: This paper presents a score-level fusion framework combining physics-informed and data-driven Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) autoencoders for anomaly detection in collaborative robots, evaluated on 1.1 million real sensor samples from a UR10e robot. A residual LSTM autoencoder operates on 12-channel intrinsic/extrinsic residuals from an FMU-based inverse dynamics model, while a raw LSTM autoencoder processes 24-channel direct sensor data. Evaluation with four synthetic fault types (motor drift, collision, encoder glitch, sensor noise) shows that weighted-average fusion reaches high detection performance and yields a substantial F1 improvement over the best individual model. Window-level complementarity analysis reveals that roughly one-quarter of anomalies are detected only by the residual model and one-quarter only by the raw model, confirming genuine complementarity between the two representations.
keywords: ["anomaly detection", "collaborative robots", "physics-informed models", "Functional Mock-up Units", "inverse dynamics", "residual decomposition", "LSTM autoencoder", "score-level fusion", "collision detection", "sensor noise", "complementarity analysis"]

title: PQDBC: Priority Queue-Driven Online Distribution-Based Clustering
abstract: Online clustering of high-dimensional data streams suffers from the O(K·d) cost of evaluating all K clusters per sample and the slow adaptation of cumulative statistics under concept drift. We propose PQDBC, a two-component method that addresses both limitations. Dimension Sketch Screening (DSS) computes sample-aware sketch distances over q ≪ d characteristic dimensions per cluster, reducing the candidate set to and the theoretical cost to. The Uncertainty-Adaptive Forgetting Gate (UAFG) responds to sudden concept drift by elevating the Welford update rate through a standardized surprise signal, enabling rapid re-adaptation. On 50000-sample, d=2000-dimensional streams, PQDBC raises ARI from 0.894 to 0.996 over CDBC under stationary conditions and from 0.895 to 0.996 under sudden concept drift. At large cluster counts (K=400), DSS achieves a 1.21× speedup.
keywords: ["online clustering", "data streams", "high-dimensional data", "concept drift", "priority queues"]

title: Learning Discrete Relational Symbols for Compound Object Affordances
abstract: Affordance defines the possible actions an object offers and plays a fundamental role in determining how robotic systems interact with their environment. However, compound object affordances are difficult to learn as they depend on complex relationships between all object pairs. Since existing continuous representations overfit to geometric details, they fail to generalize across different configurations with similar relational outcomes and cannot provide the abstraction required for planning. Driven by this motivation, we propose a graph attention network that models pairwise spatial relationships as discrete symbols. The discrete symbolic bottleneck layer enables the model to group geometrically distinct configurations that share the same relational outcome under shared symbols. Experimental results demonstrate that the model successfully predicts spatial effects and that the learned symbols can be utilized to construct compound structures that satisfy given constraints.
keywords: ["graph attention networks", "symbolic representation", "affordance learning", "robotic manipulation"]

title: A Dataset and Benchmark for Embedded Systems Information Retrieval and Generation
abstract: This study presents a dataset and a benchmark framework developed to evaluate retrieval-augmented generation pipelines in the field of embedded systems. Since large language models are pretrained on general-purpose data, they may struggle to produce contextually appropriate and reliable responses in niche and highly specialized domains. The proposed structure aims to systematically investigate this problem by combining article–chunk–question information derived from open-source documents, books, and Wikipedia content. The benchmark framework integrates retrieval quality, retrieval-augmented generation quality, and system efficiency within a single experimental setting. In this respect, the study provides a practical foundation for reproducible and comparable evaluation in the field of embedded systems by jointly presenting a domain-specific dataset and a benchmark protocol.
keywords: ["embedded systems", "retrieval-augmented generation", "benchmark", "datasets", "large language models", "domain-specific evaluation", "information retrieval", "Wikipedia", "system efficiency"]

title: Multi-Threshold Reliability Analysis of Metaheuristic-Based DV-Hop Localization
abstract: In this study, the performance of different Distance Vector-Hop (DV-Hop) based localization algorithms is comprehensively analyzed using a multi-threshold error approach. Unlike the commonly used fixed-threshold evaluation in the literature, the Localization Success Ratio (LSR) metric is examined across different threshold levels in the range of 0.05CR–0.20CR. In this way, not only the performance of the algorithms at a single accuracy level but also their behavior under varying error tolerances is revealed. In addition, simulation results for the position estimation stage of the DV-Hop algorithm, restructured using the Fire Hawk Optimizer (FHO), demonstrate that this approach provides localization performance comparable to strong metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Moreover, this enhancement applied to the third stage of the DV-Hop algorithm offers significant advantages for practical applications due to its lower computational cost and parameter-free structure.
keywords: ["DV-Hop localization", "particle swarm optimization", "wireless sensor networks", "positioning", "error tolerance"]

title: Active Transmitter Sensing and Receiver Design in Multiple LED Environments
abstract: Identifying the correct transmitter in multi-LED visible light communication (VLC) environments poses significant challenges due to alignment sensitivity, distance-dependent signal attenuation, sensor saturation, and ambient light interference. In this study, we propose a hybrid receiver architecture that enables frequency-coded transmitter sensing and camera-assisted spatial selection for multi-infrared (IR) LED setups. The proposed system employs three IR LED transmitters driven concurrently at distinct frequencies. At the receiver, the optical signal is captured by a BPW34 photodiode and converted to a measurable voltage using an MCP6022-based transimpedance analog front-end. The embedded ESP32 microcontroller samples the analog output to evaluate the peak-to-peak amplitude and estimate the zero-crossing frequency, thereby identifying the active transmitter. To prevent saturation across varying distances, a multi-stage gain selection architecture (incorporating 100x, 50x, 10x, and 1x gain steps) is implemented. Furthermore, a Raspberry Pi camera subsystem detects bright circular light sources, providing secondary spatial validation. Experimental results indicate that the system achieves stable detection up to a distance of 40-50 cm, maintaining a frequency identification accuracy of over 90% within the 40–100 kHz band.
keywords: ["visible light communication", "transmitter identification", "transimpedance amplifier", "gain selection", "ambient light interference", "infrared LEDs", "ESP32 microcontroller"]

title: Multi-Class Network Intrusion Detection: Machine and Deep Learning Benchmark with Live Stream Deployment
abstract: The rapid rise of advanced cyber threats is exposing the limitations of traditional, signature-based network intrusion detection systems. While machine learning and deep learning models offer proactive defense mechanisms, current research is often compromised due to temporal data leakage, impractical threat classifications, and significant discrepancies between offline evaluation and online deployment. This study presents a comparative evaluation of traditional machine learning and deep learning architectures integrated into a fully functional real-time inference pipeline. Additionally, we propose an operationally motivated three-class classification encompassing Benign, Volumetric, and Semantic traffic to contextualize incident response. When the trained XGBoost, Random Forest, Decision Tree, LSTM, and BiLSTM models were evaluated and compared under the same constraints, the BiLSTM model achieved the highest Macro F1 score at 97.72%. However, XGBoost closely followed with a Macro F1 of 95.87%, while achieving 15.5 times faster inference. To translate these findings into practice, a Kafka-based live system architecture was designed that integrates real-time stream inference, zero-downtime model switching, and automated threat response capabilities.
keywords: ["network intrusion detection", "multi-class classification", "volumetric attacks", "semantic attacks", "Franz Kafka", "automated threat response", "XGBoost", "BiLSTM", "LSTM", "inference latency"]

title: Data Quality Assessment with Hu Moments for Vision-Language Model Customization
abstract: This study investigates the applicability of Hu invariant moments for data quality assessment in vision-language model customization. The proposed method replaces CLIP-based cross-modal similarity metrics with Hu moments-based shape similarity for quality assessment of image-text pairs retrieved from web-scale datasets. Our experimental analysis reveals that only the first two of the seven Hu moments produce stable results. Experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets with varying training data sizes demonstrate that Hu moments yield positive results for shape-distinctive classes, but exhibit significantly lower performance compared to cross-modal scoring in natural image classification.
keywords: ["Hu moments", "data quality assessment", "vision-language models", "CLIP", "cross-modal similarity", "shape similarity", "image-text pairs", "training data size", "MNIST", "CIFAR-10"]

title: Enhancing Pavement Distress Classification via Supervised Contrastive Learning
abstract: The performance of deep learning models in pavement distress detection is often limited by data scarcity and interclass visual similarities. This study proposes a hybrid training strategy combining Cross-Entropy and Supervised Contrastive Learning to enhance discriminative feature learning. Experiments conducted on the PaveDistress dataset using ResNet50 and EfficientNetB0 architectures demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms traditional fine-tuning approach. The EfficientNetB0 model achieved a test accuracy of 92.74% (a 1.63% improvement), and t-SNE analyses confirmed significantly improved class separability and clustering quality.
keywords: ["pavement distress classification", "supervised contrastive learning", "cross-entropy loss", "data scarcity", "discriminative feature learning", "EfficientNetB0", "ResNet50", "fine-tuning"]

title: Generating Attacks for LLM with GFlowNets
abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has facilitated their ubiquitous integration into various domains, leading to widespread adoption. However, this escalating trend has introduced significant security vulnerabilities, necessitating the identification and mitigation of flaws arising from malicious exploitation. Red teaming assessments, conducted to evaluate model robustness through diverse adversarial inputs, are essential for exposing security risks and implementing countermeasures. Currently, red teaming is performed either manually by experts or automatically using predefined attack datasets. Nevertheless, manual testing remains time-consuming, while existing automated methods suffer from limited creativity due to their inherent dependency on fixed datasets. In this study, we propose an automated, human-independent, and adaptive approach leveraging GFlowNets to identify LLM vulnerabilities by utilizing one large language model to test another. Within this framework, an attacker model is trained against a specified victim model to perform automated red teaming and provide a quantitative robustness score. This research aims to generate more effective adversarial attacks in English compared to existing benchmarks and, as a novel contribution to the literature, introduces a model capable of generating attack inputs in the Turkish language.
keywords: ["large language models", "adversarial attacks", "generative flow networks", "red teaming", "model robustness"]

title: Personalized Visual Aesthetic Alignment via Direct Preference Optimization
abstract: Visual aesthetics assessment models often focus on general crowd preferences, thereby overlooking individual and subjective tastes. This study investigates how a generic aesthetic model can be aligned with personal preferences using limited user data and proposes a framework based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). Due to the instabilities and "scale blindness" caused by absolute scoring systems, the problem was reformulated into a pairwise preference structure, and the DPO algorithm was integrated into a CLIP-based model. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method reduced the test loss from 0.6931 to 0.5140 and increased the pairwise accuracy from 60% to 78.33%. These findings confirm that fine-tuning with DPO provides accurate personal aesthetic alignment compared to generic models.
keywords: ["direct preference optimization", "CLIP", "fine-tuning"]

title: Gain Enhancement of Antenna Using Epsilon-Near-Zero Metamaterial
abstract: In this study, a single-layer Epsilon-Near-Zero (ENZ) metamaterial (MTM) superstrate is designed and systematically optimized to enhance the electromagnetic radiation performance of a 10 GHz quarter-wave microstrip patch antenna (MPA). A 7×7 unit cell array is developed, and both the geometrical parameters and the antenna-superstrate spacing are optimized through full wave simulations. Simulation results indicate a realized gain enhancement of 7.34 dB compared to the reference antenna while maintaining the resonance frequency. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed single-layer ENZ superstrate configuration for high gain antenna applications, such as X band radar and satellite communication systems, with stable gain performance over the 9-11 GHz frequency range. The antenna performance exhibits high gain, low profile, low cost, easy integration, and optimal matching characteristics.
keywords: ["epsilon-near-zero metamaterials", "antenna gain enhancement", "microstrip patch antenna", "metamaterial superstrate", "unit cell array", "10 GHz antenna", "X-band radar", "satellite communication antennas"]

title: Experimental Evaluation of RF Hardware Impairments Across Receiver and Transmitter Origins
abstract: This study presents a theoretical and experimental investigation of DC offset and I/Q imbalance impairments in direct conversion (zero-IF) transceiver architectures. It first analytically demonstrates that the two distinct components of these impairments, arising from receiver and transmitter hardware imperfections, affect the desired signal band differently. This distinction is then validated with experimental data obtained using the AD9363-based ADALM-PLUTO software-defined radio platform. Furthermore, the effects of the integrated correction properties in this platform on the received signal band are examined, demonstrating that these methods suppress only receiver-originated impairment components. Although DC offset and I/Q imbalance have been extensively studied in the literature, the separate experimental analysis of their components originating from both the receiver and transmitter has received limited attention. In this regard, the study contributes to the literature.
keywords: ["DC offset", "I/Q imbalance", "direct-conversion transceiver", "direct conversion receiver", "ADALM-PLUTO", "software-defined radio"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Automatic Modulation Recognition of Harmonic-Modulated Signals
abstract: In this study, the problem of deep learning-based automatic modulation recognition (AMR) of harmonic-modulated signals is investigated. Within the scope of the study, a dataset consisting of M-PSK signals under both standard and harmonic modulation effects is generated and analyzed using a convolutional neural network (CNN) based classifier. In the proposed approach, raw I and Q components of the signals are used as input data; the training and testing processes are conducted under various SNR values. The obtained results show that while the deep learning-based approach achieves high accuracy for low-order modulations, the classification performance drops to the 30%-40% range as the modulation order increases due to the micro-phase variations induced by harmonic components. These findings demonstrate that harmonic modulation provides a high low probability of intercept (LPI) capability against artificial intelligence-based surveillance systems.
keywords: ["automatic modulation classification", "harmonic modulation", "convolutional neural networks", "low probability of intercept"]

title: Reinforcement Learning Based Autonomous Agent Society Simulation
abstract: Measuring the impact of socioeconomic indicators such as education quality, social welfare, and crime on macroeconomic outcomes such as Gross Domestic Product is empirically challenging due to complex causal relationships. This study presents a deep reinforcement learning–based agent simulation to model these relationships. It is run in parallel across four economic models from the literature, using as inputs the averaged socioeconomic indicators of nine representative countries. Each model is trained with eighty household agents over a four-year episode; outputs are compared against real-world data to identify the reward function yielding the highest alignment. The simulation results offer exploratory insights into the potential effects of small-scale input changes on macroeconomic outcomes, and should be regarded as a starting point for further analysis rather than direct policy prescriptions.
keywords: ["deep reinforcement learning", "agent-based modeling", "socioeconomic indicators", "macroeconomic effects", "gross domestic product", "educational quality", "social welfare", "crime", "reward function design", "economic models"]

title: A Reliable Data Annotation Framework for Suicidal Ideation Detection
abstract: Özetçe -İntihar düşüncesi tespiti, gerçek zamanlı önleme için kritik öneme sahiptir, ancak sınırlı dil kapsamı ve güvenilmez etiketleme uygulamaları, bu alandaki çalışmaları ve ilerlemeyi kısıtlamaktadır.Mevcut veri kümelerinin çogu İngilizce olup yüksek kaliteli, insan etiketli, halka açık örnekler azdır.Bu çalışma, sosyal medya gönderilerinden türetilen yeni bir Türkçe intihar veri kümesi ve üç insan etiketleyici ile iki büyük dil modeli kullanan kaynak verimli bir etiketleme çerçevesi sunmaktadır.Sekiz önceden egitilmiş sınıflandırıcı ile transfer ögrenimi kullanılarak etiketli veri kümesi ve üç İngilizce veri kümesi arasında etiket güvenilirligi ve model tutarlılıgı degerlendirilmiştir.Bulgular, ruh saglıgı odaklı dogal dil işleme (DD İ) alanında daha titiz, dil kapsayıcı etiketli verilere ve model güvenilirligine ihtiyaç oldugunu göstermektedir.
keywords: ["suicidal ideation detection", "social media posts", "annotation framework", "inter-annotator reliability", "model consistency", "transfer learning", "multilingual language models", "low-resource annotation"]

title: Analyzing Subthreshold Motor Cortical Activity at Trial Onset in a Visuo-Motor Task
abstract: In this study, we investigated the temporal evolution of the subthreshold component of extracellular motor cortical recordings band-pass filtered in the action potential frequency range (400 Hz–8 kHz) around trial onset in a visuomotor task. Previous work has shown that behavior can be decoded with high accuracy using the mean and standard deviation of this subthreshold component during the response period. It has also been observed that these features change in a stable manner over the final 2 s preceding trial initiation. Here, we examined the statistical significance of this change. Using recordings obtained from multiple intracortical electrodes, we analyzed the time-dependent linear slope of subthreshold activity during the last two seconds before trial onset.In addition, using data from the same electrodes, we evaluated whether there is an association between the statistical significance of these slopes and behavioral decoding accuracy. In the final stage of the study, we tested whether subthreshold activity exhibits an abrupt change at trial onset. Our results indicate that the changes in the pre-start period are statistically significant for multiple electrodes, whereas no abrupt change in activity occurs at trial onset. However, within the available dataset, we did not find a statistically significant relationship between the statistical significance of the time-dependent linear slope and the decoding accuracy obtained from the same electrode. These findings are important for understanding how the subthreshold component evolves in relation to behavior.
keywords: ["visuomotor task", "intracortical electrodes", "motor cortex", "neural decoding"]

title: The Effect of Freezing and Thresholding Selection in Transfer Autoencoders on Time Series Anomaly Detection
abstract: Anomaly detection in multivariate time series within industrial control systems is challenging due to label scarcity, domain shift, and process differences. This study investigates the cross-domain transfer performance of an LSTM-based sequential autoencoder (SeqAE) on the SWaT, WADI, and TEP datasets. The model was pre-trained in the source domain and evaluated in the target domain with a zero-training base and four transfer/freeze strategies. Four training ratios (10%, 20%, 50%, 70%), four thresholding methods (quantile, MAD, adaptive_MAD, top_k), and five random seeds were used in the experiments. The results show relatively high F1 values in the SWaT objective, low but close values across strategies in the WADI objective, and high F1/PR-AUC values in the TEP objective. Overall findings indicate that the effect of the freeze strategy is dataset-dependent and that threshold selection plays a critical role in performance.
keywords: ["time series anomaly detection", "multivariate time series", "transfer learning", "LSTM", "layer freezing", "thresholding", "domain shift", "limited labeled data", "industrial control systems", "SWaT dataset", "WADI dataset"]

title: Rule-Based Myocardial Infarction Screening from Paper ECG Images via Digitization and Clinical Criteria
abstract: This paper presents a rule-based, explainable screening system that distinguishes Myocardial Infarction (MI) from paper or photographic ECG images. ST-segment elevation, convexity analysis, posterior MI detection, and reciprocal depression rules were applied to signals digitized via computer vision. The end-to-end pipeline achieved 77.0% sensitivity and 86.1% specificity on 924 images; the analysis module reached 81.5% sensitivity and 86.8% specificity on PTB-XL (n=999). These results confirm that a transparent clinical decision support mechanism can be built on medical rules alone, without opaque black-box models.
keywords: ["rule-based diagnosis", "ST-segment elevation", "convexity analysis", "PTB-XL"]

title: A Hybrid Attention U-Net and ResNet101-Based Deep Learning Approach for Left Atrium-Ventricle Segmentation in Echocardiography Images
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are among the leading causes of mortality worldwide; therefore, improving early diagnosis processes is of paramount importance. Although echocardiography is a widely used imaging modality for assessing the morphological structure of the heart, diagnostic accuracy is often limited by subjectivity in clinical evaluations and class imbalance issues in automated image analysis. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning approach that integrates the Attention U-Net and ResNet101 architectures. Utilising the CAMUS dataset, this approach segments the left atrium-ventricle region to enable the automatic and objective analysis of echocardiography images. Specifically, the proposed method focuses on left ventricular segmentation utilizing the CAMUS dataset. The model offers a more robust architecture than existing methods for both extracting deep features and preserving spatial resolution. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid model outperforms conventional methods, achieving a superior Dice score of 95.51%. This high accuracy not only highlights the effective management of the class imbalance problem but also reinforces the potential of artificial intelligence-based approaches in facilitating early diagnosis.
keywords: ["echocardiography", "Attention U-Net", "ResNet-101", "hybrid deep learning model", "CAMUS dataset", "class imbalance", "left ventricle segmentation", "cardiac image analysis", "early diagnosis of cardiovascular disease"]

title: MedRAG-TR: Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation Framework for Turkish Pharmaceutical Documents
abstract: Multilingual Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems often suffer from performance degradation when queries and documents are written in different languages. This study proposes MedRAG-TR, a domain-specific multilingual RAG framework designed for Turkish pharmaceutical documents. The approach constructs a symmetric bilingual corpus using glossary-guided translation to preserve medical terminology. Domain-specific question–answer pairs are generated to fine-tune a multilingual embedding model, improving cross-lingual retrieval. The system integrates language detection and FAISS-based retrieval to select relevant document chunks before answer generation. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in retrieval accuracy and in semantic similarity compared to the baseline model.
keywords: ["retrieval-augmented generation", "medical terminology translation", "cross-lingual information retrieval", "question-answer pairs", "language identification", "semantic similarity"]

title: Rotational Post-Training Quantization for Biomedical Vision-Language Models
abstract: Deploying biomedical vision-language models (VLMs) on resource-limited clinical hardware requires reducing memory use and inference cost without sacrificing diagnostic reliability. Post-training quantization (PTQ) is practical for this purpose but degrades at low bit-widths due to extreme activation outliers. Recent rotation-based PTQ methods suppress these outliers via orthogonal transformations, yet they target decoder-only architectures and do not extend to CLIP-style dual encoders. Here, we propose a rotation-based PTQ pipeline for CLIP-based biomedical VLMs. The method converts LayerNorm to RMSNorm through column-centered output projections, and applies modality-specific deterministic Walsh-Hadamard absorption to the pre-norm ViT image encoder and post-norm PubMedBERT text encoder. On the PCam histopathology benchmark, the proposed method preserves zero-shot accuracy at low-bit precision with substantial model compression, while standard PTQ baselines collapse to chance-level performance under the same conditions.
keywords: ["post-training quantization", "CLIP", "low-bit precision", "activation outliers", "RMSNorm", "Hadamard transform", "histological classification", "model compression"]

title: Real-Time Cockpit CO 2 Monitoring Using a Triboelectric Nanogenerator Supported Embedded System
abstract: This study presents the design of an embedded system that enables real-time monitoring of carbon dioxide (CO2) levels inside a cockpit while also evaluating the energy harvesting approach within an auxiliary power architecture. In the developed system, the low-level output obtained from a triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) is investigated within a hybrid power architecture operating with a lithium battery. The main motivation of the study is to examine the feasibility of using the energy harvested from the environment through the TENG as an auxiliary energy harvesting approach in battery-while CO2sensor data are transmitted to the microcontroller using the UART (Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter) communication protocol. To improve measurement accuracy, software-based filtering methods such as oversampling and averaging are applied during data processing. In addition, a threshold-based approach is used to distinguish low-level noise signals in the evaluation of the signals obtained from the TENG system. With the developed system, cockpit air quality is monitored in real time, and the auxiliary energy harvesting potential of the low-level electrical output obtained from the TENG module is evaluated at a preliminary experimental level.
keywords: ["triboelectric nanogenerator", "CO2 monitoring", "embedded systems", "energy harvesting", "lithium batteries", "CO2 sensor", "microcontroller", "UART communication", "noise reduction", "real-time monitoring"]

title: Comparative Performance Analysis of Anti-Jamming Methods in the GPS L1 Band
abstract: Global Positioning System (GPS) signals in the L1 band are inherently vulnerable to both intentional and unintentional jamming because of their low received power levels. In this study, the performance of three different adaptive filtering algorithms is investigated against five representative jammer types in a GPS L1 receiver employing a single-element patch antenna. The considered jammer types include continuous-wave, swept, pulsed, wideband, and Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK)-modulated interference. The evaluated algorithms comprise the Least Mean Squares (LMS), Recursive Least Squares (RLS), and Adaptive Notch Filter-based approaches. Simulation-based assessments are carried out in terms of signal-to-noise-and-interference ratio improvement, bit error rate, convergence speed, and computational complexity. The results indicate that each algorithm offers distinct performance advantages depending on the characteristics of the interfering signal.
keywords: ["GPS anti-jamming", "GPS L1", "adaptive filtering", "LMS algorithm", "recursive least squares", "adaptive notch filter", "wideband jamming", "bit error rate", "convergence rate", "computational complexity"]

title: Design Implementation of a OTA-Based Memristor Emulator Circuit without Passive Components
abstract: This study presents a novel memristor emulator that does not require external passive components. The proposed topology allows full electronic control of circuit parameters and contributes to minimizing the area occupied on the chip. The performance of the designed circuit was evaluated through simulations. The results demonstrate that the circuit exhibits stable memristive behavior over a wide frequency range and can be effectively controlled through bias currents.
keywords: ["memristor emulator", "operational transconductance amplifier", "OTA", "memristive behavior", "bias current control", "chip area reduction", "analog circuit design"]

title: Developing a Sign Dictionary using Continuous Turkish Sign Data via Sign Spotting
abstract: Sign language recognition and translation require large-scale signed data. In this study, I3D, DINO, and SHu-BERT architectures were used to automatically capture signs corresponding to target words in subtitles on the BUTID dataset compiled from television programs interpreted in Turkish Sign Language (TİD) and their capture performances were analyzed comparatively. It was shown that the system's performance was increased with an bootstrapping procedure supported by human validation.
keywords: ["Turkish Sign Language", "sign language recognition", "sign language translation", "I3D", "DINO", "subtitles", "bootstrapping", "human validation"]

title: Representation Analysis for 3D Avatars
abstract: Recent generative models have enabled the creation of photorealistic 3D avatars from a limited number of images. However, the impact of generation settings on representation quality and computational cost has not been sufficiently studied. In this work, instead of proposing a new avatar generation method, we analyze the effect of different generation settings in a CAP4D-based 3D avatar pipeline. The results show that medium-cost configurations, where the generation time is reduced to approximately one quarter, can preserve visual quality close to high-cost settings. PSNR, LPIPS, CSIM and JOD results indicate that these configurations should be interpreted not as a strict quality improvement, but as an efficient cost–quality trade-off for practical use.
keywords: ["3D avatar generation", "computational cost", "cost-quality trade-off", "representation quality", "image-based 3D reconstruction", "visual quality metrics"]

title: Real-Time Android Telemetry and Crowdsourcing-Based Multi-Criteria Electric Vehicle Charging Station Recommendation System
abstract: This study presents an integrated platform designed to reduce range anxiety for electric vehicle (EV) users during long-distance travel. The system combines real-time Android vehicle telemetry, a multi-criteria charging station recommendation algorithm, estimated cost analysis, and crowdsourced station status validation. An Android Automotive-compatible Kotlin service collects battery, speed, and location data at 2-second intervals and transmits them to a Python Flask REST API. The Haversine-based EVChargingRecommender algorithm suggests suitable charging stations according to three user preference modes (economical, nearest, fastest) while estimating charging time and cost in real time. Users can contribute to station data through status reports and written feedback. Station information was retrieved from the Open Charge Map API and includes 103 real charging stations along the Bolu-Ankara-Sakarya route [12]. All functional scenarios were successfully completed, and API response times remained below 200 ms.
keywords: ["electric vehicle charging stations", "charging station recommendation", "range anxiety", "crowdsourcing", "multi-criteria decision making", "Haversine distance", "long-distance travel", "Kotlin"]

title: Underwater Localization using Forward-Looking Sonar and Artificial Object References
abstract: As an alternative to underwater acoustic positioning systems, a low-cost underwater vehicle localization method based on the detection and machine-learning driven classification of known underwater artifacts using a forward-looking imaging sonar is presented. Distance and bearing based approaches are used for vehicle position estimation. Dead-reckoning is employed when no artifacts are detected by the sonar. A linear Kalman filter is used for sensor fusion to achieve optimum accuracy in position estimation. Computer simulations reveal that localization errors can be reduced more than a half for the proposed cost-effective positioning approach.
keywords: ["underwater vehicle positioning", "forward-looking sonar", "imaging sonar", "machine learning classification", "dead reckoning", "sensor fusion", "Kalman filter", "positioning", "low-cost localization"]

title: A Calibration-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Profit-Optimal Pricing of Flight VIP Ancillaries
abstract: Optional ancillary products are a key component of online flight retailing, but their pricing is challenging because purchase propensity varies across trip context, customer segment, and platform conditions. This paper proposes a calibration-aware machine learning framework for pricing a VIP ancillary that provides priority 24/7 customer support. Purchase propensity is modeled using decision-time context and offered rate, allowing candidate rates to be evaluated within observed pricing support. Five models are compared: XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, Random Forest, and Logistic Regression. XGBoost performs best (AUC 0.821, F1 0.611). Post-hoc calibration substantially improves probability quality; for XGBoost, ECE decreases from 0.2456 to 0.0649 and Brier score from 0.1818 to 0.1043. Results support the use of calibrated rate-conditioned probabilities for profit-oriented ancillary pricing.
keywords: ["purchase intention", "profit maximization", "XGBoost", "CatBoost", "LightGBM", "random forest", "logistic regression", "expected calibration error", "Brier score", "customer support services"]

title: D3QN-Based Emergency Department Staff Scheduling: A Comparative Analysis under Stochastic Demand and Surge Conditions
abstract: This study models the emergency department (ED) staff shift scheduling problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) that incorporates realistic uncertainties: stochastic patient demand, acuity-based priority (ESI), staff absenteeism, and sudden patient surge events. The proposed D3QN (Dueling Double DQN + Prioritized Experience Replay) algorithm is compared, within the same environment, against seven baselines: DQN, PPO, GRPO, MAPPO, Greedy, Rule-Based, and Random. The results show that D3QN attains superior sample efficiency in the early learning phase, adapts effectively to surge scenarios, and achieves competitive coverage with about 18.7% fewer staff than the Greedy baseline. Multiple independent runs and paired significance tests support the statistical reliability of these findings.
keywords: ["shift scheduling", "dueling double deep Q-network", "prioritized experience replay", "Markov decision process", "patient surge", "Emergency Severity Index", "absenteeism", "deep reinforcement learning", "sample efficiency"]

title: #Boykot: Brand-based Political Polarization
abstract: This study examines Instagram discussions around #boykot as a case of digital activism and political polarization in Turkey following March 19, 2025. Using the hashtags #boykot, #boykotadevam, and #boykotadevamturkiyem, we collected 51,610 posts from 14,588 users between March 27, 2025 and September 24, 2025. We combine temporal analysis, sentiment classification, and hashtag co-occurrence network analysis. Sentiment labels are generated with TurkishBERTweet, a model adapted to Turkish social media language. Results show that domestically focused boycott narratives are strongly event-driven, peaking rapidly and then declining over time, while negative discourse toward brands associated with the Israel-Palestine conflict is more stable and persistent. Network findings further reveal a structurally polarized communication space with two salient poles, alongside a central area dominated by engagement-oriented and agenda-agnostic content. Overall, #boykot functions not only as a consumer boycott signal but also as a multi-layered arena where political identities, grievances, and polarization dynamics become visible.
keywords: ["boycotts", "political polarization", "digital activism", "Instagram", "brand boycott", "Israeli-Palestinian conflict", "sentiment analysis", "consumer boycotts"]

title: A Hybrid Recommender System for Opportunity Products in FMCG Field Sales
abstract: This paper presents an artificial intelligence based hybrid recommender system that identifies opportunity products for retail outlets in FMCG field sales. The goal is to support sales representatives by recommending products that an outlet is likely to purchase but has not purchased within a recent frequency window, configured between 60 and 90 days. The proposed framework combines three complementary signals: behavioral outlet similarity retrieved with FAISS, geographic neighborhood similarity computed from outlet locations and latent product affinity learned via singular value decomposition. Candidate outputs from these models are merged and refined through operational post processing: products with return rates above three percent are removed, category exposure is balanced using outlet segment weights, and the final list is capped at 5, 10 or 15 items depending on the outlet’s annual purchase breadth. We evaluate the system through a 12 day pilot integrated into the tablet workflow, generating 51,107 offers across 4,027 outlets. Over the pilot period, recommendation adoption was 34.7 percent and offer acceptance was 6.35 percent. During a subsequent rollout between May and October 2025, overall offer acceptance remained in the 9 to 10 percent range at scale.
keywords: ["hybrid recommendation", "salespeople", "FAISS", "singular value decomposition", "acceptance of offer"]

title: Autonomous Spider Robot with Hybrid Locomotion
abstract: Biomimetic approaches play a critical role in overcoming the performance limits of mobile robotic systems. In this context, bio-inspired robots provide promising terrain-adaptive solutions by exploiting locomotion strategies and environmental adaptability observed in nature. In this study, a hybrid robot inspired by Cebrennus rechenbergi is designed, capable of both walking and rolling on uneven, and flat terrains. To achieve this complex hybrid locomotion capability, a novel inverse kinematics model is developed to ensure precise leg placement on the ground. For attitude estimation, an IMU-based Extended Kalman Filter (EKF), insensitive to magnetic disturbances caused by the motors, is employed, while a LiDAR sensor is integrated for environmental perception. The resulting agile prototype combines completed mechanical and control infrastructure with hybrid locomotion capability, demonstrating adaptability across diverse terrain conditions.
keywords: ["spider robot", "hybrid locomotion", "bio-inspired robotics", "legged robots", "inverse kinematics", "attitude estimation", "terrain adaptability"]

title: Dual Transformer-based Prediction of Player and Ball Trajectories in Basketball
abstract: In modern basketball, trajectory prediction and real-time feedback systems have become useful tools for game analysis, tactical planning, and decision-making. Our paper is a contribution on short-term prediction of player and ball movement in professional basketball, using historical movement and contextual game information as input. We use data from 500 games from a professional basketball league, provided by a sports analytics company. The raw video feeds are processed to extract 3D positions of all ten players and the ball, sampled at 60 Hz. We propose a dual transformer architecture, using masked autoencoders for pretraining, and report very good results. We additionally conducted a perceptual study to verify that the predicted trajectories look realistic.
keywords: ["basketball", "trajectory prediction", "player movement", "ball movement", "dual transformer", "masked autoencoder", "professional basketball", "real-time feedback", "perceptual evaluation", "sports analytics"]

title: Adaptive Embedding Dimensions Technique
abstract: The number of distinct values a feature can have reflects its complexity, diversity, discriminative strength, and popularity. Consequently, features with more unique values benefit from larger embedding dimensions to reflect their variability more effectively. Using a uniform embedding size across all features leads to inefficient use of model capacity. We introduce the adaptive embeddings dimensions (AED) technique that allocates embedding dimensions based on clustering to reduce the model size and improve the performance. With AED, we can maintain an overall model size to a projected level and obtain best improvements reaching 0.14 in RelaImp of AUC and 5.51% and 1.19% in logloss and PRAUC respectively in offline results and 4.02% in total advertiser value (TAV) and 5.09% in eCPM in the online prediction results on advertisement recommendation.
keywords: ["feature diversity", "model size reduction", "advertisement recommendation", "online prediction"]

title: Comparison of Slow-Time Coded MIMO and Phased Array Radar Systems Under Phase Noise
abstract: This paper evaluates the performance of slow-time coded MIMO and phased array radars under transmitter and receiver phase noise. Utilizing a genie-aided joint angle-Doppler processing framework, we compare the SINR performance of both architectures in interference-rich environments. Numerical results indicate that while both systems degrade under high phase noise, MIMO radar exhibits superior angular selectivity and faster SINR recovery in clutter. These benefits are attributed to the waveform diversity and increased degrees of freedom provided by slow-time coding, which improves directional interference mitigation over single-waveform phased array systems.
keywords: ["phased array radar", "SINR performance", "clutter", "interference mitigation", "waveform diversity", "angular selectivity", "degrees of freedom"]

title: Temporal Convolutional Networks for Electrical Power Forecasting in Micro Gas Turbine
abstract: Micro gas turbines are increasingly used as flexible distributed generation units in microgrids, where short horizon electrical power prediction is critical for operational planning and decision support. This study presents a temporal convolutional network model to predict electrical power output using only minimal inputs, namely time and input voltage, on the data set "Micro Gas Turbine Electrical Energy Prediction". Evaluation follows a run level split protocol and uses a run aware windowing pipeline, where independent runs are not concatenated and training and testing samples are generated within each run before pooling. The average R2, RMSE, MAE, and MAPE values of the proposed model achieves 0.8392, 324.88, 203.15, and 10.72 on the test set, respectively. Qualitative diagnostics indicate strong alignment in steady state regions, while larger errors concentrate around transition periods following input changes
keywords: ["micro gas turbine", "temporal convolutional network", "short-term power forecasting", "microgrids", "distributed generation", "input voltage", "prediction error analysis"]

title: Spatial Knowledge Distillation in Video Models via Vision-Language Guided Zero-Shot Pretraining
abstract: Video action recognition tasks require large-scale labeled data to achieve high performance when pretraining is not used. However, annotating video data is costly and time-consuming. To reduce this dependency on labeled data, transfer learning approaches are commonly employed. Vision–language models, which learn generalizable visual representations from large-scale data, are effective at capturing spatial information and thus serve as suitable teacher models for spatial knowledge distillation. In this work, we propose a knowledge distillation-based pretraining approach that leverages zero-shot predictions from vision–language models to initialize video models. In this framework, the resulting soft class distributions are used as supervisory signals and transferred to the student video model. Experimental results on the UCF101 and HMDB51 datasets demonstrate that the proposed method provides an effective weight initialization strategy and yields consistent performance improvements.
keywords: ["video action recognition", "vision-language models", "teacher-student models", "weight initialization", "transfer learning", "annotation cost reduction"]

title: Uncertainty-Aware Multiclass Retinal OCT Lesion Segmentation on AMD-SD via MC Dropout
abstract: This study addresses multiclass segmentation of retinal OCT lesions associated with neovascular (wet) age-related macular degeneration (wAMD) on the AMD-SD dataset (SRF, IRF, PED, SHRM, IS/OS). Five baselines from the U-Net family (U-Net, U-Net Plus Plus, ResUNet, Attention U-Net, U-Mamba) and SwinUNet were compared using a common training and evaluation protocol. To make reliability information explicit for clinical use, Monte Carlo (MC) Dropout is enabled during inference, and pixel-wise uncertainty maps are produced using predictive entropy and mutual information (MI). Quantitative results indicate that under class imbalance and boundary ambiguity, architectural differences become particularly apparent on small and fragmented lesions. Under this protocol, SwinUNet achieves the highest mean Dice score excluding background with a limited margin (0.6307); the uncertainty maps concentrate around lesion boundaries and low-contrast challenging regions, providing a practical review signal for potential error risk.

title: Combined PK-PD Model for 6-MP, MTX, and VCR Treatment in Childhood ALL
abstract: This study presents an integrated pharmacokinetic–pharmacodynamic (PK–PD) modeling framework for multi-drug chemotherapy used in pediatric Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL). The model addresses the pharmacological effects of three commonly used drugs (6-mercaptopurine (6-MP), methotrexate (MTX), and vincristine (VCR)) simultaneously within a unified mathematical structure. For each drug, PK models describing absorption, distribution, metabolism, and elimination processes are combined under a drug effect function and integrated into the overall system. The model predicts hematological responses based on white blood cell (WBC) and absolute neutrophil count (ANC), as well as vincristine-induced peripheral neuropathy (VIPN) indicators. The simulation results demonstrate treatment response by capturing interactions between drugs and patient-specific variables across a four-phase treatment protocol, and provide a computational basis for personalized dose optimization in pediatric ALL treatment.

title: New Approaches for TDOA Source Localization: Selection Based LS and Deep Learning
abstract: In electronic warfare systems, the position of a target radar can be estimated using time difference of arrival (TDOA) measurements. This study focuses on a location estimation scenario with three receivers, where position uncertainty is significant. Two methods are proposed for this problem that eliminate ambiguity by narrowing the solution space. The first is the least-squares (LS) being an analytical solution-based, intelligent selective estimator. This estimation method offers lower computational complexity while performing similarly to maximum likelihood methods. The second method is an artificial neural network-based estimator. Although this method lags behind maximum likelihood methods in terms of position accuracy, it is considered a good alternative when an analytical solution is not available.
keywords: ["time difference of arrival", "radar target localization", "electronic warfare", "least squares estimation", "solution space reduction", "position uncertainty", "computational complexity"]

title: Low-Cost Integrated Sensing and Communication System Design with Ultrasonic Sound Waves
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology is an important approach that reduces hardware cost and energy consumption for next-generation communication systems. While existing ISAC studies in the literature generally focus on complex orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) waveforms requiring high processing power and costly radio frequency (RF) or underwater acoustic hardware, this study overcomes this complexity problem in the literature by designing a lightweight, low-cost system that combines both functions on a single ultrasonic platform. In the developed system, the distance of the target is measured using the time-of-flight (ToF) method, while data transmission is performed via on-off keying (OOK) pulse interval modulation (PIM) over the same ultrasonic signals. The basic design of the system consists of an ESP32 microcontroller, an HC-SR04 ultrasonic module, and an LM358based analog receiver circuit. Multipath echo signals, which are the biggest challenge in ultrasonic communication systems, are successfully suppressed by the amplification/comparison layer realized with the LM358 and the interrupt-based time filtering algorithm running on the ESP32. Experimental results show that the system can perform target sensing up to 78 cm and transmit data packets error-free to the detected target up to a range of 28 cm.
keywords: ["integrated sensing and communication", "ultrasonic communication", "time-of-flight ranging", "on-off keying", "pulse interval modulation", "low-cost hardware", "ESP32 microcontroller", "target sensing"]

title: Deep Learning-Based Target Parameter Estimation in MIMO-OFDM ISAC Systems
abstract: In this study, the problem of estimating the target angle, range, and velocity parameters in MIMO-OFDM based Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) systems is investigated. The conventional three–dimensional Cell Averaged Constant False Alarm Rate (3D CA-CFAR) algorithm, widely used in radar-based approaches, suffers from limited estimation accuracy and high computational complexity, particularly under low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions. Motivated by this limitation, a deep learning-based approach is proposed to estimate target parameters through regression by directly processing ISAC detection matrices. In this study, models based on EfficientNet-B1, EfficientViT-B1, and SE-ResNeXt-26 architectures are trained on a synthetically generated dataset covering a wide SNR range and evaluated in comparison with the conventional 3D CA-CFAR method. The results demonstrate that the transformer-based EfficientViT-B1 model achieves lower estimation error and improved robustness, especially under low SNR conditions.

title: An AI-Driven Hybrid Framework for Cephalometric Landmark Detection via Metaheuristic-Optimized Heatmap CNN and Stationary Wavelet Transform
abstract: High-precision detection of cephalometric skeletal landmarks (CSLs) enables accurate analysis of skeletal, dental, and soft-tissue relationships, which is essential for orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning. In this study, regional inference using YOLOv11 was employed to automatically detect 17 CSLs on lateral cephalograms, and a heatmap-based ViTPose model was developed for each landmark. To enhance localization performance, stationary wavelet transform and hyperparameter optimization of the ViTPose model were used. The results show that the proposed approach improves CSL localization performance, reducing the mean radial error by approximately 19.75% and increasing the success detection rate by about 5% across all error thresholds. This highlights the suitability of the proposed model for cephalometric analysis.
