title: Exponential Moving Average of Vision Transformers for Skin Lesion Classification
abstract: Skin lesion classification is a critical medical image analysis task in which early diagnosis significantly improves survival rates. In this work, we address the parameter variability problem of Vision Transformer based models arising from small batch sizes at the end of training. We propose maintaining an auxiliary model that tracks the Exponential Moving Average (EMA) of the online model parameters during training. The proposed approach smooths parameter fluctuations and improves training stability without introducing any additional computational overhead. Experiments on the ISIC 2019 dataset demonstrate that, in addition to reducing parameter variability, the EMA model consistently achieves higher Macro-F1 scores (6.93%) and accuracy rates (2.67%) compared to the online model.
keywords: ["skin lesion classification", "vision transformer", "exponential moving average", "parameter variation", "auxiliary model", "training stability", "small batch sizes", "ISIC 2019", "dermatological image analysis"]

title: Few-Shot Spatial Adaptation in Medical Vision-Language Models
abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have significantly advanced open-vocabulary image understanding by learning aligned representations from large-scale image-text datasets. Despite their zero-shot generalization capabilities, adapting these foundation models to specific application domains remains challenging. Full fine-tuning is often infeasible due to computational costs and the risk of overfitting when labeled data are limited. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches promise to address this issue by updating only a small set of parameters while keeping the pre-trained encoders largely frozen. However, existing PEFT strategies often exhibit insufficient spatial awareness, rendering them suboptimal for medical imaging, where subtle visual differences can lead to distinct clinical diagnoses. To address this challenge, in this study we propose a novel PEFT technique that leverages natural-image pretrained DINOv3’s attention maps to enforce spatial alignment.
keywords: ["vision-language models", "parameter-efficient fine-tuning", "diagnostic imaging", "DINOv3", "attention maps", "spatial alignment", "zero-shot generalization", "domain adaptation"]

title: Floquet-Based Periodic Matrix Reconstruction in Discrete-Time LTP Systems
abstract: This paper investigates Floquet-based periodic matrix reconstruction for discrete-time linear time-periodic (LTP) systems. The constant Floquet state matrix is obtained from the P-th root of the monodromy matrix using the Schur–Padé algorithm. Given this matrix, two approaches are considered to reconstruct the periodic input and output matrices. The first approach (Naive) constructs periodic coordinate transforms algebraically, whereas the second approach (Least Squares – LS) estimates the periodic matrices directly from data via phase-wise linear regression. The methods are evaluated through an extensive Monte Carlo study over varying system orders and period lengths using success rate and normalised RMSE metrics.
keywords: ["Floquet theory", "linear time-periodic systems", "monodromy matrix", "linear regression", "discrete-time systems"]

title: Receiver-Centric TDOA Localization Framework for DAB Signals under Synchronization Impairments
abstract: In Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS)-denied environments, terrestrial signals of opportunity (SoOP) offer an alternative for positioning, but synchronization impairments such as clock offsets, drift, and multipath limit performance. This paper proposes a receiver-centric multi-channel time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA) localization framework based on Digital Audio Broadcasting (DAB) signals. The method exploits the DAB null symbol for coarse timing and the phase reference symbol (PRS) for fine synchronization, followed by sub-sample time-of-arrival (TOA) estimation. A double-difference formulation removes inter-receiver clock offsets, while a peak-to-sidelobe ratio (PSR)-based weighting improves robustness. A bias correction step mitigates errors due to multipath. Finally, a coordinated-turn extended Kalman filter (CT-EKF) further refines position estimates. Results show improved accuracy over conventional TDOA with Gauss–Newton estimation, especially in challenging conditions.
keywords: ["TDOA localization", "digital audio broadcasting", "signals of opportunity", "GNSS-denied positioning", "clock offset", "multipath propagation", "bias correction"]

title: Improving Cypher Query Generation from Natural Language using Reinforcement Learning with Large Language Models
abstract: This study addresses the automated generation of Cypher queries from natural language expressions for graph databases, systematically analyzing the impact of various training strategies and data augmentation techniques on model performance. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate significant potential in natural language-to-query tasks, their generalization to unseen schemas and structural accuracy remain critical challenges. In this context, the study investigates the contributions of Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), Reinforcement Learning (RL), and cross-domain training strategies utilizing relational database (SQL) data to the Text-to-Cypher task.
keywords: ["Cypher query generation", "natural language to query translation", "graph databases", "large language models", "reinforcement learning", "supervised fine-tuning", "data augmentation"]

title: Explainable AI-Based Misclassification Analysis
abstract: This study employs the SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) method to interpret erroneous model decisions. We evaluated Random Forest, Multi-Layer Perceptron, and XGBoost classifiers using three datasets from the error-sensitive fields of healthcare and e-commerce fraud. Through SHAP value analysis of misclassified instances, we identified the specific features leading to incorrect outputs. Additionally, we examined the minimum feature changes necessary to correct these decisions using a counterfactual SHAP approach. Our experimental results indicate that SHAP-based analysis provides a robust framework for diagnosing error mechanisms and assessing the severity of model failures.

title: On the Tunability of Hyperparameters in Support Vector Regression
abstract: This study investigates hyperparameter tunability in Support Vector Regression models using 32 datasets. The objective is to determine which hyperparameters should be prioritized for optimization to maximize model performance, and to propose a tuning strategy. Experiments were conducted with 5-fold cross-validation, and a search space of 50,000 configurations was explored. Results show that tunability is higher and more variable for NRMSE, while gains in R2are more limited but dataset-dependent. At the hyperparameter level, defaults remain sufficient for kernel (radial) and degree, whereas optimizing cost, gamma, and epsilon provides additional improvement. Mean optimal values were 3.42 for cost, 1.57 for R2and 1.96 for NRMSE for gamma, and 0.18 for R2and 0.19 for NRMSE for epsilon. For resource-constrained settings, a two-stage strategy—focusing first on cost and gamma, then refining epsilon—is recommended; more broadly, metric-sensitive optimization is preferred over a single fixed configuration.

title: Feature Interaction-Based Blood Cell Classification: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning and Ensemble Methods
abstract: Accurate and efficient classification of blood cells is crucial for the early diagnosis of hematological diseases. In this study, a feature engineering-based approach is proposed for multi-class classification of blood cells by leveraging morphological and color-based feature interactions. To enhance the representational power of the tabular dataset, meaningful interactions are constructed among features such as cell area, perimeter, color channels, and staining intensity. Various machine learning algorithms are evaluated on the proposed feature set, with a particular focus on comparing gradient boosting-based methods with conventional classifiers. In addition, ensemble learning approaches, including weighted voting and stacking, are investigated to assess their potential performance improvements. Experimental results have shown that the CatBoost model outperformed all other methods with 98.55% accuracy and a macro F1 score of 97.92%. In contrast, it has been observed that ensemble methods have not been able to significantly surpass this performance level.

title: Plant Monitoring and Irrigation System with ESP32, MQTT, and HomeKit Integration via Homebridge
abstract: Indoor and small-scale plant care is often influenced by important environmental factors such as temperature, humidity, light, and soil moisture, as well as by issues such as inconsistent watering and limited visibility. This paper presents a low-cost Internet of Things (IoT)-based facility monitoring and irrigation system built around an ESP32 microcontroller and integrated into Apple HomeKit via Homebridge. The ESP32 collects readings from a DHT22 temperature/humidity sensor, a BH1750 ambient light sensor, and an analog soil moisture sensor connected to the ESP32 ADC. The system enables real-time monitoring and control through a cloud MQTT broker (HiveMQ Cloud) over TLS from the smart home dashboard. It supports both manual and automatic pump control, irrigation based on soil moisture thresholds, and includes safety mechanisms such as invalid sensor detection and maximum pump-on timeout. Experimental validation demonstrates reliable MQTT-based telemetry delivery, accurate HomeKit visualizations, and reactive control through MQTT messages.

title: Deep Learning-Based Target Localization and Deghosting in Multistatic Radar
abstract: This study presents a deep learning method for target detection, localization and deghosting using range observations obtained from a multistatic radar system. To mitigate the ghost target problem, which emerges as a byproduct of the employed target detection algorithm, motion information is incorporated into the system and compared against the baseline case without motion. Cartesian grids generated from three consecutive coherent processing intervals (CPI) are fed into the proposed network as input channels. Within the scope of the performance analysis, U-Net++ and ConvLSTM U-Net architectures are compared in terms of parameter count, inference time, and ghost target reduction. The proposed spatio-temporal approach successfully distinguishes true targets from structurally similar ghost intersections.

title: EEG Signal Classification with a Novel Adaptive Quadratic Activation Function
abstract: In this study, the effect of different activation functions on the multi-class classification of EEG time series is investigated. For this purpose, a learnable activation function called AdaQuad is proposed, which has a quadratic structure in the positive region and a linear structure in the negative region. The proposed method is compared with classical activation functions under the same architecture and training protocol. MLP and 1D-CNN models are used in the experiments, and performance is evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score metrics. The results show that the choice of activation function has a significant impact on model performance and that the AdaQuad activation produces competitive and stable results in many cases.

title: Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM and Adaptive Channel Fusion Approach for Sleep Stage Classification from Multi-Channel PSG Signals
abstract: Sleep stage classification is an important component of computer-aided sleep analysis; however, manual scoring of polysomnography (PSG) recordings is time consuming and observer dependent. This study proposes a hybrid CNN-BiLSTM model with adaptive channel fusion for multi- channel PSG-based sleep stage classification on the Sleep- EDF Expanded dataset. The model combines channel-wise CNN representations extracted from EEG/EOG/EMG signals, handcrafted time-frequency features, and BiLSTM-based temporal context over neighboring epochs. In response to the review comments, the experimental evaluation is expanded beyond an XGBoost baseline and includes Random Forest, SVM, MLP, CNN-1D, BiLSTM and CNN-BiLSTM models under the same evaluation protocol. The proposed CNN-BiLSTM-AKF model achieves 0.8297 accuracy, 0.7699 macro F1 and 0.7583 Cohen’s kappa. It also provides the best N1 and REM F1 values among the compared models, supporting its balanced behavior for transition-like stages.

title: On the Effectiveness of Adversarial and Diffusion Models for EEG Augmentation in ASD
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder that affects individuals’ speech, social interaction, and behavior. Early diagnosis of ASD is very challenging and subjective. Developing an objective diagnosis method requires the use of artificial intelligence (AI) and large, well-collected, and labeled databases. Due to the lack of datasets with a large sample size, this study investigates a conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty (cWGAN-GP) and diffusion model (DM) on the resting-state Electroencephalography (rs-EEG) dataset, to produce synthetic data. The similarity between real and synthetic data produced by these models was investigated using power spectral density (PSD), nearest neighbor analysis (NNA), frequency band mean square error (FB-MSE), mean and standard deviation (STD). The experimental results demonstrate that cWGAN-GP has a higher potential to produce synthetic data with a higher similarity to the real data.

title: Outlier Detection Algorithms and Autoencoders for Financial Anomaly Detection
abstract: This study aims to detect errors or suspicious patterns in the data reported by financial institutions to the Risk Center as part of a regulatory obligation before the reporting process is completed. The primary objective is to prevent erroneous notifications, improve data quality at the source, and minimize operational risks by establishing an early warning mechanism. Within the scope of this study, machine learning and deep learning techniques are applied to identify anomalies in daily credit reporting data submitted by financial institutions. Key attributes requested by the Risk Center during the reporting process—such as loan type, maturity, loan amount, and reporting date—are used as primary features in the modeling stage. Inconsistencies, data integrity violations, or rule-breaking transactions occurring between these reported fields are flagged as anomalies by the model. Regulatory frameworks require financial institutions to maintain high data accuracy when reporting to the Risk Center. If the anomaly rate in daily notifications exceeds 5%, the relevant financial institution may face regulatory sanctions. Therefore, early detection of anomalous records is critical for maintaining compliance and ensuring data reliability. The proposed approach enables financial institutions to identify potential anomalies before the data is officially reported to the Risk Center, allowing institutions to correct erroneous records at the source. As a result, the system contributes to improving data quality, reducing operational risks, and preventing potential regulatory penalties.
keywords: ["financial anomaly detection", "outlier detection", "autoencoder", "financial institutions", "regulatory compliance", "data quality", "operational risk", "early warning mechanism"]

title: RIS-Assisted Secure Transmission with Artificial Noise: Element Allocation and Measurements
abstract: Physical layer security in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted wireless systems can be improved through coordinated control of signal transmission and RIS configuration. In this work, the base station simultaneously transmits the communication signal (CS) and artificial noise (AN) in the presence of a potential eavesdropper. The RIS is partitioned into two groups of reflecting elements, where a portion enhances the desired CS toward the legitimate receiver, while the remaining elements contribute to AN transmission. Two key parameters govern the system design: a transmit power allocation factor between CS and AN, and an RIS element allocation ratio controlling the partitioning of the reflecting elements. An iterative binary phase optimization strategy is employed to enhance the received signal power at Bob while degrading Eve’s reception. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that proper joint design significantly improves the achievable secrecy capacity.

title: RAG-Based Drug Information Chatbot on Turkish Medication Package Inserts
abstract: This study presents a Turkish Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-based medication information chatbot built on drug package inserts published by the Turkish Medicines and Medical Devices Agency (TITCK). The proposed system aims to reduce hallucinations in healthcare applications by grounding large language models on reliable medication leaflets. A knowledge base containing package inserts for 14,738 medications was constructed, and a gold evaluation dataset consisting of 1,199 queries was developed to assess retrieval performance. Dense, sparse, and hybrid retrieval approaches were compared using Hit Rate and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) metrics across multiple embedding models. Experimental results demonstrate that the BAAI/bge-m3-based hybrid retrieval approach achieved the best performance, obtaining a Hit Rate of 83.57% and an MRR of 0.4799.

title: Learning-Based Joint Antenna Selection and Hybrid Beamforming for Multi-User Massive MIMO
abstract: This study proposes learning-based joint antenna subset selection and hybrid beamforming for multi-user massive multiple-input multiple-output systems under imperfect Channel State Information (CSI). The problem is formulated as a combined classification task for antenna selection and an estimation task for analog beamformers’ prediction. To address this, a deep learning-based framework has been developed to directly predict antenna subsets and analog beamforming from imperfect CSI. The predicted analog beamformers are combined with a structured, regularized zero-forcing minimum mean square error baseband precoder organized based on the effective channel, while phase quantization is included to reflect practical hardware constraints. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a near-optimal sum-rate, making it robust and efficient even under imperfect CSI.

title: Classification Model Selection Using a Mahalanobis Based Multi Criteria Decision Making Metric
abstract: Selecting the most suitable classifier in machine learning requires evaluating multiple performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, sensitivity, and F1 score together. However, examining these metrics separately makes comparison difficult when different models excel in different criteria. This study proposes a Mahalanobis-based composite metric that considers both the correlation between performance metrics and model stability across cross-validation folds within a multi criteria decision making approach. The proposed method represents each model as a performance vector, calculates the weighted distance from the ideal values of the metrics, and integrates stability by adding the standard deviation as a penalty score. The results of the study demonstrate that the approach is simple, understandable, and applicable for multi-criteria model evaluation.
keywords: ["classifier selection", "model selection", "multi-criteria decision making", "Mahalanobis distance"]

title: Hierarchical Text Classification of Public Petitions: Comparing Hybrid and Ensemble-Based Approaches
abstract: Automatic classification of legal petition documents is critical for analyzing similar cases and developing decision support systems. However, the long and complex structure of legal texts, along with the morphological characteristics of Turkish, makes this task challenging. In this study, a dataset of 5,123 petition documents is modeled within a hierarchical structure consisting of seven top-level categories and forty-eight subcategories. A two-stage hybrid architecture is proposed and compared with classical, transformer-based, and ensemble learning approaches. In the proposed method, top-level classification is performed using an MLP, while subcategory prediction is handled by category-specific models. In addition, a multi-model stacking strategy is evaluated. Experimental results show that the three-model stacking approach achieves the best performance and highlights the complementary strengths of different model families.
keywords: ["hierarchical text classification", "public petitioning", "legal documents", "Turkish language", "ensemble learning", "stacking", "transformer models", "multilayer perceptron", "decision support system"]

title: Detection of Sleep Spindles using Temporal Convolutional Networks
abstract: Sleep spindles, which are directly associated with the diagnosis of sleep disorders, are analyzed from sleep electroencephalograms (EEG) based on their distinct morphological structures. Due to the subjective nature of manual scoring, sleep spindle detection remains a challenging task in biomedical signal processing. Therefore, the application of deep learning models for automated sleep spindle detection is currently an active area of research. In this study, a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) model is presented, which possesses a high generalization capability in capturing local features through its dilated convolution architecture. Using the open-access DREAMS dataset, 5-second EEG segments were provided to the model as input. To prevent data leakage, a subject-independent validation strategy was employed. By optimizing the receptive field size of the model, an accuracy of 97.16%, precision of 84.41%, recall of 66.42%, and an F1-score of 74.34% were achieved in sleep spindle detection. Consequently, an objective and clinically reliable model has been developed for the automated detection of sleep spindles, which reduces inter-scorer variability and operates end-to-end without requiring any external post-processing steps.

title: Efficient Magnitude-Domain Plug-and-Play Regularization Method for SAR Imaging
abstract: Radar imaging seeks to reconstruct the reflectivity distribution of a scene using measurements of backscattered electromagnetic waves. In this study, an efficient plug-and-play reconstruction approach with deep priors is adapted to synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imaging. For this purpose, the measurement model is first presented. For the solution of the inverse problem corresponding to the image reconstruction problem, regularization is enforced in the magnitude domain due to the random nature of the phase. In the adapted ADMM-based reconstruction approach, for the proximal operator, a closed-form efficient solution is used for the phase update step, while a U-Net-based denoiser is used for the magnitude component. Based on the training and experiments performed on Sentinel-1 SAR images, it is observed that the developed method provides higher image quality than classical FFT-based reconstruction at different data availability and noise levels.
keywords: ["synthetic aperture radar imaging", "plug-and-play regularization", "deep priors", "alternating direction method of multipliers", "phase retrieval", "inverse problems", "Sentinel-1", "SAR image reconstruction"]

title: Illicit Pattern Analysis in Bitcoin Transactions via Graph Neural Networks
abstract: Cryptocurrency transactions are pseudonymous and irreversible, which allows for fast and efficient global transfers. However, these features can also enable illegal activities such as money laundering. Detecting suspicious transactions is challenging because financial flows form complex relationships that traditional tabular methods cannot capture. In this work, we model Bitcoin transactions as a directed graph and formulate illicit transaction detection as a node classification problem. Experimental results show that graph-based models significantly outperform the feature-only baseline. Among the evaluated architectures, GraphSAGE achieves the best performance with an illicit-class F1-score of 0.8615 and ROC-AUC of 0.9788. Our analysis shows the importance of transaction connectivity for financial crime detection in blockchain networks.

title: An Explainable and Attention-Mechanism-Based Deep Learning Framework for Reliable Plant Disease Detection
abstract: The escalating global food crisis, exacerbated by climate change-induced yield losses and the increasing impact of pests and plant diseases, has reached a critical level. The early and accurate detection of plant diseases is of strategic importance not only for ensuring sustainable agricultural production but also for reducing economic dependency and safeguarding food security. Although deep learning-based approaches proposed in the existing literature often achieve high classification accuracy, their decision-making processes largely remain opaque, thereby limiting model reliability and practical adoption. In this study, a MobileNetV2-based deep learning architecture was employed for plant leaf disease classification, and the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) was integrated to enhance model performance. By emphasizing salient regions within leaf images, CBAM improved classification accuracy while simultaneously reducing computational overhead associated with processing irrelevant features. Furthermore, to enhance model interpretability, the Grad-CAM technique was applied to visualize the specific features and image regions that influenced the model's predictions. The experimental results not only demonstrate the contribution of the attention mechanism to classification performance but also address a significant gap in transparency and reliability within deep learning-based agricultural decision support systems.

title: DilHiper: Multi-View Hypergraphs for Multi-Label Text Classification
abstract: Multi-label text classification is a challenging problem due to label dependencies, class imbalance, and the complexity of intra-text relationships. While current approaches mainly rely on Transformer-based text representations, graph- and hypergraph-based methods have also been used for modeling relational structures more explicitly. These methods first became prominent in the broader context of text classification and were later explored for multi-label text classification as well. In particular, hypergraph-based modeling strategies for this setting remain relatively limited and open to further development. In this work, we propose DilHiper, a multi-view hypergraph-based architecture for multi-label text classification. In the proposed framework, each document is first encoded by a pre-trained Transformer, after which four different hypergraph views are constructed. These views are processed by a shared hypergraph neural network, contrastive learning is employed to encourage consistency across views, and the resulting hypergraph branch is combined with the document-level representation. Experiments on the GoEmotions dataset show that the proposed approach outperforms baseline Transformer models as well as current state-of-the-art methods.
keywords: ["multi-label text classification", "hypergraph neural networks", "multi-view learning", "label dependencies", "class imbalance", "contrastive learning", "GoEmotions", "text representation learning"]

title: Deep Learning Based Channel Estimation for THz Band Ultra Massive MIMO Systems
abstract: THz ultra-massive MIMO is a key technology for 6G systems, but hybrid near- and far-field propagation, limited RF chains, and severe path loss make channel estimation challenging. Model-driven deep learning approaches, such as FPN-OAMP, address this problem by combining a physics-driven linear estimator with a learnable nonlinear estimator (NLE) within a contractive fixed-point framework with convergence guarantees. In this paper, we redesign the NLE of the FPN-OAMP framework through three deep-learning schemes: Differentiable Architecture Search (DARTS), DARTS with Block Recurrent Transformer (BRT) and Vision Transformer (ViT). DARTS optimizes multiscale convolutional operations, BRT provides iterative global refinement, and ViT enables attention-driven spatial modeling in the FPN-OAMP framework. Our simulations show consistent performance improvements for FPN-OAMP across a wide range of signal-to-noise ratio levels, while retaining similar asymptotic complexity.
keywords: ["channel estimation", "terahertz communication", "ultra-massive MIMO", "differentiable architecture search", "DART", "vision transformer", "6G", "near-field and far-field propagation", "limited RF chains"]

title: Bearing Fault Diagnosis under Small-Sample Conditions Based on Unsupervised Representation Learning
abstract: Early detection of bearing faults in rotating machinery is essential for predictive maintenance. Although deep learning-based methods have achieved strong results in fault diagnosis, they usually require large amounts of labeled data. In industrial settings, however, faulty samples are limited, which restricts the applicability of fully supervised approaches. In this study, a bearing fault diagnosis framework based on unsupervised representation learning is proposed for limited-label scenarios. Firstly, a convolutional autoencoder is trained on raw vibration signals without using labels to learn informative latent representations. After that, these learned representations are classified using only a limited number of labeled samples. The proposed method is evaluated on the CWRU bearing dataset under same-load and cross-load settings with both single and dual-channel inputs. Experimental results show that the proposed framework achieves strong performance under low-label conditions and that the dual-channel setup further improves classification performance.

title: Low-Complexity Hybrid CNN-LSTM Based SINR Estimation For DS-UWB Systems In Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: Direct Sequence Ultra-Wideband (DS-UWB) technology is a promising physical-layer solution for wireless sensor networks due to its high temporal resolution and low power consumption. In this study, a low-complexity Signal-to-Interference-plus-Noise Ratio (SINR) estimation architecture capable of operating under sudden Multiple Access Interference (MAI) and varying channel conditions in DS-UWB-based networks is proposed. The proposed architecture is a hybrid neural network that combines Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) layers for extracting local feature patterns and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) layers for learning temporal dependencies. The model was trained using I/Q datasets generated based on the IEEE 802.15.4a CM1/CM2 channel models and evaluated under different active node scenarios. The results while also showing that the interference signal tends to exhibit Gaussian characteristics as network density increases. Furthermore, the proposed architecture achieved promising results for real-time deployment on resource-constrained nodes, requiring only 58.6 thousand parameters and a memory footprint of 216 KB. The study comprehensively addresses both the modeling aspects of the proposed architecture and its suitability for edge applications in terms of energy efficiency.

title: LLM-Based Natural Language Explanation of Vessel Behaviors Derived from AIS Data: A Comparison of Zero-shot and Few-shot Approaches
abstract: Automatic Identification System (AIS) data are widely used for monitoring and analyzing vessel movements in maritime domains. However, the numerical and low-level nature of AIS data makes it difficult for human operators to interpret vessel behaviors effectively. In this study, a novel approach is proposed to generate natural language explanations of vessel behaviors derived from AIS data using Large Language Models (LLMs).In the proposed framework, meaningful behavioral events such as speed changes, course deviations, and traffic interactions are first extracted from AIS data using a rule-based method. These structured representations are then provided as input to an LLM to generate concise and human-readable explanations. To evaluate model performance, zero-shot and few-shot prompting strategies are compared. The evaluation is conducted using macro-averaged F1 score for multi-label classification and hallucination rate to measure the tendency of the model to generate non-existent events.Experimental results on AIS data demonstrate that prompting strategy has a significant impact on model performance. The few-shot approach improves event coverage accuracy (F1 = 0.667) and eliminates hallucinations (0.000), whereas the zero-shot approach yields lower accuracy (F1 = 0.506) and higher hallucination rate (0.236).These findings indicate that the direct use of LLMs may not be sufficient for reliable outputs; however, carefully designed prompts can substantially improve both accuracy and reliability. The proposed method enhances the interpretability of AIS data and shows strong potential for maritime decision support systems

title: Machine Learning-Aided Optimal Wavelength Selection for Stratospheric Free-Space Optical Links
abstract: Free-space optical (FSO) communication is a promising solution for high-capacity airborne non-terrestrial networks. This paper analyzes the BER of a stratospheric airborne FSO link as a function of wavelength in the presence of atmospheric attenuation, geometric loss, and pointing error. The results show that BER varies non-monotonically with wavelength, leading to an optimal operating wavelength. A regression-based machine learning model is then proposed to predict this optimum from channel and transceiver parameters.

title: EKG Skalograflarının CLIP Tabanlı Sıfır-Atışlı Sınıflandırmada Spektrogramlara Üstünlüğü
abstract: Biyomedikal sinyal yorumlamada büyük görme-dil modellerinin kullanımı hızla artmaktadır. Bu çalışmada, PTB-XL veri kümesinden elde edilen EKG sinyallerinin iki farklı zamanfrekans gösteriminin-Sürekli Dalgacık Dönüşümü (CWT) ile Kısa Zamanlı Fourier Dönüşümü’nün (STFT)-CLIP modeliyle sıfır-atışlı semantik hizalanma başarımı karşılaştırılmaktadır. Beş kardiyak durum sintfı üzerinde kosinüs benzerliği, ilk-k geri getirme doğruluğu ve silhouette ölçütleriyle gerçekleştirilen deneyler, CWT skalogramlarının ortalama kosinüs benzerliğini %23,4 artırdığını ve CLIP gömülme uzayında istatistiksel olarak anlamlı daha iyi kümeleşme sağladığını göstermektedir. Bu bulgular, gösterim seçiminin çok modlu biyomedikal sinyal yorumlamada kritik bir tasarım değişkeni olduğunu ortaya koymaktadır.

title: Secrecy Performance of RIS-Assisted Communication Systems with Antenna Selection
abstract: This study investigates the secrecy performance of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted communication systems employing antenna selection techniques. In particular, transmit antenna selection (TAS), receive antenna selection (RAS), and joint transmit–receive antenna selection (JTRAS) schemes are considered, and the system is analyzed over Rayleigh fading channels. The secrecy performance of the system is evaluated in terms of ergodic secrecy capacity (ESC) and secrecy outage probability (SOP). The impacts of the number of reflecting elements on the RIS, different antenna configurations, and the distance ratio between the legitimate user and the eavesdropper (EVE) on system security are investigated. Numerical results obtained via Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that the antenna selection schemes significantly enhance the physical layer security of RIS-assisted communication systems.

title: Federated Learning for Hybrid Recommendation Systems
abstract: Recommendation systems play a crucial role in enhancing user experiences by delivering personalised suggestions. However, they face persistent challenges in balancing personalization, privacy, and transparency. This paper introduces the recommendation engine for CAPE, an architecture that integrates Federated Learning (FL) with feature detection based on speech-to-text outputs from CAPE’s multimodal emotion detection pipeline. The proposed architecture supports secure, interpretable, and context-aware recommendations while preserving sensitive user data locally and enabling continuous model improvement without centralising user information.

title: Cost-Efficient Hybrid Human-AI Handoff System: A Density-Based Semantic Clustering Approach for Customer Support Dialogs in the Wild
abstract: Integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into customer support workflows offers strong automation potential, yet raises risks related to hallucination, operational cost, and the handling of sensitive requests. This study proposes a label-efficient Semantic Router for hybrid human-AI handoff. The proposed approach combines unsupervised semantic clustering of historical agent responses with domain-informed Weighted Complexity Scoring (WCS) to identify latent support categories and route high-risk clusters to human operators. A distance-based out-of-distribution (OOD) filter is also introduced to detect queries that fall outside known support patterns. Experiments on an internal customer support dataset, Banking77, and CLINC150 show that the framework achieves a 0.56 Silhouette Score, 0.76 NMI, and 0.88 ROC-AUC for OOD detection. The results indicate that the proposed system can support safer and more cost-efficient human-in-the-loop customer support automation.

title: Zero-Shot versus Few-Shot Prompting for Complex Intent Recognition in E-Commerce Dialogue Systems: An Evaluation on an Adversarial Dataset
abstract: E-commerce dialogue systems often encounter difficulties with complex, highly specific customer intents not represented in standard training sets. Conventional intent classification requires comprehensive, labeled datasets that are costly to create. This work focuses on assessing the effectiveness of Large Language Models for custom intent recognition using zero-shot and few-shot prompting techniques. We examine a synthetically generated domain-specific, adversarial dataset of e-commerce support intents with closely related meanings. We compare an efficient open-weight model (Llama-3.1-8B-Instant) against two proprietary models (GPT-3.5-Turbo and Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite). Our findings show the impact of few-shot prompting on classification accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, and macro F1-score. The results indicate that although smaller open-weight models struggle with zero-shot scenarios, few-shot prompting guides their reasoning, enabling them to potentially achieve high accuracies.

title: Deep Learning Approaches for Bearing Fault Diagnosis Using Motor Current Signals
abstract: Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) is a non-invasive technique that enables the detection of bearing faults in rotating electrical machines without the need for additional sensors. In this study, the Paderborn University bearing dataset was utilized to perform a two-stage analysis. In the first stage, motor current data were processed directly using 1-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (1D-CNN). In the second stage, scalogram images obtained via Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) were used to train five different deep learning models, with the ResNet18-based 2D-CNN model providing the best performance. To prevent data leakage, the training and testing sets were partitioned based on individual bearings to ensure complete isolation. The experimental results demonstrated that both 1D-CNN and ResNet18-based 2D-CNN methods achieved 100% accuracy in detecting outer race faults. However, it was observed that the impact of inner race faults on the stator current remains weak due to the complex physical transmission path of the fault signal, resulting in significantly lower detection rates.

title: A New Energy and Spectrum Efficient Optical MIMO-OFDM System
abstract: This study proposes the use of IFHT/FHT transforms instead of IFFT/FFT transforms in a 2×2 MIMO-OFDM system to improve energy efficiency and spectral efficiency. This study is the first in the literature to conduct comparative performance analyses of BPSK, 4-CSK, 8-CSK, and 16-CSK modulations in a 2×2 MIMO optical channel environment. The results obtained from the simulation studies show that the proposed MIMO-DHT-OFDM system provides a PAPR gain of up to 3 dB. However, it is evident that the proposed method achieves 100% spectral efficiency in the modulation schemes used in this study.
